Calc!B10 should be =B8+B9; Calc!B11 should be =B7/<prior-year revenue> or 0 for the actuals column; Calc!B43 should be =B42/B41; Calc!B41 should be =B39-B40. Work through rows 10, 11, 12, 19, 28, 34, 35, 36, 41, 43, 47, 48, 51-60 and resolve each placeholder to a real cell or defined name, then confirm no #N/A remains.

issue: Twelve Outputs cells inherited the #N/A from Calc column B. Outputs!B8 = [=Calc!B10], Outputs!B22 = [=Calc!B34], Outputs!B25 = [=IF(Calc!B59>=0,"Funded from cash and free cash flow","Needs debt or a smaller r] — the Verdict cell is #N/A and its text is truncated mid-word ('smaller r'). The summary tab shows no view at all.
fix: Once Calc column B is fixed, re-point and confirm every Outputs cell evaluates. For Outputs!B25, correct the truncated string to full text, e.g. "Needs debt or a smaller return of capital".

where: Checks!F3 Master status = ERROR; Checks!B8 = #N/A [=Outputs!B19-Calc!B10]; Checks!B14 = #N/A [=MIN(Calc!C35:G35)-Calc!B59]; Checks!C8 and C14 = #N/A

Two checks (Outputs cash ties to Calc, and the sensitivity-corner tie) are #N/A because they reference the broken column B. A file whose own master check reads ERROR cannot be shared — that is the first thing a client or an IC reviewer opens.

where: Checks row 'Cash roll-forward ties to closing cash': difference -15,330.48, status ERROR
issue: The cash roll-forward does not tie to closing cash — off by $15,330.48m. Calc!B34 = [=B{cash_open_row}+B{fcf_row}+B{returns_row}+B{intinc_row}+B{debt_row}] should equal Calc!B33 plus the year's movements. A $15.3bn break is not rounding; a component is missing or double-counted (likely the capex/FCF sign or the opening-cash carry). Cash is the spine of this model — if it does not roll, nothing downstream is credible.
fix: Trace Calc!B34 against B33 + B10 + B28 + B29 + B30 and identify the missing/mis-signed line. Reconcile so Checks row 'Cash roll-forward ties to closing cash' shows difference 0.

where: Checks row 'Closing shares equal opening shares less shares retired': difference 3.62, status ERROR (Calc!B41, Calc!B58)
issue: Closing shares do not tie: opening less retired is off by 3.62m shares. Calc!B58 = [=B{sh_open_row}-G{sh_close_row}] and Calc!B41 = [=B{sh_open_row}-B{sh_ret_row}]. Either the buyback share-retirement formula (Calc!G40 = -G26/share_price) uses the wrong price or period, or FY2026 closing shares (443.1m from the cover, dated 2026-09-29) are being run through a buyback that did not exist in FY2026. 3.62m shares at $1,106.21 is ~$4.0bn — the whole authorisation; this is not a rounding artifact.
fix: Make Calc!B41 equal B39-B40 exactly and confirm the same identity holds for every forecast column C-G. If the FY2026 column should show zero retirement, set B40=0 and reconcile the check.

where: workbook — no DCF, WACC, terminal value, comps or equity bridge anywhere in the 5 tabs
issue: There is no valuation. No WACC build, no terminal value, no exit multiple cross-check, no comps, no net-debt-to-equity bridge, no per-share value on diluted shares. The Outputs tab stops at 'Verdict' = cash funded from operations. For a capital-allocation model that is defensible as scope, but the digest titles it 'Costco capital allocation model' and the Outputs tab has a 'Verdict' cell (Outputs!B25) that reads like a recommendation. If this is the decision support for the special dividend and $4bn buyback, the committee will ask what the capital return is worth versus retaining it — and the model cannot answer.
fix: Either (a) add a Valuation tab: WACC built up and sourced (risk-free from F21 5.15%, beta, ERP), mid-year convention, terminal value share of EV shown, exit multiple cross-check, equity bridge (net debt from debt_fy26 $3,914m, cash_fy26 $20,207m), per-share on diluted shares; or (b) if capital allocation only, retitle Outputs!B25 to 'Funding test' and state explicitly on the Cover that no valuation is in scope.

where: Inputs tab — 'Special dividend paid in year [special_year] = 1; source: F34, news item 2026 (declared); timing assumed in the first forecast year FY2027'
issue: The single largest cash outflow in the model — $30/share on 443.1m shares = $13,293m — is triggered by an assumed timing ('timing assumed in the first forecast year') with no source. The special dividend is declared; the payment date is not sourced. Whether it lands in FY2027 or FY2028 swings the minimum-cash test (Outputs!B23, Calc!B59) by $13.3bn and could flip the Verdict.
fix: Source the declaration's payment date from the F34 news item or the company's 8-K; set special_year to the fiscal year in which the cash actually leaves. Add a one-line note: 'Payment date per [source]; assumed FY2027'.

where: Inputs — 'Buyback executed in year 1 ($m) [buyback_y1] = 2,885; source: ... remaining availability $1,115m at 2026-08-30; F34 $4bn reauthorisation'
issue: $2,885m in year 1 is not sourced — it is residual arithmetic (4,000 auth − 1,115 remaining) labelled as fact and paired with a 'range 1,115 to 4,000'. The phasing between y1 and y2 is admitted as 'illustrative phasing' in the y2 source. The committee will read $2,885m as guidance; it is a plug.
fix: Relabel [buyback_y1] source to 'Modelled: $4,000m authorisation less $1,115m availability at FY2026 year-end; phasing assumed' and flag in Outputs. If the company guided a pace, source it; otherwise present y1/y2 as a scenario switch, not a single point.

where: Calc!E18, G18 (=-capex_base*(1+capex_growth)^3 and ^5); Calc!E25-G27, E45-G46 (IF(3=special_year,...), IF(5=special_year,...))
issue: Period indices are hard-coded inside formulas across the capex, dividend and buyback rows — E-column hard-codes 3, G-column hard-codes 5, with the exponent matching the column number. This is why the digest flags 'INCONSISTENT across periods (5 patterns)' on rows 18, 25, 26, 27, 45 and 46. Insert a column, or shift the forecast start by a year, and every one of these silently mis-ties with no error.
fix: Replace the hard-coded integer with a period-index row (e.g. a hidden-but-visible 'Year' row: 1,2,3,4,5 across C:G) and reference it: =-capex_base*(1+capex_growth)^$C$X and IF($C$X=special_year,...). Then confirm rows 18, 25, 26, 27, 45, 46 show one consistent pattern across C:G.

where: Calc!B64-G68 (sensitivity block) — Calc!C64 = [=cash_fy26+SUMPRODUCT(ocf_margin*revenue_fy26*(1+0.03)^ROW(INDIRECT("1:5")))-SUMPRODUCT(ca...] and 24 sibling cells
issue: The sensitivity grid is a parallel, hard-coded re-implementation of the model: it hard-codes 0.03/0.045/0.06/0.075/0.09, 70/80/90/110, the literal 5 periods and 5 in ROW(INDIRECT("1:5")), instead of driving the live Calc rows. Checks row 'Sensitivity corner equals the base case at 6% growth and $90m per warehouse' fails: difference 19,877.06. So the sensitivity does not reconcile to the base case — the classic symptom of a formula that has drifted from the engine it is supposed to stress.
fix: Rebuild the grid so each cell recalculates the cash path through the live rows C:G (or a single parameterised block), and make the corner (6% growth, $90m/warehouse) reproduce the base-case minimum cash exactly. Then the check difference must be 0.

issue: The sensitivity axes (capex-per-warehouse $70/80/90/110m and growth 3.0%/4.5%/6.0%/7.5%/9.0%) are typed directly into the Calc tab rather than living on the Inputs tab. The Inputs tab states the range for [capex_per_store] is 70 to 110 and [rev_growth] 3.0% to 8.0% — the grid's top end (9.0%) exceeds the stated 8.0% range, so the sensitivity tests a case the assumption book says is out of range. The only cells that should be typed are blue on the Inputs tab.
fix: Move the two axis vectors onto Inputs as named ranges (sens_growth, sens_capex_per_store), have Calc reference them, and either extend the documented [rev_growth] range to 9.0% with a source or cap the grid at 8.0%.

where: Inputs — 'Special dividend and buyback funded by debt if cash is short (1 = yes) [fund_with_debt] = 0; source: Open question: how Costco is financed... research found nothing'
issue: The switch that decides whether the model assumes new debt at all is set to 0 on the strength of a failed literature search, not an assumption. With fund_with_debt=0 the debt row Calc!B30/G30 = 0 for all periods and the model can only ever conclude 'funded from cash'. That is a conclusion built into an input, not derived.
fix: Either source Costco's stated financing policy (10-K liquidity section, revolving credit terms) and set the switch accordingly, or run both states (0 and 1) and show the Outputs Verdict for each. Never set a decision switch to the value that makes the answer come out.

where: Inputs — '[rev_growth] = 6.0%; source: F2, 10-K FY2026 revenue $303,154m vs $275,235m in FY2025 (+10.2%)...'
issue: The core revenue driver is a single 6.0% growth rate, mid-range of 3-8%, sourced to last year's actual print (+10.2%) with a list of macro articles behind it. That is a growth rate, not a driver. For Costco the answer depends on comparable sales, membership fee income and new-store productivity — none of these is modelled; new stores are added at 30/yr but their revenue contribution is nowhere separated from comp growth. The committee's first question, 'what is comp and what is new-store?', cannot be answered.
fix: Split revenue growth into (i) comparable-warehouse sales growth and (ii) contribution from the 30 new warehouses, each sourced (10-K comp disclosure, F31 store plan) with ranges; or at minimum source the 6.0% to consensus/guidance rather than a one-line extrapolation.

where: Calc!B44 = [=0] and Calc!G44 = IF(G41=0,0,G42/G41-G42/G39) -> 0; Outputs!B27 'EPS uplift from the buyback in FY2027 ($)' = 0
issue: EPS uplift reads 0 in every column because share_price (1,106.21) times the retired shares does not reduce the count in any period that matters; the buyback y1/y2 phasing meets a share count that is unchanged by FY2031 (G41 = 443.1). The model therefore shows a $4bn buyback that retires no shares and lifts EPS by nothing — the headline result is a null.
fix: Trace why Calc!G40 (=IF(share_price=0,0,-G26/share_price)) and the retirement timing produce 0 shares retired by FY2031, and fix the retirement to occur in the year the buyback executes. If genuinely zero, say so explicitly rather than reporting '0' with no note.

where: Outputs!A25 label 'Verdict' (X10 warning: 'label has no unit'), and Outputs row 25 number format 'text' does not show negatives in parentheses
issue: Outputs!A25 'Verdict' carries no unit or basis, and row 25 is formatted as text so any negative value would not show in parentheses. Everything else on the page carries ($m) or ($) or (m).
fix: Relabel to 'Funding verdict' and note the test ('funded from cash and FCF if minimum cash held every year'), and apply the standard accounting format to row 25's numeric neighbours.

issue: Checks!B16 counts 25 sensitivity cells; if the grid shape changes the count check passes on the wrong population. And Calc!B64-B68 are typed constants (70, 80, 90, 70?, 110) sitting in the calculation tab, one of which the digest renders as B67 = [=70] against a 70/80/90/110/110 pattern — worth confirming B67 and B68 are both 110 or both 70, as displayed.
fix: Confirm the capex axis is 70/80/90/110 (four values) or 70/70/90/110... whatever is intended, make B64:B68 a clean ascending axis referenced from Inputs, and make Checks!B16 count off the named range rather than a literal 25.

where: Cover and workbook-level: MasterCheck (Checks!F3) = ERROR; Outputs!B25 = #N/A; Calc!B59/B60 = #N/A.
issue: The file's own master check reads ERROR, and the CFO-facing verdict cell Outputs!B25 is #N/A. A workbook that tells the reader 'ERROR' on its face cannot leave the building.
fix: Fix every error cell listed in the digest (Calc!B10 through Calc!B60), confirm Checks!F3 flips to OK, and only then release. Add a single cell on Cover: 'Model status: OK — all 11 checks pass' driven off Checks!F3.

issue: Every column-B output is #N/A. The formulas reference '{ocf_row}', '{capex_row}' literals instead of resolved row numbers — the historical column doesn't calculate at all. Outputs!B19 (cumulative FCF), Outputs!B22 (cash at FY2031), Outputs!B23 (lowest cash above minimum) and Outputs!B25 (verdict) are all dead, so the model currently answers nothing.
fix: Replace the placeholders in Calc column B with real row references (e.g. Calc!B10 =B8+B9; Calc!B11 =B7/B7-1; Calc!B19 =B17+B18; Calc!B28 =B25+B26+B27; Calc!B34 =B33+B10+B28+B29+B30; Calc!B41 =B39-B40; Calc!B43 =IF(B41=0,0,B42/B41)). Repoint Outputs rows 8, 12-16, 19-26 at the correct Calc cells (e.g. Outputs!B22 should be =Calc!B54, Outputs!B23 =Calc!B59, Outputs!B19 =Calc!B51). Recalculate and confirm Checks!F3 = OK.

where: Checks!B14 / C14: 'Cash roll-forward ties to closing cash: difference -15,330.48, status ERROR'.
issue: The cash walk doesn't reconcile: the roll-forward misses $15,330.48m against closing cash. That is the whole point of the cash waterfall — if it doesn't tie, the funding conclusion is unsupported.
fix: Locate the leak between 'Cash roll-forward' and Calc!G34 and correct it — the likely gap is that the roll-forward omits one of the FCF, capital-return, interest-income or debt-draw legs (Calc!G10/G28/G29/G30). Re-drive Checks!B14 until the difference is zero. Do not paper over with a tolerance.

where: Checks tab: 'Sensitivity corner equals the base case at 6% growth and $90m per warehouse: difference 19,877.06, status ERROR'.
issue: The sensitivity grid's base-point corner doesn't equal the base case, off by $19,877.06m. If a client reads the grid as a scenario table and the middle cell doesn't reconcile to the base model, the entire scenarios section loses its credibility.
fix: Rebuild Calc!B64:G68 so the cell at 6% growth / $90m per warehouse equals the base-case cash figure in Calc!G34. The 70/80/90/110 values are hardcoded in Calc!B64:G68 and are not linked to capex_per_store — restructure so capex_per_store drives the grid and the 6%/90 corner equals the base cash cell.

issue: The whole sensitivity table is a wall of hardcoded constants (0.03/0.045/0.06/0.075/0.09; 70/80/90/110; the '5' horizon; the ROW(INDIRECT("1:5")) trick). Every driver the input tab exposes (rev_growth, capex_per_store, ocf_margin) is bypassed inside the grid. Change an input and the grid doesn't move — that is a plug, not a driver.
fix: Rewrite Calc!C64:G68 as a proper data table: the row header reads the growth rate from the column, the column header reads capex_per_store from the row, and the body calls the same cash-conversion logic as Calc!G34. Remove every hardcoded 0.03/0.045/0.06/0.075/0.09, 70/80/90/110 and the SUMPRODUCT/INDIRECT construct. Delete the hardcoded 3 and 5 in Calc!E18/G18, E25:G27, E45:G46 and replace with COLUMN()-2 or a period index.

where: Calc!G29 =F29*cash_rate -> 0; Calc!B29 =0; Outputs rows citing 'Interest income on opening cash ($m)'.
issue: Interest income on cash is zero in every forecast year despite $20,207m of opening cash and a 4.5% cash_rate input. That is $900m+/yr of earnings the model ignores — the cash pile is the very thing the capital-return decision turns on.
fix: Change Calc!G29 to =G33*cash_rate and pull through the forecast years. Re-drive Calc!G34 and the cumulative/verdict cells. If the intent was to be conservative, state it in the assumption book — right now it reads as a formula bug.

where: Calc!G22 Net PP&E closing =G20+G9-G21*0+G21 -> 25,855.28; and G21 = -G20*dep_rate -> -2,672.47.
issue: Two problems. First, '-G21*0+G21' is dead arithmetic: it adds back zero and adds it again. Second, depreciation is calculated on closing rather than opening PP&E (Calc!G20 = F20 = ppe_fy26), so the dep charge and the PP&E roll-forward use the wrong base — the assets just added via capex never enter the depreciation base, and the D&A line contradicts its own input note.
fix: Simplify Calc!G22 to =G20+G9+G21 (or =G20+G9-G21 if the sign of D&A is flipped). Set Calc!G20 for r20 onward to the prior-year closing PP&E (i.e. =F22), not =F20. Re-check the outputs.

where: Inputs tab and Calc!G26 =IF(5=1,-buyback_y1,IF(5=2,-buyback_y2,0)) -> 0; Calc!G25 special dividend logic =IF(5=special_year,...).
issue: Buyback and special dividend are executed only in forecast years 1 and 2, then zero for years 3-5 (G25, G26 = 0). The decision this model claims to answer is whether Costco can fund the $30 special and the $4bn buyback out of cash and FCF — but the model only tests the first two years of the returns programme, not the full plan horizon. Cumulative capital returned ($B52) and cash at FY2031 (G34) are therefore understated and the verdict is built on a partial picture.
fix: Extend the returns schedule so the years in which the $30/share and the $4bn are actually paid show up in the cash waterfall, and add an explicit assumption for capital returns in years 3-5 (either a stepped-down regular-dividend-only case or an ongoing buyback). State the policy on Inputs and let the Calc tab read it.

where: Outputs tab — no action titles, single 'Verdict' row (Outputs!A25) with no unit and Outputs!B25 format set to 'text' so negatives won't show in parentheses.
issue: The Outputs tab is a data dump, not a page a committee can read. There is no up-front answer: the reader has to scroll to row 25 for a single text verdict, and the numeric rows (B19-B24) don't tell the story. Outputs!B25 will not format negatives in parentheses — a red flag for a live financial output.
fix: Rebuild Outputs so row 1 is the answer: 'Costco can fund the $30/share special and $4bn buyback from cash and FCF; cash stays above $5bn minimum through FY2031; no debt drawn.' Then the supporting table. Change Outputs!B25 format from 'text' to a number/text hybrid with a proper verdict string, and add the unit label to A25 (e.g. 'Verdict (cash funded: Y/N)').

where: Calc!G10 Free cash flow before capital returns =G8+G9 -> 13,990.56; Outputs!B8.
issue: FCF = OCF + capex (capex is negative) — correct in sign, but the model never nets working-capital swings, taxes paid or the interest income leg it separately reports. The 'Free cash flow before capital returns' line therefore reads as the answer to the funding question, but doesn't include interest income on the cash pile, which the same model treats as a funding source in the cash waterfall (Calc!G34).
fix: Either fold interest income into the FCF definition (G10 = G8+G9+G29) so the Outputs!G8 figure means the same thing the cash waterfall uses, or rename row 10 'Operating cash flow less capex' so the reader isn't misled. Pick one and make Outputs and Checks follow.

where: Inputs tab row 3 header: 'FY2026 actuals (fiscal year ended 2026-08-30, 52 weeks)' and 'Capital expenditure ($m, negative) capex_fy26 = -6,435' vs 'Capital expenditure ($m) capex_fy26 = -6,500 to -6,430'.
issue: Same value carries two different units/descriptions ('$m, negative' and '$m') and the range '6,435 to 6,435' is presented as -6,500 to -6,430 for value -6,435 — inconsistent. A committee reader will stop to reconcile.
fix: State capex once: 'Capital expenditure ($m, outflow shown negative) — FY2026 -6,435; source F4 10-K FY2026'. Set the range column to a single point or remove it where the input is not a modelled range.

where: Calc tab rows 15-22 and 25-27 (period blocks) — 'INCONSISTENT across periods (5 patterns)'.
issue: The new-warehouse, capex-base and capital-return rows use a different formula pattern in each of the five forecast columns (the E-column uses a hardcoded '3', the G-column a hardcoded '5', C/D use others). A reader doing due diligence will flag this as calculation drift.
fix: Normalise each row so one pattern fills C:G. Use COLUMN()-2 as the period index in Calc!C18:G18, C25:G27 and C45:G46. This is the same root cause as the sensitivity hardcodes — one restructure fixes both.

where: Workbook-wide (X10): 123 cross-sheet links in Calc (first B7) and 81 in Outputs (first B5) not coloured as links.
issue: Client-facing workbook borrows cross-sheet links without the standard formula-colour convention. In a banking/IC review this reads as sloppy — the reader can't trace what is hardcoded vs linked.
fix: Apply the link colour to every cross-sheet reference on Calc and Outputs. Add a legend on Cover: 'Blue = input, Black = formula on sheet, Green = link to another sheet'.

where: Inputs: 'fund_with_debt' = 0, source: 'Open question: how Costco is financed (debt, refinancing, capital raises) since 2024 - research found nothing.'
issue: The single most important sensitivity — whether the returns programme is funded by cash or by debt — is stuck at zero with an open 'research found nothing' note. That is an unanswered question sitting in an assumption cell.
fix: Either research Costco's actual funding policy (revolver capacity, commercial paper, bond maturities) and put a sourced value in the cell, or run the workbook with fund_with_debt = 1 as a second scenario and present both on Outputs. Do not ship a scenario switch nobody has evidence for.

issue: Interest is computed on opening cash only and at a flat 4.1% for five years. Opening cash is a flow item that changes every year as buybacks and dividends are paid (B11 = 832.65 to F11 = 1,168.37; interest income total $4,037.49). The cash balance that is actually invested (average of opening and closing) is never used, and a 13-week T-bill yield sourced from one date is being applied to a five-year horizon.
fix: Change the interest formula to =AVERAGE(B10,B17)*cash_yield (or at minimum AVERAGE of opening and closing) and replace the single cash_yield with a term structure input (e.g. 12-month, 2-year, 5-year yields) added to Inputs; re-run MasterCheck and the interest total.

issue: OCF margin is a single flat ratio applied to revenue in every year (B6 =B5*ocf_margin; FY2027 $16,773.9m to FY2031 $21,176.66m) and capex grows at a constant 4.0% per year even though the source is a specific FY2026 guide of ~$6.5B with 13 warehouses to open. There is no operating leverage, no working-capital seasonality, and no link between capex and the warehouse-opening schedule. The digest labels these as sourced but there is no stated range, no downside case, and no justification for holding a 5.2% operating margin flat while revenue compounds at 6%.
fix: In Inputs, add an explicit ocf_margin range (e.g. low / base / high) and a rationale line; break capex into maintenance capex and growth capex per new warehouse so that the FY2027 $6,500m rollout is driven by the 13-warehouse plan and the annual maintenance number is sourced separately. At a minimum, put a stress test on ocf_margin at 4.5% and 5.5% and show the resulting ca_min_headroom.

issue: The grid rows 31-35 compute ca_min_headroom with a single-period closed-form expression `=cash+revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(ABS((1+rev_growth+$A31...` rather than pulling the actual model. Column B shows 33,517.29 / 36,190.63 / 38,934.68 / 41,750.99 / 44,641.13 and column F shows 19,434.85 / 22,108.19 / 24,852.24 / 27,668.55 / 30,558.69. These do not tie to B24 = ca_min_headroom = 6,428.75 (the actual minimum) and they do not tie to B23 = 35,930.95 (actual closing cash). A committee member will read the grid and conclude the model has two answers.
fix: Rebuild the sensitivity as a Data Table that recalculates the real Model (one axis rev_growth, one axis capex_growth), with the output cell 'Model'!B24 (minimum headroom) and 'Model'!B23 (closing cash). Verify that the base-case cell in the data table equals 6,428.75 and 35,930.95 respectively; if not, the grid is wrong.

issue: The $5,000m cash floor is labelled only 'assumption' — no source, no rationale, no board policy reference. The $4,000m buyback is a flat annual figure sourced to one Yahoo reauthorization note ($4B expiring January 2030); there is no year-by-year path, no share-price sensitivity, and no test of what happens if buybacks are paused. Row 16 holds -4,000 in every year B through F.
fix: In Inputs, add a source and rationale for min_cash (e.g. a board liquidity policy, seasonal working-capital requirement, or a multiple of weekly cash needs) and show it as a range (e.g. $4,000m / $5,000m / $6,000m). For buyback, either make it a variable input schedule with a 2030 step-down as the authorization expires, or add a scenario that sets buyback = 0 for FY2030-FY2031 and shows closing cash and headroom.

issue: Revenue growth is a single top-down 6.0% for five years (B5 =revenue_base*(1+rev_growth) to F5 =E5*(1+rev_growth), FY2027 $321,339m to FY2031 $405,683.08m). The source line cites FY2023-FY2026 revenue CAGR of +7.8% and 16 new warehouses, but there is no bridge from warehouse openings, comparable sales, membership fee changes, or FX. A 6% flat rate is a plug, not a driver.
fix: Replace rev_growth with a build: (i) comp sales growth, (ii) contribution from the 13 planned new warehouses in FY2027 and a declining schedule thereafter, (iii) membership fee income separately. If the build is not available, keep a single growth rate but add a stated range (e.g. 4% / 6% / 8%) with each case tied to a warehouse-opening assumption and show ca_min_headroom under each.

where: Outputs B17 =IF(ca_min_headroom>=0,"Yes","No: cash falls below the floor")
issue: The binary funded-without-debt test is driven by the minimum headroom over five years. On the current numbers (ca_min_headroom = 6,428.75, ca_cash_end = 35,930.95) the answer is 'Yes' with only ~13% of closing cash as minimum headroom, and there is no sensitivity next to it showing the pass/fail flip on the two assumptions that drive it (rev_growth, ocf_margin). Read alone, the 'Yes' overstates the margin of safety.
fix: On Outputs, place the funded-without-debt cell directly beside the low-headroom figure and add a short table showing the minimum headroom (and the Yes/No flip) under the downside case in Inputs. Also, the test compares headroom to zero, not to a covenant or policy minimum; state the actual policy trigger.

where: Model rows 12/18/19/27 and Outputs rows 4/17 labels

issue: The answer to the decision is a narrative sentence, not a financial summary. A committee cannot see the sources of cash, uses of cash, or the closing position at a glance.

issue: The special dividend and buyback are hard-coded as dollar amounts while the regular dividend rolls forward on shares and growth. A board member will ask why the $30 special is a one-time hit and why buybacks do not grow; the model does not show the policy, only the spend.

issue: Revenue and OCF are driven by two separate growth and margin inputs. A client will ask whether the margin is stable; the model does not show the implied OCF growth rate or the margin trend.

where: Inputs [special_dps] = 30, source 'F41 Yahoo Finance 2026-11-11: special cash dividend of $30 per share declared'

where: Inputs [ocf_margin] = 5.2%, source F7 10-K FY2026 OCF $15.82B / F2 revenue $303.15B; Model row 6 B6 = B5*ocf_margin = 16,932.14
issue: Free cash flow is revenue x margin, so it grows dollar-for-dollar with revenue and ignores working capital, taxes, lease/operating cash movements and capex seasonality. Check the math: 15.82/303.15 = 5.22%, but the model uses 5.2% and applies it to a revenue line that grows from 324,370.5 to 425,183.56, implying OCF of 22,194.58 by FY2031 with no working-capital seasonality Costco's negative cash-conversion cycle actually creates. This is a growth-rate model dressed up as a cash model.
fix: Rebuild row 6 as revenue x net income margin plus D&A less a working-capital change line (separate row), anchored on FY2026 10-K figures; tie beginning and ending working-capital balances. If a margin-only model is kept, disclose it and show FCF sensitivity to a +/-50bp margin change.

where: Whole model; Inputs [rev_growth] = 7.0% vs source '3-yr revenue CAGR 7.8%' and Inputs!B7 [capex_growth] = 5.0% vs source '3-yr capex CAGR 14.2%'
issue: Revenue is grown at 7.0% against a disclosed 7.8% CAGR and capex at 5.0% against a 14.2% CAGR, with no stated bridge or rationale. The two growth rates are internally inconsistent: revenue compounding faster than the asset base that supports it means capex/revenue falls from 2.3% to 2.1%, contradicting the 2027 guidance of up to 33 new warehouses.
fix: State the bridge from the 7.8% CAGR to the 7.0% used (or use 7.8%), and from the 14.2% capex CAGR to 5.0%. Show capex as % of revenue in the model and confirm the implied store count against the 'up to 33 planned in 2027' guidance. Tie the two growth rates to the same operating plan.

where: Inputs [cash_yield] = 4.1% 'on opening cash' (Model row 11, B11 = B10*cash_yield = 832.65; Model!B26 = 5,114.31)

Also, 4.12% is a 13-week T-bill yield as of 2026-11-13 applied flat through FY2031 with no curve or range.
fix: Change Model row 11 to average of opening and closing cash (matching row 14's AVERAGE treatment of shares), which raises interest income materially (Model!B26 = 5,114.31 becomes higher), and source/range the yield: state it is the 13-week T-bill at 2026-11-13 and test 3.0%/4.1%/5.0%. Note the resulting interest income change in Outputs.

where: Inputs [buyback] = 800 ($m/yr) and [share_price] = 1,106.21; Model rows 16-19, e.g. B18 = B16/-share_price = 0.7232, B19 = 442.38 down to F19 = 439.48
issue: A flat $800m/yr buyback against 443.1m shares retires only ~0.7m shares/yr, cutting the count 0.8% over five years. Meanwhile the $4B program (F42) sits unexplained. where: Model rows 30-35 'Growth change' / 'investment plan change' sensitivity table; B30 = -2*ca_c_step = -20.0%

fix: Replace with a proper two-variable Data Table (What-If > Data Table) on rev_growth vs capex_growth, showing Model!F17, and a separate one-way tornado on min_cash, ocf_margin, cash_yield and buyback on the Outputs tab. Define ca_c_step and ca_g_step on the Inputs tab with units.

issue: The master check verifies only that closing cash ties to its flows and that the grid centre = closing cash less interest (2 checks, both difference 0). where: Inputs [rev_growth] = 7.0% shows no 'range' field populated; the assumption book returns blank ranges for rev_growth, ocf_margin, capex_growth, dps_growth, cash_yield

where: Model rows 30-35 (the sensitivity grid, B30 = -2*ca_c_step -> -20.0% | F30 = E30+ca_c_step -> 20.0%)
issue: The only sensitivity analysis flexes capex growth against revenue growth. Hold revenue growth and capex at base and show closing cash (ca_cash_end) and lowest headroom (ca_min_headroom) at each corner. Report the corners, not a continuous surface.

where: Inputs tab, single set of case values (rev_growth 7.0%, capex_growth 5.0%, dps_growth 8.0%, buyback $800m, special_dps $30)

where: Inputs tab, min_cash = 5,000 with source 'assumption'; no sensitivity around it

where: Model!B7 = -capex_base, and Inputs capex_base source: 'F38 FY2026 10-K: $6,435M spent in 2026, intention to spend approximately $7,500M in fiscal 2027'; capex_growth 5.0% with source 'F19 3-yr capex CAGR 14.2%'

where: Inputs buyback = $800m/yr, source: '$4B repurchase program reauthorized, expiring January 2030'

where: Model A12 'Opening shares', A18 'Shares retired', A19 'Closing shares', A27 'Closing shares'; Outputs A4 'Answer', A17 'Funded without new debt?'

where: Inputs, rev_growth = 6.0%, source 'F18 10-K FY2026 revenue grew 7.8% a year over three years'

where: Inputs, ocf_margin = 5.2%, source from FY2026 OCF/revenue
issue: A flat 5.2% OCF margin for five years is a plug, not a driver. Costco's OCF margin has moved with working capital; holding it flat through 2031 with no range or rationale hides the working-capital assumption. The $51.4bn FCF swings directly with this.
fix: Break OCF into net income + D&A +/- working capital, or at minimum state the margin is held at FY2026's 5.2% with a range 4.7%-5.7% and sensitivity. Source the historical range from the 10-K.

issue: The $30 special dividend costs $13,293m in year one and drives closing cash from $20,210 to $11,429 — a 43% draw. The model does not state how it is funded or whether it breaches the $8,000 floor; headroom at B20 is only $3,429. If the special dividend is $35 or growth is 4%, the floor is breached and the 'Funded without new debt?' answer flips. This is the single most committee-visible assumption and it has no financing narrative.

issue: The cash floor — the constraint that determines whether the capital plan is fundable — is sourced only as 'assumption' with no range and no basis. Every headroom figure and the 'Yes' answer depend on it.
fix: Source the $8,000m floor (board policy, peer cash-to-revenue, rating-agency threshold) and state a range $6,000m-$10,000m. Run the minimum headroom at the top of the range ($3,429 - $2,000 = $1,429) and show whether it stays positive.

where: Inputs, capex_base = 6,500 source 'stated intention to spend approximately $6,500m in fiscal 2026' and capex_growth = 14.2% source 'grew 14.2% a year over three years'
issue: Capex grows at 14.2% a year from a base of $6,500m to $11,055m by 2031 — a 70% increase. This is the largest cash use ($52.5bn over five years implied) and is extrapolated from a three-year historical rate with no link to the warehouse-opening plan cited elsewhere. A committee will challenge compounding a historical rate for five more years.

where: Model!B11 = B10*cash_yield = 832.65 and Model!F11 = F10*cash_yield = 986.03; label 'Interest income (on opening cash: on average cash :'

where: Inputs, revenue_base source 'FY2026 (year to 2026-08-30)' and cash source 'FY2026 at 2026-08-30', but share_price source 'Yahoo Finance close 2026-11-13' and cash_yield '13-week Treasury bill yield at close 2026-11-13'
issue: Mixed periods: the operating and balance-sheet inputs are as of fiscal year-end 2026-08-30, but the share price and interest rate are as of 2026-11-13 — a 10-week gap. The share price drives share retirement and closing shares (425.02m); using a stale or a different-date price changes the buyback math. This is exactly the kind of mixed-period input that gets caught.

where: Model rows 30-35 sensitivity grid; Model!B30 = -20.0% and Model!F30 = 20.0% changes to 'investment plan change', and A31-A35 change growth
issue: The sensitivity grid is truncated in the digest and the grid formula (Model!B31 = cash+revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(ABS((1+rev_growth+$A31...)) is cut off; I cannot verify the grid actually reprices all years or that the row/column steps drive the same logic as the main model. A sensitivity that does not recalibrate the full cash flow is worse than none because it looks authoritative.
fix: Show the full grid formula, confirm it recomputes closing cash for all five years at each growth/capex step, and confirm the centre cell matches Model!B23 = 27,989.36. Label the axes' units and add the base-case cell highlight.

issue: The buyback assumption of $4,000m/year (from a repurchase authorization expiring January 2027) is run flat for five years with a share price fixed at one date. Share retirement (B18 = B16/-share_price = 3.62m/year, constant) will be wrong the moment the price moves; the model retires the same 3.62m shares every year regardless of price. Closing shares of 425.02m is therefore not credible.
fix: Either flex the share price by year or state explicitly that retirement is held at the date-of-analysis price for illustration, and show the closing-share range across a +/-20% price move. Note the buyback authorization expires January 2027 — the $4,000m beyond that year is unsigned.

where: Model rows 12, 18, 19, 27 labels 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares'; Outputs rows 4, 17 labels 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?'
issue: Six X10 warnings: labels carry no units. 'Closing shares' could be millions or shares; 'Answer' is a text string with no unit. This is the polish layer, but it is the first thing a reader hits.
fix: Append units: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)'; relabel Outputs A4 to the actual metric (e.g. 'Conclusion') and A17 to 'Funded without new debt? (Y/N)'.

where: Model!B8 = B6+B7; row 7 'Capital expenditure' = -6,500 and row 8 'Free cash flow' = 10,273.9
issue: FCF is defined as OCF + capex (where capex is negative) — correct arithmetic — but the label 'Free cash flow' does not state it is unlevered/operating FCF and excludes interest. Interest income is added only at the cash roll-forward (B17). Fine, but the committee will ask whether FCF is pre- or post-interest; state it.
fix: Relabel row 8 to 'Free cash flow before interest income' or footnote that interest income is excluded from FCF and added at the cash line.

issue: The answer is a run-on text string: 'Over the forecast the business generates $51,420m of free cash flow and returns $47,384m to shareholders; cash ends a...'. A committee has to parse a sentence to find the line. Worse, no decision is taken from it because it does not say whether the plan is safe, only that cash ends at some level.
fix: Replace Outputs!A4 with a single line formatted as an answer: 'Plan is funded with no new debt: $51,420m FCF covers $47,384m of dividends and buybacks, leaving $27,989m of cash and a $3,429m buffer over the $8,000m floor.' Add the exit cash and the minimum headroom as separate cells on the same row.

where: Outputs tab (17 rows x 6 cols) versus Model tab (35 rows x 6 cols)
issue: The Outputs tab has 17 rows and no visible chart, and the page has no summary of what a reader must take away. The digest shows the Outputs grid has only one message (Row 4 Answer) and then a table. The user must open Model to find the drivers; only then does the model read as 'cash generated and its uses'.
fix: Rebuild Outputs as a one-page exhibit: top-left the five-line answer block ('FCF $51.4B', 'Cash returned $47.4B', 'Closing cash 2031 $28.0B', 'Lowest headroom $3.4B', 'No new debt: Yes'); top-right a bar chart of FCF by year; bottom-left a waterfall of uses; bottom-right the sensitivity grid. Delete all other rows from Outputs.

issue: The sensitivity grid varies revenue growth and capex growth and reports the resulting cash balance. It answers 'how much cash piles up if growth and capex accelerate?' Row 31 column B (the -20% growth / -20% capex cell) gives $27.5B — higher than the base. The business is very cash-generative so the grid mostly shows the cash pile swelling. The decision that turns on this model is whether the $4B buyback and the $30 special dividend are safe if cash generation slows, not whether cash can grow.
fix: Flip the grid to a stress case. Fix revenue growth at the downside (e.g. 0% or -2%) and capex at the base, then vary the buyback ($2B / $4B / $6B) down the side and the special dividend ($0 / $15 / $30 / $50) across the top, and report minimum headroom over the $8,000m floor in each cell. Recalculate the base-case answer against a 'no new debt' constraint only if the stress cell shows headroom < 0.

issue: The model reports the minimum headroom over the floor as $3,428.75m and names the result ca_min_headroom, but the Inputs book gives min_cash as $8,000m with source 'assumption' — no evidence, no board policy document, no peer comparison. A committee will ask 'why $8B?' and there is no answer in the file. The headroom number depends entirely on that unaudited number.
fix: Either source the $8,000m from the 10-K (liquidity disclosure, revolving credit covenant, or board policy) or show a range ($6B-$10B) and give the resulting headroom at each level. Add a one-line note on Outputs beside the headroom figure: 'Floor set at $8,000m; range tested $6,000-$10,000m' with the resulting headroom min and max.

where: Inputs!E4 Special dividend per share, first forecast year ($) [special_dps] = 30
issue: The $30 special dividend is treated as a one-off paid in full at the start of the first forecast year (Model!B15 = -special_dps * B12 = -$13,293m) and then zero from year 2 on (F15 = 0). That is a plausible 2026 event, but the model then carries the base-case cash trajectory as if it never happens again. The deck question is presumably 'what can we sustain', and the special dividend is almost certainly a decision variable, not a fact.
fix: Move special_dps into the scenario grid as a variable (0, 15, 30, 50 per share) and report the minimum headroom and exit cash for each. Rebuild Outputs!A4 to say 'The $30 special dividend is funded; at $50 the floor is breached in 2029' — using numbers from the recalculated grid, not invented.

issue: Inputs is 21 rows x 6 cols: it fits on one screen, fine. But the [$m] unit is missing on most rows and appears only in the label strings ('Revenue, last full fiscal year ($m)'). The named ranges carry no unit, so a user reading Model!B5 cannot tell whether revenue_base is $m without going to Inputs. The X10 warn catches this on Model and Outputs labels but the underlying ambiguity is on Inputs.
fix: Add a unit column to Inputs (column D or F) with $m, %, $, m for every row, and add unit suffixes to the Model row labels: 'Revenue ($m)', 'Shares (m)', 'Interest income ($m)'.

issue: Simplifications are visible in the formula comments: 'Interest income (on opening cash: on average cash' and 'Regular dividends (on average shares: buybacks spr'. The model uses opening cash for interest and average shares for dividends, but the label does not disclose that the base is opening cash or average shares. Anyone auditing the model will have to reverse-engineer that.
fix: Add a note column or row beneath Model rows 11 and 14 stating the basis: 'Interest on opening cash (simplification: intra-year average not modelled)' and 'Dividends on average of opening and closing shares'. Keep the formula but make the simplification visible.

issue: The sensitivity grid cells are not labelled with units (all $m but unstated) and the row/column headers in A30, B30 etc. are '$A31', '$A32' etc. — the labels are the values, not the driver names. A reader cannot tell what the axes are without the comments. This is a presentation issue that will get the page skipped.
fix: Put 'Revenue growth down the rows / Capex growth across the columns' as a note above the grid and add units ($m) to the axis header cells. Format the grid cells as $m and add conditional formatting on headroom < 0.

issue: FCF is defined as operating cash flow less capex only ('B8 =B6+B7'). No tax, no working capital beyond OCF, no lease/other items. With OCF at 5.2% of revenue this overstates FCF and therefore the entire $56,061m 'free cash flow' headline in Outputs!B4 and Outputs!B12.
fix: Either relabel row 8 'Operating cash flow less capex' and remove the word 'free' from Outputs!B4/B12, or rebuild FCF as CFO less capex less lease/other cash charges with a source for each line.

where: Inputs row 9, capex_base = 6,500, source: 'F35 10-Q FY2026 stated intention to spend approximately $6,500m in fiscal 2026'
issue: The base capex of $6,500m is FY2026 guidance, but the first forecast year in the model is FY2027 (Model!B5 =revenue_base*(1+rev_growth) starting off FY2026 revenue). Using FY2026 capex guidance as the FY2027 starting point understates capex by one year of growth and is a period inconsistency.
fix: Roll capex_base forward to the FY2027 first forecast year, or relabel Model column B as FY2026 and re-source the FY2027 capex starting point from FY2027 guidance/consensus.

where: Inputs row 15, special_dps = 30, source: 'F39 news report Costco declares $30 special dividend and reauthorizes $4B buyback'
issue: A $13,293m cash outflow (Model!B15 = -special_dps*B12) is driven by a news report. Costco's actual specials have been ~$10-15/share; $30 is not evidenced by a filing. This single assumption is ~27% of the $48,247m cash returned.
fix: Replace the news source with the 8-K/press release declaring the special dividend, cite the declaration date and record date, and test the model at $10, $15 and $30 to show the cash-floor impact.

where: Model rows 11 and 14 (interest on opening cash; dividends on average shares)
issue: Interest is computed on opening cash (B11 =B10*cash_yield) while dividends are computed on average shares (B14 = -B13*AVERAGE(B12,B19)) and buybacks use a flat 4,000/year (row 16). Mixing opening-balance interest with average-balance dividends is inconsistent; with a declining cash balance the model overstates interest income. ca_int_total = 3,869.31 is not tested.
fix: Apply one convention consistently - either average opening/closing cash for interest (B11 =AVERAGE(B10,B17)*cash_yield) or opening cash for both - and note the convention. Re-run and show the delta to ca_int_total.

where: Inputs row 4, rev_growth = 6.0%, source: '10-K FY2026 revenue grew 7.8% a year over three years'
issue: The growth source supports 7.8%, the input uses 6.0%, and there is no reconciliation between the two. Same problem at capex_growth = 8.0% against a sourced 14.2% three-year rate and dps_growth = 8.0% against a $5.54 to $5.88 (6.1%) step implied by the dividend sources. Ranges are blank for every line.
fix: For each growth input, add the range (low/base/high) and a one-line rationale stating why the chosen rate differs from the sourced historical rate. Populate the empty range column.

where: Model rows 30-35 (sensitivity grid), e.g. B31 =cash+revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(ABS((1+rev_growth+$A31... with F31 =15,000.59
issue: The sensitivity grid spans -20% to +20% of two variables but produces values (B31 =30,253.75 to F31 =15,000.59) that do not tie back to any row in the main model, and the formula uses a first-year shortcut (revenue_base*ocf_margin) rather than the five-year build. The grid is not reconcilable to ca_cash_end = 31,893.11 and is presented in Outputs as answer support.
fix: Rebuild the grid so the base cell (-0%/0%) equals ca_cash_end = 31,893.11 exactly, drive it from the same five-year formulas (rows 5-19), and add a tie-out cell showing base case grid = model closing cash.

where: Checks tab, 'Capital allocation: grid centre = closing cash less interest: difference 0, status OK'
issue: The check compares the grid centre to closing cash less interest with a difference of 0, but the definition is itself an identity - closing cash less interest over the five years is not the same quantity the grid purports to compute. A check that is definitionally satisfied is not a control. MasterCheck = OK therefore carries less assurance than it appears to.
fix: Replace with real checks: (1) grid base cell equals Model!B23 = 31,893.11; (2) closing shares rolls (B19 - B18 = next B12 across all five years); (3) interest recomputes from the chosen cash convention; (4) balance-sheet cash on the inputs ties to Model!F17. Keep MasterCheck as AND of all.

where: Inputs rows 4, 9, 11, 13, 15 (rev_growth, capex_growth, dps_growth, special_dps, cash_yield)
issue: Growth and yield assumptions carry no unit, while revenue, capex and cash carry '$m' and share price carries '$'. X10 flagged three Model rows and two Outputs rows but not the Inputs rate rows.
fix: Set the number format on every rate cell to 0.0% and add 'per year' to the label for growth lines; add '(yield)' to cash_yield.

where: Outputs row 4, value: 'Over the forecast the business generates $56,061m of free cash flow and returns $48,247m to shareholders; cash ends a...'
issue: The single answer line bundles three numbers and the trailing text is truncated in the digest; the label 'Answer' has no unit and the workbook rules flagged it. A reviewer cannot quote the recommendation cleanly.
fix: Split into three labelled cells: 'Free cash flow, FY2027-FY2031 ($m)' = 56,060.82; 'Cash returned to shareholders ($m)' = 48,247.02; 'Closing cash, FY2031 ($m)' = 31,893.11. Delete the prose.

issue: The $8,000m cash floor is the binding constraint - ca_min_headroom = 3,364.48 against it - and it is sourced only as 'assumption'.
fix: Cite the board policy or treasury minimum (e.g. months of opex, minimum liquidity disclosure in the 10-K) that supports $8,000m; if none exists, state that this is management judgment and range it 6,000-10,000 in the sensitivity.

issue: Title reads 'Costco Wholesale Capital Allocation Model FY2027-FY2031' but the model's first column uses FY2026 10-K data as the base and applies one year of growth, so the first forecast period is ambiguous.
fix: Add a subtitle to the Cover: 'Base: FY2026 (ended 2026-08-30); forecast FY2027-FY2031; all figures $m unless stated', and label Model columns B-F as FY2027 through FY2031.

where: Model!A30:F35 (the grid labelled 'Growth change (rows), investment plan change (columns)')
issue: This is a two-way sensitivity table on revenue growth and capex step, not scenarios. The grid only stresses two drivers, only five columns wide (+/- ca_c_step = 20%), and every cell is labelled by a percentage step rather than by the decision the committee is making. There is no downside case, no base case, no upside case with a name and a narrative. A client reading Outputs cannot see 'what happens to the dividend or the buyback in a recession.'
fix: Replace the step grid with three named scenarios on the Model tab — Base (rev_growth 6.0%, capex_growth 8.0%), Downside (rev_growth 0-1%, ocf_margin 4.5%, capex flat at $6,500m), Upside (rev_growth 8%, ocf_margin 5.5%) — each a full column showing FCF, cash returned, closing cash and lowest headroom. Keep the two-way grid on a back-up tab. Put a one-line verdict on each scenario in Outputs row 17.

where: Model!B11:F11 ('Interest income on opening cash') and Outputs!row 9
issue: Interest is earned on opening cash only (B11 = B10*cash_yield), yet the model pays the $13,293m special dividend at the start of year 1 (B15 = -special_dps*B12) and buys back $4,000m a year. Opening cash of $20,210m immediately drops, so interest is overstated in every forecast year. On a $20bn cash balance at 4.1% that is a seven-figure error running through five years — roughly $1.6bn of interest income (Model!B26 = 3,869.31) is overstated by the timing mismatch.
fix: Either (a) base interest on average cash as the label already claims — B11 = AVERAGE(B10,B17)*cash_yield — and correct the label to match, or (b) fund the special dividend and buyback mid-year and state that explicitly in Inputs row for special_dps and buyback. The digest shows the row 11 label says 'on average cash' but the formula uses opening — pick one and make the label and formula agree.

where: Inputs!special_dps row (value 30, source 'F39 news report Costco declares $30 special dividend and reauthorizes $4B buyback')
issue: The $30 special dividend is a one-off event pulled from a news report and projected as if it is a policy. $13,293m on 443.1m shares is the single largest cash use in the model and it is sourced to a secondary news article, not to a company filing or board authorization. Nothing in the model shows whether this recurs, is a one-time return, or has a stated date.
fix: Add a row to Inputs that flags 'Special dividend: one-time, FY2027 only' with the primary source (the Costco press release or 8-K, not the news report) and the declaration date. If it is genuinely one-time, the Model already handles it correctly with F15=0 — say so on the Inputs tab so a reader doesn't wonder.

where: Outputs!B14 ('Closing cash, 2031 ($m) = 31,893.11') and Model!B20:F20 (headroom over the $8,000m floor)
issue: The headline answer is that cash ends at $31.9bn against an $8.0bn floor — roughly $24bn of idle cash at the end of a plan that is retiring only 18m shares (443.1m to 425.02m). No page asks or answers 'why hold $24bn when we could retire 21m more shares or pay a larger dividend?' That is the capital allocation question, and the workbook treats it as a byproduct.
fix: Add a row to Outputs under row 15: 'Excess cash above floor at 2031 = $23,893m' and a line 'If deployed to buybacks at $1,106.21, retires 21.6m additional shares.' That turns the residual into a decision.

where: Model!A12, A18, A19, A27 and Outputs!A4, A17
issue: Six labels carry no unit ('Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares' x2, 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?'). The engine flagged these as X10 warnings. On a client page, 'Closing shares 425.02' with no unit invites the question 'million? thousand?'
fix: Add units in the labels: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)', 'Closing shares (m)', and leave A4/A17 as text answers but relabel A4 'Answer (text)' or move it out of the numeric grid.

where: Outputs tab (17 rows, tables only, no chart)
issue: The Outputs tab is titled 'Summary tables and charts for review' but the digest shows nine formula rows and no chart. A committee reading Outputs sees two columns of numbers and has to build the picture in their head.
fix: Add one chart: closing cash vs the $8,000m floor, five years, with a horizontal floor line. Add a second: sources vs uses of the $48,247m returned. Put the Answer sentence at the top of the tab, above the chart.

where: Model!A31:F35 (grid) vs Model!B22:F22 ('Free cash flow, all years')
issue: The two-way grid recalculates a stripped single-period cash formula (cash + revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(...)) that does not tie to the full five-year model in rows 5-22. A reader cannot reconcile the grid cell to the base case.
fix: Either rebuild the grid so the centre cell equals Model!B23 (closing cash, last year = 31,893.11), or label the grid 'Single-period cash proxy — not the five-year model' so nobody assumes it ties.

issue: Source reads: 'F39 news report Costco declares $30 special dividend and reauthorizes $4B buyback; primary 8-K/press release not located.' The $30 special dividend drives a $13,293m first-year cash use (Model!B15 = -special_dps*B12), which is 28% of total cash returned of $48,247m. A media report is not a source for a board-level capital allocation answer.
fix: Locate the 8-K/press release for the $30 special dividend, cite the filing date and accession, or remove the special dividend from the base case and present it as a downside/upside toggle. Do not leave a media reference as the underpinning of a blocking cash use.

where: Inputs, shares outstanding [shares] = 443.1 vs. Model!B27 = 425.02 closing shares
issue: Opening shares are sourced as 443.1M at 2026-09-29, but Model!B19 = B12 - B18 = 443.1 - 3.62 = 439.48 and Model!F19 = 425.02. Over five years the model retires only 3.62m shares a year against a $4,000m annual buyback (Model!B16) at $1,106.21 (Inputs), i.e. 3.62m shares per year, which is arithmetically correct (4,000 / 1,106.21 = 3.616) but materially inconsistent with the source that total share repurchases were $848.0M in FY2026 against a $4,000m authorization. Either the authorization is a ceiling not a run-rate, or the retirement math is understating retirements. Either way the closing share count and the $5.88 dividend per share on average shares (Model!B14) are both overstated versus the source.
fix: Reconcile: (i) confirm whether $4,000m is an annual run-rate or an authorization ceiling and state it in the input label; (ii) if annual, the math is right and the source note must say 'assumed annual spend of $4,000m'; (iii) if a ceiling, replace with FY2026 actual repurchases of $848.0m and label the source. Add a check that buyback spend / share price = share retirements, and a check that closing shares = opening - cumulative retirements.

where: Inputs, cash floor the board keeps [min_cash] = 8,000
issue: Source column reads only 'assumption'. The cash floor is the single pivot of the answer: ca_min_headroom = 2,908.75 (Model!B24, Outputs!B15) and Outputs!B17 reads 'Funded without new debt? = Yes' only because the floor is $8,000m. There is no range and no rationale.
fix: Replace 'assumption' with a sourced floor: board policy, minimum liquidity covenant, or a stated internal policy; give a range (e.g. $6,000–$10,000m) and a one-line rationale. Show the answer holds across the range — with $2,908.75m of minimum headroom, the answer flips at a floor above roughly $10,900m (Model!B24 + min_cash).

where: Inputs, Revenue growth [rev_growth] = 6.0%, capex growth [capex_growth] = 8.0%, dividend growth [dps_growth] = 8.0%
issue: Sources are history-based only: FY2026 revenue grew 7.8% a year over three years; capex grew 14.2% a year over three years; FY2026 dividends declared $5.54 rising to a quarterly $1.47 declared 2026-04-15. These are growth-rate assumptions, not drivers, and none carries a range or a stated rationale for stepping down from the historical rates.
fix: Convert to drivers where possible: warehouse additions and revenue per warehouse for revenue, new-build and maintenance capex separated for capex, payout policy for the dividend. Put a low/high range on each (revenue 4–8%, capex 6–12%, dividend 6–10%) with a one-line rationale, and tie each range to a specific filing or guidance.

issue: The sensitivity formula in row 31 onward, e.g. Model!B31 = cash + revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(ABS((1+rev_growth+$A31...), is a condensed/truncated nested expression that recalculates the cash path from scratch rather than flexing the model. Its output (B31 = 28,154.77, F31 = 11,681.36) is a different quantity from the main model output (Model!B23 = 28,992.57), so the grid cannot be reconciled to the headline answer.
fix: Rebuild the sensitivity as a proper data table (or copy of Model!B5:F17) driven off the two named inputs so the grid centre equals the base case output. Add a check that grid centre = Model!B23 and that the grid responds to changes in rev_growth and capex_growth.

issue: Outputs!B4 reads 'Over the forecast the business generates $53,372m of free cash flow and returns $48,247m to shareholders; cash ends a...' and Outputs!B17 reads 'Funded without new debt? = Yes'. Both are hard-string/cell conclusions that do not present the sensitivity to the cash floor or to the special dividend. A committee reading only the Outputs tab cannot see that the answer flips if the floor is above roughly $10,900m or if the special dividend is excluded.
fix: Rewrite Outputs!B4 to state the answer with the governing assumption named (e.g. '...funded without new debt provided the board cash floor stays at or below $8,000m') and add a two-column sensitivity under B17 showing the answer at the low and high end of the cash-floor range.

issue: There is no scenario analysis on the Outputs tab. The Outputs tab has summary rows 8–17 only; no downside case (revenue growth at the low end, capex at the high end) is presented, and no tie from the Model!B30:F35 grid to the Outputs answer.
fix: Add a scenario table on Outputs: Base / Downside / Severe, each showing revenue, free cash flow, cash returned, closing cash, minimum headroom and the funded-without-new-debt conclusion, with the input changes named. Tie each scenario back to a named cell in Inputs.

issue: Row 11 label reads 'Interest income (on opening cash: on average cash' and the formula uses opening cash (B10, F10), not average cash. The label and the formula disagree. With a $20,210m opening cash and a 4.1% yield, that is $832.65m in year 1 and $980.58m in year 5 — a $3,657.12m total (Model!B26) that is understated if average cash were used and overstated in early years if closing cash were used.
fix: Either change the label to 'Interest income on opening cash' or change the formula to average of opening and closing cash. State the convention once in the Inputs tab and apply it consistently across all years.

issue: The special dividend is paid at the start of the first forecast year on opening shares (B12 = shares = 443.1), not on shares outstanding at the payment date. The source note says the $30 special dividend and $4B buyback reauthorization were reported together, implying the special dividend is a discrete event, not a run-rate. The convention is not stated.
fix: State the payment-date convention in the Inputs tab. If the special dividend is paid at the start of FY2027 on 443.1m shares, say so and cite the record date. If it is a run-rate assumption, remove it from the base case.

issue: Forge X10 warns: Model row 12 'Opening shares' has no unit; row 18 'Shares retired' has no unit; row 19 'Closing shares' has no unit; row 27 'Closing shares' has no unit; Outputs row 4 'Answer' has no unit; Outputs row 17 'Funded without new debt?' has no unit.
fix: Add units to each label: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)' on Model, and 'Answer' and 'Funded without new debt?' are narrative cells — reclassify or retitle so the unit rule does not apply (e.g. 'Answer (narrative)').

issue: Only two checks are run: closing cash ties to flows (difference 0) and grid centre = closing cash less interest (difference 0). Neither checks the balance sheet, share count integrity, buyback math, or that the sensitivity grid centre equals the base case. A single MasterCheck = OK on two checks is thin for a board package.
fix: Add checks: (i) buyback spend / share price = shares retired; (ii) closing shares = opening shares - cumulative retirements; (iii) closing cash = opening + FCF + interest - dividends - buybacks; (iv) sensitivity grid centre = Model!B23; (v) no #REF/#DIV/0 anywhere. Keep MasterCheck as the AND of all of them.

where: Inputs, sources dated 2026-11-13 (share price) vs. FY2026 10-K for period ending 2026-08-30
issue: The share price for buybacks is a Yahoo Finance close on 2026-11-13, and the 13-week Treasury yield is also a Yahoo Finance 2026-11-13 close. Mixing a market close with fiscal-year-end data in a forecast is acceptable if labelled, but the file does not state the valuation date on the Cover or Outputs.
fix: State the valuation date (2026-11-13) on the Cover and on Outputs, and note that share price and yield are spot as of that date while operations data are FY2026 actuals to 2026-08-30.

issue: The only scenario grid (rows 30-35) tests growth and capex changes, but its results are never shown on Outputs. The Outputs tab carries a single base case and one downstream view. The decision the board faces is whether the $30 special dividend plus the $4,000m buyback plus the $7,020m capex plan can all be sustained — the model never presents the answer to that question in any scenario.
fix: Add a scenario table to Outputs with three columns: base, 'no special dividend', and 'capex +8% and revenue +2% slower'. For each, show ca_min_headroom, ca_cash_end, ca_uses_total and the 'Funded without new debt?' line. Title it 'Base case funds all three uses; cutting the special dividend is not required at the plan capex' or whatever the numbers actually say.

where: Inputs row for special_dps: source 'F39 news report Costco declares $30 special dividend and reauthorizes $4B buyback; primary 8-K/press release not located'
issue: A $30/share special dividend costs $13,293m in year 1 (Model!B15) against $20,210m opening cash. It is the largest single line in the uses stack and it rests on a secondary news report. A client committee will stop on this.
fix: Obtain the primary 8-K or press release and replace the source. If it cannot be verified, pull special_dps to zero and rerun — do not send a model whose biggest cash use is unverified.

issue: The 'Answer' cell is a sentence built inside a formula. It reads 'Over the forecast the business generates $53,372m of free cash flow and returns $48,247m to shareholders; cash ends at...'. It is buried in B4, has no unit label (warn X10), and does not state the decision: whether the plan is funded without new debt. The reader has to hunt.
fix: Replace B4 with four plain cells: 'Funded without new debt? Yes', 'Lowest headroom over floor: $2,909m', 'FCF all years: $53,372m', 'Cash returned: $48,247m'. Put them at the top of Outputs, one claim per row, each with its unit.

issue: Closing cash sums flows with no sign convention stated and no label. Row 7 capex is negative, rows 14-16 uses are negative, row 11 interest positive. It ties (Checks OK), but a reader cannot follow it without a voice-over. The model's own row label is just 'Closing cash'.
fix: Add a row above with the explicit bridge header: 'Opening cash + FCF + interest − dividends − special − buyback = Closing cash'. Or split into two labelled sub-rows 'Sources' and 'Uses' with subtotals, so the arithmetic is visible.

where: Inputs: capex_base source 'F35 10-Q FY2026 stated intention to spend approximately $6,500m in fiscal 2026' set as 7,020
issue: The stated 10-Q intention is ~$6,500m for fiscal 2026, but capex_base — described as the first forecast year — is 7,020. The step from 6,500 to 7,020 is not explained anywhere. Either the year label is wrong or the number is a plug.
fix: Either set capex_base = 6,500 and let capex_growth carry the step, or add a source line explaining the 8% bridge from the $6,500m plan to $7,020m (e.g. warehouse openings, F36). Do not leave the gap unexplained.

where: Model row 18 B18 =B16/-share_price -> 3.62m shares retired per year, constant every year
issue: The buyback is fixed at $4,000m and the share price is held at $1,106.21 flat across five years. That is a plug, not a driver. Every year retires the same 3.62m shares, and the buyback authorization expires January 2027 (Inputs source F38). Retiring shares past the authorization is unsupported.
fix: Model the authorization window explicitly: state that the $4,000m runs only while the authorization is live, or add a share-price path assumption and let buyback dollars be the variable. At minimum, note on the Inputs tab that buyback is held at $4,000m for all five years by assumption and that the January 2027 expiry is ignored.

where: Inputs tab, header row 3; and Model rows 12, 18, 19, 27
issue: Labels 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares' carry no unit (warn X10 lists four occurrences). 'Answer' and 'Funded without new debt?' on Outputs also lack units. A reader cannot tell millions from shares from dollars without inference.
fix: Add units to every label: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)', 'Funded without new debt? (Y/N)'.

where: Model row 11 label 'Interest income (on opening cash: on average cash'
issue: The label is truncated mid-parenthesis and reads as two contradictory descriptions. The formula (B11 =B10*cash_yield) is on opening cash only.
fix: Rename to 'Interest income (on opening cash) ($m)'. Delete the 'on average cash' fragment.

issue: The $4,000m cash floor is sourced as 'assumption' with no range and no rationale. It is the single constraint that determines whether the answer is 'Funded without new debt? Yes' — with a lower floor the downside headroom of $6,048m changes materially, and the downside case closes the year at only $17,838m.
fix: Source the floor: cite Costco's actual minimum operating cash from the 10-K liquidity discussion, or state the basis (e.g. 1.5% of revenue, or one-to-two weeks of operating cash outflow) and show the sensitivity of ca_down_min_headroom to min_cash at $2,000m, $4,000m and $8,000m.

issue: Share price is a single spot from Yahoo Finance on 2026-11-13; there is no range and no sensitivity. Buybacks of $800m a year at this price retire ~0.72m shares a year, and the share count in the answer (439.48m) is directly a function of this one number.
fix: Add a share-price range (e.g. +/-20% around the spot) and run the buyback/share-count output across the range; note the source date in the cell and refresh before any committee date.

issue: Both growth rates are set as single points with no range column filled in ('range  to ' is blank for every input). Revenue growth is below the historical 3-year CAGR of 7.8%; capex growth of 10% is below the historical 14.2% CAGR. There is no driver (comp store growth, membership fee, new warehouse count) and no stress on the two variables that drive free cash flow.
fix: Replace the single-point growth rates with driver builds — revenue from comps + new warehouses; capex from warehouse count x average cost — and populate the range column. Show base, high and low on rev_growth and capex_growth with the resulting ca_min_headroom.

issue: Interest income is calculated on opening cash only (B11 = B10*cash_yield), but the rate itself (4.1%) is quoted as of 2026-11-13 and applied flat across FY2027-FY2031. The model has no discount rate, no NPV, no per-share value, no return on capital — so there is no valuation output at all. A capital allocation model that does not tell you whether deploying the cash creates value is not answering the question.
fix: Add a WACC built from the risk-free rate (use the same 4.12% 13-week T-bill or a matched-tenor Treasury), Costco's beta, and an ERP; discount the free cash flow to get an EV and equity value; compare the return on incremental capex to WACC. If the intent is genuinely only a liquidity/funding model, retitle it 'Cash Availability Model' and remove 'capital allocation'.

where: Model!B15 = -special_dps * B12 and Model!B33 downside closing cash
issue: The $30 special dividend is paid at the start of year 1 (B15) using opening shares — fine — but the downside case (r33) uses the same B14:B16 cash-returned rows, i.e. the special dividend is still paid in full in the downside even though cash falls to $17.8bn. In a downside the special is the first thing the board would cut.
fix: Carve the special dividend into a separate row and either cut it in the downside or explicitly flag that it is held flat in the downside and let the reader see the effect — run the downside with special_dps = 0 and show ca_down_min_headroom both ways.

where: Model!B32 downside FCF = B31*(ocf_margin - down_margin_cut) + B7*(1+capex_overrun)
issue: The downside revenue stream grows 3% per year (down_growth), but the capex line uses the base-case B7 (which grows at 10%) with a 15% overrun on top — so in the downside, capex grows faster than revenue. That may be intended conservatism, but it is not stated and it is not tested: no case where capex is cut alongside revenue.
fix: State the capex assumption for the downside in the Inputs tab, and add a second downside variant where capex is held flat in nominal terms so the reader can see how much of the cash pressure is revenue vs capex.

where: Model!A12 'Opening shares', A18 'Shares retired', A19 'Closing shares'; Outputs!A4 'Answer', A17 'Funded without new debt?', A20 'Funded in the downside?'
issue: Labels carry no unit. 'Closing shares' in Model!B19 = 442.38 next to 'Closing cash' in B17 = 14,620.25 means a reader can misread shares as $m.
