issue: Several sources are already months old or of mixed date — Yahoo Finance close 2026-11-13, Yahoo Finance special dividend 2026-11-11, 10-Q period ending 2026-05-10. The mixing of dated market data with fiscal-year filings is not labelled as such.
fix: Add a 'last checked' timestamp column to the Inputs tab and re-stamp every market-data source immediately before the file is circulated.

issue: The one-line answer is hardcoded into a text formula: 'Over the forecast the business generates $54,873m of free cash flow and returns $31,917m to shareholders; cash ends a...'. It has no source note for the cash floor or the special dividend, which are the two items a committee will ask about.
fix: Break the answer into three labelled lines — FCF, cash returned split regular/special/buyback, closing cash vs floor — and footnote each with its Inputs reference.

where: Model!B34 and Model!B36; Outputs!B20 'Funded in the downside?'
issue: The stated purpose is a capital allocation decision and Outputs!B17/B20 answer 'Funded without new debt?' / 'Funded in the downside?' purely by whether cash stays above the $4,000m floor (Model!B20 =B17-min_cash, Model!B34 =B33-min_cash). No debt issuance, maturity or leverage constraint is in the model at all, so the 'without new debt' question is answered by construction, not by the model. A committee will see through this immediately.
fix: Either (a) add a debt block to Inputs (opening debt, maturities by year, max net debt/EBITDA or interest coverage the board will tolerate) and make Outputs!B17/B20 read from that lever, or (b) re-label Outputs!B17 as 'Stays above the $4,000m cash floor?' and Outputs!B20 as 'Stays above the floor in the downside?' and delete the 'new debt' framing. Do not leave the current wording.

where: Model!B15 =-special_dps*B12 (a single −$13,293m hit in the first forecast year only)
issue: The $30/share special dividend is a decision variable, but the model treats it as an all-or-nothing lump in year 1 with no alternative shown. The board's real question is 'special dividend vs. buyback vs. phased return', and this workbook silently forecloses two of the three.
fix: Replace Model!B15 with a lever: either (i) add an Inputs cell 'Special dividend year' (1-5) and gate the cash outflow to that column, or (ii) add a parallel scenario column showing the same $13,293m spread evenly across the five forecast years, and put the lowest-headroom result for each on Outputs next to ca_min_headroom. Use the model's own numbers — $30 × 443.1 shares = $13,293m — for both.

where: Inputs row 'Downside: revenue growth per year' = 3.0% and 'Downside: cut to the operating cash flow margin' = 1.0%
issue: The downside is a single softer-revenue case. It does not stress the two things that will actually break the return plan: a step up in capex above the 10%/yr growth assumption (Inputs row 'Capex growth per year' = 10.0%) and a compression in the operating cash flow margin beyond 1.0pt. A committee will ask 'what if capex is 12.5% not 10%?' and the workbook cannot answer without re-typing assumptions.
fix: Add two sensitivity rows to Outputs that flex (a) capex growth 8%/10%/12%/14% and (b) OCF margin 4.2%/4.7%/5.2%, each showing lowest headroom over the floor, reusing the grid logic already in Model rows 39-44. Report the binding cell in text, e.g. 'lowest headroom $X at capex growth 14% and OCF margin 4.2%'.

where: Outputs!B4 'Answer' formula (the TEXT() string) and Outputs tab structure
issue: The 'Answer' cell concatenates four numbers into a sentence inside a formula in B4. That is a deck-in-a-cell. It cannot be read on a page, cannot be cut into a title, and any client change to a named cell silently rewrites the sentence. Also, the reader has to scroll past the answer to reach ca_down_* rows.
fix: Break the sentence into four labelled cells at the top of Outputs: 'FCF, forecast ($m)' = ca_fcf_total; 'Cash returned, forecast ($m)' = ca_uses_total; 'Closing cash, 2031 ($m)' = ca_cash_end; 'Lowest headroom over floor ($m)' = ca_min_headroom. Delete the TEXT() concatenation. Put the downside row set (ca_down_cash_end, ca_down_min_headroom) immediately under the base row set, side by side.

issue: Interest is computed on opening cash only (Model!B11 uses B10, not the average of B10 and B17). The row label even says 'on average cash' in the digest but the formula does not. That understates interest in every year and is exactly the kind of thing a bank reviewer will circle.
fix: Change Model!B11 to =AVERAGE(B10,B17)*cash_yield and drag across B:F. Update the row label to 'Interest income (on average cash)'. Re-run the three checks; ca_int_total should rise and Checks!F3 should still read OK.

where: Model rows 12, 18, 19, 27 labels: 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares'; Outputs rows 4, 17, 20 labels: 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?'
issue: Seven X10 warnings — labels have no unit. 'Opening shares' and 'Answer' are unreadable to a reader who opens the tab cold.
fix: Rename in place: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)' on Model rows 12/18/19/27; and on Outputs replace 'Answer' with 'Headline, base case (in $m unless noted)', 'Funded without new debt? (Y/N)', 'Funded in the downside? (Y/N)'. Clears all seven X10 warnings.

where: Inputs 'Cash and equivalents, opening ($m)' = 20,210 vs Model!B17 = 14,620.25 in the first forecast year
issue: Opening cash is $20,210m and closing cash in year 1 is $14,620m — the business burns $5.6bn of cash in year 1 despite positive FCF, because the special dividend lands in full. That is a real and important fact, and nothing in the workbook flags it. A reader will be confused why 'highest headroom' begins lower than the opening balance.
fix: Add a Model line under row 17: 'Year-1 change in cash ($m)' = B17-B10, and surface the year-1 figure on Outputs next to the headline. If it is negative, say so in the Outputs label.

issue: Revenue growth 6.0% is sourced only to '3-year CAGR 7.8%' and capex growth 10.0% to a 3-year 14.2% CAGR — these are growth rates, not drivers, and 6.0% is a ~180bp step down from the cited 7.8% with no reconciliation. Nothing in the file shows warehouses, comps, membership fee income or gasoline/FX split, which is what actually drives Costco revenue.
fix: Replace the single revenue growth input with a driver build on Inputs: new warehouse openings x average revenue per warehouse, plus comp growth (comp sales and membership fee income), tied to the 10-K disclosures; replace capex_growth with a build of new warehouses x cost per warehouse plus remodels, cross-checked to the $6,500m FY2026 guidance in capex_base. Keep one line reconciling the driver output back to the 3-year 7.8% CAGR already in the book.

where: Inputs tab, 'range' column is blank for every one of the 18 inputs
issue: The digest shows 'range  to ' empty for rev_growth, ocf_margin, capex_growth, dps_growth, cash_yield, down_growth, down_margin_cut and the rest. A committee cannot see whether 6.0% growth or a 1.0% margin cut is the middle of a plausible band or the low end of one. ca_min_headroom (Model!B24) = 10,620.25 and ca_down_min_headroom (Model!B36) = 6,048.07 both sit above the floor, but with no ranges nobody can tell how close to the floor the low case actually is.
fix: Fill the range column on Inputs for every assumption with the low and high values you would defend (e.g. rev_growth low 3.0% / base 6.0% / high 8.0%; ocf_margin low 4.2% / base 5.2% / high 5.5%; capex_growth low 8% / base 10% / high 14%), each with its source. Any assumption with no source and no range should be flagged as a judgment call in a one-line note in the adjacent column.

issue: The $30 special dividend is taken from a single Yahoo Finance item ('F36 Yahoo Finance 2026-11-11: special cash dividend of $30 per share declared') and is paid in full in year 1 at $13,293m, roughly equal to the entire FY2027 free cash flow (Model!B8 = 10,273.9). One unchecked retail source loading a $13.3B cash outflow in the first forecast year is not committee-grade.
fix: Confirm the $30 special against the company's own declaration (8-K or press release) and cite the filing and date, not Yahoo. If confirmed, keep it in year 1 but state in the Model notes that it consumes 129% of year-1 FCF (13,293 / 10,273.9) and is funded out of the 20,210 opening cash; if the timing slips a year, re-run and show the impact on ca_cash_end and ca_min_headroom.

issue: The buyback line is a flat -800 per year (Inputs!buyback = 800), which retires 0.7232m shares a year at the 1,106.21 share price regardless of the cash position, and it is not sized to the '$4B repurchase program reauthorized, expiring January 2030' cited in the input source. So Model!B27 closing shares 439.48 is a function of a fixed dollar amount, not of the cash the company actually has available, and the model never tests whether the $4B authorization is exhausted.
fix: Make the buyback a function of available cash above the floor each year (e.g. buyback = MIN(remaining authorization, max(0, closing cash - min_cash))) with a line tracking the $4B authorization drawn down; re-run and show closing shares change from 439.48 when the buyback flexes.

issue: Interest is earned on opening cash only (B11 = B10*cash_yield), but the label in the formula sample says 'Interest income (on opening cash: on average cash'. Interest on opening cash understates income in years when cash is building — closing cash goes from 14,620.25 in year 1 to 47,771.5 in year 5 — and the 4.1% cash_yield sourced to the 13-week T-bill (4.12%) is applied to the full cash balance forever, which ignores that most of that balance would realistically earn a lower blended rate.
fix: Switch to interest on average cash (AVERAGE(opening, closing) x cash_yield) consistently across B11:F11 and the downside rows, and add a note or a second input for the blended rate if the board keeps cash in shorter-dated instruments. Reconcile ca_int_total (currently 5,200.45) after the change.

where: Model!B39:F44 sensitivity grid (growth change rows, investment plan change columns)
issue: The grid rows 40-44 evaluate 'cash + revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(ABS(...))' — a closed-form approximation of the multi-year build, not the model itself, and the formula sample is truncated so the IF logic cannot be verified from the digest. If the sensitivity does not re-run the actual Model rows 5-19, its answer can diverge from ca_cash_end and nobody would see it.
fix: Rebuild the grid as a data table or explicit re-run of the Model rows over the base row and column inputs, and add a check cell on Checks comparing the grid centre to ca_cash_end (year-5 closing cash 47,771.5) so any divergence fails MasterCheck.

where: Inputs!cash_yield = 4.1%, source 'Yahoo Finance 2026-11-13: US 13-week Treasury bill yield 4.12%'
issue: A single-day yield on a single instrument for a 5-year forecast (FY2027-FY2031) with no term structure and no sensitivity is a material unsourced judgment across a five-year horizon, particularly given ca_int_total = 5,200.45 is over 9% of the total FCF (54,872.86).
fix: Add a short rate path (or at minimum a low/base/high on cash_yield, e.g. 2.5% / 4.1% / 5.0%) with the source for each point, and show the effect on ca_cash_end and ca_min_headroom in a one-line sensitivity on Outputs.

issue: The Checks tab has three checks — closing cash ties to flows, grid centre = closing cash less interest, downside closing cash not above base — plus MasterCheck OK. There is no check that opening cash in each year equals prior-year closing cash (Model!F10 =E17 is the mechanism, but it is not asserted), no check that shares roll forward (Model!F12 =E19), and no check that the sum of uses ties to the sum of sources line by line.
fix: Add checks: (1) Model!B10 = cash and Model!C10 =Model!B17 ... for every year; (2) B12 = shares and each subsequent opening = prior closing; (3) ca_fcf_total (54,872.86) = SUM(Model!B8:F8); (4) ca_uses_total (32,511.81) = -SUM(Model!B14:F16); (5) ca_cash_end (47,771.5) = Model!F17. Route all into MasterCheck.

where: Outputs!A4 'Answer', Outputs!A17 'Funded without new debt?', Outputs!A20 'Funded in the downside?'; Model!A12 'Opening shares', A18 'Shares retired', A19/A27 'Closing shares'
issue: Seven X10 warnings: labels without units. 'Answer' at Outputs!A4 is also not a label a committee can use — the row holds a TEXT-concatenated sentence, which is fine as a headline but the tab should name what it is.
fix: Rename Outputs!A4 to 'Answer (summary text)'; add units to Model!A12/A18/A19/A27 ('Opening shares (m)'), Outputs!A16 'Closing shares (m)' is already correct — mirror it; add units or explicit Yes/No parentheticals to Outputs!A17 and A20 ('Funded without new debt? (Yes/No)').

where: Inputs tab header row 3, sections [Operations], [Balance sheet and shares], [Cash returned], [Rates], [Downside case]
issue: One Inputs tab with five sections is the right shape, but 'assumption' is the only source for min_cash (4,000) — that is a board policy number and should carry a citation (proxy, 10-K risk factor, or management guidance) rather than the literal word 'assumption'. Same discipline should apply across sections.
fix: For min_cash, cite the source of the board's minimum-cash policy (e.g. the proxy statement's capital-return policy or the last earnings call where management stated the operating cash target); if there is no public source, label it 'management estimate — rationalized as X weeks of opex/capex' with the arithmetic in the cell note.

where: Outputs!B4 = 'Over the forecast the business generates $54,873m of free cash flow and returns $32,512m to shareholders; cash ends a...' (truncated)
issue: The headline on Outputs!B4 quotes FCF and shareholder return but does not carry through to closing cash (47,771.5 beyond the 4,000 floor) or the downside headroom (6,048.07), which is the actual decision variable for a capital-allocation paper.
fix: Rewrite the B4 string to include: '...; cash ends FY2031 at $47,771m, $43,772m above the $4,000m floor; in the downside cash ends at $17,220m, $13,220m above the floor in the last year and $6,048m at the tightest point.'

issue: The answer is a run-on sentence crammed into one cell: "Over the forecast the business generates $54,873m of free cash flow and returns $32,512m to shareholders; cash ends a..." — a committee cannot read the headline number at a glance, and the string is truncated.
fix: Break Outputs!B4 into three labeled rows with the number in its own cell: 'Free cash flow, FY27-FY31 ($m)' = 54,873; 'Cash returned to shareholders ($m)' = 32,512; 'Closing cash, 2031 ($m)' = 47,771. Keep the formula's TEXT() concatenation but only as a one-line caption, and drop the comma-heavy formatting.

issue: The downside case reuses the base case's cash returned: B33 =cash+B32+B11+B14+B15+B16 pulls the same -13,293 special dividend and -800 buyback. A committee will ask whether the $30 special is affordable if revenue grows 3% and margin falls 1pt, and the model forces the answer to be yes by construction.

issue: The sensitivity grid formula embeds the whole model inside a single IF(): '=cash+revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(ABS((1+rev_growth+$A40...' — no reviewer can follow it, and the ABS() construction suggests a boundary correction that is not documented.
fix: Replicate the five-year cash path in a small helper block (one row per row of Model 5:F17) driven by $A40 and B$39, then reference the helper in B40:F44. Add a cell comment stating what the ABS() term does; if it is just a sign guard, replace with the direct formula.

where: Inputs: 'Cash floor the board keeps ($m)' [min_cash] = 4,000; source: assumption
issue: The single most decision-relevant number — the cash floor that determines every 'Yes' in Outputs!B17 and B20 — is labeled 'assumption' with no basis. A CEO will reject the funding conclusion on this alone.
fix: Document min_cash: cite Costco's stated minimum operating cash (10-K liquidity discussion), or if none exists, replace with a computed floor — e.g. 2 weeks of revenue ($303,150 × 2/52 ≈ $11,660m) — and show the sensitivity of the 'Funded?' answer to the floor in Outputs.

where: Model!A12, A18, A19, A27 and Outputs!A4, A17, A20
issue: Forge flagged seven unit-less labels — 'Opening shares', 'Closing shares', 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?' — so the reader cannot tell whether 443.1 is millions, thousands or a count.
fix: Append units: A12/A19/A27 → 'Opening shares (m)', 'Closing shares (m)'; A18 → 'Shares retired (m)'; Outputs!A4 → 'Answer ($m, m shares)'; A17/A20 → 'Funded without new debt? (Y/N)'.

issue: Row labels carry truncated memo text: A11 says 'Interest income (on opening cash: on average cash' and A14 'Regular dividends (on average shares: buybacks spr' — half-sentences cut off mid-word.
fix: Shorten to 'Interest income ($m)' and 'Regular dividends ($m)' and move the method note ('on opening cash') to a cell comment or a footnote row beneath the table.

issue: The cover names the model but carries no headline result, so the first thing anyone opens to says nothing about the answer.
fix: Add a single line under the title: 'FY27-FY31: $54.9B free cash flow, $32.5B returned, closing cash $47.8B; funded in base and downside without new debt.' (all figures already in Outputs).

where: Model!B31 dry; Inputs: down_growth = 3.0%, down_margin_cut = 1.0%, capex_overrun = 15.0%
issue: The downside varies three inputs independently with no stated joint rationale — 3% growth plus a 1pt margin cut plus a 15% capex overrun is a coherent story, but the deck does not say what scenario it is (recession? competitive entry? FX?).
fix: Add a one-line scenario definition above row 31: 'Downside = revenue growth halves to 3%, OCF margin compresses 100bp on price/wage pressure, capex overruns 15% on remodel pipeline' — all three figures already in Inputs.

issue: Interest convention is inconsistent with the label and with the dividend convention. Model!B11 is labelled 'Interest income (on opening cash: on average cash' — formula is =B10*cash_yield, i.e. opening cash, not average. Model!B14 regular dividends uses AVERAGE(B12,B19) (average shares). Two different conventions in one model, unexplained.
fix: Either change B11:F11 to =AVERAGE(B10,B17)*cash_yield to match the average-balance convention used for dividends, or change the label to 'Interest income (on opening cash)' and add a one-line note in Inputs that the convention is opening balance, stated consistently. Do not leave the label half-edited as it is now.

issue: The cash floor — the single number that determines the headroom result (2,891.94 base, -1,678.42 downside) — is sourced only as 'assumption: computed floor of 2 weeks of revenue = $303,150m x 2/52'. That is a made-up convention, not company policy. No citation, no range, no explanation of why 2 weeks.
fix: Replace with a sourced figure: either Costco's stated minimum operating cash (pull from 10-K liquidity discussion) or, if none exists, label it explicitly as 'Analyst assumption: 2 weeks of revenue' with the range tested (1 week to 4 weeks) and show the headroom at each. Currently the reader sees a concrete dollar figure with a hand-wave source.

issue: Buyback of $800m/yr is sourced to a '$4B share repurchase program reauthorized, expiring January 2030' plus FY2026 actual $848m. The program authorization is a ceiling, not a plan. Using 20% of a $4B authorization as an annual run-rate with no stated rationale is an unsourced assumption dressed as a citation.
fix: State the driver: either 'FY2026 actual $848m held flat' or 'management has run ~$800m-$1.0B/yr; we assume $800m'. Give the range ($0 to $848m) and show headroom impact at both ends. If the plan is to preserve cash, say so; if to return it, say so.

where: Model!F33 vs Model!B33 and Model!F34 vs Model!B34
issue: The downside closes at 17,450.13 in FY2031 (headroom +5,790) but bottoms at -1,678.42 in an earlier year (B34). The model shows the trough without flagging which year it occurs. A committee will ask 'in what year does the downside breach the floor?' and the workbook does not answer it in Outputs.
fix: Add a row to Outputs: 'Downside: year of lowest headroom' returning the year index (MATCH(MIN(...),...) across B34:F34). Then the output reads: downside breaches the floor in FY2028 by $1,678m, recovering by FY2031.

issue: The sensitivity grid rows 40-44 use =cash+revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(ABS((1+rev_growth+$A40... — the formula is truncated in the digest but appears to compute a single-period cash outcome, not the five-year closing cash used in the base case (Model!B23 = 47,970.9). The grid values (45,343 to 56,424) do not reconcile to the base-case 47,970.9 at the base column/row, so the grid is either built on a different definition or a different horizon than the answer.
fix: Rebuild rows 40-44 so the centre cell equals ca_cash_end (47,970.9) exactly at the base-case growth and capex growth. Whatever the grid measures (FCF? closing cash?), label the row header with the metric and unit and confirm the centre ties to Model!B23.

issue: Revenue growth of 6.0% is sourced to 'three years 7.8%' historical — i.e. the forward assumption is a material step-down from the cited history with no stated rationale for the step-down.
fix: State the rationale in the Inputs note: e.g. 'historical 3-yr CAGR 7.8%; we assume 6.0% to reflect FX headwinds and competition cited in F39/F40/F42'. Give the range (5%-8%) and stress it — the 6.0% is the assumption the answer depends on.

issue: Capex growth of 10.0% is sourced to '3-yr history 14.2%' — again a step-down from cited history with no rationale, and capex is the largest single use of cash in the model ($6,500 base growing at 10%).
fix: State the rationale and give the range. The downside already applies a +15% capex overrun (Inputs capex_overrun = 15.0%); show in Outputs the headroom at the base growth of 6.0% and at the downside 3.0% with the capex overrun applied together, not as separate rows.

issue: Special dividend of $30/share = $13,293m (Model!B15) is paid at the start of the first year, i.e. against opening cash of $20,210m. That is 66% of opening cash in one line, and it is not reflected in the interest income for year 1 (B11 = B10*4.1% = 828.61, computed on the pre-special-dividend opening cash).
fix: Either move the special dividend to end of year 1 (so opening cash earns interest for the full year), or if it is genuinely paid day one, recompute B11 as AVERAGE(B10, B17)*cash_yield so the interest reflects the full-year average balance. As drawn, the model overstates year-1 interest.

issue: Seven labels lack units: Model!A12 'Opening shares', A18 'Shares retired', A19 'Closing shares', A27 'Closing shares', Outputs!A4 'Answer', A17 'Funded without new debt?', A20 'Funded in the downside?'.
fix: Add units: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)' etc. For the yes/no rows, unit is n/a — label 'Funded without new debt? (Y/N)'.

where: Model!B21 vs Model!F21 (cash cover of capex)
issue: Row 21 formula uses IF(B7=0,"NM",...) but B7 is always negative capex; the guard is never triggered. Fine, but the same convention is applied inconsistently — row 21 is not in the Outputs tab, so the reader has to find it.
fix: Either surface row 21 in Outputs or drop it; if kept, note 'cash cover of capex = closing cash / |capex|'.

issue: The downside shows a breach of the cash floor — ca_down_min_headroom = -1,678.42 — yet Outputs row 20 only says 'No: in the downside cash falls below the floor' with no magnitude, no year, and no consequence. The single most decision-relevant number in the model is delivered as a yes/no.
fix: Change Outputs!B20 to name the number and the year: 'No: cash falls $1,678m below the floor in FY2027.' Add a row above it 'Downside: year the floor is breached' returning the first year where Model row 34 is negative. Place B19/B20 above the base-case rows so the reader hits the downside first.

issue: The downside holds cash returned constant ('same cash returned' per the Model row 33 sample) while simultaneously cutting revenue growth to 3%, cutting OCF margin by 100bps and adding a 15% capex overrun. That is the wrong downside. A board facing the conditions that cause the revenue and margin cut would cut or suspend the buyback and delay the special dividend before it let cash fall through its floor.
fix: Add a downside cash-return switch to Inputs: 'Downside: buyback ($m)' and 'Downside: special dividend paid? (Y/N)'. Wire Model row 33 to those inputs. Recompute ca_down_min_headroom and report it. If the answer stays negative even with the buyback cut, the model says Costco cannot fund its plan in a downturn — that is the finding and it should be the headline.

issue: Free cash flow is defined as OCF plus capex with capex sign-flipped by the formula (=B6+B7 where B7 = -capex_base). This is a definition, not an error, but nothing on the sheet states it. A reader sees '+B7' and has to reverse-engineer that row 7 is negative capex. The same trick appears in the downside at row 32 with a 1.15 multiplier applied before the sign convention is explained.
fix: Add a label above the block: 'Free cash flow = operating cash flow less capital expenditure.' On Model row 7 change the label to 'Capital expenditure' with a note in column G: 'Entered as a negative.' On row 32 add a comment: 'Downside FCF = revenue x (5.2% - 1.0%) less capex x 1.15.'

issue: The buyback is set to a flat $800m every year for five years from a reauthorised $4B programme expiring January 2030, with no rationale. The source quotes the authorisation, not the run-rate. $800m is neither the $848m historical figure nor any stated plan. A flat plug for a discretionary use of cash is exactly the number a committee will attack.
fix: Either set the buyback to the historical run-rate ($848m, source F9) and say so in the source column, or model it as 'remaining authorisation divided by years to expiry' — $4,000m over FY2027-FY2029 = $1,333m/yr, then zero from FY2030. State the choice in the source cell. Do not leave a round number with no basis.

issue: The grid varies growth and capex but the formulas in the sample are truncated mid-expression (B40 = cash + revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(ABS((1+rev_growth+$A40 ...). I cannot verify from the digest that the grid recomputes dividends, interest and buybacks year by year or whether it is a single-period shortcut. If it is a shortcut, the grid numbers (45,343 to 56,425) will not reconcile to the five-year closing cash of 47,971 and the page is misleading.
fix: Add a check: 'Grid centre cell equals ca_cash_end' with a tolerance of zero. If it does not tie, replace the shortcut with a full five-year recalculation per grid cell, or delete the grid and present three explicit cases (base, downside, downside-with-buyback-cut) instead.

issue: There are two scenarios: base and one downside. The sensitivity grid varies growth and capex but not the two variables that actually drive the cash answer: the OCF margin and the cash returned to shareholders. The decision is 'can Costco fund the plan and keep returning cash' — that question lives in those two variables.
fix: Add a third scenario row to Inputs for 'Stress': growth 1.0%, margin cut 1.5%, capex overrun 20%, buyback suspended, special dividend deferred. Report its closing cash and lowest headroom alongside the other two on Outputs. Name the scenarios on the sheet: Base / Downside / Stress.

issue: The answer is a single concatenated text string built in a formula: 'Over the forecast the business generates $54,511m of free cash flow and returns $31,917m to shareholders; cash ends a...'. It wraps across cells, cannot be read at a glance, and buries the downside. Answers belong as numbers in a table, not as prose in a cell.
fix: Split row 4 into three cells: 'Free cash flow, FY2027-FY2031 ($m)' = 54,511; 'Cash returned, FY2027-FY2031 ($m)' = 31,917; 'Closing cash, FY2031 ($m)' = 47,971. Delete the sentence. If a sentence is wanted, put it on the Cover as a one-line conclusion, and make it name the downside.

issue: Seven X10 warnings: labels 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares' (twice), 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?' carry no unit. 'Closing shares' appears on two different rows (19 and 27) meaning the same thing, and the reader cannot tell which is the output.
fix: Add units: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)'. On Outputs prefix the two questions with their scope: 'Base: funded without new debt?' and 'Downside: funded without new debt?'. Delete Model row 27 as a duplicate of row 19, or relabel it 'Closing shares, FY2031 (m)'.

issue: Downside lowest headroom is -$1,137.46 (Outputs!B19) and the answer cell reads 'No: in the downside cash falls below the floor', but no funding plan, no draw on the revolver, and no comparison to the $4,000m min_cash is given beyond the floor breach. A committee cannot approve a capital allocation plan that is unfunded in its own downside.
fix: Add a downside funding row to Model and Outputs: show the incremental debt or reduced buyback required to hold closing cash at min_cash ($4,000m), compute the gap as $4,000 - $2,862.54 = $1,137.46m, and state in Outputs!B20 the specific action (e.g. 'Funded by cutting the $4,000m buyback by $1,137m in 2031').

where: Inputs, [Operations] rev_growth = 6.0%, range 4.5% to 7.5%; capex_growth = 8.0%, range 5.0% to 12.0%
issue: Two of the three drivers that determine the answer (revenue growth and capex growth) carry ranges but no scenario/sensitivity is run on them in the outputs; the only sensitivity is a 2-way grid on Model rows 39-44 whose formula is truncated and whose link to Outputs is unstated. The 6% growth and 8% capex are midpoint picks, not tested.
fix: Wire the Model!B39:F44 grid (growth change vs investment plan change) to a named output and surface it on Outputs, and add one-way sensitivity rows on rev_growth (4.5%/6.0%/7.5%) and capex_growth (5%/8%/12%) showing ca_cash_end and ca_min_headroom for each.

where: Inputs, [Rates] cash_yield = 4.1%, range 4.1% to 4.1%; [Balance sheet and shares] min_cash = 4,000, source: assumption; share_price = 1,106.21, range 850 to 1,106.21
issue: Three inputs have no range or no source. cash_yield range is a single point 4.1%-4.1% from a single Yahoo 13-week T-bill quote (F24), so interest income of $3,932.87 over five years has zero sensitivity; min_cash is literally 'assumption' with a 3,000-6,000 range but no board policy citation; share_price range $850-$1,106.21 is the 52-week range, not a forecast range for a 2030 buyback.
fix: Source min_cash to Costco's stated liquidity/working-capital policy in the 10-K (cite the filing paragraph), widen cash_yield to the observed 3.5%-4.5% band over the forecast with the Fed/Treasury source, and replace the share_price range with a forward P/E or analyst-target band; then re-run interest income and buyback share retirement.

where: Model!B11 'Interest income (on opening cash: on average cash' and Model!F11 =F10*cash_yield
issue: Interest is computed on opening cash only (B11 = B10*cash_yield = 832.65), so cash accumulated through the year earns nothing; the label even says 'on average cash'. Understates ca_int_total ($3,932.87) and closing cash.
fix: Change interest to average of opening and closing cash with a circularity control, or state explicitly 'interest on opening cash only' in the row label and add a one-line note quantifying the understatement; keep the workbook circularity switch on if using average.

issue: Dividend per share grows 5.0% while shares retire ~3.6m/yr (B18) and EPS is $20.76 (F13 source), implying a payout that silently rises; there is no payout-ratio check and no link from dps to the board's stated dividend policy.
fix: Add a payout-ratio row (dps / EPS) across the forecast and show it stays within Costco's historical band; source the 5.0% dps_growth to the 10-K dividend policy language rather than the stockanalysis.com $5.88 figure.

issue: Signs are mixed: FCF (B8) is positive, dividends and buyback (B14-B16) are negative, so the closing cash formula is a net add — it works, but the tab mixes a positive cash-flow sign with negative uses, and the downside row B33 uses 'cash+B32+B11+B14+B15+B16' with the same convention. A reader cannot tell whether ca_uses_total = 47,384.47 is positive-outflow or negative-inflow without flipping signs.
fix: Adopt one convention (outflows negative throughout) and add a legend on Inputs row 3 and on Model row 9; restate ca_uses_total as -47,384.47 or label it 'Cash returned, $m (absolute)'.

where: Inputs, special_dps = 30, source F36 Yahoo Finance 2026-11-11; buyback = 4,000, source F37 Yahoo Finance 2026-11-11
issue: The special dividend ($30/sh, $13,293m in B15) and the $4B buyback authorization both rest on a single Yahoo Finance article; the 10-K cites are given as F1/F9 but the special dividend timing (paid at the start of the first forecast year, B15 label) is not tied to a declared ex-date.
fix: Replace the Yahoo citations with the 8-K/press release for the special dividend (record the record and payment dates) and the board authorization language for the $4B program; if the special dividend pays in FY2027, confirm it falls in B15's period and not before opening cash.

issue: X10 warnings: nine labels have no unit — 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares' (twice on Model), and Outputs 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?', 'Year of the lowest headroom, base/downside'.
fix: Append units to each label: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)', 'Year of the lowest headroom, base (fiscal year)'.

issue: Capex is entered as a negative and grown multiplicatively; the sign is consistent but the sign of capex_base on Inputs is positive (6,500). Mixing a positive input with a negative model line invites a double-negative error if anyone edits the input.
fix: Keep capex positive on Inputs and make the model row 'Less: capital expenditure' = -1* the positive driver, or state the sign convention explicitly in the row label.

issue: The answer is a concatenated TEXT() sentence — 'Over the forecast the business generates $56,423m of free cash flow and returns $47,384m to shareholders; cash ends a...' — truncated in the digest and not auditable as separate numbers.
fix: Split the answer into discrete cells (FCF $56,423.1m, returns $47,384.5m, closing cash $33,181.5m) and build the sentence from references so the figures tie to Model!B22, B25, B23.

where: Model tab rows 39-44 (grid: growth change x investment plan change)
issue: The Model tab has a sensitivity grid (rows 39-44) that appears to flex revenue growth and capex growth to compute closing cash, but it sits below the core model without any clear linkage to the Outputs tab or the decision. The grid has no labels for what the 5x5 matrix actually answers.
fix: Either move the grid to the Outputs tab with a clear title ('Closing cash ($m) under revenue growth x capex growth') and add a callout for the break-even cell where closing cash crosses the $4B floor, or delete it if it doesn't drive the decision. If it stays, add unit ($m) to the row/column headers.

issue: The downside case is a single scenario with all three adverse drivers applied simultaneously, but there's no bridge showing which driver does the damage. The output (ca_down_min_headroom = -1,137.46) tells the reader it fails but not why or which lever matters most.
fix: Add a one-way sensitivity on the Outputs tab: show closing cash and minimum headroom when only down_growth moves to 3%, when only down_margin_cut moves to 1.0%, and when only capex_overrun moves to 15%. Use the Model!B33 formula structure but flex one input at a time. Label the columns clearly.

issue: The special dividend of $30/share ($13,293m) is paid in year 1 on opening shares (443.1M), and the buyback of $4,000m/year is layered on top. But the model doesn't show whether the special dividend is a one-time event (it should be) or whether the $4B buyback is constrained by the cash floor. The downside case (ca_down_min_headroom = -1,137.46) shows the combination breaches the floor, but the base case doesn't force a buyback cut.
fix: Add a line in the Model tab (or a new row in Outputs) that shows 'Buyback actually funded' vs. 'Buyback authorized' and triggers a cut when headroom < 0. Show the mechanism: if cash floor would be breached, buyback reduces to zero. This is the actual decision lever.

issue: The label 'Answer' in Outputs!A4 is vague and doesn't tell the reader what question is being answered. The text in B4 is long and reads like a paragraph, not a headline.
fix: Change A4 to 'Can Costco fund its plan without new debt?' or similar, and move the B4 text to a separate cell below a proper headline. Make the headline: 'Costco generates $56.4B FCF, returns $47.4B, ends with $33.2B cash — no new debt needed in the base case.'

where: Outputs tab rows 17, 20, 21, 22 (labels 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?', 'Year of the lowest headroom, base', 'Year of the lowest headroom, downside')
issue: The X10 rule flagged these labels as having no unit. While some are Yes/No or year labels, the ones returning values (e.g., year of lowest headroom) should specify the unit or context.
fix: Add '(year)' to rows 21 and 22 labels, and '(Yes/No)' to rows 17 and 20. For row 17, the output 'Yes' needs context — change label to 'Funded without new debt? (base case)'.

where: Model!A12, A18, A19, A27 (labels 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares')
issue: The X10 rule flagged these as missing units. Shares are in millions but the labels don't say so, and the Inputs tab specifies 'Shares outstanding (m)'.
fix: Change labels to 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)' on all four rows.

issue: The Checks tab only has 3 checks, and they are all arithmetic ties (closing cash to flows, grid centre, downside < base). No check ensures that the buyback doesn't breach the cash floor in the base case, or that the special dividend is only paid once.
fix: Add two checks: (1) 'Base case: minimum headroom >= 0' showing ca_min_headroom = 7,428.75 and OK status. (2) 'Special dividend paid only in year 1' verifying that Model!C15 through F15 = 0.

issue: The written Answer reads 'Over the forecast the business generates $56,423m of free cash flow and returns $47,384m to shareholders; cash ends a...' and stops there — it never states that the downside (Outputs!B19 = -1,137.46, Outputs!B20 = 'No: in the downside cash falls below the floor') fails in FY2031. The central conclusion of a capital allocation model is whether the plan is affordable; the Answer tab is the one thing a committee reads. This is the single most important output and it is missing.
fix: Rewrite Outputs!B4 to lead with the base case AND the downside in one sentence: 'Base case: FCF of $56,423m funds $47,384m of cash returned and closing cash of $33,181m, $29,182m above the $4,000m floor. Downside (3% growth, 100bp margin cut, 15% capex overrun): closing cash of $2,863m in FY2031, $1,137m below the floor — the plan is not fundable at the current dividend and buyback without a change to one of the drivers.' Then add a bullet naming which driver to change first (see downside issue).

issue: The downside cash line reuses the BASE case interest income (B11 across to F11) rather than the interest the downside's own — and rising — cash balance would earn. Check: Model!F33 = 2,862.54, but the closing cash path in the downside is different from base in every year (FY2031 downside closing cash 2,862.54 vs base 33,181.51), so FY2031 downside interest is materially overstated at base-case F11 = 1,103.94. The interest is a formula link to the base interest row, not an independent calc; this hides the fact that the downside is closer to breaking the floor than it looks. It is not an error in the check (the check ties because it is defined that way), but it makes the downside understate the cash shortfall.
fix: Replace B33:F33 in the interest component with a downside interest line: down_int = prior-year downside closing cash * cash_yield, and add a row so Outputs!B19 reports ca_down_min_headroom from the re-computed path. Then the printed downside headroom is honest.

issue: ca_min_headroom = 7,428.75 at Model!B24 and Outputs!B21 says the base-case lowest headroom is FY2027 — but Model!B10 opens at 20,210 and Model!B15 pays the $30 special dividend ($30 * 443.1 = 13,293) at B15. That is intentional (special is 'paid at the start of the first y'), but the reader sees FY2027 as the trough year with 7,428.75 headroom, which happens to be above the 4,000 floor by only 1,857 on a base-case OCF of 16,774. The model then grows headroom monotonically. There is no scenario where the special dividend is smaller, delayed, or paired with the buyback being cut — the special is $30 fixed (Inputs, special_dps range 30 to 30). A source note says 'special cash dividend of $30 per share declared 2026-11-11' — that is a declaration, not a forecast. Locking a range of 30-to-30 into a forecast is a plug.
fix: Widen the special dividend range in Inputs from '30 to 30' to at least '0 to 30' with the $30 case cited as the declared amount and the 0 case cited as the alternative (no special; larger buyback). Then add a sensitivity on the special (e.g. 0/15/30) in the Outputs tab, because for the base case it is the largest single line of cash returned after buyback and the one thing the answer hinges on.

issue: Several inputs carry a range that is a point: capex_base range '6,000 to 7,000' is fine, but cash_yield is '4.1% to 4.1%' and its source is 'F24 US 13-week Treasury bill yield 4.12% at 2026-11-13' — a spot yield on one date locked for a five-year forecast. The model earns $3,932.87m of interest over five years on 4.1% flat; if rates fall to 3.0% that figure shrinks by roughly $1,100m and the downside floor is breached a year earlier. min_cash is unsourced ('assumption') — for a model whose entire verdict is 'does the plan clear the floor', the floor has no evidence behind it.
fix: Give cash_yield a range (e.g. 2.5% to 4.1%) with the low end sourced to the forward curve or a stated 'if the Fed cuts' rationale, and drive it from a short rate input plus a spread rather than a spot quote. Give min_cash a sourced anchor: e.g. Costco's 10-K statement on liquidity / minimum operating cash, or peer liquidity disclosure, with a range of 3,000 to 6,000 and a rationale sentence. State in Inputs why 4,000 was chosen.

issue: dps_growth source reads 'F12 10-K FY2026 declared $5.54; F38 current annual $5.88 (a 6.1% step-up)' — the cited evidence is a 6.1% step-up, but the input is 5.0%. The number in the cell does not match the source note in the same row; a reader will see the mismatch before they see anything else. It is a small gap, but it is the kind of thing that makes a committee question every other number on the page.
fix: Either set dps_growth to 6.1% to match the cited step-up, or change the source note to say 'held at 5.0%, below the FY2026 6.1% step-up, to reflect lower long-run dividend growth' — one or the other, so the number and its evidence agree.

where: Model!B12:F12 and Model!B14:F14 ('Regular dividends (on average shares : buybacks spread evenly)')
issue: Both the share count and dividends are computed on average balances, but the special dividend at B15 = -special_dps * B12 uses opening shares (B12), and shares retired at B18 = B16/-share_price retires at the current spot price of $1,106.21 (Inputs) every year from FY2027 to FY2031 (Model F16 = -4,000, F18 = 3.62). That prices five years of buyback at today's close. If the stock is at $1,400 by FY2031, FY2031 retires 2.86m shares, not 3.62m — a 21% overstatement of the annual retirement and roughly 3.5m shares over five years, which is about $4bn at $1,106.21. Not wrong by convention — models price buybacks at spot — but the numbers must not be labelled a forecast of share count without a price path.
fix: Add a 'share price, forecast' input row with a range (e.g. $1,000 to $1,400) and let B18:F18 use the forecast price, or hold it at $1,106.21 but rename the row 'Shares retired (at spot $1,106.21)' so the assumption is visible. Either way, state in the Inputs source note that the buyback price is held flat at the 2026-11-13 close.

issue: The Outputs tab has 14 formula rows and one sensitivity grid on Model rows 39-44 (growth change vs investment plan change) — but the grid never surfaces a worst case that names the year the floor is breached; the only 'year of lowest headroom' rows quote MIN across FY2027-FY2031 and print '2027' (base) and '2031' (downside). The Outputs do not show the crossover: at what down_growth or capex_overrun the plan first fails. A committee will ask that question and the workbook cannot answer it.
fix: Add a two-way sensitivity on Outputs: down_growth (2.0% to 4.0%) down, capex_overrun (10% to 20%) across, cell = ca_down_min_headroom (from the re-computed downside). Then add one line: 'The plan first breaches the $4,000m floor at down_growth below X% and capex_overrun above Y%.' Use only the driver values already in Inputs.

where: Model row 21 ('Cash cover of capex (x)') vs Model row 20
issue: Row 21 defines cover as closing cash divided by capex, using closing cash — which includes the interest income and the special dividend. It reports 1.76x in FY2027 and 3.75x in FY2031. That is a coverage metric nobody uses: it mixes a stock (cash) with a flow (capex) and includes the one-off special dividend in the numerator in FY2027. Outputs does not report it, so it is not load-bearing — but it is on the Model tab where a client will read it.
fix: Either delete Model rows 21 and replace with a conventional metric (FCF/capex, or cash+capex commitment coverage) or label it precisely: 'Closing cash / capex (x), includes one-off special dividend in FY2027'. Do not report 1.76x and 3.75x without that label.

where: Model!A12, A18, A19, A27; Outputs!A4, A17, A20, A21, A22
issue: X10 flags nine labels with no unit: Model row 12 'Opening shares', row 18 'Shares retired', row 19 and row 27 'Closing shares', Outputs row 4 'Answer', row 17 'Funded without new debt?', row 20 'Funded in the downside?', rows 21 and 22 'Year of the lowest headroom, base/downside'. Same class of issue as the version that goes to a client — a reviewer cannot tell whether shares are m or 000s, or whether rows 17/20 are a Yes/No or a $m.
fix: Append units to the nine labels: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)', 'Answer (text)' (or drop the unit for a text row and mark it as text), 'Funded without new debt? (Yes/No)', 'Funded in the downside? (Yes/No)', 'Year of the lowest headroom, base (fiscal year)', 'Year of the lowest headroom, downside (fiscal year)'. Check the Outputs 'Answer' row does not need a unit because it is a sentence.

issue: Inputs row 3 is headed in the digest as 'Inputs (header row 3)' with sections [Operations], [Balance sheet and shares], [Cash returned], [Rates], [Downside case]. Two conventions are mixed: [Operations] mixes %-of-revenue drivers (rev_growth, ocf_margin) with $m drivers (revenue_base, capex_base) in the same section. In a board book, drivers are grouped by income statement / balance sheet / cash returned, not by 'operations'. Small, but this is the table a reviewer audits first, and mis-grouping costs a scanning minute.
fix: Re-order Inputs to: [Revenue drivers], [Cost and margin drivers], [Capex drivers], [Balance sheet and shares], [Cash returned], [Rates], [Downside case]. Keep value/unit/range/source columns as is.

issue: Opening cash (B10 =cash) and opening shares (B12 =shares) are hard-linked to inputs in year 1 and then linked to prior-year closing in later years (F10 =E17, F12 =E19). That is correct, but the workbook digest does not show a named 'opening_balance' convention, and X7 and X11 rules are 'not_run' — the balance-sheet roll-forward convention is not machine-verified. Not a defect in the numbers; a structure gap.
fix: Nothing to change in the model. Flag in the workbook's own documentation tab that X7 and X11 were not run, so the next reviewer knows which rules were and were not checked. Do not ship with two validation rules in 'not_run' state without saying so.

issue: The 'Answer' cell says cash ends around the floor, but the only material downside number is two lines down (B18 = 2,862.54, B19 = -1,137.46) and nothing resolves it. The workbook poses the question 'can Costco fund the special dividend and buybacks?' and then leaves the reader with a Yes in base and a No in downside with no bridge.
fix: Add a short 'What this means' block to the Outputs tab immediately under r4: state in one line the base result (Yes, $33,181.5m ending cash, $7,428.75m minimum headroom) and the downside result (No, $2,862.5m ending cash, -$1,137.5m minimum headroom in 2031), then one line on the lever (e.g. 'funding the $30 special dividend in full is what tips the downside through the floor') and one line recommendation. Use only numbers already in the workbook.

where: Outputs!B20 'Funded in the downside?' = 'No: in the downside cash falls below the floor'
issue: The workbook says the downside fails but does not size the gap or the fix. A reader cannot act on 'No'.
fix: Directly under Outputs!B20, add the shortfall ($1,137.5m at the 2031 trough, from ca_down_min_headroom) and one line on what closes it: cutting the special dividend, reducing the $4,000m annual buyback, or trimming capex growth from 8.0%—quantify the smallest change that clears the floor using only inputs already in Inputs.

issue: No chart and no year-by-year base/downside cash path, so the reader cannot see where the downside trough sits or how close the base is to the floor. 'Year of the lowest headroom, base' = 2027 and 'Year of the lowest headroom, downside' = 2031 are useful but sit as bare values near the bottom (r21, r22).
fix: Insert a single line chart on the Outputs tab with closing cash (Model!B17:F17) and downside closing cash (Model!B33:F33) against the cash floor (min_cash = 4,000), years FY2027-FY2031. Chart title should state the takeaway ('Base never breaches the floor; downside breaches it from 2029'), not 'Cash balance'. Move r21 and r22 next to the chart.

issue: The headline reach of the model—closing cash—is dominated by interest income within the forecast ($3,932.87m over five years, from ca_int_total) and the special dividend of $30/share. A reader cannot tell whether the conclusion is a cash-generation story or an interest-on-cash story.
fix: Add one line under Outputs!B14: 'Closing cash before five years of interest income would be $29,248.7m' (33,181.51 - 3,932.87) so the reader sees how much of the ending position is earned versus invested.

issue: The base-case revenue growth (6.0%) sits mid-range of 4.5%-7.5%, but capex growth of 8.0% sits in a 5.0%-12.0% band with a source note claiming a 14.2% three-year CAGR. The base case is more conservative on capex than the company's own recent trend, while revenue is toward the top of the band—the two are not consistent with each other.
fix: State on the Inputs tab which point in the range is the case (e.g. 'base case: mid-range on revenue, below the 14.2% three-year capex CAGR because guidance suggests a slower step-up'). If the base case is meant to be mid-range, set rev_growth and capex_growth to mid of their stated ranges and document why.

where: Model!r33 'Closing cash, downside (same cash returned, interest...)' and Model!r32
issue: The downside line holds cash returned at the base level ('same cash returned') while cutting revenue growth, OCF margin and raising capex. That conflates the decision (does the buyback/special dividend still work) with a demand shock. A committee will read -$1,137.5m as 'Costco cannot afford the plan' when in fact the plan is fixed and forward returns are worse.
fix: Add a second downside column set (or a row note) that flexes cash returned alongside the operational deterioration, so it is clear whether the failure is operational or a policy choice. Keep the existing rows labelled 'Stage 1: operations only' and 'Stage 2: operations and cash return fixed'.

issue: Nine X10 warnings flag labels without units on 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares', 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?', 'Year of the lowest headroom, base/downside'.
fix: Add the unit to each label (m for shares; $m for cash; $m for headroom; year for the two 'Year of...' rows; 'text' or no unit for the two Yes/No labels). Clear the X10 warnings.

issue: The Inputs tab is a topic list. There is no single up-front answer line and no grouping by decision (growth, cash return, rates, downside). Blue-cell convention is stated in the tab description but not visible in-cell.
fix: Add a legend at the top of Inputs ('Blue = input, change here; grey = formula') and reorder rows into the four groups named in the capture: Operations, Balance sheet and shares, Cash returned, Rates, Downside. Keep ranges and sources as-is.

issue: Cover only has a title and no reading order, so a CFO has to hunt through tabs.
fix: On the Cover tab add three lines: 'Question: can Costco fund its stated capital return plan?', 'Answer: Outputs!B4 (base), Outputs!B20 (downside)', 'Checks: Checks!F3'.

where: Outputs!B4 (Answer) and Outputs!B20 (Funded in the downside?)
issue: The headline answer at Outputs!B4 reads 'Over the forecast the business generates $56,423m of free cash flow and returns $47,695m to shareholders; cash ends at $32,859m' — this is the base case only, and it does not disclose that the downside case breaches the $4,000m cash floor by -$1,460m in 2031 (Outputs!B19/B22, Model!B36). A committee reading the answer cell alone would conclude the $30 special dividend (Inputs special_dps=30, Model!B15=-$13,293m) and the $4,000m/yr buyback are funded. They are not, in the stress case.
fix: Amend Outputs!B4 to append the downside explicitly, e.g. '...cash ends at $32,859m (base); in the downside case cash ends at $2,540m and headroom over the $4,000m floor is -$1,460m in 2031, so the $30 special dividend is not funded in the stress case.' Do not change the numbers; only state both.

issue: The $30 special dividend (-$13,293m, Model!B15) and the $4,000m/yr buyback (Model!B16=-4,000) are held constant in the downside (Model!B33 = cash + B32 + B11 + B14 + B15 + B16). The downside is not a downside of the capital plan — it is a downside of operations with the same capital plan. A committee will read the -$1,460m headroom (Model!B36) as the consequence of not flexing the return of capital, not of the business deteriorating.
fix: Add a second downside column or a toggle by the special dividend that cuts/suspends special_dps to 0 in the downside and reruns Model!B33. Report both: headroom with the plan unchanged and headroom with the special dividend cancelled. This is the number the board needs to see.

where: Inputs, [Cash returned] share buyback per year [buyback] = 4,000 and Model!B18
issue: The buyback is held at exactly $4,000m/yr for five years (Model!B16:F16) but the retire formula is shares = dollars / share price (Model!B18 = B16/-share_price = 4,000/1,106.21 = 3.62m/yr flat), and share_price (Inputs, $1,106.21 as of 2026-11-13) is held flat across 2027-2031. A flat dollar buyback against a flat price means the model assumes zero price drift over five years and, more importantly, the source is a spot price, not a five-year path.
fix: State the buyback as a policy of $4,000m/yr (which the $4B reauthorization supports, F37) and label the shares retired row as 'at the current $1,106.21 price, held flat for illustration only.' Add a note that a higher price in later years retires fewer shares and reduces the cash return needed to hold shares flat; do not change the retire formula but flag the assumption.

where: Inputs, [Rates] cash_yield = 4.1% and Model!B11 (interest on average cash)
issue: Both the base (Model!B11) and the downside (Model!B33 uses B11) earn 4.1% on opening cash for 2027-2031, sourced to the 13-week bill at 2026-11-13 (F24). Holding a single spot yield for five years is stale as a forecast; the terminal-year closing cash of $32,858m (Model!B23) carries the same yield.
fix: Add a range for cash_yield (the input already shows 2.5%-4.1%) and run the headroom sensitised on cash_yield at the low end. In the downside this materially changes the -$1,460m number.

where: Model!R7 and Model!B18-B19, Model!B12-B19 versus Model!A12-A19
issue: Model row 7 (Capex) is placed above the FCF rows at r8 and after OCF at r6, but the ordering shows OCF (r6), Capex (r7), FCF (r8) — good — while the share roll-forward at r12-r19 is interleaved with the cash grid r10-r17. The lowest headroom row r24 (B24=7,428.75) computes MIN(B20:F20)=7,428.75 in 2027, yet Outputs!B21 says the year of lowest headroom in the base is 2027 — consistent, but the cash walk shows closing cash rises monotonically from $11,429m (Model!B17) to $32,859m (Model!F17), so the binding year is the first year and it is the special dividend that binds it.
fix: On Outputs, add a line under the Answer: 'The binding year in the base case is 2027, driven by the $13,293m special dividend paid at the start of the first year (Model!B15).' The current Outputs!B21 title 'Year of the lowest headroom, base' = 2027 does not tell the reader why.

issue: Three checks pass (closing cash ties to flows; grid centre = closing cash less interest; downside closing cash is not above the base) but nothing checks that the downside headroom is disclosed as negative, nor that the special dividend is tested against the floor. MasterCheck returns OK while Model!B36 = -1,460.41. The check family is too narrow relative to the decision.
fix: Add a check: 'Downside headroom over floor' — expect -$1,460m and show as WARNING not OK, or add a second MasterCheck 'MasterCheck with frictions' that fails when downside headroom < 0. A green tick on a file whose downside breaches the floor is misleading.

where: X10 warnings across Model!A12, A18, A19, A27 and Outputs!A4, A17, A20, A21, A22
issue: Nine label-without-unit warnings from the workbook validator: 'Opening shares' (Model!A12), 'Shares retired' (Model!A18), 'Closing shares' (Model!A19, Model!A27), and Outputs row 4, 17, 20, 21, 22. These are cosmetic in isolation but a client reviewer flags mixed-unit files.
fix: Add units to the labels: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)' in Model, and to the affected Outputs rows suffix '(m)', '($m)', '(x)' as applicable. Leave 'Funded without new debt?' as a Yes/No label with no unit.

where: Inputs header, [Cash returned] regular dividend growth per year [dps_growth] = 6.1%
issue: The 6.1% DPS growth is derived from the step of the current annual $5.88 vs. FY2026 declared $5.54 — that is a single-year step, not a growth policy. It is sourced and ranged (3.0%-8.0%), but the label invites the reader to read a one-year step-up as a forecast rate.
fix: Relabel to 'Regular dividend growth per year (from FY2026 declared $5.54 to current $5.88; then held at 6.1%)' so the derivation is on the face of the input, or set the input to a policy rate (5.0%, the mid of the shown 3.0%-8.0%) and remove the $5.88/$5.54 step reference from the growth cell.

issue: The downside holds cash returned constant ('Closing cash, downside (same cash returned, interest...') so it mechanically drives cash to $2,539.59m and headroom to -$1,460.41m. That answers 'can Costco fund today's return plan in a downturn?' but the capital-allocation decision the board faces is 'what do we do about it?' — and no scenario shows the response (slower buyback, trim the special dividend, or new debt). The model poses a question it doesn't let you solve.
fix: Add a third scenario column set on Model rows 31-36: downside revenue/margin/capex from the existing down_* inputs, but flex the response. Add two carved inputs on Inputs: 'Downside: share buyback per year ($m)' (default 0) and 'Downside: special dividend per share ($)' (default 0), and compute downside closing cash as cash+B32+B11+B14'+B15'+B16'. Then on Outputs add one line: 'Downside: years the cash floor is breached, before response' = the count of negative cells in Model!B34:F34, and 'Downside: closing cash, returns paused' = the new ca_down_response_cash_end. Now the page states the trade-off: breach by $1,460m, cured by pausing the buyback (or whatever the numbers show).

issue: Outputs!B22 says the lowest downside headroom is in 2031 — but only $1,460m below the floor at that point. Anyone reading 'lowest year is 2031' will conclude the plan survives four years and breaks on the last. The right conclusion is different: Model!B34 shows the breach starts in 2027 (first forecast year) at $2,856.57m headroom passing through zero early, then recovering. The single lowest-headroom number is the wrong cut of the time series.
fix: On Outputs row 21/22 change the metric from 'year of the lowest headroom' to 'first year the floor is breached'. Replace Outputs!B22 formula with =IFERROR(INDEX($B$7:$F$7,MATCH(TRUE,INDEX('Model'!$B$34:$F$34<0,0),0)),"none") and relabel A22 to 'First year the cash floor is breached, downside'. Keep the minimum as a separate line if useful, but the timing of the breach is what the board needs.

issue: Rows 40-44 compute a mini-grid (revenue growth +/- 2% by investment-plan step) that never surfaces on Outputs and never feeds a named result. It is invisible work on the main model tab: it doesn't appear in KEY OUTPUTS and produces no number a decision-maker reads. Either it's the sensitivity that answers the question, and it needs a page, or it's dead weight on the working tab.
fix: Decide. If it is the sensitivity the board wants, move it to its own tab 'Sensitivities', add an action title, and put the 'good zone / cash floor breached' boundary on Outputs. If it is exploration, delete rows 39-44 from the Model tab and reduce the workbook to the two scenarios that matter.

where: Model!B11, Model!B14 and Model row ids
issue: The engine had to annotate the row labels because they are too long and partly cut: 'Interest income (on opening cash: on average cash', 'Regular dividends (on average shares: buybacks spr', 'Regular dividend per share' column header note. A client cannot read these truncated row headers without a voice-over.
fix: Shorten each label so it fits the column: r11 'Interest income', r14 'Regular dividends', r15 'Special dividend', and move the explanatory phrase ('on opening cash', 'on average shares') into a cell comment or a footnote row under the grid. Do this for every label that is currently truncated on the Model tab.

issue: Opening cash in the first forecast year is hard-linked to the cash input (B10 =cash) while later years roll (F10 =E17). That's correct, but nothing on the Model tab flags it — a reviewer changing Model!B10 breaks the tie to the opening balance on Inputs. Likewise Model!B17 opening-cash formula starts from B10, so the two are coupled without a comment.
fix: Add a note cell above the Model grid or a cell comment on B10: 'Opening cash ties to Inputs!cash (B10 = cash). Do not overwrite.' Keep the formula.

issue: Fifteen unit-less labels flag on the FORGE X10 check ('units missing'). They are the 'Answer' text row and result labels the board actually reads — a unit-less 'Closing shares' or 'Downside: closing cash ($m)' inconsistency signals carelessness on the page that matters.
fix: Add units to every flagged label. Outputs!A4 -> 'Answer'; Outputs!A17 -> 'Funded without new debt? (Yes/No)'; Outputs!A20 -> 'Funded in the downside? (Yes/No)'; Outputs!A21 -> 'Year of the lowest headroom, base (FY)'; Outputs!A22 -> 'Year of the lowest headroom, downside (FY)'; Outputs!A18/A19 already carry '($m)'. Model!A12 -> 'Opening shares (m)', A18 -> 'Shares retired (m)', A19 -> 'Closing shares (m)', A27 -> 'Closing shares (m)'. Reload the Checks tab and confirm MasterCheck (Checks!F3) still reads OK.

issue: The generated answer sentence ('Over the forecast the business generates $56,423m of free cash flow and returns $47,695m to shareholders; cash ends at...') gives the base case only. The driver of the decision is the downside result already computed in the workbook, and it isn't in the sentence the reader sees first.
fix: Append to Outputs!B4: '; in the downside case cash ends at $2,540m (headroom -$1,460m) and the cash floor is breached in 2027 unless the return plan is flexed.' Use only figures already in the workbook.

where: Inputs!min_cash = 4,000 (range 3,000–6,000, source: 'assumption'); Inputs!special_dps = 30 (range 30 to 30, source: Yahoo Finance special cash dividend $30/sh)
issue: The cash floor is the single assumption that drives the entire 'Funded without new debt?' conclusion (Outputs!B17 = 'Yes' on ca_min_headroom = 10,620.25 vs min_cash 4,000), and its source is literally the word 'assumption'. The $30 special dividend is a hard-coded single point with zero range, and $30 x 443.1m = $13,293m at Model!B15, i.e. 42% of all cash returned (31,917.32).
fix: Source min_cash to Costco's stated minimum operating cash / revolver covenant (10-K liquidity discussion) and show the floor as a range 3,000–6,000 with the conclusion sensitivity to it; state the $30 special as an announced event with its filing/8-K reference and add a range or '0 if not declared' toggle, since removing it changes the answer from funded to funded-by-a-hair.

issue: Three of the four real drivers are labelled 'assumption' or traced to a 3-year historical CAGR (F19 FY2026 three-year capex CAGR 14.2%) rather than to a driver or guidance. Rev growth 6.0% has no tie to compstore sales, membership fee changes, new-club openings or FX; the capex growth 8.0% sits below the 14.2% historical CAGR and below nothing in the material explains the deceleration.
fix: Rebuild rev_growth from comp-store sales (10-K disclosure) x new-club unit growth + membership fee step-up, with the FY2027 guidance range as the bound. Replace capex_growth with a maintenance-plus-growth build from club openings and remodels. Each driver gets a filing citation and a stated range, not a single point.

issue: The downside case never suspends the buyback in any year (ca_down_suspended = 0, lowest downside headroom 7,609.29 > 0), so the 'downside' is not a downside: it does not test the mechanism it was built to test. The downside only flexes revenue growth, margin and capex, and still clears the floor every year even at the low end of the grid (ca_grid_low 31,671.82).
fix: Extend the downside grid to where headroom actually goes negative (e.g. down_growth 0%–2% combined with capex_overrun 20% and a T-bill yield cut to 2%), and report the year the buyback suspends in the Outputs. If it still does not suspend, delete the suspends-flag row and say so.

where: Model!B15 = -special_dps*B12 = -13,293 funded at the start of year 1; Model!B11 = B10*cash_yield = 832.65
issue: The $30 special is paid from opening cash at t=0 (B12 = 443.1m shares, no discount for the ex-date) and the interest income row earns 4.1% on opening cash that is immediately spent. B11 = 832.65 assumes the cash is still there all year. Interest is overstated in FY2027 by roughly 30 x 443.1 x 4.1% ≈ $545m.
fix: Pay the special from an average-balance basis or move it to end of FY2027; recompute B11 as cash_yield x AVERAGE(opening cash, closing cash), consistent with the dividend row which already uses AVERAGE(B12,B19).

issue: Buyback is modelled as a fixed $800m and the share price is pinned at the current $1,106.21 for five years (range 850–1,106.21, no growth). Shares retired are 0.72m/yr, so closing shares 439.48m barely move (443.1 → 439.48) while the $4B reauthorization to January 2030 (F39) implies a materially different pace. The $800m is also below the FY2026 actual $848m (F9) with no rationale in the material.
fix: Model buybacks as $/year drawn against the $4B authorization, and either grow share_price with an explicit assumption or show the share count under the authorization being fully used; reconcile 443.1 − cumulative retired to the closing 439.48 in the Checks tab.

where: Inputs!ocf_margin = 5.2% (range 4.7%–5.5%) traced to FY2026 actual 5.22%; Inputs!cash_yield = 4.1% (range 4.1%–4.1%)
issue: OCF margin is a single historical point held flat for five years with a range that is never run through a sensitivity; cash_yield is a single-point 4.1% with no range at all (range column shows 4.1% to 4.1%), despite being applied to opening cash that grows to 40,079.64 by FY2030 (Model!F10) and generating 5,283.48 of interest income cumulatively.
fix: Add both drivers to the sensitivity grid on Model!B42:F46 (currently only rev growth and capex are flexed); state cash_yield's range (e.g. 2.5%–4.5% from the F24 13-week T-bill series) and show the effect on ca_min_headroom.

issue: The grid on Model!B42:F46 is a closed-form cash+revenue*ocf_margin calc that does not include the special dividend, buyback or dividends; it is not the same engine as B17. The min/max differ from ca_cash_end (49,999.26), so the 'outputs' on Outputs!B22:B23 do not reconcile to the base case in the grid the reader is shown.
fix: Replace the grid formulas with a re-run of the Model rows B8:F17 (including special, dividends and buyback) or label the grid explicitly as 'cash excluding shareholder returns'; reconcile each corner of the grid to the corresponding line in Model.

where: Model!A12 'Opening shares' 443.1m; Model!B14 dividend uses AVERAGE(B12,B19); Model!B18 buyback uses closing shares
issue: Share count handling is inconsistent: dividends are on average shares, buyback is on closing shares minus a same-period retirement, and there is no diluted share count or treatment of the FY2026 buyback already executed. The 443.1m is described as 'shares outstanding at 2026-09-29' (F1), not diluted.
fix: Build one share rollforward with opening, issues, retirements and closing, use it consistently for both dividends and buybacks, and use diluted shares for any per-share output; tie FY2026 opening to the F1 10-K count.

where: Model rows 12, 18, 19, 27 and Outputs rows 4, 17, 20, 24, 25 (X10 warnings)
issue: Nine unit labels missing: 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares' x2, 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?', 'Year of the lowest headroom' x2. A committee reader cannot tell shares in millions from dollars in millions from a year index without the label.
fix: Add units to each: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)', 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt? (Y/N)', 'Year of lowest headroom (FY)'.

where: Inputs header row 3 'All assumptions and raw data. Blue cells are the only cells to change.'
issue: Fourteen of the assumptions have a source of 'assumption' or a single-point range; the reader cannot tell which the model actually depends on.
fix: Tag each assumption cell as Sourced / Guidance / Assumption, and list the top three by impact on ca_min_headroom at the top of the Inputs tab.

issue: The scenario grid is built on base-case growth and capex only: formula is 'cash+revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(ABS((1+rev_growth+$A42)...)' and never touches down_growth, down_margin_cut or capex_overrun. The downside case (Model r31:r38) is a single fixed scenario, not a grid. A committee will ask 'what if growth is weak AND capex overruns at the same time' and the file has no answer.
fix: Rebuild the grid so the row driver uses down_growth and down_margin_cut and the column driver uses capex_overrun (or add a second 5x5 grid keyed to the downside inputs, reported at Outputs!B22:B23). Keep the base grid; add the downside grid. Re-point ca_grid_low / ca_grid_high or add ca_down_grid_low / ca_down_grid_high and surface both on Outputs.

issue: Two of the inputs that drive the answer are labelled 'assumption' with no source: min_cash = 4,000 with range 3,000 to 6,000, and dps_growth = 6.0% with range 4.0% to 8.0%. The $4.0B cash floor is what makes the headline 'Funded without new debt? Yes' true — it is not a free parameter.
fix: Source min_cash to Costco's disclosed minimum operating cash or treasury policy (10-K MD&A liquidity section); if Costco does not disclose one, say so explicitly in the source cell and note the analyst's rationale. Source dps_growth to the 10-K dividend history or the board's stated payout policy.

issue: Outputs!B4 answer text ends '...cash ends at $50.0B' against a 4,000 floor without saying what the floor is, and B17 'Funded without new debt?' / B20 'Funded in the downside?' answer Yes/No with no margin. A reader cannot see how close the call is.
fix: Reword Outputs!B4 to include the cushion: 'cash ends at $49,999m, $45,999m above the $4,000m floor'. Append the headroom to B17 ('Yes — $10,620m above floor') and B20 ('Yes — $7,609m above floor'). Numbers are already in the file (Model!B20, B24, B35, B38).

where: Outputs!A21 'Downside: years the buyback is suspended'
issue: It reads 0 but with no context a reader cannot tell whether that is good news or evidence the trigger never fires.
fix: Change the label to 'Downside: years the buyback is suspended (buyback tripped by floor test)' and add a footnote next to B21: 'Trigger tested each year in Model r33; not triggered in FY27-FY31 downside.'

issue: Forge X10 flags nine labels without units: 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares' (twice), 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?', 'Year of the lowest headroom, base', 'Year of the lowest headroom, downside'.
fix: Append units: Model A12 'Opening shares (m)', A18 'Shares retired (m)', A19 'Closing shares (m)', A27 'Closing shares (m)'; Outputs A4 'Answer (text)', A17/A20 'Funded without new debt? (Yes/No)', A24/A25 'Year of the lowest headroom (FY)'. Rerun validate_xlsx.

where: Model row 11 label vs row 11 formula
issue: Label says 'Interest income (on opening cash' but the formula uses opening cash in every year (B11 = B10*cash_yield, F11 = F10*cash_yield). Consistency is fine, but the truncated label is misleading if a reviewer skims.
fix: Shorten to 'Interest income (on opening cash balance)' and widen the column. Do not change the formula.

issue: The sensitivity grid is not built off the model. Row 42 formula reads '=cash+revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(ABS((1+rev_growth+$A42...' — it recomputes cash from cash + revenue_base*ocf_margin with an IF/ABS switch, not from the Model's own flows (rows 5-17). Grid low/high (B48=31,671.82, B49=58,048.82) therefore do not tie to ca_cash_end (49,999.26) by construction; the centre of the grid cannot be reconciled to the base case on the face of the workbook. This is the single biggest thing a committee will pull.
fix: Rebuild rows 42-46 as a proper data table (or INDEX/MATCH on a delta-recalc of rows 5-17) so the centre cell equals ca_cash_end = 49,999.26 and each row/column is the base case flexed by ca_g_step and ca_c_step.

issue: These three drive 31,917 of 'cash returned' and 5,283 of interest income, and they are the weakest-sourced inputs in the book: special_dps rests on 'F38 Yahoo Finance 2026-11-11' with no filing or company confirmation; buyback = 800 has a stated range of 0 to 1,000 with no stated basis for 800 versus any other point in that range; cash_yield = 4.1% is sourced to a 13-week T-bill (F24) but is applied to all five years flat — the range shown is 2.5% to 4.5% and the model takes the top of the range for the full period.
fix: Cite the Costco press release or 8-K for the $30 special dividend (or replace with the disclosed figure); set buyback to the run-rate implied by the $4B authorization divided by its stated useful life, and show that arithmetic in the source cell; split cash_yield into a near-term rate tied to the T-bill and a long-run rate at the lower end of the stated range.

issue: The downside revenue growth value (3.0%) sits OUTSIDE its own stated range (0.0% to 2.0%). Either the value cell or the range cell is wrong; as written, the downside case is not the stated downside. A committee will catch this on the first read of the assumption book.
fix: Reconcile the value and range: either set down_growth to a value inside 0.0%-2.0% or restate the range. Whichever is the intended downside, the other cell must move.

issue: min_cash is labelled 'assumption - Costco does not disclose a minimum operating cash or treasury floor in the FY2026 10-K' with a 3,000-6,000 range and no anchor: $4,000 is presented with no bridge to working capital, rent, or seasonal peak. dps_growth = 6.0% is sourced to two data points (FY2026 $5.54, quarterly raised to $1.47) with no stated policy or payout linkage, despite Costco's pattern of periodic specials making the regular/special split the actual decision variable.
fix: Anchor min_cash to a disclosed or derivable figure (e.g., seasonal peak working capital or one quarter of opex) and state it; replace dps_growth with a payout-ratio or 'regular dividend grows with EPS, specials declared opportunistically' driver, and put the dollar consequence in the source cell.

issue: Row 11 is labelled 'Interest income (on opening cash' but the formula '=B10*cash_yield' uses opening cash; row 14 uses AVERAGE(B12,B19) for average shares. Interest is thus credited on the opening balance even though dividends, buyback and capex move cash during the year — a systematic overstatement of interest income of roughly half a period's flows each year, compounding to part of the 5,283 total.
fix: Either rename row 11 to state 'on opening cash' clearly and accept the convention, or switch to average cash (AVERAGE(Opening, Closing)) consistent with the share treatment. State the convention in a cell comment either way.

issue: The downside block references the base-case interest row (Model!B11:F11) and base-case dividends/share rows (B14:F14, B15:F15) rather than downside-consistent values — 'Closing cash, downside (dividends kept, buyback su...' confirms the intent, but interest is credited on base-case opening cash while the downside has different cash. The downside closing cash (ca_down_cash_end = 27,969.04) therefore mixes base-case interest with downside operations.
fix: Either recompute interest on the downside opening cash within the downside block, or add an explicit note on the row stating that interest is held at the base case for comparability — but make the choice visible in the sheet, not inferred.

issue: The special dividend is 13,293 in year one (=30 * 443.1 opening shares) and then zero for the remaining four years, but the workbook treats the total cash returned (ca_uses_total = 31,917.32) as a five-year capital-allocation plan without flagging that 42% of it is a one-off. A reader comparing years sees an irregular line that the summary 'Cash returned, all years' (Outputs!B13) buries.
fix: Split Outputs!B13 into 'Regular dividends', 'Special dividend (one-off, 2027)', and 'Buybacks' with subtotals, and state on the Outputs tab that the special is a single-year item.

issue: Both 'Year of the lowest headroom, base' and 'Year of the lowest headroom, downside' return 2027. In the base case, the low is the first forecast year (B20 = 10,620.25) even though cash rises every year after — which means the answer to 'is the plan funded?' depends entirely on the starting-year cash before any forecast dynamics occur. That is a starting-balance statement, not a forecast result, and should be labelled as such.
