issue: Labels 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares', 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?', 'Year of the lowest headroom' carry no unit (X10 warnings). A reader cannot tell if 'Closing shares (m)' is millions of shares or dollars.
fix: Add units to each label: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)' on Model A12/A18/A19/A27; 'Answer (summary)', 'Funded without new debt? (Y/N)', 'Funded in the downside? (Y/N)', 'Year of the lowest headroom, base (FY)' on Outputs A4/A17/A20/A25/A26.

issue: The downside does not stress anything. Buyback suspended 0 years, special dividend deferred $0, and headroom only falls from 20,895 to 15,888. The deferral and suspension logic in rows 33-34 never fires. A committee reads that as 'the downside is the base case with a smaller number' and discounts the whole scenario section.
fix: Calibrate the downside so it actually bites: push down_growth toward the low end of its range (toward 0%), widen down_margin_cut, and raise capex_overrun until the closing-cash-downside row breaches the floor in at least one year so the suspension/deferral logic demonstrably triggers. If the answer is 'even the downside stays funded,' say so explicitly in the Outputs answer line.

issue: The grid (ca_grid_low=50,875.87, ca_grid_high=77,530.33) is a cash-only sensitivity: the formula 'cash + revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(...)' computes closing cash from one year's operating cash flow and does not roll the five-year FCF, dividend or capex path. It will not tie to the Model tab's actual closing cash, so a reviewer who reconciles the grid to B23 will find two different worlds.
fix: Rebuild the grid to run the same five-year roll-forward as the Model tab (revenue growth and capex growth as the two axes) so each cell equals the corresponding Model!F17 outcome. Re-label Outputs!A23 to state what the grid actually varies, e.g. 'Closing cash 2031 ($m) across revenue growth +/-2pp and capex growth +/-10pp'.

issue: Nine labels carry no unit: 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares', 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?', 'Year of the lowest headroom, base/downside'. A diligence reviewer hunting a $m vs $ error will trip on these.
fix: Add units to each: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)'. For the yes/no and year rows, drop the unit requirement wording and instead append the basis, e.g. 'Funded without new debt? (Yes/No)' and 'Year of the lowest headroom (fiscal year)'.

issue: The answer at Outputs!B4 is a long concatenated sentence that runs off the cell ('Over the forecast the business generates $62,178m of free cash flow and returns $18,336m to shareholders; cash ends a...'). On the Cover, the reader gets a title, not the answer.
fix: Put the answer as a single short claim at the top of Outputs and mirror it on the Cover, e.g. 'Five-year FCF $62.2bn fully funds $18.3bn of returns; cash ends at $72.7bn vs a $6.4bn floor.' Break the long string into labelled lines (FCF, returns, closing cash, lowest headroom, downside verdict).

where: Outputs!A18 vs Outputs!A19 (Downside: closing cash $37,366m; Downside: lowest headroom $15,888m)
issue: Two different 'downside' numbers sit adjacent with no label stating one is end-of-period and the other is the minimum across the period. The lowest headroom ($15,888m) occurs in 2027 per Outputs!B25/B26, but the closing-cash row shows 2031. Readers will reconcile the wrong pair.
fix: Re-label: 'Downside: closing cash, 2031 ($m)' and 'Downside: lowest headroom over the floor, any year ($m)' and add the year inline, e.g. '...lowest headroom, any year (2027)'.

where: Inputs (5 cells): capex_base (7,500), cash (20,210), shares (443.1), share_price (1,106.21), dps (5.88), special_dps (0), dps_growth (5.0%)
issue: Seven named inputs have a source URL but no range, no rationale, and in some cases no unit. capex_base 7,500 has no range and no explanation of why the first forecast year is the anchor vs. FY26 actual capex; share_price 1,106.21 is a point-in-time quote with no date; special_dps 0 is set to zero on a Yahoo Finance article that talks about a record special dividend — the source contradicts the value.
fix: Add a range and a one-line rationale to each. capex_base: show the FY26 actual capex and the FY26 10-K capex guidance, set the range at actual to guidance, source both. share_price: add the quote date as of which 1,106.21 held and a sensitivity to a +/-25% move. special_dps: either set it to a non-zero number drawn from the article cited (state the figure from that article) or change the source to the company's stated dividend policy and write 'no special dividend assumed; the 2024 special was a one-off'.

where: Model row 11 interest income and row 14 dividends
issue: Interest is computed on average cash and dividends on average shares — fine—but the formula AVERAGE(B10+B15,B10+B15+B8+B14+B16) is a hand-rolled mid-period average that assumes cash accumulates linearly through the year. That is a convention, not a sourced assumption. If cash is lumpy (special dividend, big buyback), the average is wrong by up to half the flows. There's no note explaining it.
fix: Either switch to explicit beginning-of-year cash x cash_yield (simpler, defensible) or keep the average and add a note in Inputs: 'Interest earned on average cash; assumes flows accrue evenly. Actual cash balances are sourced from the 10-K and the convention is tested in the sensitivity grid.' Do not leave a convention unexplained in a model the board will ask about.

issue: Downside closing cash -7,461 and lowest headroom -13,891 are computed, but Outputs!B21 says 'years the buyback is suspended: 3' and puts the suspension in years with buyback=0 — the check is COUNTIFS(B34:F34,0,B16:F16,"<>0"), which counts cells where the downside buyback is 0 because the base was also 0, not only because the floor was breached. If the base buyback is 0 in some year (it isn't here, 848 across all years), the count would be wrong. The number 3 happens to be right, but the formula isn't.
fix: Change Model!B38 to =SUMPRODUCT((B34:F34=0)*(B16:F16<>0)) so the count is conditional on the base buyback being non-zero, and add a check on Checks: 'Downside suspensions = number of years closing cash < min_cash in the downside path'.

issue: The downside case assumes zero revenue growth, a 3.0% margin cut and 35% capex overrun — none of these have a range, and the three are correlated (a recession would hit all three at once). There's no rationale for why 3% margin cut and 35% capex overrun, no comparator (e.g., what happened in 2008-09 or 2020), and no probability attached. A committee will ask 'why not 5% margin cut and 50% overrun?' and the model has no answer.
fix: Source each: cite 2008-09 or FY2020 actual Costco revenue growth, OCF margin and capex as the recession benchmark, then set the downside at or below the worst of those. Add a line in Inputs: 'Downside calibrated to FY2020 (COVID) and FY2009 (GFC) actuals; see source.' Attach a probability (e.g. '20% weight') in Outputs.

where: Outputs row 4 'Answer' cell (B4) and Outputs row 17 'Funded without new debt?'
issue: The answer text says 'Over the forecast the business generates $59,831m of free cash flow and returns $18,572m to shareholders; cash ends at $69,954m' — that is a sentence, and it is the only place the answer appears. There is no NOPAT/ROIC, no return on buybacks, no statement of what the answer is on the central question: is capital being allocated well? The sentence reports totals, but does not say whether that is good or bad.
fix: Add a slide title and a bullet in Outputs: 'Base case: $59,831m FCF, $18,572m returned, $69,954m cash at FY31 — $63,524m above the floor.' Then next bullet: 'That is excess cash, not capital allocation: 69% of FCF is not being deployed.' Set the two numbers against the cash floor so the committee sees the pile, not just the total.

where: Checks!F3 MasterCheck and Checks tab (3 checks only)
issue: Only three checks: closing cash ties, grid centre = closing cash less interest, downside closing cash ≤ base. No balance sheet check (no balance sheet in the model — fine for a cash flow model), no check that shares are consistent (Model!B19 = B12-B18 and B27 = F19), no check that the grid uses rev_growth and capex_growth as advertised. The MasterCheck is 'OK' trivially.
fix: Add: 'Closing shares = opening less retired, each year' (=B12-B18-B19, difference 0); 'Grid low ≤ base closing cash ≤ grid high' (=IF(AND(B50<=ca_cash_end,ca_cash_end<=B51),"OK","FAIL")); 'Downside buyback suspensions consistent with base buyback policy'. MasterCheck = IF(COUNTIF of all checks, "OK") so it is a real aggregate.

where: Inputs row 3, Model rows 12, 18, 19, 27, Outputs rows 4, 17, 20, 25, 26
issue: X10 warns on nine labels missing units: 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares' (twice), 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?', 'Year of the lowest headroom' (twice). A client reading 'Closing shares 439.27' does not know if that is thousands or millions until they trace the input.
fix: Append the unit to each label: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)' (both rows), 'Year' for the year rows, and rewrite 'Funded without new debt?' as 'Funded without new debt? (Yes/No)'. Then re-run the validation and clear the warnings.

issue: Row 5 forecast revenue formula B5 = revenue_base*(1+rev_growth) = 326,795.7 uses rev_growth 7.8% from the first forecast year. Row 31 downside B31 = 303,150 uses down_growth 0.0%. The downside therefore grows revenue at 0%, but the actual implied 5-year CAGR differs (base ~7.8%, down ~0%). No reconciliation note telling the reader whether the downside is a CAGR or a single-year step. It is a single-year step repeated — but the label 'per year' is right and the reader has to infer it.
fix: Add a line beneath each: 'Base revenue CAGR FY27-FY31: 7.8%; downside revenue CAGR: 0.0%.' Two cells (per year and the CAGR) tie to the source rows and end the ambiguity.

issue: The model has no recommendation and no decision framed. It reports 'generates $59,831m FCF, returns $18,572m, cash ends at $69,954m' and a downside where buybacks are suspended 3 years and cash ends at -$7,461m. That is the central fact an IC needs: on the company's own policy (cash floor $6,430m, buyback $848m/yr, dividend growing 5%/yr), the base case piles up cash the company has not decided how to use, while the downside breaks the floor. There is no recommendation on capital allocation, and no tie to the equity/valuation story. For a capital allocation model going to an IC, that is the question it must answer.
fix: Write the recommendation at the top of Outputs: 'Base case: $63.5bn of cash above the floor by FY31 — the board must decide now: (a) raise the dividend, (b) raise the buyback, or (c) hold the cash as optionality. The downside case (-$7.5bn cash, buyback suspended 3yrs) argues for holding more cash than the current floor implies, so at minimum the floor should be raised to 1x capex.' Then tie it: the model already shows 'lowest headroom over the floor $20,841m' base vs '-$13,891m' downside, so the spread is $34.7bn of idle capital through the cycle. State that number.

issue: The downside answer reads 'No: in the downside cash falls below the floor' and Outputs!B18 shows closing cash of -7,461 and B19 lowest headroom -13,891 — but nothing on the Outputs tab says what the board should DO about it. The reader sees a negative number and panic; the model doesn't tell them the buyback is suspended 3 years (Outputs!B21) or that the special dividend is already zero (Outputs!B22). That is the decision.
fix: Add a line under Outputs!B20 that quantifies the mitigation: 'In the downside, 3 years of buyback are suspended; regular dividends go from $2,603m in 2027 to $3,142m in 2031 — headroom is negative $13,891m at the trough even after that.' Pull the numbers already in Outputs!B21 and Model!B14/F14.

issue: The downside is a flat-revenue, 3pp margin cut, 35% capex overrun case. There is no recession/revenue-decline scenario, and 0.0% growth is a benign 'flat' case, not a downside. A board asks: what if revenue falls 5%? The input range allows -5.0% but the workbook never runs it.
fix: Add a second downside column (or a sensitivity row) with down_growth = -5.0% and hold margin_cut at 3%. Label it 'Severe downside: revenue down 5%/yr'. Report closing cash and lowest headroom for it. The input range already permits -5.0%.

issue: The Outputs tab is a label-with-value list, not a decision page. The one-line 'Answer' (B4) is buried under rowwise outputs and there is no title stating the conclusion, no visual ordering of base vs downside, and no 'what changes the answer' block. A client needs a voice-over to read it.
fix: Put a claim title at the top of Outputs (e.g., 'Base case funds itself with $20.8B of headroom; a flat-revenue downside breaks the floor in 2031 and suspends the buyback for 3 years'), then group base case (B8–B17) above downside (B18–B26), and add a three-row 'what would flip the answer' block citing the grid range ca_grid_low = 47,830 to ca_grid_high = 75,409.

where: Model!A12, A18, A19, A27 and Outputs!A4, A17, A20, A25, A26
issue: Unit-check warnings X10: labels like 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares', 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Year of the lowest headroom' carry no unit. 'Answer' and 'Funded without new debt?' are free text, so the rule misfires — but 'Opening shares' / 'Closing shares' genuinely need '(m)'.
fix: Add units: Model!A12 'Opening shares (m)', A18 'Shares retired (m)', A19 and A27 'Closing shares (m)'; Outputs!A16 'Closing shares (m)', Outputs!A25/A26 'Year of the lowest headroom (fiscal year)'. For the text cells (Outputs!A4, A17, A20), rename to signal type: 'Answer (text)', 'Funded without new debt? (text)'.

issue: Model!B24 'Lowest headroom over the floor' = 20,841 — which is the FIRST year (2027), because headroom only grows. Outputs!B25 confirms the lowest headroom year is 2027. So the headline base-case number is the year-one number, not a trough. That reads as less impressive than it is and looks like the model isn't testing the later years.
fix: Either relabel B24 'Minimum headroom (2027, year 1)' or add a line showing headroom in the final year (Model!F20 = 63,524) so the reader sees the base case improves. The current number is correct, just misleadingly named.

issue: Topic label, not a claim. Same on Cover.
fix: Replace Outputs!A1 with the one-sentence answer and move the model name to a footer.

issue: The special dividend is mathematically deferred in the downside — every B33:F33 evaluates to 0 because the IF() cash test fails — yet the cell is still labelled 'Special dividend deferred, downside'. No outflow is funded in the downside; the $13,293m quoted is a reclassification of an amount that was never in the downside cash flow.
fix: Relabel Model!B39 to 'Special dividend not paid in downside (never funded)' and add a footnote to Outputs!B22 stating it. If the intent is that the dividend is deferred but still paid in a later year, model the later payment explicitly.

where: Inputs row for capex_overrun [35.0%], source: 'assumption'; Inputs row 'Downside: revenue growth' source: F18
issue: capex_overrun's only source is the word 'assumption'; down_growth's source is F18 (the FY base filing), which cannot be a source for a hypothetical -5.0% down case. Down_margin_cut likewise sourced 'assumption'.
fix: Source the 35% overrun against a peer or historical capex surprise (e.g. a 2022-2023 supply-chain overrun on a specific project) or reduce to a documented 10-15%; source the -5.0% down-growth against a consensus bear case or 2008-09 trough; source the 3.0pp margin cut against Costco or peer peak-to-trough OCF margin.

where: Inputs: capex_base = 7,500 ($m); capex range 6,435 to 7,500; rev_growth = 7.8%
issue: The stated capex range sits BELOW the base case (6,435 to 7,500): the range brackets only downside from base, which biases the model optimistic on the largest cash use. Revenue growth sourced to F18 (the 10-K) rather than guidance/consensus, so the range 5.0%-9.0% is not anchored to a forward source.
fix: Widen the capex range to 6,435 to 8,500 (≥ base, matching the 35% down overrun used in the model) and re-source the upper bound to a guidance or supply-chain filing. Re-source rev_growth to the FY guidance or sell-side consensus with that source URL.

issue: The Outputs page shows 'Downside: years the buyback is suspended = 4' but does not tell the reader that number equals the whole 5-year window minus one year (208 of five years buys no share back). The '—or $848m/yr count' isn't shown alongside the years.
fix: Add a line under Outputs!B21: 'Share buyback suspended in 4 of 5 years; $3,392m of the base-case buyback is not executed.' Use the input $848 multiplied by 4, not a new number.

issue: Cash cover of capex uses the CLOSING cash of that year over that year's capex. In 2027 that gives 1.79× and in 2031 6.36× — a 3.5× lift purely from accumulation, not from improved coverage. This is a loan-to-value style metric whose denominator and numerator are not on a comparable basis; a banker reading it will ask which year's cash and which year's capex.
fix: Redefine to opening cash + FCF over capex (or opening cash over capex) for a consistent test; label the metric 'Closing cash ÷ capex' if you keep it and state the convention in a footnote.

issue: Interest income uses average opening cash (B10+B15) plus flows (B8+B14+B16), but row 15 (special dividend) is a start-of-year outflow included in the base for averaging. The digest does not show a circularity guard, and the same pattern recurs across B11:F11 — no #REF backs out the special dividend timing.
fix: Add a footnote under Model!r11 stating the average-cash convention and confirming no circular reference; if the special dividend is truly at t=0, exclude it from the average and add to the opening balance instead so the average reflects cash actually on hand.

issue: 'Year of the lowest headroom, base' = 2027 contradicts the story: Model!B20 = 7,005 and Model!F20 = 47,289, so the lowest headroom is indeed 2027 — but Outputs!B14 shows closing cash at 53,719 and B15 shows minimum headroom 7,005. The Outputs page presents these as if the trough were late in the window.
fix: Add one line under Outputs!B15: 'Lowest headroom is 2027 ($7,005m, ~3 months of capex run-rate); headroom builds monotonically thereafter.' Makes clear the risk is front-loaded, not back-loaded.

where: Inputs: dps_growth = 5.0%, no stated range; special_dps = 30, no range; cash_yield = 4.1%, range 2.0%-6.0% sourced to ^IRX
issue: dps_growth has no range even though a 5% annual rise over five years compounds to 27.6% — that materially affects cash returned and shares it as an un-ranged point assumption. cash_yield sourced to 13-week T-bill, but the model applies it to five years of cash — a duration mismatch.
fix: Add a range to dps_growth (e.g. 3%-7% anchored to the 10-K dividend history); state in Inputs that cash_yield uses the ^IRX curve and could decay to 2%-3% by 2031 — apply a term structure or flat-line to a sourced rate.

where: Model rows 12, 18, 19, 27 ('Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares'); Outputs rows 4, 17, 20, 25, 26
issue: X10 warnings (9): labels lack units. A reviewer scanning with a ruler cannot tell if 443.1 is shares (m) or a percentage.
fix: Add units to the label text: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)', and to the Outputs labels — 'Answer' becomes 'Answer ($m, shares)' etc. — so the digest warning clears.

issue: The downside model has the two most discretionary uses of cash — the special dividend and the buyback — auto-protected by formula. B33 =IF(cash+B32+B11+B14+B15<min_cash,0,B15); B34 =IF(cash+B32+B11+B14+B33+B16<min_cash,0,B16). This means the downside is defined as 'base business stress with automatic payout protection,' which is not the downside the committee will test. In the real downside the board could cut the special, defer it, or cut it further than the formula allows. The model as written cannot answer the question 'what does the downside look like if the board keeps the regular dividend and cuts everything else?' or 'if it keeps the buyback and cuts the special?'
fix: Split Model rows 33-34 into three labelled scenarios: (a) 'downside, keep all payouts' (B33=B15, B34=B16, no protection), (b) 'downside, defer the special' (B33=0, B34=B16), (c) 'downside, defer the special and suspend the buyback' (B33=0, B34=0). Put the closing cash and lowest headroom for each in Outputs r18-r22 alongside the current single downside. Label row 34 in the base case as 'mandatory minimum buyback, board discretion above'.

issue: The downside is a single scenario with one set of numbers. There is no probability attached, no historical or peer basis cited, and no indication whether -5% revenue is a recession, a consumer slowdown, or a competitive shock. A committee will ask 'how bad is this, how likely, and when does it bite?' The workbook cannot answer because the three downside drivers are labeled 'assumption' with no justification.
fix: Add an Inputs block 'Downside cases' with three labeled columns — 'Mild recession', 'Severe recession', 'Recession + tariff shock' — each with growth, margin cut and capex overrun, and one line each of source/rationale. The recommended-downside column should be stated up front on Outputs.

issue: The answer returns one number for one base case: '$59,860m of free cash flow and returns $31,865m … cash ends a…'. It does not state the decision (should the board approve the special dividend, the buyback pace, and the capital plan?), the downside outcome, or the headroom. The most important fact in the workbook — ca_down_min_headroom = -20,714.36, i.e. the downside breaches the $6,430m floor by $20.7bn — is buried on Outputs!B19 and only described as 'No: in the downside cash falls below the floor'.
fix: Rewrite Outputs!B4 to one sentence that names the decision and the range, e.g.: 'Base case: $59,860m FCF, $31,865m returned, $53,719m closing cash. Downside: cash breaches the $6,430m floor by $20,714m; the board must cut $13,293m of special dividend and suspend the buyback in 4 of 5 years.' Then add a 'Decision' row above it: 'Approve special dividend of $30/share funded from cash and FCF; fund the buyback from FCF; no new debt required in base.'

issue: The 5x5 grid of growth x investment shows only low $34,564m and high $62,146m. It does not show the centre cell, the break-even growth rate, or the minimum growth at which closing cash hits the floor. A committee reading this will ask 'where in the grid does the plan fail?' and the workbook gives no answer. The grid also cross-references row A44 etc. in a way the digest calls out as difficult to follow.
fix: On Outputs, add three cells next to the grid: 'Centre ($m) = [value from Model!D46]', 'Break-even growth at 7.5% capex = [compute]', and 'Minimum investment plan at 7.8% growth that ends above the floor = [compute]'. Label the grid axes on the Outputs tab, not just the Model tab.

issue: The 'Year of the lowest headroom' answer reads '2027' for base and '2031' for downside. That contrast is worth a headline in the summary, but it is not surfaced anywhere. Base case headroom is tightest in year 1 ($7,005m) — i.e. the special dividend is the pinch point, not the later years. Downside headroom is worst at the end — i.e. the buyback pace compounds. Two different stories.
fix: Add the sentence to Outputs!B4 or a new row: 'Base case: headroom is tightest in 2027 ($7,005m) — the special dividend is the near-term constraint. Downside: headroom is worst by 2031 (-$20,714m) — the buyback pace compounds the shortfall.'

issue: Revenue growth of 7.8% into perpetuity is the single biggest driver of $59,860m of FCF, and the cited source is the latest 10-K. The 10-K does not forecast 7.8%; it reports a trailing number. The assumption book should not cite a historical filing to justify a forward growth rate. The 5.0%-9.0% range is a sensitivity band, not a probability distribution, and no rationale is given for 7.8% as central.
fix: Change the source cell on Inputs!rev_growth to a consensus or internal view ('FY27 consensus revenue growth = x%; management long-term plan = y%; central case = 7.8% because z'), or drop to a more defensible central number. State the rationale in one line in the source column.

issue: Nine unit-less labels: 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares' (x2), 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?', 'Year of the lowest headroom' (x2).
fix: Add units to every one: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)', 'Answer ($m, where applicable)', 'Funded without new debt? (Y/N)', 'Year of the lowest headroom (FY)'.

issue: Interest formula is AVERAGE(open cash, open cash + FCF + dividends) * cash_yield — effectively yield on opening cash plus half the year's net flows. The comment in the digest says 'no circularity,' which is correct, but the intra-year timing assumption is not stated. Interest on $40bn of cash at 4.1% is a real number ($1,916m in 2031) and the committee will ask how it is earned.
fix: Add a note under Model!B11: 'Interest earned on average of opening and closing cash, simple average, no intra-year compounding.'

issue: The sensitivity grid is computed on a single-year cash formula, not the full 5-year model: Model!B44 =cash+revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(ABS((1+rev_growth+$A44... — one year of OCF added to opening cash, not the accumulated B8:F8 build that produces the 73,004.3 base. The grid therefore does not tie to ca_cash_end; it understates the range of outcomes and its low/high are not comparable to the base closing cash.
fix: Rebuild rows 44-48 so each grid cell runs the same 5-year cash roll-forward as B17:F17 (revenue path, OCF margin, capex, dividends, interest, buyback) with the row/column growth and capex deltas applied, and reconcile the centre cell to ca_cash_end before re-exporting B50/B51.

issue: The grid is built off a single formula in rows 43-48 while the base model is built in rows 44-48 from a different construct (ca_g_step / ca_c_step, -2*ca_c_step = -20.0% at B43). Two different engines for the same quantity; the digest cannot tell whether the guardrails agree with the master.
fix: If the grid cannot be made a full roll-forward, add a check that the grid centre equals ca_cash_end and link the 'investment plan change' columns to $A44/$A48 (currently $A44 only) so they expand them.

where: Inputs, dps_growth = 0.0% with blank range; dps = 5.88; special_dps = 0; buyback = 0
issue: The distribution assumptions are the whole answer — cash returned of 13,027.14 is 1.0% of 10-K revenue — and two of them (dps_growth, buyback) carry no range and buyback's upper bound is 283 (share price 1,106.21 implies 0.26m shares, or under one tenth of one percent of shares outstanding). The policy is not sourced to the board's stated payout, only to a filing page number with no figure.
fix: Source the payout policy (10-K dividend/repurchase disclosure or the last 8-K declaration) and state a range for dps_growth and buyback consistent with it; if the intent is 'no buyback', say so and justify 0 rather than leave the field blank.

issue: The cash floor is set equal to opening cash (20,210 = cash), so any headroom is positive by construction and Outputs!B15 (ca_min_headroom = 7,633.7) and B17 ('Yes') cannot fail unless the model actively creates a shortfall. The floor has no stated operating rationale (weeks of cost, minimum liquidity, rating covenant).
fix: Derive the floor from a stated driver — e.g. weeks of cost of sales or a rating agency minimum — and set the range independently of the opening balance; re-run the check.

where: Inputs, cash_yield = 4.1% 'US 13-week Treasury bill yield' (^IRX via Yahoo)
issue: A money-market proxy for a forecast to 2031 is stale-sensitive and unsourced to a dated observation; the value 4.1% has no as-of date and the range 2.5%-5.5% is wide. Interest income is 8,791.87 cumulative (Model!B26) — 15% of FCF — so this rate materially moves the answer.
fix: Stamp the rate with an as-of date and source (e.g. the Treasury/FRED series on a stated date), or forecast it from a forward curve; note the interest contribution to the closing cash bridge on the Outputs tab.

issue: There is no cost of capital, no discounting, no return on the retained cash and no hurdle by which a board can compare returning cash today against investing it in capex or buybacks. Every capital-allocation recommendation in the material depends on that comparison; without it the 57,029.56 of FCF and the 13,027.14 returned are arithmetic, not a decision.
fix: Add a cost of equity/WACC assumption (sourced) and a present-value of the buyback/dividend vs reinvested-at-return comparison, or explicitly restate the question as a liquidity question and cut the recommendations that imply return on capital.

where: Inputs, ocf_margin = 5.2% and capex_base = 7,500 (both sourced to same 10-K URL)
issue: Both carry single-point base values with source F2/F7/F49 and F39 — the workbook does not show the historical series behind them, so the committee cannot test whether 5.2% is a mid-cycle margin or a peak. Capex growth range -3.0% to 8.0% on 7,500 is 7,275-8,100, a $825m band against FCF of 57,030.
fix: Put the 5-year historical series for OCF/Revenue and capex in the Inputs tab, tie 5.2% to the trailing average, and widen the capex range to the observed high/low or state the plan behind the 7,500.

where: Forge X10: Model!A12 'Opening shares', A18 'Shares retired', A19/A27 'Closing shares', Outputs!A4 'Answer', A17 'Funded without new debt?', A20 'Funded in the downside?', A25 'Year of the lowest headroom, base', A26 '...downside'
issue: Nine labels carry no unit; the checks engine flags every one.
fix: Append the unit to each: '(m)' for shares, '(Yes/No)' for the funded flags, '(year)' for the headroom-year rows, and replace 'Answer' at Outputs!A4 with a descriptive label carrying its $m unit.

issue: The interest formula averages the opening balance with the opening balance after the special dividend and FCF — i.e. it assumes the FCF arrives at the start of the period and the buyback leaves at the start, which is a mid-year convention applied to one line only. No other line applies a convention.
fix: Apply one stated convention across dividends, buyback and interest (e.g. average balance throughout), or move interest to a separate schedule and footnote the timing.

where: Model!A25 'Cash returned, all years' = -SUM(B14:F16) = -13,027.14, reported positive at Outputs!B13 = 13,027.14
issue: Sign flip between Model (negative, a use of cash) and Outputs (positive). The digest is internally consistent (B25 is negated at B13) but a reader moving between tabs will mis-read the direction.
fix: Keep Model in negative-presented uses and Outputs in positive amounts, but label each explicitly 'use of cash' / 'cash returned' on both tabs.

where: Inputs and Model row 16 'Share buyback' [buyback] = 0; Model row 16 shows B16 = -buyback = 0 across all years
issue: The core capital-allocation decision — how much to return — is not modelled. Buyback is zero and capex is a plug at 7,500 flat, so the only thing the model actually decides is how large the cash balance grows. Outputs!B4 reports '$57,030m of free cash flow and returns $13,027m to shareholders' — 77% of FCF is unexplained. An investment committee reads that as the model avoiding the question.
fix: Add an explicit capital-return plan: set buyback to a stated annual figure (even one figure the board is debating, e.g. the $283m currently the upper range bound), and add a line 'Surplus cash held vs returned' so the reader can see what is being recommended. If the decision is 'hold cash', that is the answer the model must state and defend on Outputs, not left blank.

issue: Three of the four growth drivers are set to zero. A flat-dividend, flat-capex, zero-growth-downside model is not a scenario, it is a base case with the downside dial turned to 'no change' — the downside result (36,792 closing cash, 2,528 headroom) is then a mechanical artefact of one margin cut, not a stress test a board would recognise.
fix: Give each driver a defensible value from the filings already cited. DPS growth should track the dividend history in the F42/F54 source; capex growth should reflect the store-opening plan in F39. In the downside, down_growth = 0.0% while base rev_growth = 6.0% leaves a 6pp swing unexplained — either set it to a recession case (the range says -3.0% to 2.0%) or state on Inputs why flat is the downside.

where: Model!B44:F48, the sensitivity grid 'Lowest closing cash'
issue: The grid flexes growth ±2pp and investment plan ±, but buyback = 0 and dps_growth = 0, so the flexed variable (capex) barely moves the answer: low 51,297, high 77,417 — a range of ~26,000 on a base closing cash of 73,004. The grid is doing work on a lever that is switched off and ignoring the one the board controls.
fix: Rebuild the grid around the decision levers: buyback per year on columns, revenue growth on rows. If a 2x2 is too sparse, keep the current capex grid as a second table and lead with the buyback one. Every cell in the new grid should be labelled with its units and the scenario it represents (e.g. '$0 / $283m buyback').

where: Outputs!A4-B4: 'Answer' = "Over the forecast the business generates $57,030m of free cash flow and returns $13,027m to shareholders; cash ends at..."
issue: The 'answer' is a narration of the mechanics, not a recommendation. It tells the reader what happened, not what to do. A committee chair reading 'funded without new debt? Yes' and 'funded in the downside? Yes' has to assemble the conclusion themselves.
fix: Rewrite B4 as an action claim with the number in it, e.g.: 'Costco can fund the store plan and return $[X]m a year with no new debt; cash still ends 2031 at $73.0bn (base) / $36.8bn (downside).' The number X must come from adding the buyback you introduce above. Add a second line: the one decision the board needs to take.

where: Inputs: [down_growth] = 0.0%, [down_margin_cut] = 1.0%, [capex_overrun] = 15.0%; Model row 32 'Free cash flow, downside'
issue: The downside is a margin haircut with flat revenue and a 15% capex overrun. That is a margin squeeze, not a recession. The question any board turns on is 'what if sales fall and we have already committed the capex?' — the current downside cannot go below zero growth, so it never tests the real risk.
fix: Add a third scenario (severe) with down_growth at the bottom of its stated range (-3.0%), the margin cut at 1.5%, and capex overrun at 20% (all within the existing ranges or state the new range on Inputs). Report closing cash and headroom for base, downside and severe on Outputs rows 15-22 side by side, so the committee sees the tail.

where: Outputs tab (26 rows x 6 cols), all outputs
issue: The answer is on Outputs!B4 as a run-on sentence and the outputs below it are an undifferentiated list of 25 rows: base, downside and grid results are interleaved with no grouping, no headline and no visual. The tab is called 'Summary tables and charts for review' but there is one narrative cell and no priority order.
fix: Restructure Outputs into three blocks with a title on each: (1) 'Recommendation' — the one-line answer and the ask; (2) 'Base case' — FCF, cash returned, closing cash, headroom, in that order; (3) 'Downside and sensitivities' — closing cash, headroom, buyback suspension, and the grid. Put the recommendation block at the top and keep it to four rows.

where: Outputs!A4, A17, A20, A25, A26; Model!A12, A18, A19, A27
issue: The validation run flags nine labels with no unit: 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?', 'Year of the lowest headroom, base/downside', 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares' (x2). They are boolean or year labels so the unit warning is a false positive for some, but shares genuinely need '(m)' and cash figures need '($m)'.
fix: Add units where they are real: Model!A12/A19/A27 -> 'Opening/Closing shares (m)'; Model!A18 -> 'Shares retired (m)'. For the boolean and year labels, they are self-describing; the engine flags them, not the reader — leave or suppress with a note. Do not add '($K)' or '$m' to a Yes/No cell.

where: Model rows 12-19 vs rows 27; Outputs!B16 'Closing shares (m)' = ca_shares_end = 443.1
issue: Closing shares are 443.1 in every year because buyback = 0, so the shares row is constant and carries no information. The reader will assume the share count is a plug and stop reading rows 12-19.
fix: Once you set a buyback, this resolves itself. If buyback stays zero for the base case, delete rows 18-19 from the main block and state 'share count held flat at 443.1m (no buyback)' in a single labelled line so the reader is not misled into thinking the model computes dilution.

issue: Buyback is set to zero, so the base case (Model!B16/F16 = -buyback = 0) never draws cash for repurchases and Outputs!B17 returns 'Yes' for funded-without-new-debt only because the largest discretionary use is switched off. That is not a solvency test, it is an assumption doing the work.
fix: Set buyback to at least the F43 average ($283m per the range given), re-run the base and downside, and update Outputs!B17 and Outputs!B21/B22. If the intent is a zero-buyback scenario, rename the column/flag so the Outputs 'Answer' is explicit that no repurchase is assumed.

where: Model!B11 and Model!F11 'AVERAGE(B10+B15,B10+B15+B8+B14+B16)*cash_yield' — and the same pattern in B33/B34 and F33/F34
issue: Interest is computed on ending cash that already depends on interest (Model!B17 = B10+B8+B11+B14+B15+B16 includes B11). That is a circular reference that LibreOffice resolves by iteration; Excel may flag it and a client will. It also makes the downside IF() tests in B33/B34 depend on a value that includes the very item being tested.
fix: Break the circularity: use opening cash for interest (drop the +B11 term), or add an explicit switch/copy-paste-values for the interest line, and add a Checks row showing that interest on the cash balance is non-circular. Document the chosen convention on Cover.

issue: The grid's 'investment plan change' column variable appears to scale the final-year cash formula, but B43 = -2*ca_c_step = -20.0% while the inputs carry no named cell ca_c_step that matches 'investment plan change'; the column moves -20% to +20% and the underlying driver is opaque. The B50/B51 outputs (ca_grid_low 45,889.73, ca_grid_high 73,259.42) therefore cannot be reconciled without reading the raw formula, and the cell isn't documented.
fix: Add ca_c_step (and ca_g_step) as named, sourced inputs on the Inputs tab with explicit units. Rewrite the row 44-48 formula to reference the grid-axis cells only (no embedded constants), and add a Checks cell showing the grid centre equals the base closing cash (Checks! shows 'grid centre = closing cash less interest'; make that the documented cross-check).

issue: The 'Answer' narrative ($53,907m FCF, $14,687m returned, cash ends at $67,923m) is a cash-flow solvency answer, not a capital allocation recommendation, and there is no equity bridge: no net debt, no minorities, no per-share value / total shareholder return, no diluted share reconciliation (Model!B12/B19 shares are 443.1 with zero retirement — no dilution). A committee asked to allocate capital will ask what the alternative is worth and what the return is.
fix: Add an Outputs row computing TSR decomposition (dividends + change in shares × share price + ending cash surplus over floor) in dollars and per diluted share, tying to Model!B27 = 443.1. If no buyback is assumed, say so explicitly in Outputs!B17 and B4, and mark the answer as a liquidity test, not a capital-allocation recommendation.

where: Inputs 'Capex growth per year' range -3.0% to 10.0%, and 'Revenue growth per year' range 3.0% to 7.8%
issue: Bands are given but no sensitivity to OCF margin (4.2% to 5.7%), cash yield (2.5% to 5.5%) or dps growth (0.0% to 13.1%) is run. Only growth (±2pp) and capex are flexed; the free-cash-flow answer depends at least as much on OCF margin, which is the input that drives the entire FCF line (Model row 6 = revenue × ocf_margin).
fix: Add a second sensitivity table flexing ocf_margin (±1pp) against rev_growth (±2pp), and report the min/max closing cash and headroom alongside Outputs!B23/B24. Keep the same 'no cash below floor' test in each cell.

where: Inputs cells with no range or no source: revenue_base, capex_base, cash, shares, share_price, dps, special_dps, buyback
issue: Several inputs carry only a single-point source: e.g. buyback = 0 with source 'F9, F43' — if F43 shows a $283m range, a zero input is inconsistent with that source unless F9 shows zero repurchases. Also 'share_price 1,106.21' is sourced to a live Yahoo URL (F21), which is a point-in-time snapshot and will not reproduce.
fix: For each zero or point-valued input, add the periodicity and the date (e.g. 'Buyback FY2026 = $0 per F9; historical F43 range $0–$283m'). Replace the Yahoo URL with either the 10-K cover price or a dated internal price deck, and state the as-of date.

issue: Nine labels carry no unit: 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares', 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Funded in the downside?', 'Year of the lowest headroom'. A committee reading Outputs cannot tell whether 'Answer' is $m, and 'Year of the lowest headroom' reads as a number. Also Model!B27/F27 'Closing shares' = 443.1 is a share count, not a dollar line, and the label doesn't say (m).
fix: Add units: shares in '(m)', dollar rows in '($m)', years in '(FY)', and text answers as 'Yes/No'. Fix Model!B14 to reference the average-share convention explicitly ('Regular dividends ($m, on average shares)') since it averages B12:B19 and a reviewer will check that against the dps line.

issue: Your downside is a revenue contraction of -3% with a 1pp margin cut and 15% capex overrun, and it still shows 'Funded in the downside? Yes' with $11.3B of headroom (Outputs!B19) and zero buyback suspension (Outputs!B21). That is not a downside, that is a mild wobble. No committee believes Costco's worst case is -3% revenue when the model's own input range for down_growth runs to -5.0%. The scenario the board would actually lose sleep over is flat-to-negative comps plus the dividend commitment and the buyback still running.
fix: Rebuild the downside on the decision's real question: set Inputs!down_growth to the bottom of its own stated range (-5.0%), and add a second stress where the buyback is held at a policy level (say the historical run-rate inside the 0-283 range) rather than zero so the model has to show whether the buyback gets cut. Label Outputs!B20 with the specific assumptions that produce the 'Yes' so the reader knows what has to be true for it to hold.

issue: Shares outstanding never move: opening 443.1, closing 443.1 (Model!B19), and the all-years closing shares output is 443.1. That is only true because Inputs!buyback = 0. A capital allocation model whose answer to 'what happens to the capital you return' is a share count that never changes is a plug, not a driver. If the buyback input moves off zero, dividends are computed on average shares (Model r14) and the share retiral (r18) only changes the count by the buyback dollars divided by price — that logic is fine, but with buyback pinned at zero the reader cannot see it work.
fix: Run at least one case at a non-zero buyback inside the stated range (Inputs!buyback range 0 to 283) and show the closing share count and the average-shares dividend mechanic moving. If buyback is genuinely policy zero, say so on Outputs!B16 with a one-line note ('no buyback assumed; shares flat'), otherwise the 443.1 reads as an error.

issue: 'Answer' cell B4 is a text concatenation — 'Over the forecast the business generates $53,907m of free cash flow and returns $14,687m...' — with no unit on the label (X10 warns 'Answer has no unit'). The actual answer to the board's question ('can we fund capex and return cash without new debt?') is buried in B17 and B20 beneath a sentence. The number a reader needs on page one is the Yes/No and the headroom, not a prose string.
fix: Make Outputs!A3 'Can Costco fund capex and returns without new debt? ($m)' and put the verdict and its drivers on the first three visible rows: B3 = Yes/No, B4 = lowest headroom ($m, =ca_min_headroom), B5 = closing cash ($m, =ca_cash_end). Drop the concatenated sentence or move it to a note.

issue: Interest income is $8,493m over the forecast (Model!B26) — that is 16% of your $53,907m free cash flow (Model!B22) — and it is driven by a yield sourced to a Yahoo Finance quote page for a T-bill index. The model averages opening and closing cash balances (Model r11) to earn 4.1% on a stock that swings $20B+ to $68B; a committee will ask who earns 4.1% on average operating cash for five years and whether the yield should step down as short rates normalize.
fix: Replace the yield source with a dated curve or a stated assumption range, and add a sensitivity line so interest income is shown, not buried: e.g. a cell on Outputs giving closing cash at 2.5% and 5.5% yield (the stated input range).

where: Cover tab (18 rows x 3 cols) and workbook navigation
issue: The Cover is a title page. For a capital allocation workbook going to a committee, page one should carry the answer, the question, and the one-way doors. Right now the reader opens the file on 'Costco Capital Allocation and Liquidity Model' — a topic title — and has to find Outputs to learn what the model concludes.
fix: Put the Outputs answer block (verdict + lowest headroom + closing cash) at the top of the Cover, or point the Cover's first row at Outputs!B3 and state the headline: 'Funded without new debt in the base case; headroom $16,793m; the question is the downside.'

where: Model r44-r51, 'Grid: lowest/highest closing cash' (B50 = 45,889.73, B51 = 73,259.42)
issue: Rows 44-48 are a two-way grid that computes closing cash from a one-flush formula — cash + revenue_base * ocf_margin * IF(...). The digest shows the grid formula starts the same way in every column and jumps straight to a level of closing cash, bypassing the year-by-year build that produces the base case $67,923 (Model!B23). A grid that does not reconcile to the model it sits under is a second model. The Checks tab verifies 'grid centre = closing cash less interest' (difference 0), which tells me the grid deliberately excludes interest — but nothing on the grid says so.
fix: Either rebuild the grid to run the same r5-r17 mechanics per cell, or label it explicitly: 'Grid excludes interest income; grid centre equals closing cash less interest income of $8,493m (see Model!B26).' Add a note on the grid rows stating what varies by row (growth) and column (capital investment).

where: Model tabs, X10 warnings on Model!A12 'Opening shares', A18 'Shares retired', A19 'Closing shares', A27 'Closing shares', Outputs!A17 'Funded without new debt?', A20 'Funded in the downside?', A25/A26 'Year of the lowest headroom'
issue: Ten labels have no unit. On a share-count row this matters: 443.1 is a count in millions, not dollars. On the Yes/No rows a unit is meaningless but the engine flagged them, so the file will not pass the house check as submitted.
fix: Add units to the flagged labels — 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)' — and where the label is a qualitative row (Yes/No, year), suppress the unit flag per the validator's convention rather than inventing one.

where: Outputs r23-r24 'Closing cash across growth +/-2pp and investment ...'
issue: The label is truncated mid-sentence and gives no takeaway. The grid's range ($45,890m low to $73,259m high) is the most useful sensitivity in the file and it reads as a table of output with no message.
fix: Write the claim: 'Closing cash stays above the floor across growth ±2pp and investment ±20%: low $45,890m, high $73,259m.' Then cut the surrounding label text to the axis names only.

where: Model row 11, e.g. Model!B11 and Model!F11: '=AVERAGE(B10+B15,B10+B15+B8+B14+B16)*cash_yield'
issue: The interest-income formula averages two values that are identical in structure — (opening cash + special dividend) and that same figure plus FCF, dividends and buyback — which is not a real average of period cash balances and is undocumented. It is a smoothed plug, not a driver, and a committee will read it as such; the 'no circularity' comment in the label papers over the fact that the second half of the average already embeds the flows.
fix: Replace with an explicit average-cash calculation, e.g. interest = cash_yield * AVERAGE(opening cash, closing cash), and add a one-line note in the Inputs tab stating the convention and that it avoids circularity. If circularity is acceptable in this file, turn it on with a documented iteration setting and a separate check that the interest line converges.

where: Inputs, 'Regular dividend growth per year [dps_growth] = 0.0%', range blank, source 'Assumption'
issue: $5.88 dps held flat for five years (Model row 13 propagates 5.88 every year) is itself a major capital-allocation decision — Costco has raised the regular dividend every year — and it is asserted with no range and no rationale. The entire answer ($68.1B closing cash, $53.9B FCF, $14.4B returned) is sensitive to this assumption.
fix: Set a sourced range (e.g. 0% to 8% based on the historical dividend growth in the FY2026 10-K / annual report) and show the base case at a defensible mid-point. Reflect the range in the grid or a sensitivity, and state the rationale in the source column.

issue: The sensitivity grid varies revenue growth and capex only, and shows only closing cash ($46.2B–$73.5B). It does not stress the assumption the answer most depends on: the buyback, the dividend, or the cash floor (min_cash range 15,158–25,263 is in Inputs but never sensitised). 'Lowest headroom over the floor = $7,345.64m' at base and '$1,600.51m' in the downside means the whole question — can the board fund this without debt — turns on the floor, which is held fixed.
fix: Add min_cash as a grid axis (15,158 / 20,210 / 25,263) or add a small table showing closing cash and lowest headroom for each floor level in base and downside. State the sensitivity of the answer to the floor explicitly.

where: Inputs, 'Share buyback per year [buyback] = 283' and 'Special dividend per share [special_dps] = 0'
issue: The buyback is set at $283m/yr with range '0 to 283', i.e. the current year's number is treated as the ceiling and held flat — that is a plug pointing backwards, not a policy. The special dividend is assumed to be $0 forever with no probability or scenario for the board actually declaring one, even though the Outputs tab carries 'Downside: special dividend deferred' = 0 (a check that can never fire at $0).
fix: Source the buyback to an authorisation (remaining $ under the existing programme in the 10-K) and show a policy basis for the run-rate; add a scenario where a special dividend is declared and the buyback is accelerated, and make the deferral line in Model rows 33/39 meaningful by running that scenario.

issue: The downside FCF formula gives Model!F32 = −194.53 (FCF is negative in the final downside year), yet Model row 35 (downside closing cash) still adds the regular dividend and buyback (−2,599 + −283 in that year) and shows closing cash of $22,482m with headroom of $2,272m. Cash cannot fall when FCF is −$195m while $2.9B is paid out unless the opening cash and interest are large enough — they are, per the mechanics — but the model does not show the year in which the floor is breached, only the minimum headroom over five years, and the headline 'Funded in the downside? = Yes' is being made on a path where the final year generates negative FCF.
fix: Add a line in Model rows 35–40 showing closing cash and headroom by year in the downside (it exists for the base in row 20), and show the year in which headroom is lowest (Outputs row 26 already computes 2027). If the downside breaches the floor in any year, the Outputs answer must change from 'Yes'.

where: Outputs row 4 (Answer cell) and whole Outputs tab
issue: There is no valuation content anywhere in the workbook: no WACC, no DCF, no terminal value, no comps, no per-share equity value. The file is titled 'Capital Allocation and Liquidity Model', and the outputs are cash-generation and funding metrics only. If this is intended as a capital-allocation model, the title and the Outputs page should say so; if the committee is being asked whether this policy creates value, the answer cannot be given from this file.
fix: Either (a) retitle the Outputs page 'Capital allocation and liquidity: cash generation and funding capacity' and remove any implication of value, or (b) add a valuation section — cost of equity/capital built up and sourced, DCF with an explicit split of terminal value as a % of EV and an exit-multiple cross-check, and value per share on diluted shares — and tie the recommendation to it.

where: Model!A12, A18, A19, A27; Outputs!A4, A17, A20, A25, A26
issue: Nine X10 warnings on missing units: 'Opening shares', 'Closing shares', 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?', 'Year of the lowest headroom'. Shares (m) and the answer cells (text or year) are unlabelled, and the audit engine flags each one.
fix: Add units to the labels: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Closing shares (m)', 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt? (Y/N)', 'Year of lowest headroom (FY)'.

where: Outputs!B25 / B26, e.g. 'Year of the lowest headroom, base = 2027'
issue: The INDEX/MATCH returns 2027 for both base and downside, but the minimum headroom in the base is 2027 = $7,345.64 and closing cash rises monotonically — so the 'lowest' is the first year by construction, not because 2027 is uniquely stressful. The output is technically correct and analytically uninformative.
fix: Either drop the row or add the headroom figure alongside the year so the committee can see why 2027 is the low point and how much slack there is in later years.

where: Inputs, 'Share price for buybacks = 1,106.21 (Yahoo Finance close on November 13, 2026)' and 'cash_yield = 4.1% (13-week T-bill, November 13, 2026)'
issue: Both market-based inputs are single-day closes. The buyback sensitivity to the price is real ($283m buys 0.256m shares at $1,106; at $900 it buys 0.314m) and the workbook shows only one path.
fix: Use a trailing 20-day or 30-day VWAP for the buyback price, or show the shares-retired line under a ±15% price band, sourced to the same data provider.

where: Model!B44:F48 'Grid: lowest/highest closing cash' and Model!B50/B51
issue: The sensitivity grid (ca_grid_low 46,153 to ca_grid_high 73,523) is computed by a single one-line formula per cell using revenue_base*ocf_margin, not by the actual Model engine — the dividends, buybacks, interest and cash compounding that drive closing cash in rows 8-17 are missing. The base case closing cash is 68,138 but the grid's high corner is 73,523 and the low is 46,153, and the base case is not even a cell in the grid. Two different formulas for the same quantity, only one of which is real. A committee member who checks the grid against the base will find it doesn't reconcile and stop reading.
fix: Rebuild the grid on the same engine as rows 5-17: for each (growth, capex) pair, re-run the five-year cash flow, adding dividends and buyback and interest. Simpler: add a data table from the Model's closing-cash cell, driven by the growth and capex input cells. Or drop the grid and replace it with two explicit sensitivities the engine can compute honestly (e.g., closing cash at rev_growth = 3.0% and 7.8%). Whatever you do, the base case must appear in the grid.

where: Inputs rows 1-25, [Cash returned] block: dps=5.88 with dps_growth=0.0%, special_dps=0, buyback=283
issue: The cash-returned assumptions are frozen, not driven. 5.88 dividend held flat for five years, no special dividend, buyback fixed at 283 a year and reading 283 (a single year's figure) as an annual run rate. Costco has grown the regular dividend and its S&P 500 capital-return record is not a flat 283 a year. The Outputs page says '$14,423m returned to shareholders' — that number is an artifact of a flat assumption, not a management plan. If the committee asks 'why is the payout flat?', there is no answer in the book.
fix: In Inputs, set dps_growth to the historical Costco dividend CAGR (source the 5-year DPS series from the 10-K/annual report, roughly low double digits) and set buyback to the 3-year average annual repurchase, not the single 283. Recheck the Outputs answer string: '$14,423m returned' will change. If the intent is to hold payout constant to isolate the funding question, say so in one line on Inputs and on the Outputs page.

where: Model rows 3-27 vs rows 30-40 vs rows 43-51
issue: Rows 8-17 are the base case; rows 31-40 are the downside; rows 43-51 are the grid. Only rows 8-17 have the opening/closing cash flow logic (B10 = cash, B17 = closure, B21 cash cover). The downside uses a different formula shape in B32 and the grid uses a third shape. The reader has to reverse-engineer three models to see that they answer the same question.
fix: Refactor to one engine driven by a switch cell (case = base/downside) on Inputs, so the driver rows exist once and the columns carry the case. Then Model holds one cash flow block, not three. At minimum, mirror the base-case line structure (revenue, ocf, capex, fcf, cash returned, cash end) exactly in the downside block so a reader can scan rows 5-40 as one table.

where: Outputs!B4 'Answer' string and Outputs!B17/B20 'Funded without new debt?'
issue: The answer string is a run-on that buries the finding, and the two 'Funded...' cells return a bare Yes/No with a text caveat. The real news is asymmetric: base-case closing cash 68,138 against a 20,210 floor; downside closing cash 22,482 against the same floor, i.e. 2,272 of headroom on an 303,150 revenue base. Neither number appears at the top. 'Funded in the downside? Yes' is the headline but reads like a checkbox.
fix: Rewrite Outputs!B4 as two short sentences. First: 'Even on the downside, cash never falls below the board floor — lowest headroom is $1.6B (2027) and closing cash is $22.5B against the $20.2B floor.' Second: 'The base case is not constrained: closing cash is $68.1B, headroom $47.9B.' Move B15 and B19 dollar figures into those sentences. Delete the caveat text from B17/B20 or move it to a note below the table.

where: Outputs rows 4, 17, 20, 25, 26 and Model rows 12, 18, 19, 27 (per X10 warnings)
issue: Six Outputs labels and four Model labels lack units ('Answer', 'Funded...', 'Closing shares', 'Year of the lowest headroom'). A reviewer reading only the Outputs tab cannot tell whether closing shares is a count or a percent, or whether the years are calendar or fiscal.
fix: Retitle: Outputs A16 'Closing shares, end of 2031 (m)'; A25 'Year of the lowest headroom, base (fiscal)'; A26 same for downside; A17/A20 'Funded without new debt? (yes/no)' — the '(yes/no)' is the unit. Model A19/A27 'Closing shares (m)'; A12 'Opening shares (m)'; A18 'Shares retired (m)'.

where: Model row 35 column label 'Closing cash, downside (regular dividends kept; bu...' and Outputs row 18 label truncated similarly
issue: Both the Model row header and the Outputs label are truncated mid-word in the sheet, so the reader cannot see that buybacks are kept in the downside — that is material. The downside case in B38 shows 0 suspended buyback years, so the assumption reads as 'buybacks continue in the downside', but the label doesn't say it cleanly.
fix: Widen the column or shorten the label to 'Closing cash, downside (dividends and buybacks maintained)'. Same fix on Outputs row 18. If the intent is that buybacks are suspended only when the floor is breached, say that in the label, not in the formula.

where: workbook — Inputs, Calc, Outputs each reported as "3 rows x 3 cols"
issue: The workbook is empty in substance: every tab is 3x3, there is no Cover tab, no Checks tab, no assumption book, and no calculation tabs. Rule X12=fail ("No checks sheet. Add one row per integrity check and a master flag on the cover sheet"). Nothing in this file answers a capital allocation question.
fix: Rebuild to the standard B.banker_workbook structure: add a Cover tab carrying a master check flag, an Inputs tab with every driver in one place, a Calc tab with live formulas only, a Checks tab with one row per integrity test, and an Outputs tab that ties to the deck. Populate with Costco (COST) actuals from the latest 10-K/10-Q before any projection work.

where: workbook — "no_formulas : workbook has no live formulas"
issue: Zero live formulas in the entire file. With no formulas there is no tie between inputs, calculations and outputs, no recalc on input change, and no audit trail. Any number shown is a typed constant.
fix: Rebuild the Calc and Outputs tabs so every output cell is a formula referencing the Inputs tab (no typed constants outside Inputs). Re-run validate_xlsx and clear X12 and the no_formulas failure before resubmitting.

issue: No assumption book: no named inputs, no units, no ranges, no sources. Every driver that capital allocation turns on — capex, buyback pace, dividend policy, membership fee economics, ROIC, WACC — is unstated and unsourced.
fix: Create the assumption book with one row per driver: name, value, unit, low/high range, source (filing page, guidance, consensus, peer set), and rationale. Minimum set: revenue growth, membership fee growth, gross margin, SG&A %, capex, D&A, working capital, tax rate, buyback authorization, dividend per share, share count, WACC inputs.

where: workbook — "KEY OUTPUTS (named results, computed values)" is blank
issue: No valuation output of any kind: no WACC build, no DCF, no terminal value or its share of EV, no exit multiple cross-check, no equity bridge, no per-share value, no capital-allocation scenarios. There is nothing to test and nothing to recommend against.
fix: Build the valuation: sourced WACC build-up, explicit forecast DCF with mid-year convention, terminal value with the % of EV it represents shown on the page, exit multiple cross-check, equity bridge (net debt, minorities, diluted shares), and per-share outputs on diluted count. Show the buyback/dividend/capex scenarios each as its own column with the per-share result.

issue: No sensitivities or scenarios can function because there are no formulas and no driver inputs to flex. A committee cannot see what happens if the key assumption is wrong.
fix: Once the model is live, add a sensitivity grid on the Outputs tab flexing the two drivers the answer depends on most (e.g. WACC vs terminal growth, membership fee growth vs buyback pace) and show that the outputs recalculate when inputs change.

issue: Two validation rules (X7, X11) were not run because there is nothing to run them on. The workbook has never been integrity-checked.
fix: After rebuild, run the full validate_xlsx suite and clear every not_run and fail, then confirm the Checks tab master flag reads OK on the Cover tab.

where: workbook — Inputs, Calc, Outputs tabs (each 3 rows x 3 cols)
issue: The workbook is empty. Three tabs of 3x3 cells with no content means the model does not exist; nothing here answers any capital allocation question, and the digest confirms 'no calculation tabs', 'no formulas', 'no assumption book'.
fix: Rebuild the file from the B.banker_workbook structure: a Cover tab with the decision and master check flag, an Inputs/Assumptions tab with one row per driver (name, value, unit, range, source), driver-based Calc tabs (one per business question), and an Outputs tab that leads with the answer. Populate every cell; an empty stub is not a draft.

issue: The workbook has no live formulas (validate_xlsx X12 / no_formulas). Without formulas there are no drivers, no linkage from inputs to outputs, and no way for a client to follow the logic — every number is absent or a hard-coded plug.
fix: Build the calculation chain: every output must trace to Inputs through live formulas with no hard-coded numbers outside the input tabs. If any figure cannot be derived, put it on Inputs with a source. Nothing downstream of a plug.

issue: There are no named results and no computed values. The decision-maker has nothing to read — the answer is not on page one because there is no page one.
fix: Create named cells for the key outputs (e.g. incremental EBITDA, ROIC, payback, NPV by scenario, capital freed) and put them at the top of the Outputs/cover, each with a one-line title that states the claim, not the topic.

issue: No assumption book. A capital allocation model lives or dies on its drivers (capex per new warehouse, sales per warehouse, build cost, ramp, WACC, tax), and none are documented with a value, unit, range or source.
fix: Add an Assumptions tab: one row per driver with name, value, unit, low/high range and a source (10-K, earnings call, internal). Every downstream number must reference these cells. No source, no assumption.

issue: No integrity checks and no master flag on a cover sheet. A committee cannot trust a model with no balance, tie-out or reasonableness checks.
fix: Add a Checks tab with one row per check (inputs reconcile to source, outputs tie to Calc, balance identity holds, no hard-codes outside Inputs) and a master PASS/FAIL cell on the cover referencing them.

issue: No scenarios. Capital allocation turns on a handful of real forks (pace of new warehouse openings, capex per unit, membership renewals, margin on core vs ancillary) and none are modelled.
fix: Add three scenarios keyed to the decision: base, faster build / higher capex, and demand or margin downside. Drive them from named input cells, not by re-typing numbers, and show the decision output under each.

issue: No cover. The reader has to open three empty tabs to discover there is nothing. The answer should be the first thing on the first tab.
fix: Add a Cover tab: the decision in one line, the recommended answer, the key outputs, the scenario table, and the master check flag. Everything below supports that page.

issue: Tab names are generic placeholders; nothing tells a reader what business question Calc answers.
fix: Rename tabs to the question they hold (e.g. 'Capex & Build', 'Returns by Scenario', 'Summary'), keep Inputs and Checks, and add colour coding: inputs one colour, formulas another, outputs a third.

issue: Both growth rates — the two assumptions the entire five-year forecast depends on — are sourced only as 'assumption'. Nothing in the workbook earns the 6% revenue CAGR or the 4% capex growth; every dollar of the $59,349.91M FCF and $54,794.41M closing cash traces back to them.
fix: Source each one. For rev_growth: anchor to Costco's 10-K historical revenue CAGR and to consensus revenue estimates, cite the figures, and show the implied FY2031 revenue of $405,683M as a growth rate versus the FY2026 base of $303,150M. For capex_growth: tie to the capex plan behind the FY2027 ~$6,500M guidance (distribution/warehouse buildout, e-commerce). If no filing or guidance supports 6% and 4%, cut them to the sourced rate and show the new outputs.

where: Inputs!cash_yield = 5.1%; source F21 'US 10-year Treasury yield 5.15% at 2026-11-13'
issue: Costco's cash is in short-duration deposits and cash equivalents, not locked in 10-year notes. A 5.1% yield on the average opening cash balance produces $6,874.85M of interest income over five years — 9.8% of total uses — and it is unearned. The 10-year is also the wrong benchmark for a rolling cash balance.
fix: Re-source to a short-rate benchmark (money market / T-bill yield, or the weighted average interest rate actually disclosed in the 10-K interest income note) and cite the figure. Present it as a range (e.g. 3.5%–5.1%) so the committee can see the interest-income line move.

issue: The grid is a closed-form approximation, not a recalculation of the model. B31 is 'cash + revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(...)', it ignores capex entirely, ignores the cash floor draw, ignores interest on opening cash, and starts from opening cash rather than carrying the year-by-year build. Compare Model!B23 = 54,794.41 (the model) to the grid: the grid is a different calculator. A sensitivity that does not move the actual model is not a sensitivity; it is a second, unreconciled number.
fix: Rebuild the grid as a live recalc of the model: for each (rev_growth, capex_growth) pair, recompute the full Model!B5:F19 stack and return F17 (closing cash, 2031) and MIN(B20:F20) (minimum headroom). Put the model's own base case in the centre cell and reconcile that centre back to Model!B23 so the grid reads 54,794.41 at the base.

where: Inputs!special_dps = 30; source 'F33 special cash dividend of $30 per share declared 2026-11-11'
issue: The $30 special is declared, and it is entered as an FY2027 cash use (Model!B15 = -13,293 for year 1). Whether it lands in FY2027 or FY2026 is a period question, and it is the single largest year-one outflow ($13,293M) — it flips B17 from positive to well below the $8,000M floor if it is misdated. There is no note in the model on the ex/pay date versus fiscal-year boundary.
fix: State the record/pay date of the 2026-11-11 declared special in a note to Inputs!special_dps and confirm which forecast year the cash actually leaves. If it pays in FY2026, move it out of the forecast and disclose the change to opening cash of $20,210M.

issue: min_cash of $8,000M is the number the recommendation ('Funded without new debt? Yes', Outputs!B9) actually hangs on — ca_min_headroom = 6,826.28 vs an $8,000M floor. It is unsourced. OCF margin at 5.2% is a single historical ratio shown through FY2026; no range, no look at how 5.2% behaves in a stress year (membership fee economics are stable, but the note gives a point, not a defensible floor).
fix: Source min_cash to the company's disclosed liquidity policy or to average peak working-capital/seasons needs from the 10-K, and give it a range (e.g. $6,000M–$10,000M) with the headroom recomputed at each level. For ocf_margin, show using FY2022–FY2026 OCF/revenue and flag the low year; state the FY2027 OCF of $16,773.9M you are asserting.

issue: First forecast year revenue is FY2026 revenue ($303,150M) grown 6.0% in a single step to $321,339M. FY2026 revenue is the 'last full fiscal year', but the workbook never states the forecast periods (FY2027–FY2031 per the Cover) against the actual year-end. The FY2027 line is therefore a full year of growth starting from a base year that may already include part of it. Period labels on Model!row 4 are absent.
fix: Label the forecast columns FY2027E–FY2031E on Model!row 4 and state the FY2026 actual period (year ended 2026-08-30) in a note. Confirm FY2027E revenue of $321,339M is a full-year FY2027 figure and not a stub.

where: Outputs!B9 =IF(ca_min_headroom>=0,"Yes","No: cash falls below the floor") -> Yes
issue: The cover says this is a capital-allocation model for the board, and the one-line conclusion is 'funded without new debt'. It is not a complete answer. Share retirement over five years is 3.62M shares (443.1 to 439.48) against a $4,000M buyback program authorized through January 2030 — the model runs buyback at only $800M a year, $4,000M program or not, and returns only $31,640.35M of $59,349.91M FCF, leaving $54,794.41M of closing cash. The recommended use of the excess is the question the board is asking, and the outputs stop at 'no new debt'.
fix: Add an output line showing the buyback capacity actually deployed ($4,000M/yr vs $800M/yr) and the implied share count at each; add a line showing the $54,794.41M excess over the cash floor and where it goes (special return / accelerated buyback / retained). Make the recommendation on Outputs a sentence the numbers support, e.g. the closing cash of $54,794.41M and headroom of $46,794.41M against an $8,000M floor imply room to accelerate the buyback to $4,000M/yr.

where: Workbook: 5 tabs (Cover, Inputs, Model, Outputs, Checks); no sensitivity/scenarios tab, no sources tab
issue: The grid at Model!r30:r35 is labeled in the digest as a sensitivity but the headline checks (Checks!F3 = OK, difference 0) test only the base case. Scenarios (recession, flat membership, dividend cut) are absent, so the file cannot answer 'what if the 6% is wrong'. Sources live in a cell-comment-style 'source:' field; there is no list a reviewer can audit against.
fix: Add a Scenarios tab with 3 named cases (Base, Downside, Upside) driven off the same Inputs, and a Sources tab listing every F-reference with the filing name, period and figure. Wire the Outputs page to the chosen scenario.

issue: Labels 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares' carry no unit; the digest flags all four. Everything else on the sheet has a unit.
fix: Append the unit to each: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)' on rows 12, 18, 19, 27.

issue: Buyback dollars and share retirement are computed at a single spot price (Model!B18 = B16/-share_price) held flat for five years. Every one of the 3.62M net shares retired is assumed repurchased at $1,106.21, including in FY2031. No disclosure of this.
fix: Add a note that buybacks are modeled at the 2026-11-13 spot of $1,106.21 held constant, and show the share count under a +/−20% price range.

where: Model!B5 = 321,339 shown rounded to $m, but B11 interest = 1,040.82, B20 = 6,826.28
issue: Rounding conventions are mixed on the sheet: some rows to whole $m, others to cents. Presentation only, but it makes the tie-out harder to read at a glance.
fix: Set a single number format per block (whole $m for revenue/cash flows, one decimal for x and shares), so a reviewer can trace without recalculating.

issue: The special dividend is paid only in FY2027 while the regular dividend compounds. The two most likely client-facing alternatives — a $30/share special in FY2027 versus spreading the $13.3B across the window, or a larger special in one year — are not reconciled, so the headline 'Cash returned' number is a one-off event dressed as a capital allocation policy.
fix: Rebuild row 15 as a driver: Special dividend per share (input) times a year-of-payment selector, and add a side-by-side 'Special in FY2027 vs. spread FY2027–FY2029' tie-out on Outputs. Show the cumulative return per share in each case.

where: Model rows 30–35: r31–r35 formula `cash+revenue_base*ocf_margin*IF(ABS((1+rev_growth+$Axx...` with A30 = -2*ca_c_step = -20.0% and A34 = 20.0%
issue: The data table varies growth and capex in 10% (cash) and 10% (growth) increments. These are not the two variables the decision turns on. The decision turns on (1) the size of the special dividend, (2) the pace of buyback against the $4B authorized, and (3) whether OCF margin holds at 5.2% (it was 5.2% in FY2026, and a 50bp miss is a $1.5B annual swing). Growth and capex are second-order for a balance-sheet question.
fix: Keep one growth × capex sensitivity as back-up, and make the front grid: special dividend per share (rows: $0, $15, $30, $45) × annual buyback (columns: $800m, $2B, $4B) with the output cell being lowest headroom over the floor (ca_min_headroom). Relabel A30/A31 etc. to match so the axis labels say what they vary.

where: Outputs!B9 = 'Yes' from IF(ca_min_headroom>=0,"Yes","No: cash falls below the floor")
issue: The first thing anyone reads is a one-word answer with no quantification of the cushion. 'Yes' hides that headroom is $6.8B, i.e. 0.9x the cash floor — a user cannot see whether that is comfortable or tight.
fix: Change Outputs!B9 to a quantified sentence: 'Yes — lowest headroom $6.8B (0.9x the $8.0B floor) in FY2027; cash rises to $54.8B by FY2031.' Put the sensitivity grid directly under it so the reader sees what would flip 'Yes' to 'No'.

where: Inputs!buyback = 800, source 'F34 $4B repurchase program reauthorized 2026-11-11, expiring January 2030'
issue: The model's own source says $4B authorized, expiring January 2030. The model spends $800m a year — five years at $800m is $4.0B, which happens to consume the authorization exactly, so the choice of $800m is not arbitrary, but the model never says that. A reader will read $800m as a plug and ask why not $4B up front.
fix: Add a text cell next to buyback: '=$4B authorization / 5 years = $800m per year; full authorization used by FY2031.' Add a row 'Remaining authorization' starting at $4B and decrementing by $800m so it hits zero in FY2031.

where: Model!B11 = B10*cash_yield and B11 = 1,040.82; Model!B26 = SUM(B11:F11) = 6,874.85 across five years
issue: Interest income is 12% of total FCF ($6.9B of $59.3B). It is generated on a growing cash pile that the model itself says is excess. That is doing work in the answer but is never surfaced. A reader of the Outputs tab has no idea how much of the 'cash generated' line is interest on idle cash.
fix: Add a row to Outputs: 'Of which interest on cash: $6,874.85m (11.6% of total FCF).' If the answer to the capital allocation question is 'you have too much cash', the interest income is an argument for giving more back, not for accumulating it.

where: Inputs!cash_yield = 5.1%, source 'F21 US 10-year Treasury yield 5.15% at 2026-11-13'
issue: The model assumes cash earns the 10-year yield indefinitely for five years. That is a term-premium assumption, not a cash assumption. Short rates or a money-market yield would be the right reference — the 10-year as of the same date may be very different from what Costco actually earns on its cash.
fix: Change the source line to read 'Cash yield 5.1% ≈ blended T-bill / MMF yield as of 2026-11-13' and add a sensitivity: worst case 2.0% (2024-era), best case 5.1%. Show closing cash under both.

issue: Two of the most load-bearing inputs are labelled 'assumption' with no evidence. Costco's last 10 years of revenue CAGR and capex trajectory are known and in the public filings the model already cites. An 'assumption' with no anchor is a plug.
fix: Replace 'assumption' with the trailing 5-year and 10-year actual CAGRs from the same F2/F4 filings the model already uses; state 'we forecast at the mid-point / below trend because X'.

where: Model!A12 'Opening shares', A18 'Shares retired', A19 'Closing shares', A27 'Closing shares'
issue: Four unit warnings (X10) on share-count labels. Any reader could misread 443.1 as $443.1m.
fix: Append '(m)' to each of the four labels.

issue: The 'Cash cover of capex' row jumps 3.2x between FY2027 and FY2031. That is a real finding — cash builds faster than capex — and it is not carried anywhere. It is the strongest argument in the model for returning more.
fix: Lift row 21 onto Outputs as a line or chart: 'Cash cover of capex rises from 2.3x in FY2027 to 7.2x in FY2031.'

where: Inputs header row 3 lists unit fields as 'range to' with blanks for every input
issue: No input has a plausible range documented. The sensitivity grid exists but the ranges are 10% haircuts, not evidence-based bounds.
fix: Fill the range column with the bounds implied by the sensitivity (e.g., 'rev_growth 4.0%–8.0%; capex_growth 2.0%–6.0%') so a reader sees the tested bounds without opening the grid.

issue: The dividend input is internally inconsistent: dps is sourced to 'Costco annual dividend $5.88 per share' (which the source notes includes the FY26 $30 special), but special_dps for FY2027 is set to 0 with a source noting 'Costco declared a $30 special dividend on 2026-11-11'.
