The model therefore runs a regular dividend at a special-inclusive rate while eliminating the special — a hidden double-count. This is the figure a client's analyst will catch first.
fix: Set dps to the regular-only rate (10-K FY2026 regular dividend, with a research request to confirm the declared regular rate going forward) and either keep special_dps at 0 with an explicit rationale that no special is forecast, or set special_dps to 30 in the first forecast year with a clear note that it is a one-time event and zero thereafter. Add a note in Inputs explaining the FY26 figures and the FY27 assumption.

issue: Capex growth is 8% per year — above the 6% revenue growth — while the source cited is 'capex grew 14.2%/yr over three years to $6.43B (10-K FY2026)'. The 5-year forecast compounds capex from $6,500 to $8,843 (Model!F7), a 36% increase, on no stated expansion plan. This assumption drives the FCF total ($56.4B) and the headroom, and a committee will ask why capex outgrows sales.
fix: Re-source capex_growth: either (a) hold capex growth to the revenue-driven level implied by the company's plan, or (b) anchor it to sourced store-count and capex-per-store guidance and cite it. If the 8% is intentional, add a note in Inputs tying it to management's stated expansion plans, not to trailing growth.

issue: Dividend growth (8%) sits above revenue growth (6%) and above OCF growth (which is revenue-driven at 5.2% margin, so also 6%) and above the FCF trajectory; the dividend payout therefore rises every year on top of a 438.58M share count that shrinks only modestly. There is no payout-ratio discipline and no range on the assumption.
fix: Add a payout-ratio or FCF-coverage test to the Model and constrain dps_growth to a defensible range (e.g., link to the three-year history of dividend increases). State the payout ratio at the end of the forecast and confirm it is consistent with management's stated policy. Add a low/base/high range for dps_growth and rev_growth to the assumption book.

issue: The capex base ($6,500) is sourced to the 10-Q 'intention to spend approximately $6,500 in fiscal 2026' while ocf_margin (5.2%) is sourced to FY2026 operating cash flow of $15.82B on FY2026 revenue of $303.15B — but the forecast labeled FY2027+ begins in Model!B5 with revenue_base*(1+rev_growth) = 321,339, i.e., the FY2026 numbers are being grown into FY2027. The capex base of 6,500 is stated as FY2026, not FY2027. Confirm the forecast years are consistently labeled and that no FY2026 figure is used as the FY2027 starting point.
fix: Relabel the Model year headers to match the forecast period explicitly and, if 6,500 is FY2026, either use it as the base and grow it once to get FY2027 or restate the base to the FY2027 capex guidance. Make the year labels on Model!row 4 explicit ('FY2027E' ... 'FY2031E') so the reader can tie each driver to its source period.

issue: Interest on cash is forecast at 5.1% for all five years, sourced to a single-day 10-year Treasury print (5.15% on 2026-11-13). Costco's cash is short-duration; the 10-year is not the right benchmark, and a spot rate is not a five-year forecast. The interest line alone contributes $9,534.81 to closing cash (Model!B26), so this materially drives the output.
fix: Re-source cash_yield to a short-dated rate (e.g., 3-month T-bill / money-market yield) and either hold it flat with a cited long-run assumption or model a declining path consistent with the forward curve. Show the year-by-year rate in Inputs rather than a single cell so the sensitivity to the rate is visible.

issue: Share price is a single-day close (Yahoo Finance, 2026-11-13) used to compute shares retired (Model!B18 = B16/-share_price, 0.904M per year) and the closing share count (438.58M). Buyback dollar amount is held flat at $1,000/yr for five years; the share price is not forecast, so the share count outcome is an artifact of a stale spot price rather than a driver.
fix: Either (a) model buybacks as a share count (retire N million shares/yr) with a price path or note that share count is held flat for modeling simplicity, or (b) run the buyback in dollar terms but flag in Inputs that a rising price will retire fewer shares and show that sensitivity. Update the spot price to the latest close before circulation.

issue: The sensitivity grid varies revenue growth (rows, via ca_g_step, -20% to +20%) and something labeled 'investment plan change' (columns, ca_c_step), but the grid formula in Model!B31 multiplies revenue_base*ocf_margin and ignores the capex and dividend drivers that actually determine cash headroom. The grid therefore understates the sensitivity of the answer to capex growth and dps_growth, the two assumptions that carry the most weight.
fix: Rebuild the grid to flex the drivers that matter — at minimum capex_growth and dps_growth on the axes, or one of those against rev_growth — and label the row/column headers with the driver name and the range. Ensure the grid starts at the same closing cash as the base case at the centre (65,950.06) and document the step size.

issue: 'Cash floor the board keeps' of $5,000 is sourced to 'assumption' with no range, no rationale, and no benchmark (e.g., % of revenue or months of opex). The buyback of $1,000/yr is sourced to a $4B authorization through January 2030 — an authorization is a capacity, not an annual run-rate, and $1,000/yr uses only 25% of it with no explanation.
fix: State the basis for the $5,000 floor (e.g., days of operating expense, % of revenue, or working-capital needs) and tie it to Costco's own disclosed minimum. For the buyback, either justify $1,000/yr against recent actual repurchase history from the 10-K cash flow statement, or set it to the observed run-rate and cite the page. Add both to the Checks tab as monitored constraints.

issue: The Checks tab validates only that closing cash ties to flows and that the grid centre equals closing cash less interest. There is no check that the Modell!B18 share-retirement formula uses the same share price as Inputs!share_price, no check that the forecast years are correctly labeled FY2027-FY2031, and no check that the special dividend of zero is the intended assumption. Two checks is thin for a five-year capital allocation model heading to a board.
fix: Add checks for: (1) each forecast year's revenue = prior year * (1+rev_growth); (2) shares retired = buyback / share_price each year; (3) dps reported equals the regular-only rate used; (4) if special_dps > 0 it is applied in exactly one year. List all checks on the Checks tab with named targets and statuses.

where: Model rows 12 and 19 (labels 'Opening shares' and 'Closing shares') and row 27 ('Closing shares')
issue: The X10 rule flagged four labels with no unit ('Opening shares', 'Closing shares', 'Closing shares'). A client reading the back-up will not know whether the figures are millions or thousands.
fix: Append the unit to each label: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Closing shares (m)', 'Closing shares, 2031 (m)'. Apply consistently to Model rows 12, 19, and 27.

issue: The Outputs tab carries a single column of figures with no units on the row labels (e.g., 'Free cash flow, all forecast years ($m)' is fine but 'Closing shares (m)' at B8, 'Lowest headroom over the cash floor ($m)' at B7) and — per the digest, 'Summary tables and charts for review' — no evidence of charts or a build-up. It is a value map, not a page.
fix: Add the source cell reference next to each output (e.g., '= Model!B22') so the reader can trace every figure, state the forecast years in the header, and add the two charts referenced in the tab purpose (closing cash path and cash-returned bar) before this goes out.

where: Outputs tab (9 rows x 2 cols) versus Model!B22:B27 and Inputs
issue: The Outputs tab is a 9-row afterthought: six named results stacked in a column and one Yes/No. There is no answer up front, no page that says what the decision is. The coversheet says 'Capital Allocation Model FY2027-FY2031' and nothing more. A CEO cannot find the point.
fix: Rebuild Outputs around the decision: page one states the question ('How much cash can Costco return without breaching the board's $5B floor?') and the answer in one line — e.g. 'Costco generates $56.4B FCF over FY2027-31; returning $20.2B leaves $66.0B closing cash and $22.9B lowest headroom; funded without new debt.' Then one small table of the six named results, one chart of closing cash versus the $5B floor by year.

issue: The scenarios are a 5x5 grid on the two growth rates (-2% to +2% on revenue growth, -20% to +20% on capex growth) — a sensitivity tornado with no decision attached. The decision turns on how much cash to return and whether to fund a special dividend, and the scenario set does not vary the two levers the board actually controls: buyback and special dividend. Worse, the source note on Inputs!special_dps records a $30 special dividend declared 2026-11-11, yet the input is 0 and no scenario tests it. You have a live board decision sitting in your source notes and you modelled it as zero.
fix: Replace the growth-rate grid with three named cases the board will recognise, each varying the controllable levers: Base (buyback $1,000/yr, special $0), Accelerated return (buyback $2,000/yr, special $30/share in FY2027), Stress (rev_growth 3%, buyback $2,000/yr, special $30/share). Report for each: closing cash, lowest headroom vs the $5B floor, and the headroom test. Keep the growth/capex grid as a back-up sensitivity, not the front page.

issue: 'Funded without new debt?: Yes' is the only decision-shaped sentence in the file, and it is computed from a single base case (ca_min_headroom = 22,919.28) with no debt or financing line anywhere in the Model. The answer is true by construction — cash only falls if uses exceed flows, and no scenario pushes it there. It reads as a conclusion but proves nothing.
fix: Either add a financing row to Model (debt issued/repaid, blank in base case) so the claim is falsifiable, or relabel the cell 'Cash never breaches the $5B floor in the base case' and put the same test against each of the three named scenarios on Outputs.

issue: The three drivers that carry the whole model have no stated downside. Revenue grew 7.8%/yr over three years and you forecast 6.0%; capex grew 14.2%/yr and you forecast 8.0%; OCF margin is held flat for five years. Each is defensible alone; together they assume a benign five years and no scenario tests a break. The note cites history but not why the forward numbers sit below it.
fix: On Inputs, add a one-line rationale beside each of the three drivers ('below the 3-yr trend because X'). In the Stress case set ocf_margin to 4.5% and rev_growth to 3.0% — both below the cited three-year history (7.8%, and OCF margin implies a 2-3pp compression) — and show the closing cash and headroom consequences on Outputs.

issue: You start the regular dividend at $5.88 (a stockanalysis.com figure) and grow it 8.0%/yr, while the 10-K note you cite says dividends declared per share were $5.54. Two different current-year dividend numbers in one file with no reconciliation; the model uses the higher one and compounds it.
fix: Set dps to the 10-K declared figure or state explicitly why the forward rate differs (e.g. 'FY2027 declared rate expected to be $5.88 versus FY2026 $5.54'), and put the reconciliation in a note on Inputs. Keep dps_growth at 8.0% only if you can cite the basis.

where: Model row 30 formula: B30 =-2*ca_c_step -> -20.0% and F30 =E30+ca_c_step -> 20.0%
issue: The sensitivity grid axis is unlabelled in the formula extract and its orientation is inverted: B30 is -20% and F30 is +20%, but the A-column labels (A31 to A35) are not visible in the digest and the reader cannot tell whether columns are capex growth and rows revenue growth without the header. A client cannot follow the page without a voice-over.
fix: Put explicit axis titles on the grid: 'Rows: revenue growth versus plan; Columns: capex growth versus plan' above the A30 cell, and a note 'Cells show closing cash in FY2031, $m; the base case is 0/0'. Then shade the base cell and format the grid with a single scale so the reader sees where cash breaches the $5B floor.

where: Forge X10 warnings: Model rows 12, 18, 19, 27 — 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares'
issue: Four row labels in the Model have no unit while every money row does. Small, but it is the kind of thing a client's analyst notices and it makes the share block look unfinished next to the dollar rows.
fix: Add '(m)' to Opening shares, Shares retired and both Closing shares labels on the Model so the units match Inputs!shares and Inputs!share_price.

issue: Closing shares 438.58 is reported with two decimal places on a share count that moved from 443.1 over five years — a 1% reduction. It is a real number but it carries no decision: the buyback retires 0.904m shares a year at $1,106.21, which is immaterial against 443m shares. The reader will ask why it is on the answer page.
fix: Either drop closing shares from Outputs or replace it with the buyback in dollars and as a % of shares outstanding, and note that at the current price $1,000m/yr retires under 0.3% of the register a year — the buyback is not the capital-allocation lever here.

issue: Dividend is computed on opening shares, not on shares net of the year's retirement: B14 = -B13*B12 = -2,605.43 uses opening shares B12 = 443.1, while closing shares B19 = B12-B18 = 442.2. The retirement (0.904m at $1,106.21 = $1,000m) is effectively treated as occurring after the dividend. Over five years the dividend base is overstated by the cumulative retired share count.
fix: Charge the dividend on the average or a defined timing basis (state the convention in Inputs) and change B14 to = -B13*AVERAGE(B12,B19) or -B13*B19 if retirement is assumed at the start of the year; apply the same to the special dividend B15. Re-run the model and confirm Model!B25 and ca_min_headroom change.

where: Workbook, no DCF or valuation tab
issue: This is a capital-allocation / source-and-use projection only. There is no DCF, no WACC build, no terminal value, no exit multiple cross-check, no equity bridge (net debt, minorities), no per-share value on diluted shares. Nothing in the workbook answers what the cash returned is worth to a shareholder or supports the $1,106.21 share price assumption for the buyback.
fix: Add a Valuation tab: build unlevered FCF from the Model FCF rows, build WACC line by line (risk-free = the 5.15% 10-year already sourced; equity risk premium, beta, cost of debt, tax rate - all sourced) and compute a DCF with a stated terminal-value method and midpoint convention. Then a separate equity bridge (net debt = cash minus debt; minorities; diluted shares from the 10-K). Show the terminal-value share of EV as a row on that tab.

issue: Every assumption carries a source but no range - e.g. rev_growth = 6.0%, ocf_margin = 5.2%, capex_growth = 5.0%, dps_growth = 8.0%, cash_yield = 5.1% all have blank range fields. A committee cannot tell whether 6.0% revenue growth is the mid-point of a range or a round number picked for the answer.
fix: Add a low/high column to Inputs with a sourced range for each driver: revenue growth low/high from the 10-K three-year CAGR range and any guidance; ocf_margin range from the FY2024-FY2026 realisation; capex from the FY27 plan ($7.5B) versus consensus; dps growth from the last three declaration years; cash_yield range around the 5.15% 10-year.

where: Inputs!B column, [Balance sheet and shares] and [Rates]
issue: Several inputs are stated without adequate source: min_cash = 4,000 is labelled source 'assumption' with no basis; dps = 5.88 sources stockanalysis.com rather than the 10-K declared dividend of $5.54; share_price = 1,106.21 is a single Yahoo close from 2026-11-13 with no date range. The board's cash floor drives the entire 'Funded without new debt?' answer (Outputs!B17) and it is unsourced.
fix: Replace the min_cash source with a board policy reference or a working-capital requirement derived from the 10-K (minimum operating cash = 4,000 needs a stated basis, e.g. one month of revenue + seasonal build); switch the dividend input to the FY2026 10-K declared figure $5.54 and state the fiscal-year basis; use a 30-day VWAP for share_price and annotate the range.

issue: Headroom and cover are computed on the closing cash balance after all cash uses including buybacks (B21 = B17/-B7 = 1.82x). That is not cash cover of capex - it is a residual. A reader will read it as a coverage ratio. The number is also driven by a floor (B20 = B17-min_cash) that is itself an unsourced input.
fix: Either rename B21 to 'Closing cash / annual capex (residual after distributions)' and state it, or compute true cover as (opening cash + FCF) / capex before distributions. Do the same to B20 - label it 'Closing cash less board floor'.

issue: The special dividend of $30 is charged once in FY2027 (B15 = -special_dps*B12 = -13,293) but no source ties it to an announced record/payment date, and no source explains why it does not recur. The gearing of the returns - $13.3B special plus $1B buyback plus regular dividend - swallows most of the FY2027 free cash flow of $9,273.9 (Model!B8), which is why headroom falls from $9,626.28 to zero over the year.
fix: Add a note to Inputs!B for special_dps capturing the announcement date and ex-date (source cited is 2026-11-11); add a row showing 'Cash returned as % of FCF' by year so the FY2027 shortfall is visible; if the special is announced but not paid in FY2027, move it to the correct forecast year.

issue: The summary rows (free cash flow all years, closing cash, cash returned all years, closing shares) are hard-wired to single cells on row B of the Model and do not recompute as a scenario changes the forecast horizon - they sum only B:F. The sensitivity grid (Model!B30:F35) changes growth and capex but the summary rows B22-B27 do not become scenario outputs, so the outputs do not move when the scenario does.
fix: Rebuild the summary rows as scenario-driven references to a scenario switch (e.g. drive the grid off an input cell that the summary rows also reference), and add a scenario column to the Outputs tab showing the same ca_cash_end, ca_min_headroom and ca_shares_end under low/mid/high cases.

where: Model!B10 and Model!F10, Model!B12 and Model!F12
issue: Opening cash B10 = cash = 20,210 but closing cash B17 = 13,626.28 uses a formula whose signs include B15 (special dividend, -13,293) and B16 (buyback, -1,000) and B14 (regular dividend) with the same negative sign convention as capex B7 = -7,500. The row signs are inconsistent: B8 = free cash flow = B6+B7 where B7 is negative capex but B6 is positive OCF, so B8 can be read as either net cash flow or a leftover. Then B17 = B10+B8+B11+B14+B15+B16 mixes FCF and distributions in one line.
fix: Split rows: free cash flow (OCF less capex), then financing/distributions as separate lines, then net change in cash; one sign convention per block, all inflows positive, all outflows negative, and a stated row label on each. Verify the sum still tie to ca_cash_end = 45,930.96.

where: Model!A12, A18, A19, A27; Outputs!A4, A17
issue: Six row labels carry no unit - 'Opening shares' (A12), 'Shares retired' (A18), 'Closing shares' (A19, A27), 'Answer' (Outputs!A4), 'Funded without new debt?' (Outputs!A17). The FORGE rule X10 flags all six.
fix: Add the unit to each label: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)' on Model rows 12/18/19/27, and 'Answer' / 'Funded without new debt?' should be labelled as a summary header or given the underlying unit (e.g. 'Funded without new debt? (Yes/No)').

issue: The claim text B4 = 'Over the forecast ... $53,114m of free cash flow ... $33,511m to shareholders; cash ends ...' uses ca_fcf_total and ca_uses_total rounded to the nearest million, while the underlying values are 53,113.78 and 33,510.85 - the text over-rounds in a way that could be challenged in a line-by-line review against the model.
fix: Change the TEXT() format in B4 to one decimal ($53,113.8m / $33,510.9m) or state the rounding convention on the Outputs tab so the printed figure ties to Model!B22 and Model!B25.

issue: Only two checks are live and both test closing cash; there is no check on the share roll-forward (B12 = E19 linkage), no check that total cash returned ties to a stated distribution ('returns $X to shareholders' in Outputs!B4), and no cross-check of the sensitivity grid outputs.
fix: Add a checks row for opening shares B12 = prior closing shares F19 (difference = 0), a row for cash returned = regular dividend + special + buyback sum, and a row that the Outputs summary equals the Model summary. MasterCheck F3 currently OK; re-confirm after additions.

issue: Revenue B5 = revenue_base*(1+rev_growth) = 321,339 uses a single growth driver for all five years; the 10-K three-year CAGR is 7.8% and the input is 6.0%. There is no driver decomposition (comps, new warehouse openings, membership fee changes) even though the capex assumption mentions 16 new warehouses.
fix: Either decompose revenue growth into (a) comp growth and (b) unit growth from new openings sourced to the 10-K/10-Q, or add a note to Inputs explaining why 6.0% is below the 7.8% realised three-year CAGR and what would change it.

issue: The workbook answers 'does cash cover the floor and capex' when the deck's question is how to allocate capital. Outputs!B4 says 'Over the forecast the business generates $53,114m of free cash flow and returns $33,511m to shareholders; cash ends a...' — the answer is buried inside a TEXT() concatenation in cell B4, not a headline a reader can find.
fix: Replace Outputs!B4 with a single action title: 'FCF of $53.1B funds $33.5B of returns and leaves $45.9B of cash — the constraint is deployment, not funding,' and move the TEXT() string to a sub-line below the table.

issue: The only scenario grid varies revenue growth and capex growth (ca_g_step / ca_c_step around rev_growth 6.0% and capex_growth 5.0%). It never flexes the decisions the board actually controls: buyback size ($1,000m/yr fixed), dividend growth (8.0%), or a larger special dividend. The grid also reports only closing cash — it does not show what the decision variable (capital returned) does.
fix: Add three named scenarios on a new 'Scenarios' tab: Base (buyback $1,000m, special $30), Accelerated return (buyback $1,000m→$4,000m over five years, special $30), and Hold (no special). Report for each: FCF, cash returned, closing cash, lowest headroom, and closing shares. Drive them from one switch cell, not a new grid shape.

where: Model row 21 ('Cash cover of capex') and Outputs!B17
issue: The two header metrics are 'Funded without new debt?' (Outputs!B17 = 'Yes') and 'Lowest headroom over the cash floor' ($9,626m). Both answer a solvency question Costco is not being asked. Neither tells the board what mix of dividend, buyback and reinvestment is best.
fix: Replace the two header metrics with: (1) 'Cash returned to shareholders over FY27-FY31: $33,511m' and (2) 'Optional capital available for deployment: $45,930m (cash) less $4,000m floor = $41,930m'. Keep the headroom row only as a supporting check.

issue: Buyback is held at $1,000m a year for five years against a $4B reauthorization (Inputs source F38) — the model uses a quarter of the authorization with no explanation, so the board cannot see whether the number is a policy choice or a placeholder.
fix: Either raise buyback to reflect the full $4B authorization amortised over the forecast (e.g. $800m/yr for five years = $4,000m) or add an assumption note in Inputs column F: 'Buyback held at $1B/yr pending board decision; $4B authorization provides $3B of upside.'

issue: Interest is earned on the opening cash balance every year at 5.1% (Model!B11 = B10*cash_yield), the same rate on $20B in FY27 and $45.9B in FY31. No rate path is shown even though Inputs source F24 cites the 10-year at 5.15% as a point-in-time observation.
fix: Add a cash_yield row (one yield per forecast year) in Inputs and point Model!B11:F11 at it. Hold it flat at 5.1% if that is the view, but make it visible.

where: Checks tab and Model row 30-35 grid
issue: The two checks only prove the cash roll-forward and grid centre tie. Nothing checks that shares retired times share price equals buyback spend, or that the sum of regular dividends equals dps times shares in each year, or that total uses equals total returns plus capex.
fix: Add three checks to Checks: (1) Model!B16:F16 = B18:F18 * -share_price, difference 0; (2) Model!B25 = -SUM(B14:F16), difference 0; (3) Outputs!B14 = Model!F17, difference 0.

where: Outputs tab (17 rows x 6 cols) and Model tab (35 rows x 6 cols)
issue: Outputs tab is 17 rows including six rows of 'no unit' labels ('Answer', 'Funded without new debt?' — X10 warnings). The five-year table sits under a single answer string and no chart is shown even though the tab is described as 'Summary tables and charts'.
fix: Delete 'Funded without new debt?' row and add a units column to every row. Add one chart: closing cash by year with the $4,000m floor as a line. Cut Outputs to 10 rows.

issue: X10 flagged six label rows with no unit ('Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares', 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?'). A reader cannot tell from the sheet whether shares are millions or thousands.
fix: Rename Model!A12 to 'Opening shares (m)', A18 to 'Shares retired (m)', A19 and A27 to 'Closing shares (m)', Outputs!A4 to 'Answer ($m and m)' and drop Outputs!A17.

issue: cash_yield = 5.1% is sourced to 'F24 US 10-year Treasury yield 5.15% at 2026-11-13'. Two defects: (a) the rate is mis-applied — Costco's interest income is earned on short-duration cash and equivalents, where the 10-year is the wrong benchmark; the correct input is the yield on cash/short-term investments. (b) The stated source (5.15%) does not equal the input (5.1%), a 5bp unexplained haircut. 'US 10-year Treasury yield' is also stale-dated to a single day. This single input drives ca_int_total = 6,641 and lifts the closing cash position.
fix: Replace cash_yield with a rate tied to Costco's actual yield on cash and short-term investments, evidenced by the 10-K/10-Q interest income line and the yield on its short-duration portfolio as of the most recent quarter-end. If 5.1% is retained, state explicitly the source, the period, and why the input differs from the quoted source; correct the 5.15% vs 5.1% mismatch.

issue: min_cash = 5,000 carries the source 'assumption' with no range and no rationale. This is the cash floor every headroom figure (ca_min_headroom = 9,828.41; Model!B20:F20) and the 'Funded without new debt?' = Yes (Outputs!B17) depend on. An unsourced number is doing substantial work in the conclusion.
fix: Source min_cash: minimum operating cash plus the disclosed working-capital/seasonal buffer need, or the board's stated policy. Provide a range (e.g., low/base/high) and show ca_min_headroom at each level.

issue: capex_base = 6,500 is sourced to 'F36 10-Q Q3 FY2026: intention to spend approximately $6,500m in fiscal 2026'. A Q3 FY2026 10-Q covers the period to roughly May 2026 — fiscal 2026 is nearly over at that date. Setting the FY2026 spend as the FY2027 base is a period mismatch, and the source is a guidance statement for the current year, not for the first forecast year.
fix: Re-anchor capex_base to FY2026 actual (the 10-K FY2026 capex figure, F4) or to explicit FY2027 guidance/board capital plan. Label the year each figure refers to in the input row.

issue: 'Special dividend per share, first forecast year' = 30 with source 'F38/F47 special cash dividend $30/share declared; F48 payable 2026-12-04; F49 total ~$13.3B'. Model!B15 = -13,293 is a one-time payment already declared and payable in fiscal 2027 (FY ends August). This is a scheduled obligation, not a forecast assumption, yet it sits in the assumptions block indistinguishable from driver assumptions and is excluded from every sensitivity and scenario (rows 30–35). The 'Funded without new debt?' = Yes answer is therefore measured with a $13.3B outflow that is certain.
fix: Reclassify the $30/share special dividend as a committed item, not an assumption; annotate it as declared/payable 2026-12-04 in the cash flow tab; and add a scenario or at minimum a note showing ca_min_headroom with the special dividend both included and excluded.

issue: The buyback is modeled at a flat $800m/yr retiring 0.7232m shares/yr, but the share price is a single 2026-11-13 close (F21) and is never grown or scenario'd. Buyback share retirement and closing shares (ca_shares_end = 439.48) therefore assume a flat price for five years — an unsourced assumption embedded in a valuation-adjacent output.
fix: Either hold price flat but state it explicitly as an assumption with a source and a range, or grow share price at a stated rate through the forecast and show the effect on ca_shares_end. Tie the $800m buyback to the $4B program over 5 years.

issue: The share retirement calculation is internally inconsistent with average-share dividend treatment: B14 = -B13*AVERAGE(B12,B19) charges dividends on average shares, while B18 retires shares during the year — about 0.7m/yr all six years. A 443.1 → 439.48 decline over five years is arithmetically wrong: 443.1 − (5 × 0.7232) = 439.48, but buyback at $800m/yr for six forecast columns implies the buyback only runs five years, or the first-year retirement is mis-timed. Verify whether FY2027 (B12→B19) should reflect a full year of buyback and whether ca_shares_end = 439.48 is a five-year or six-column result.
fix: Set the share count consistently: buyback per column, compute closing shares = opening − retired for each of B–F, and confirm ca_shares_end equals F19 with the same number of buyback periods as forecast years. Label the columns' periods.

issue: Free cash flow over the forecast (54,872.86) + opening cash (20,210) − cash returned (31,917.32) + interest income (6,641) − capex is not reconciling to closing cash 49,806.54 on the face of the summary. Note capex is already inside FCF, so no double count; nevertheless 20,210 + 54,872.86 + 6,641 − 31,917.32 = 49,806.54, which implies the closing cash figure absorbs both FCF and interest — verify FCF (B22 = SUM(B8:F8), where B8 = B6 + B7 = OCF + capex) and cash returned (B25) do not double-count the special dividend versus the cash bridge in B17. The residual ties, but the presentation of the bridge does not make the special dividend and buyback explicit.
fix: Add a bridge row (opening cash → FCF → interest → regular dividends → special dividend → buyback → closing cash) so the 49,806.54 is visibly composed and check it against B17.

where: Model! A12, A18, A19, A27; Outputs! A4, A17
issue: Labels 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares' (twice), 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?' carry no units (X10 warnings). 'Answer' and 'Funded without new debt?' are text-value rows, not numeric — an odd inclusion in a table whose other rows carry '$m'.
fix: Add units: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)'. For 'Answer' and 'Funded without new debt?', either keep as clearly-marked text lines or move them out of the numeric table.

issue: No ranges are given for any assumption (all show 'range  to '). The instruction to the model is that each assumption should carry a range. With no ranges, the sensitivities in Model rows 30–35 use only the hard-coded steps ca_c_step and ca_g_step rather than the actual driver ranges.
fix: Populate the range columns with low/base/high for rev_growth, ocf_margin, dps_growth, capex_growth, cash_yield, and min_cash, each sourced and tied to the sensitivity steps.

where: Outputs — whole tab; B4 '...cash ends at $49,807m'; B17 = Yes
issue: The Answer row asserts a conclusion ('generates $54,873m of free cash flow and returns $31,917m; cash ends at $49,807m') and 'Funded without new debt?' = Yes, but no tab reports the key vulnerability: the answer hinges on cash_yield = 5.1% (unsourced as applied) and min_cash = 5,000 (unsourced). The conclusion is presented without the qualifiers the inputs require.
fix: Annotate the Outputs tab with a one-line 'Key dependencies' note naming cash_yield and min_cash and the effect on ca_min_headroom of ±100bp on cash_yield and ±$2,500m on min_cash (using existing model mechanics).

issue: Sentinel cells use hard-coded steps ca_c_step = 10.0% and ca_g_step = 10.0% (B30 = -20.0% through F30 = 20.0%), but these step sizes are not tied to the assumption ranges (which are empty). The sensitivity grid therefore tests arbitrary steps rather than the drivers' evidenced range.
fix: Set ca_c_step and ca_g_step to the same range used in the Inputs range column (e.g., capex growth stress of −500bp/+500bp around the base, sourced), and label the sentinel values as stress cases.

issue: 'Free cash flow' is defined as operating cash flow plus capital expenditure and nothing else. There is no working capital movement, no cash taxes shown separately, no interest received inside it — interest is added one row below as a separate line. A client reading 'Free cash flow, all years = $54,872.86m' will reconcile that to the 10-K definition and not get there. You are labeling a memo line as FCF.
fix: Either rename row 8 to 'Operating cash flow less capex' and keep the total as-is, or build the full bridge: OCF less capex less working capital movement less cash taxes plus interest received. If you take the second route, add the two missing drivers (working capital % of revenue, cash tax rate) to Inputs with sources.

where: Model rows 30-35, ca_g_step and ca_c_step grid
issue: The sensitivity grid flexes revenue growth and capex growth and nothing else. The decision that turns on this model is capital return: the special dividend (~$13.3B at B15) and the $800m annual buyback. Neither is flexed. A three-by-six grid of revenue scenarios tells the board nothing about whether they can afford the special dividend if the buyback accelerates or the special is doubled.
fix: Rebuild the grid on the two variables the decision turns on: special dividend per share (x-axis, $0 / $30 / $50) against buyback per year (y-axis, $800m / $2,000m / $4,000m). Report closing cash and minimum headroom in each cell. Keep revenue growth as a separate one-way sensitivity.

issue: Opening cash is hard-linked to the input cash of $20,210m in year 1 but then rolls from prior closing cash. This means the opening balance sheet is never checked against the FY2026 10-K balance sheet beyond cash — no debt, no leases, no other current assets. The model is a cash-only lens, which is fine, but nothing tells the reader that.
fix: Add a note in the Cover or Outputs stating the model is a cash-flow and capital-return lens only, and that the balance sheet is held constant apart from cash. One sentence is enough.

issue: Every one of these is a single point estimate with a source, no range. The model's answer ($54,873m of FCF, cash ends at $49,806m) is only as good as four numbers none of which has a floor or ceiling shown. Rev growth is sourced to a three-year historical of 7.8% — you have marked it down to 6.0% with no explanation of why.
fix: Add a 'low / base / high' column to Inputs for each driver with a one-line rationale. At minimum, explain in the source cell why 6.0% growth vs the 7.8% three-year historical.

issue: The 'Answer' string concatenates the three key numbers into one sentence with no structure. The rule X10 flags 'Answer' has no unit. More importantly, the first thing a reader sees is a run-on sentence, not the answer.
fix: Replace B4 with a three-line block: 'FCF FY27-FY31: $54,873m', 'Cash returned: $31,917m', 'Closing cash FY31: $49,806m; minimum headroom $9,828m'. Put the 'Yes/No: funded without new debt' line directly under it, label it 'Verdict'.

where: Outputs row 17, 'Funded without new debt?' = Yes
issue: The verdict is based on ca_min_headroom >= 0, i.e. cash never drops below the $5,000m board floor. That is a good test, but it ignores the debt on the balance sheet and any refinancing need. Costco's existing debt is not modelled at all. 'Funded without new debt' is a strong claim for a model that has no debt schedule.
fix: Either retitle to 'Cash stays above the $5,000m floor in all years?' or add a debt row to the Model (opening debt, scheduled repayments, no new issuance) and drive the verdict off cash-and-undrawn-facility coverage.

issue: Dividends are paid on average shares, the special on opening shares, and buybacks are a flat $800m regardless of price. The share price input (share_price = $1,106.21) only enters through shares retired. If the price moves, buyback dollar amount is fixed but shares retired move — that is right — but the model never shows buyback as a % of shares outstanding, so a reader cannot see whether $800m is a token or meaningful.
fix: Add a line 'Buyback as % of shares outstanding' to Outputs. At $800m / 443m shares it will show ~0.16%/yr — worth seeing on the page.

issue: Six X10 warnings: 'Opening shares', 'Shares retired', 'Closing shares' (twice), 'Answer', 'Funded without new debt?' have no unit. Small thing, but a committee reviewer will flag it and it looks unfinished.
fix: Add units: 'Opening shares (m)', 'Shares retired (m)', 'Closing shares (m)', 'Answer ($m unless stated)', 'Funded without new debt? (Y/N)'.

issue: The cover is 18 rows for a title. Nothing on it tells the reader what question the model answers or where to go first.
fix: Cut to five rows: title, date, author, 'Answer is on Outputs!B4', 'Inputs!B:B are the only cells to change'.

where: Inputs, cash_yield = 5.1% sourced to US 10-year Treasury 5.15%
issue: Costco does not earn the 10-year on cash. It earns a mix of T-bills, commercial paper and bank deposits. Using 5.1% on a $20-50B cash balance over five years is a $6.6B interest line (Model!B26). That is material and it is not sourced to Costco's actual yield.
fix: Re-source cash_yield to Costco's disclosed interest income divided by average cash from the FY2026 10-K, or use a 3-month T-bill average. Add the source citation to the Inputs cell.

issue: Revenue growth is flat 6.0% for all five years. The source cites 16 warehouses opened and 13 more planned. A flat growth path with lumpy store openings is a modelling simplification that a reviewer will note.
fix: Either show the warehouse roll-forward as a supplementary schedule or add a note that growth is smoothed. One line under the Model explains it.

issue: The chart plots three different unit types as adjacent bars — a cash stock ($20.21B), an annual accrual of profit ($9.23B), and annual capex spend ($6.43B) — with no baseline or axis, so the reader's eye reads a 20.21-vs-6.43 comparison against 9.23 that cannot be compared. It needs the footnote to be honest.
fix: Replace the three-bar chart with a two-bar comparison of the same basis: net income $9.23B vs capex $6.43B, labelled '69.66% of net income absorbed by capex', and show the $20.21B cash balance as a single horizontal reference line marked 'cash available for any return'.

issue: The deck claims cash 'leaves room for a return' ($20.21B) while simultaneously flagging that total debt, leases and maturities are 'not in the material'. On the cash-return question, leverage is the constraint, not a footnote. The deck recommends a $12.86B floor against an unverified $20.21B gross cash figure.
fix: Either obtain net-debt, lease and maturity figures and show net cash, or add a line to slide 2 bullet 2: 'Gross cash $20.21B; net of debt and leases not yet confirmed.' Do not present $20.21B alone as the surplus available.

issue: The actual sizing logic — 'At 2x, it is $12.86B against $20.21B cash' — is buried in small body type in a table cell, while the page's headline claim is only 'set a floor'. The called-for floor is the one number the board is being asked to vote on.
fix: Promote the floor to the page: add a highlighted callout above the table reading 'Illustrative floor at 2x capex: $12.86B against $20.21B cash'. Keep the table action rows,

issue: Two columns of a four-row explon the left and an almost identical four-bullet text block on the right say the same thing. The right panel is a voice-over in print.
fix: Delete the grey panel and fold its two non-duplicative points (unverified debt/leases; one-year scope) into the page footnote. Let the chart carry the page.

issue: Bullets 2 and 3 mix claims with housekeeping reservations ('Treasury will confirm them', 'Sizing the return needs share price and dividend history'). Those are caveats, not messages.
fix: Move both caveats into the footnote line and give each bullet one clean message, e.g. bullet 2 becomes 'Cash of $20.21B exceeds a return at any illustrated floor'.

issue: Titles wrap to two lines unevenly across pages (slide 2 and slide 5 break after the verb, slide 1's three-line title). Title block position is consistent but the wrap poin random.
fix: Set a character-per-line limit so each title breaks at the same structural point and keeps the same two-line height on every content page.

issue: The scored metres show a fractional fill on each pie that cannot be read at a glance ('Growth first' shows roughly three-quarters on all three tests, yet scores 8 of 9). Tiny donuts cannot carry a scalar score.
fix: Replace the three donut columns with the number plus a bar: e.g. '7/3/3, 6/2/2, 6/2/2, 8/3/3' as a simple heat table, strong cells shaded. The number is the evidence.

issue: Title says 'any return would draw on cash', but the page cannot show that — it shows capex at 69.66% of net income, which leaves 30% funded from earnings before cash is touched.
fix: Retitle slide 3 to what the data supports: 'Capex consumes 69.66% of net income; only $2.80B of earnings remains'.

where: slide 5, row 3, 'Set the floor as a multiple of $6.43B capex. At 2x, it is $12.86B against $20.21B cash.'
issue: The liquidity floor, which is the entire decision, is sized off one accrual-period cash capex figure with a 1x/2x multiple that is a pure management plug. $6.43B x 2 = $12.86B is arithmetically correct, but nothing ties the floor to what it must cover: debt maturities (slide 2 and 3 both state 'Total debt and lease obligations are not in the material'), working capital swings, or seasonality. A floor set below the debt stack is not a floor.
fix: Either obtain total debt, lease obligations and the maturity schedule from the 10-K and build the floor bottom-up (near-term maturities + minimum operating cash + seasonality), or retitle slide 5 row 3 to 'Propose a floor methodology (not a floor level)' and delete the 2x illustration from the action item. Keep the 1x/2x sensitivity in a labelled appendix if the board wants a range, with the footnote already on the page stating the board sets the multiple.

where: slide 4, 'Four options scored on three equal-weight tests (1 to 3; management judgment, not measured results)' against 'Keep funding growth only (7 of 9)', 'Buybacks only (6 of 9)', 'Special dividend only (6 of 9)', 'Growth first, then return cash above a floor (8 of 9)'
issue: The recommendation is carried by a 1-2 point spread on equal-weighted management judgment with no economic input. Buybacks only scores 6 while the combined option scores 8, but the two-point gap is entirely the 'funds new warehouses' criterion, which has no number attached. The page states the test labels but not the scoring basis, so the reader cannot audit why growth-only takes 7 rather than 9. The combined option is pre-selected as the winner before the page is read.
fix: On slide 4, state the scoring anchor next to each option row — for example, the capex dollars each option leaves unfunded or the cash consumed — and show that the 'Funds new warehouses' score traces to the $6.43B capex requirement versus the $20.21B cash balance. If the grid cannot be tied to dollars, demote it from a score to a labelled qualitative screen and let the quantitative page carry the recommendation.

where: slide 2, 'Sizing the return needs share price and dividend history'; slide 4, 'Buyback or special dividend depends on share price and dividend history, which management brings back'
issue: The deck recommends a payout form be chosen by the next meeting without a single share price, share count, dividend per share, payout ratio or EPS-accretion figure anywhere in the five pages. A board cannot approve a buyback or special dividend with no per-share math — the recommendation is not supported by any number on the page.
fix: Add the dilution and accretion math before slide 5 goes out: current share price and share count, dividend per share and current payout ratio, and the per-share effect of a buyback at the recommended size. If that data is unavailable, change slide 5 row 4 from 'Choose the payout form' to 'Return with payout-form economics' and note that no per-share analysis has been prepared.

where: slide 3, chart labelled 'Three separate measures, in $B' with bars 'Cash balance 20.21', 'Net income 9.23', 'Capex 6.43'
issue: The chart places three unrelated measures on one axis and one colour scale. Cash balance is a point-in-time stock at fiscal year-end; net income and capex are period flows over 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30. The footnote on slide 3 concedes the mismatch ('Capex is a cash figure and net income is an accrual figure, so they are compared, not subtracted'), but the takeaway title then says capex 'absorbs most of net income' and the page states capex is '69.66% of $9.23B net income' — an accrual-to-cash comparison presented as a coverage ratio. A committee will pull this apart.
fix: Rebuild slide 3 so the bars are like-for-like: capex, net income and operating cash flow for the same fiscal year, with the cash balance shown as a separate labelled line or callout outside the bar chart. Keep the capex/net income ratio if you want it, but move it to a text callout with the accrual-versus-cash caveat in the same sentence, not a footnote.

where: slide 3, 'Figures cover one year only, so whether $6.43B is a step-up or steady state is not established'
issue: The deck admits the central input is a single year with no trend, yet the capex figure drives slides 2, 3, 4 and 5. No multi-year capex history, no management plan for the forward build, no comparison to depreciation or existing warehouse base. 'Growth capex absorbs most of net income' cannot be established from one year.
fix: Add a three-to-five-year capex series and the forward plan, and replace the one-year figures with the range. If only one year is available, change the slide 3 takeaway title to 'Fiscal 2026 capex was 69.66% of net income; the forward plan is not yet in the material' and flag the trend as a research gap on slide 5 row 1 rather than calling it a baseline.

where: slide 3, 'Interest expense is $145.0M for the year, stated as a fact only'
issue: Interest expense is displayed as a fact with no use. It is not carried into any coverage, interest-coverage or cost-of-capital calculation on any page, and no debt balance or weighted cost of debt is given, so the reader cannot judge the cost of holding the $20.21B cash balance against the cost of debt.
fix: Either remove the $145.0M line from slide 3, or use it: add debt and cash interest income to give a net interest position, and state the implied opportunity cost of the cash floor (cash yield foregone versus cost of debt). If the debt data is unavailable, move $145.0M to a footnote with the source line and take it off the main callout.

where: slide 4, 'Four options scored on three equal-weight tests' — tests are 'Funds new warehouses', 'Uses surplus cash', 'Keeps flexibility'
issue: There is no test for shareholder value. None of the three criteria is return on capital, IRR on new warehouses, ROIC versus WACC, or accretion to EPS. A capital allocation framework that does not test whether the growth capex earns its cost of capital can recommend funding any capex at any return. The deck also never states a WACC or a hurdle rate.
fix: Add a fourth test or replace 'Keeps flexibility' with 'Earns above cost of capital', and include the hurdle rate and the historical ROIC on new warehouses if available. If no return data exists, state explicitly on slide 4 that the framework tests funding capacity, not capital efficiency, and that the board is being asked to fund growth without a return test.

where: whole deck — no page presents a downside or stress case
issue: There is no scenario analysis anywhere in the five pages: no case where capex overshoots, cash flow compresses, or the floor is breached. Slide 2 asserts cash 'leaves room for a return' and slide 5 sizes a return, but no page shows what happens to liquidity if net income falls or capex rises.
fix: Add one page with two or three cases on the same drivers (net income, capex, floor multiple) and show the surplus cash in each. Use only numbers already in the deck ($9.23B net income, $6.43B capex, $20.21B cash) scaled by a stated percentage assumption, and label the scaling assumption as the board's judgment. Do not introduce a new unsourced growth rate as fact.

where: slide 2, 'Cash of $20.21B leaves room for a return' and 'Total debt and leases are not in the material; treasury will confirm them'
issue: The page asserts room for a return while conceding it does not know the debt stack or maturities. The claim is unsupported on the page that makes it, and the caveat sits in a sub-bullet beneath the assertion.
fix: Soften slide 2 point 2 to 'Cash of $20.21B is the pool any return would draw on; the surplus is not determinable until debt, leases and maturities are confirmed' and move the treasury confirmation to the same line, not a subordinate bullet.

where: slide 2, source line 'Costco Wholesale Corp 10-K filed 2026-10-07 (SEC XBRL), fiscal year 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30'
issue: The source line cites a 10-K filed 2026-10-07 covering a fiscal year ended 2026-08-30, and the cover and footers are dated 'Board meeting, November 2026'. Filing date, authorisation date and period label are internally consistent, but the XBRL tag is not given per figure, so the reader cannot tie $6.43B, $9.23B, $20.21B and $145.0M back to line items. Every number on the page cites one source block.
fix: Add the XBRL line-item tag next to each figure in the source footnote (for example, PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, NetIncomeLoss, CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue, InterestExpense) so each number can be traced. This is a footnote change only; the figures already on the page are unchanged.

where: slides 3 and 4, right-hand callout and bottom callout boxes
issue: Slide 3's callout repeats the chart and the title ('Growth is the first call on resources'), and slide 4's 'What this means for the board' restates the takeaway without adding a number. In both cases the box adds words, not evidence.
fix: Cut slide 3's callout to the three items that are not on the chart (the one-year limitation, the debt gap, the accrual-versus-cash caveat) and delete the repeating headline. On slide 4, replace the three restated bullets with the dollar anchor for each option row (capex unfunded, cash consumed), which is the evidence the grid currently lacks.

issue: The 'ask' is 'Confirm the growth capex plan / Confirm debt, leases and maturities / Propose a floor method, not a level / Choose the payout form' — all owned by the CFO, all 'before next board meeting'. This is a homework list, not a decision. The board cannot approve 'set a floor' when the floor level is unknown; the deck's own headline (slides 1 and 2) promises a number.
fix: Rewrite slide 5's ask to name the two things the board actually decides today: (1) 'Approve the principle: capex funded first, return only cash above the floor' and (2) 'Approve the sizing rule: floor = near-term maturities + minimum operating cash + seasonal swing'. Keep the CFO actions as a separate 'what we will bring back' line.

issue: The title claims '$2.80B of earnings' but the chart labels the third bar 'Earnings left after capex' and the footnote admits 'The $2.80B is a comparison, not free cash flow. Total debt, lease obligations and maturities are in the material and are unverified.' The page presents a hard number the deck itself flags as unverified.
fix: Change the third bar label to 'Net income less capex (unverified, excludes debt and leases)' and add a one-line note under the title: 'This is not free cash flow; $20.21B gross cash is offset by unconfirmed debt, leases and maturities.' Or cut the $2.80B bar until treasury confirms it.

issue: The right-hand box repeats the title in different words ('Growth spending takes most of the year's earnings, and only $2.80B of net income is left after capex') and the two bullets duplicate slide 2's numbers ($6.43B, 69.66%, $9.23B). The page adds no new evidence.
fix: Replace the box with the missing comparison: what 69.66% capex intensity implies against peers or the prior year. If that data is not in the material, cut the box and let the chart stand with a two-line footnote.

issue: The grid is the decision page and it is unreadable: the 'Growth first, then return cash above a floor' row scores 8/9 but the reader cannot see why 2 beats the alternatives, and the right-hand box jumps to '$20.21B cash covers $6.43B capex 3.1x, so scores differ on order of claim, not capacity' — a distinction that undercuts the whole scoring table.
fix: Make the winning row visually dominant (bold border, larger type, one colour), and replace the right-hand box with the single sentence: 'All four options are affordable; the choice is about order of claim — capex first, then surplus.' Cut the 3.1x and $13.78B unless they change the ranking.

issue: The cover has a large empty right half and the deck type, date and team are cramped in the bottom-left corner under a 4-line title. It looks unfinished next to the other pages.
fix: Left-align the title to the same margin as the body pages, move 'Board meeting, November 2026' up next to the subtitle line, and put the recipient or 'Prepared for the Costco board' on the right to balance the page.

issue: 'Cartesian' alignment breaks: the four numbered items have inconsistent vertical spacing, and item 4 ('Choose the payout form') is a single short bullet with no 'what it involves' content, leaving a half-empty row and an orphan column.
fix: Give item 4 a real 'what it involves' line (e.g. 'Compare buyback, special dividend and hybrid on EPS and share price') and align all four rows to one grid with equal gaps.

issue: The three numbered items have unequal weight — item 1 is one bullet, items 2 and 3 are two bullets each — and the 'Decision today' banner duplicates slide 5's ask with different wording ('approve a liquidity floor proposal and surplus-cash return sizing'), so the deck says the ask twice in two versions.
fix: Make all three blocks one bullet each, and change the banner to a single line: 'Decision today: approve the principle and the sizing rule.' Mirror that exact sentence on slide 5.

issue: Numbers are formatted three ways: '6.43' and '9.23' in the chart, '$6.43B' in the box, '$6.43B' and '$20.21B' in slide 4. Also '1 x or 2x' on slide 5's footnote uses 'x' as a word.
fix: Use '$6.43B', '$9.23B', '$20.21B' consistently, including chart labels (add '$B' to the axis). Change slide 5 footnote to 'multiples such as 1x or 2x'.

issue: 'Growth plus returning surplus cash funds warehouses and keeps flexibility' is a hedge — it asserts without evidence and 'keeps flexibility' is filler.
fix: Cut the bullet or replace with the test it passes: 'Funds new warehouses while keeping cash above the floor.'

issue: 'Preliminary' appears on every content page. That is an internal flag, not client-facing.
fix: Remove 'Preliminary' from slides 2–5, or replace with a single confidentiality line on the cover.

where: slide 4, grid 'Qualitative screen: four options on three equal-weight tests (1 to 3, management judgment)'
issue: The entire recommendation rests on a 9-point self-scored qualitative grid with hand-assigned weights and scores. Row 'Growth first, then return cash above a floor' scores 3/3/2 = 8, but 'Keeps flexibility' of 2 versus 3 for 'Keep funding growth only' is unsupported, and row 'Buybacks only' scores 'Uses surplus cash' 3 and 'Keeps flexibility' 2 = 6 — the difference between the winner and the last two options is a single judgment point. There is no dollar value, no per-share impact, no cost of capital anywhere in the deck; a board cannot rank capital allocation options on unweighted integers.

No valuation content exists: no share price, no dividend history, no buyback accretion/dilution math, no ROIC or capex hurdle rate against which 'fund growth first' is justified. Slide 2 states 'Sizing the return needs share price and dividend history' — and then the deck never provides either. A payout recommendation without a per-share value is not actionable.

where: slide 2, item 2 and slide 5, next step 2
issue: The central number is unresolved: '$20.21B gross cash' is stated against unconfirmed debt and leases ('the net of debt and leases is not yet confirmed', 'Treasury to confirm debt, leases and maturities'). Slide 4 then computes '$13.78B of cash sits above one year of capex' and '$20.21B cash covers $6.43B capex 3.1x' — both on gross cash, ignoring debt and leases entirely. Surplus cash cannot be sized before the net position is known; every surplus figure in the deck is provisional.

where: slide 3, bar chart and slide 2, item 1
issue: 'Earnings left after capex' of $2.80B subtracts capex (cash, $6.43B) from net income (accrual, $9.23B) — the footnote itself flags the mismatch ('Capex is cash paid for property and equipment; net income is an accrual figure. The $2.80B is a comparison, not free cash flow'). Mixing cash and accrual bases produces a number that is not earnings, not FCF, and not a distributable amount, yet the title calls it 'leaving $2.80B of earnings' and slide 2 builds the pool on it.

where: slide 4, 'What this means for the board' box
issue: '$13.78B of cash sits above one year of capex' — one year of capex is not a liquidity floor. No near-term maturities, minimum operating cash, or seasonal swing is quantified before this number is presented; slide 5 admits the floor method is not built yet ('Build the floor bottom-up: near-term maturities, minimum operating cash and seasonal swings').

The scoring basis assigns 'Put capfirst' 3 to two options and 1 to two options with no stated threshold, and 'Buybacks only' and 'Special dividend only' receive identical 1/3/2 = 6 scores, making the bottom half of the grid non-discriminating decoration. No sensitivity is shown: reweighting 'Keeps flexibility' to 2 for all options or changing one score flips the winner.

Three bars on a common $B axis is defensible (zero baseline, one unit, one period), but only one fiscal year is shown ('Only fiscal 2026 is in the material'). A single year cannot establish that 'growth comes first' is a policy rather than a snapshot; no prior-year capex, net income, dividend or buyback is shown for trend.

The deck asks the board to 'Approve management to set a floor and size the return' while every input needed for sizing — debt schedule, floor method, payout form, share price, dividend history — is still to be produced. The recommendation is a decision to decide later; there is no quantified downside case for what happens if capex exceeds plan or cash falls below the floor.

where: slide 4, left grid versus right box
issue: The grid and the 'What this means for the board' box use different type treatment and the grid's footer note 1 ('Scale: 1 = weak fit, 3 = strong fit; three criteria, equal weight...') is visually detached from the scores it governs. On slide 3 the footnote explaining the cash/accrual mismatch is set at the smallest size on the page while the title asserts '$2.80B of earnings'.

Slide 1 carries the deck date ('Board meeting, November 2026') while every data page is marked 'Preliminary' with no as-of valuation date and no page numbers reference an appendix; the tabs read 'Meshpool' rather than the bank's name.

Capex of $6.43B is 69.66% of $9.23B net income, so earnings left after capex are $2.80B. But the subtitle says 'leaving $2.80B of earnings' and the sidebar says '$2.80B of earnings remains after capex'. That is a subtraction, not earnings remaining; it is the difference between net income and capex and is not a cash return pool. Naming it 'earnings' makes the board think $2.80B is available to return.
fix: Retitle slide 3 to 'Fiscal 2026 capex took 69.66% of net income, leaving $2.80B of net income after capex' and relabel the $2.80B figure as 'residual income after capex' throughout. Delete the word 'earnings' on slide 3.

issue: The page claims cash is unconfirmed and 'surplus cannot be sized yet', but the chart presents cash, net income and capex as three comparable bars. The visual contradicts the caveat and lets a reader treat cash as free.
fix: Replace the three-bar chart with a waterfall: net income $9.23B minus capex $6.43B = $2.80B residual, then show cash $20.21B as a separate, labelled balance with the note 'unconfirmed until treasury reports debt, leases and maturities'. Remove the 3.14x coverage framing until that confirmation exists.

issue: The answer the board needs — the floor method and the payout form — is not in the deck. Slide 4 says 'The minimum cash floor is the open decision' and slide 5 admits 'No floor level is proposed yet'. The deck asks for approval to decide later, which is a deferral, not a recommendation.
fix: Put the floor method on slide 4 as the recommendation (e.g. 'Floor = near-term maturities + minimum operating cash + seasonality buffer'), and on slide 5 make the ask specific: 'Approve the floor method and authorise management to size a return within the $X range by the next meeting', using figures already in the material where possible.

issue: The options grid scores four options on three criteria but uses no chart. The scores are the message and they are hidden in a table with shading. A reader cannot see that 'Growth first, then return cash above a floor' wins without reading every cell.
fix: Keep the table but add a small ranked bar or dot chart to the right of the grid showing total scores (8, 7, 6, 6). Highlight the 8 in the accent colour used on slide 3. Cut the two-sentence 'What this means for the board' box to one sentence: 'Funding capacity is not the constraint; the floor is the decision.'

issue: Point 2 says 'Net cash is unconfirmed until treasury reports debt, leases and maturities' and 'surplus cannot be sized yet'. Point 3 says 'Sizing the return needs share price and dividend history'. These are caveats, not findings, and they undercut the decision on the same page.
fix: Move the caveats to a single footnote line under the three findings and replace point 3 with a claim, e.g. 'The board must set the liquidity floor before any return is sized', with the two supporting facts that are already in the deck.

issue: Title runs to two lines and repeats the cover almost verbatim: 'Fund growth first, then return only cash above a liquidity floor set by the board'. Nothing on the page proves the 'set by the board' clause — that is a decision, not a finding.
fix: Retitle slide 2 to 'Capex absorbed 69.66% of net income in fiscal 2026; return cash only above a board-set floor'. Keep it to one line at the existing font size. Cut 'set by the board' from the title and put it in the first finding.

issue: The right-hand 'What this means for the board' box has two sentences and a lot of dark fill. The page is half empty below the grid and the box is decorative weight.
fix: Shrink the box to one sentence and move it directly under the grid. Use the freed space to add the ranked-score chart from the visuals issue. Align the grid's left edge with the title's left edge; it currently starts further left.

issue: The footnote runs to five lines and includes 'so whether $6.43B is a step-up or steady state is not established', which is a research gap dressed as a footnote.
fix: Move the research gap to slide 5 as an explicit next step: 'Research: confirm whether $6.43B capex is steady state or a step-up.' Keep slide 3's footnote to two lines.

issue: 'Choose the payout form' has no detail under 'What it involves' — just the single phrase 'Payout form chosen'. It is the only row without substance and looks unfinished.
fix: Add one line under 'What it involves': 'Decide buyback vs special dividend vs both, and the size range.' If the size cannot be set yet, say so explicitly and name what is needed to set it.

issue: The cover has a large empty area below the subtitle. The subtitle asks a question the deck answers, but the cover does not state the recommended answer.
fix: Move the answer onto the cover as a single line under the title: 'Recommendation: fund capex first, then return cash above a board-set liquidity floor.' Keep the question as a smaller sub-line.

issue: The decision page asks the board to 'Propose a floor method, not a level' and 'Choose the payout form' with no method and no payout form proposed; the only item not deferred to the CFO is 'Payout form chosen'. Footnote 1 says 'No floor level is proposed yet... and the board sets the multiple.' A board cannot approve a return it cannot size.
fix: Add a recommended floor method and a worked level on slide 5: e.g. floor = 12 months of debt, lease and maturity obligations (to be confirmed by treasury) plus minimum operating cash, and show the implied surplus from the $20.21B of cash at 2026-08-30. If the maturities schedule is unavailable, label the level 'illustrative' and give the range, not a single number.

issue: The scores are unsourced judgment ('Score: 1 = weak fit, 3 = strong fit; three criteria, equal weight; maximum total is 9') and the weights are arbitrary: 'Funds new warehouses', 'Uses surplus cash' and 'Keeps flexibility' are equal-weighted with no basis. A committee will attack this first.
fix: Replace the 1-3 scores with quantifiable metrics per option: e.g. cash remaining after each option, capex coverage, and debt/lease/maturity headroom, and state the weighting rationale in the footnote.

issue: 'Cash covers capex 3.1x ($20.21B vs $6.43B), so funding capacity is not the constraint.' The 3.1x is cash divided by one year of capex only; slide 3 footnote 1 concedes 'Figures cover one year only, so whether $6.43B is a step-up or steady state is not established.' The statement overstates the evidence.
fix: Restate as 'Cash at 2026-08-30 covers one year of capex 3.1x; multi-year coverage depends on the capex plan and maturity schedule, to be confirmed by treasury (slide 5, items 1-2).'

issue: No share count, share price, dividend history, payout ratio or buyback capacity anywhere; slide 2 says 'Sizing the return needs share price and dividend history' but never provides it, and slide 4 footnote 1 says 'Any capex multiple shown in the notes is an illustration only'. There is no per-share or total-return figure for the board to approve.
fix: Add one page showing the return sized in dollars and per share: surplus above the proposed floor, at the current share price and share count, with the existing dividend compared. Mark all inputs as sourced or estimate.

issue: Cash ($20.21B), net income ($9.23B) and capex ($6.43B) are plotted as a single bar series, but the subtitle itself says 'Cash is a balance; net income is accrual' — one period type mandate is violated, since cash is a point-in-time balance and the other two are flow measures. The chart also presents capex at only 31.8% of cash, visually burying the $6.43B relative to the $20.21B.
fix: Split into two panels: (1) flows — net income and capex for fiscal 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30, with capex/net income = 69.66% labelled; (2) balance — cash at 2026-08-30 of $20.21B as a separate single bar, with the balance-versus-flow distinction in the axis labels.

issue: 'Fiscal 2026 capex took 69.66% of net income, leaving $2.80B of earnings' — the $2.80B is net income minus capex ($9.23B - $6.43B), which is not a cash measure and is not free cash flow; footnote 1 concedes affordability is not shown.
fix: Retitle to 'Fiscal 2026 capex of $6.43B was 69.66% of $9.23B net income; net income less capex was $2.80B' and state explicitly that this is not free cash flow.

issue: Column header reads 'Total (of 9)' but the three criteria at 3 points each only total 9; the maximum is correct, but slide 4's right-hand panel then asserts 'Cash covers capex 3.1x' using the same $6.43B and $20.21B already used on slide 3 — the same figure is presented as both a scoring input and a conclusion with no link.
fix: Cross-reference the slide 3 figures in the slide 4 footnote and delete the duplicated capex multiple from the right panel, or move it to the page where it is sourced.

issue: 1 No source or footnote on the cover, and the deck is unstamped apart from 'Board meeting, November 2026'; slides 2-5 are marked Preliminary but this is dated after the 10-K filing of 2026-10-07.
fix: Add 'Source: Costco 10-K filed 2026-10-07 (SEC XBRL)' and the preparer/date line to slide 1.

where: slide 4, "Cash of $20.2B is 3x capex, so a measured payout is affordable" and slide 5 step 3 "Size the surplus and compare a buyback with a special dividend"
issue: The deck recommends sizing a buyback or special dividend without the share price or payout history. Without them you cannot state a payout, a yield or a per-share figure, so the recommendation is not actionable for a board. The $46/share line is cash per share, not a return figure.
fix: Pull share price as of a dated close and the annual dividend per share ($/share) and buyback history ($ and shares) from Costco's 10-K or press releases, and state the liquidity floor ($B) management would set. Until then, slide 4's title must not claim affordability; make it "Cash of $20.2B funds growth and leaves room for a measured payout, subject to pricing".

issue: The waterfall on slide 3 is your strongest single claim — $9.23B net income, less $6.43B capex, $2.8B left — but it sits after the summary and repeats the summary's point 1 ("Growth capex of $6.43B takes about 70% of $9.23B net income"). Two slides make the same point.
fix: Move the waterfall evidence into slide 2 as the exhibit that proves the executive summary, and replace slide 3 with the options-vs-criteria page. Now slide 3 earns its place by weighing choices rather than repeating arithmetic.

issue: Slides 3 and 4 both argue affordability — page 3 says growth leaves $2.8B, page 4 says cash is 3x capex. A board will read these as one point stated twice with different numbers, and will ask which number to trust.
fix: Make slide 3 the decision page: four options against three criteria (funds growth, uses surplus, keeps flexibility), with the combined growth-plus-surplus option called out. Keep the affordability arithmetic on slide 2 only.

where: slide 4, "$20.21B cash, 3.1x cash to capex, $145M interest expense, and 64x net income to interest"
issue: The 3.1x and 64x ratios and the $46/share figure are derived in the deck, but the underlying values are not all in your cited facts — the model must show the formulas, not the presenter doing mental arithmetic on stage.
fix: Put the source cells and formulas in the exhibit notes (cash/capex = 20.21/6.43; net income/interest = 9.23/0.145; cash/shares = 20.21/0.4431). Label each ratio "derived from F3, F4, F5, F6".

where: slide 4, "Scores are board-level judgment and labelled as such"
issue: Board-level judgment scores with no basis are the weakest thing in a board pack. They invite the obvious challenge — "on what criteria and weighting?" — and you have no answer in the material.
fix: Add a scoring basis (three criteria, equal weight, 1-3 scale) and show the weights in the exhibit. If no basis exists, cut the numeric scores and show the options as pros/cons with a stated recommendation.

where: slide 2 exec summary note "payout size is [GAP: share price, dividend and buyback history]"
issue: A [GAP] tag visible on the board page reads as unfinished work. The board should see a stated assumption or a research line, not a placeholder.
fix: Replace the bracketed GAP with one line: "Payout size requires share price and dividend history; management to return with sizing by the next meeting." Keep the gap in your working file, not the deck.

issue: Title and subtitle are topic labels, not a claim. The cover should already tell the board the answer.
fix: Title: "Costco capital allocation: fund growth first, return surplus cash after a liquidity floor". Subtitle keeps the question and date.

where: slide 5 "Set the liquidity floor, size the surplus and decide the payout form"
issue: The closing has steps but no decision ask and no date, so the board leaves without a clear action item.
fix: Add a decision line: "Decision requested: approve management to size a surplus-cash return by the next board meeting." Date the next meeting and name the CFO as owner for steps 1-3.

issue: The recommendation is asserted, not derived. Slide 2 says 'return surplus only after setting a liquidity floor' but nothing in the deck defines the floor, so 'surplus' is undefined. Slide 4 says '$20.21B cash is 3x capex, so a measured payout is affordable' and 'the combined option scores highest,' but 3.1x cash-to-capex does not prove affordability — it ignores working capital, debt maturities and rent/lease obligations, none of which are in the material. The conclusion does not follow from the numbers shown.
fix: On Slide 4, replace 'the combined option scores highest' with the criteria test that actually drives it (funds warehouses, retains flexibility) and state explicitly that the minimum cash floor is the open variable. On Slide 2, phrase the recommendation as 'fund growth first; return only cash above a floor to be set at [X]' and flag the floor as the decision the board is making, not a given.

where: Slide 2 'payout size is [GAP: share price, dividend and buyback history]'; Slide 4 '$46 per share... size of any buyback is [GAP: share price]'; Slide 5 'using the share price and history [GAP]'
issue: The core deliverable — how much cash to return and in what form — is unsized across three slides. '$46 per share' is derived from $20.21B / 443.1M, but it is cash per share, not a payout. A board cannot approve a return with no size and no form.
fix: Do not put a payout recommendation on the slides until the research is in. Either add the missing facts (share price, current dividend, buyback history, debt/lease obligations) as sourced research before building, or restate the recommendation as 'authorize management to size a return by [date]' — which Slide 2 already half-says — and remove the '$46 per share' line from Slide 4 because it invites a payout-per-share question you cannot answer.

issue: 'Warehouse growth takes 70% of earnings and leaves $2.8B of free profit' treats capex of $6.43B as a deduction from net income of $9.23B. Capex is cash for property and equipment; net income is accrual after depreciation, interest and tax. The speaker note admits this ('not a like-for-like deduction') but the slide title and waterfall still present $9.23B − $6.43B = $2.80B as if it were free cash flow. That is a mixed-basis bridge a committee will attack line by line.
fix: Retitle Slide 3 to describe cash uses, not 'free profit.' Replace the net-income-minus-capex bridge with either (a) a simple capex-vs-net-income comparison labelled as two separate figures, or (b) a proper cash bridge that starts from cash from operations (not supplied) — if (b), flag cash from operations as required research. Do not label $2.80B 'free profit.'

issue: 'interest expense is only $145M' and '64x net income to interest' are used to argue a payout is affordable, but interest coverage on net income is not a leverage measure. With cash of $20.21B and interest expense of $145M, the missing figure is debt outstanding — and no debt balance is in the material. A committee will ask total debt, lease obligations and maturities before blessing a return.
fix: On Slide 4, drop '64x net income to interest' or relabel it clearly as a coverage metric, and add a line 'total debt and lease obligations: [research required]' so the affordability case rests on net cash, not a coverage ratio. If debt cannot be sourced, remove the affordability claim and substitute 'cash balance is $20.21B' as a fact only.

where: Slides 2, 3 and 4 — revenue $303.15B, net income $9.23B, capex $6.43B, cash $20.21B are all fiscal 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30
issue: All figures trace to a single 10-K. There is no prior-year comparison anywhere — no growth rate for capex, net income or revenue — so the board cannot judge whether $6.43B of capex is a step-up or steady state, which is the entire question ('keep funding warehouse growth'). A single-period snapshot cannot support a resource-allocation decision.
fix: Add fiscal 2025 (and if available 2024) revenue, net income and capex to Slides 3 and 4 as a comparison column, sourced to the same or prior 10-K. If those figures cannot be sourced, state on Slide 3 that the $6.43B capex is a single-period figure with no trend established, and downgrade any growth claim in the title.

issue: The four options are scored against three criteria ('funds new warehouses, uses surplus cash, keeps flexibility') on 'board-level judgment.' No scoring scale, no weighting, and no number. Slide 4's callout ('the combined option scores highest') is an opinion dressed as a result. The grid will not survive a committee that asks how the scores were set.
fix: Either give the grid a defined 3-point scale and show the score per cell with the criteria weighted, or cut the scoring and present the four options as a qualitative trade-off table with a stated rationale per cell. Do not claim a 'highest' score without a scale.

issue: The next steps ask the board to 'set the minimum cash floor against the $20.21B balance' and 'size the surplus' with no method for either. A floor is not a number to be voted on — it needs a basis (weeks of capex, working capital, debt maturities), none of which is in the material.
fix: On Slide 5 step 2, replace 'set the minimum cash floor against the $20.21B balance' with a defined basis, e.g. 'set the floor at [X] months of the $6.43B annual capex run-rate (= $Y)' and source the multiple as an assumption to be approved. If no basis is sourced, state the floor is to be calibrated with treasury and flag it as an open item.

issue: 'cash is about $46 per share, derived' — the derivation ($20.21B / 443.1M = $45.6) shares a per-share figure that implies a payout capacity, but the slide has no share price and no payout size. It raises a question it cannot answer.
fix: Either add the share price and show cash-per-share against price-per-share to frame the payout, or cut the $46 line from Slide 4 until the research is in.

issue: 'capex is 2.1% of $303.15B revenue; net margin is 3.0%' — both ratios are correct ($6.43B/$303.15B = 2.12%; $9.23B/$303.15B = 3.05%), but they sit next to a capex-vs-net-income comparison and invite the same mixed-basis confusion. Also, a 3.0% net margin is thin for a retailer and the slide does not comment on it.
fix: Keep the ratios but label them 'margins / intensity' and add one line interpreting the 3.0% net margin (thin-margin model means cash generation, not margin, funds returns) so the committee reads the right signal.

issue: Both slides make the same argument: that growth capex is the priority and cash is the source of any return. Slide 3 shows capex at 70% of net income.
