A negative spread of 2.04 points is consistent with a yield near the 2.45% low-price case and a cost of cash well above 1.88%, which contradicts the 1.88% used everywhere else on slides 3 and 4. The reader cannot reconcile the two.
fix: Show the arithmetic in the row: the yield used, the after-tax cost of cash used, and the resulting spread, all matching the 1.88% on slides 3 and 4. If the cost of cash assumption differs by case, put both cases in one line.

where: slide 4, right-hand panel '22.2% Growth return on capital, FY2026 (actual) / 1.88% Buyback earnings yield at $1,106.21 (actual) / 2.45% Buyback yield at the $850.00 52-week low (calc)'
issue: The 2.45% low-price case invites the obvious objection - if the stock falls to $850 the buyback yield beats any cost of cash - and the page never answers it. The left callout says 'surplus cash belongs in warehouses' but the third figure undercuts that.
fix: Add one line under the 2.45% figure: 'even at the 52-week low the buyback yield is below the 22.2% earned on warehouse capital', or delete the 2.45% tile. Do not leave a counter-argument standing without a response.

where: slide 3, right panel, 'The $30 special dividend costs $13.29B on 443.1M shares and retires no shares'
issue: $30 x 443.1M shares is $13.29B, so the number is right, but slide 2 says FY2026 free cash flow is $9.38B. The deck shows $13.29B of dividend against $9.38B of free cash flow and never explains the $3.9B gap or how it is funded, beyond the $20.21B cash balance mentioned on slide 3.
fix: Add the funding line to slide 2: '$13.29B dividend against $9.38B free cash flow, funded from the $20.21B cash balance', so the board sees the cash draw and the remaining buffer in one place.

where: slide 5, 'Approve the $4B buyback authorisation' as next step 1
issue: Next step 1 still asks the board to approve the authorisation while step 2 is 'Confirm record and payment dates' for a dividend the title already says is declared, and step 3 is quarterly reporting. Steps 2 and 3 are administrative and dilute a single-ask page.
fix: Keep the ask as one numbered line with owner and date, and move record/payment dates and quarterly reporting into a short 'administration' note beneath the table, or cut them from this page entirely.

issue: The cover carries the full recommendation as a three-line title plus a two-line subtitle that repeats it almost verbatim ('Approve the $4B buyback authorisation; the $30 dividend is already declared' then 'Approve the $4B buyback authorisation. The $30 special dividend is already declared.'). The lower half of the cover is empty and the title runs to the left edge of the text block with the blue rule floating above it.
fix: Shorten the cover title to 'Renew the $4B buyback authorisation' with the dividend, date and audience in the subtitle, and pull the block down the page so the white space sits above rather than below. Cut the duplicated sentence in the subtitle.

issue: The left panel is mostly empty: 'Return per dollar deployed, FY2026, % return per dollar' then two values, 22.2% and 1.88%, floating in white space with a hairline under the first. It reads as a half-finished chart next to a dense text column.
fix: Either turn the left panel into a proper two-bar chart at full height, or move the two figures into the right-hand argument as a single comparison line and give the whole page to one column. Do not ship a half-empty panel.

where: slide 2, 'Preliminary' and footnotes; slide 2 row titles
issue: The page is stamped 'Preliminary' on a board paper going to a decision today, and the footnotes carry drafting residue: '(E)' used for management estimates and 'the 5.2% cash return is an assumption on idle cash, not a stated fact'. The row titles hedge with '(actual)' and '(E)' on every line.
fix: Remove 'Preliminary' from the running head once the deck is for the meeting. Move assumptions into one clearly labelled assumptions box rather than inline caveats, and drop '(actual)' from row titles since actual is the default.

issue: Slide 1 title 'Approve the $4B buyback authorisation; the $30 dividend is already declared' and slide 3's callout 'The $4B is the authorisation, not a return-maximising choice: a larger programme needs a new board approval. Growth is the best use: 22.2% after-tax return on capital, well above the 1.88% buyback yield.' contradict each other: the cover asks the board to approve a buyback while the only analytical page argues growth beats the buyback by 20.3 points.
fix: Replace slide 1's title with a decision the analysis supports, e.g. 'Reauthorise the $4B programme as a residual-capital backstop; the $30 dividend is already declared' and add one subtitle line stating the programme is capped at $4B and deployed only after FY2026 capex, funded from the $20.21B cash balance.

issue: The 22.2% and the 1.88% are not measured on the same basis, but slides 3 and 4 both compare them: footnote 1 on each page reads 'The 22.2% is a whole-company after-tax return on book capital (equity $35.808B + long-term debt $3.918B), not a measured incremental return on new warehouses' while footnote 2 reads 'The 1.88% is an earnings yield (EPS / price), not a return on invested capital'. The slide 4 title 'a buyback earns 1.88% on the same basis' is therefore false.
fix: Either recast both on the same numerator/denominator (incremental after-tax cash return on incremental warehouse capital vs. EPS/price on the retirement) or restate the slide 4 title to 'Growth returns 22.2% on book capital; the buyback yields 1.88% on price' and move the differing-basis footnotes into the body of the page.

issue: 'Retiring shares earns 1.88%, the earnings yield at $1,106.21' and 'Even at the 52-week low of $850.00 the earnings yield is only 2.45% on EPS of $20.83' do not tie: $20.83/1,106.21 = 1.88% and $20.83/850.00 = 2.45%, but footnote 3 on slide 4 states 'the 10-K diluted EPS of $20.76 gives 2.44%' at the $850.00 low. Two different EPS figures are used on the same comparison without reconciliation.
fix: Pick one EPS, state which it is in the footnote, and show the per-share math on the page: e.g. 'EPS $20.83 (LTM diluted) / $1,106.21 = 1.88%; / $850.00 = 2.45%.' Delete the $20.76/2.44% variant or footnote the difference between the 10-K diluted and LTM figures.

issue: A two-bar exhibit without a zero baseline or axis scale - 'Return per dollar deployed, FY2026 / % return per dollar' with bars for '22.2% Warehouse growth' and '1.88% Buyback'. The two bars are drawn at visual heights that imply a far larger ratio than 11.8x and there is no y-axis.
fix: Set the y-axis 0-25% with 5% gridlines, label each bar with its value, and add a source line 'Company after-tax ROIC; EPS/price - see footnotes.'

issue: The section header reads 'Warehouse programme NPV and IRR over 5 and 10 years' but the only content is 'Per-dollar IRR is 22.2% (actual company-level return on capital)'. The 22.2% is an accounting return, not an IRR over a 5- or 10-year cash flow, and no NPV is shown anywhere in the deck. Header and content do not match.
fix: Either delete the header and open the row as 'Company-level after-tax return on capital: 22.2% (actual)', or produce the 5- and 10-year warehouse cash-flow IRR and NPV actually called for and put them in the row with the discount rate and terminal-value assumption stated.

where: slide 2, row 3 and closing slide 5 item 1
issue: Slide 2 row 3 labels the buyback comparison 'earnings yield less after-tax cost of cash: the spread is negative 2.04 points', but the callout and the closing page both recommend approving the buyback. The page states the return on the action is below its funding cost and never resolves the conflict.
fix: Choose one: if the spread is negative 2.04 points against 2.5% cash, change the recommendation to 'Do not approve the buyback; hold the $20.21B for capex and the dividend.' If the recommendation stands on optionality or the January 2027 expiry, add a line stating it: 'Approving does not require deploying; the authorisation is a backstop with no return obligation.'

issue: Retired-share and cost figures move between pages without a reconciliation: slide 5 item 1 says reauthorising to January 2030 'at the $1,106.21 close the programme will retire 3.6M shares, 0.8% of the 443.1M outstanding', which costs $3.98B, yet slide 3 says every $1B retires 0.90M shares / 0.20% of the 443.1M - i.e. $4B retires 3.6M shares / 0.81%. On slide 2 or 4, add one line: 'the $6.5B capex plan is FY2026 spend; the $4B authorisation and $30 dividend are FY2027 actions, so they are not competing for the same period's cash.'

issue: No comparables, precedents or valuation range anywhere in the deck. issue: The street source is weaker than the filing. F100 and F101 cite finance.yahoo.com for 'declared a special cash dividend of $30 per share' and 'reauthorized a $4b share repurchase program with an expiration date in January 2030', while F112 (the 10-Q) says the authorisation is '$4,000 approved by our Board of Directors in January 2023, which expires in January 2027'. One says January 2030, the other January 2027; the slide 5 footnote repeats 'reauthorised to January 2030'. The committee will ask which filing governs.

where: slide 3, closing sentence of the argument

There is no analysis of whether the $6.5B capex plan is itself the best use of the marginal dollar (new warehouses vs. remodels, payback, lease vs. own), and no downside case for the 22.2%.

If kept, add one line on what the $4B would earn if retained, sourced: e.g., 'management's current intention is $6,500 for fiscal 2026 (F98); spend through the first thirty-six weeks of 2026 was $4,228 (F98).' where: slide 4 right argument, operating lease liabilities $2.61B; F76

issue: Only the buyback-yield sensitivity is planned (2.44% at $850.00, 1.88% at $1,106.21). A board approves capital allocation against ranges, not single points.
fix: Add a three-column sensitivity to slide 4 (not a new slide): 'price $850.00 / $1,106.21' × 'capex $6.5B / $8.0B' showing shares retired and remaining cash, and one line on what happens if growth returns are 15% instead of 22.2%. Use only figures already in the material plus the research below.

issue: The cover carries $490.19B market cap derived as '$1,106.21 x 443.1M shares' (F91), but 443.1M is shares outstanding at 2026-09-29 and the price is at 2026-11-13; the product is a market value at a mixed date, and no diluted share count is used even though diluted EPS of $20.76 (F78) implies dilution.
fix: Footnote the cover: '$490.19B = $1,106.21 (close 2026-11-13) × 443.1M shares outstanding (2026-09-29); diluted share count not disclosed in the excerpt.' Or replace with a dated market cap from a primary source.

issue: Title says 'Growth returns 22.2% after tax; a buyback returns 1.9% and cash 5.2%', but the exhibit labels are '22.2%', '5.2', '1.9%' with mixed percent formatting ('5.2' has no % sign) and the cash bar has no source. Inconsistent units on one exhibit.
fix: Render all three bars as '22.2%', '5.2%', '1.9%' with sources under each; no bare '5.2'.

issue: Slide 1 title is a question ('return more cash or fund more warehouses?') and the exec summary adds 'and hold capex at about $6.5B' — the page recommends but never states the answer the title asked. The answer first is only in the box on slide 3.
fix: Retitle slide 2 'Approve the $13.3B special dividend; pace the $4B buyback; hold capex at $6.5B' and add one bolded line under it that says growth clears the 5.15% cash rate by 17.1 points, so the cash is genuinely surplus — move that claim up from slide 3.

issue: The 1.88% vs 5.15% comparison ignores the 5.15% cost of the debt-free cash it uses, so the number is not comparable to the 22.20% on slide 3 and a committee will attack it (as your own footnote admits, it is not a return on capital).
fix: Replace 'A buyback earns 1.88% against 5.15% on cash' with 'Buyback EPS yield 1.88% vs 5.15% cash — free cash flow remains positive at $9.38B' and repeat the free-cash-flow number in that row so the decision rests on cover, not yield alone.

where: slide 3, right-hand claim 'Every $1 kept in the business earned 22.2% after tax in FY2026'
issue: The 22.2% is a historical blended book return, but the title and claim read as the forward return on the next warehouse. Your footnote 1 concedes the forward return is not disclosed. That is the single unsupported number on which the recommendation rests.
fix: Either retitle to 'Growth earns 22.2% on capital, cash earns 5.15%' — matching the actual historical basis — and add the words 'FY2026 actual' under the 22.20% bar, or research the forward warehouse-level return and use it. Do not let the title imply a forward return you do not have.

issue: Two bars of unequal meaning (an ROIC on $1 and a treasury yield) share one axis with no benchmark line; 22.20% and 5.15% are printed as numbers so the bars add no information, and 80% of the panel is white space.
fix: Replace with a two-column figure: left column $1 invested in a warehouse returning 22.20% and $1 in cash returning 5.15%, with the 17.1-point gap annotated between them. That makes the comparison legible without the 8pt footnote.

issue: Three numbered points with a combined five short bullets leave roughly 40% of the page dead white space, and the boxes do not share a baseline. Half-empty pages read as unfinished to a board.
fix: Widen each row into a small table: Action | Cash impact | Basis, with rows 'Special dividend', 'Buyback', 'Capex'. Move the FY2026 capex of $6.43B and 29 warehouses planned / 16 opened into that row and delete the footnote duplication.

issue: Both titles wrap to two lines and break mid-phrase ('draws it to / $2.9B', 'post- / payment'), and both titles sit at a different height than the one-line titles on slides 2 and 3. Inconsistent title position and orphaned prepositions read as rushed.
fix: Set all content title widths to one standard and shorten so each fits one or two clean lines: slide 4 'Dividend and buyback cut cash from $20.2B to $2.9B'; slide 5 'Approve today; pace the buyback; report cash quarterly'. Lock the title baseline on all pages.

issue: 'The buffer thins to 0.4x capex, but $9.38B of free cash flow refills the cash balance in under a year' — that is the page's real so-what and it sits in a grey side box, while the body is a table of items that do not change across the three columns (debt, leases, interest expense). The point is buried next to the only numbers that matter.
fix: Move the takeaway into the title: 'Dividend and buyback cut cash to $2.9B (0.4x capex), refilled by $9.38B free cash flow within a year'. Collapse the debt, leases and interest rows into one line plus a footnote; the table then shows only what changes.

issue: There is no decision to make on the next-steps page: row 1 says the board has already declared the dividend, so 'Approve today' has nothing left to approve, and row 3's disclosure has no cadence start date or metric set. Next steps without a dated first action are not a close.
fix: State in row 1 exactly what the board is being asked to do today (e.g. ratify the declared $30 payment date and the $4B authorization), and in row 3 fix the first disclosure to the Q1 FY2027 release with the metrics named: total cash, total debt, free cash flow, buyback shares repurchased.

issue: 'Hold capex at the $6.5B intention; growth earns 22.2%' repeats the slide 3 headline verbatim and dilutes the decision page.
fix: Cut the clause after the semicolon; keep 'Hold capex at the $6.5B intention' and let slide 3 carry the return.

issue: Mixed terms for one thing: 'cash', 'cash and equivalents', and 'the post-payment position'. Also 'programme' versus 'program' and 'authorise' versus 'authorize' on slide 2.
fix: Pick one term per concept across the deck: 'cash and equivalents' on every balance reference, 'position' only in the disclosure row. Use US spellings throughout (program, authorize).

where: Slide 3, exhibit 'Growth earns 22.2% on capital, cash earns 5.15%'
issue: The decision rests on 22.2% after-tax return on capital (operating income $11.69B x (1 - 24.7%) / equity $35.808B), which is a historical FY2026 book return on total equity, not the return on the next warehouse. The page's own footnote concedes this: 'The forward return on the next warehouse is not disclosed.' You are comparing a backward-looking blended equity return to a 5.15% risk-free yield and calling the 17.1-point gap the basis for the recommendation. The footnote tries to fix it, but the headline still asserts 22.2% as though it were the marginal return.
fix: Restate slide 3's headline as 'Historical FY2026 after-tax return on equity was 22.2%; the forward return on incremental warehouse capital is not disclosed', relabel the 22.20% bar 'FY2026 after-tax return on equity (historical, company-wide)', and add a bar or callout for the marginal/forward return on the 16 opened and 13 planned FY2026 warehouses. The right-hand column already says it is 'a plan, not a disclosed return' — either source the forward return or remove the 22.2% vs 5.15% comparison as the deciding evidence.

where: Slide 4 left column vs right callout box
issue: The 'Free cash flow (FY2026) $9.38B' row is shown flat across all three columns (Pre-payout, Post-dividend, Post-buyback) as if it repeats at $9.38B. Footnote 1 states the 2030 column is 'the full-draw case', but there is no year-by-year bridge showing whether $9.38B of annual FCF actually refills the $2.9B balance 'under a year' as the callout box claims. The $9.38B is a single-period figure printed three times.
fix: Footnote or qualify the $9.38B row as 'FY2026 free cash flow, held flat for illustration only', and add a small table row showing cumulative FCF from Dec 2026 to Nov 2030 versus the $4B buyback draw to demonstrate when the $2.9B low-point is reached and when it is refilled. If the refill timing cannot be sourced, remove 'under a year' from the callout box or change it to 'subject to annual free cash flow generation.'

issue: The two bars are explicitly labelled in footnote 2 as 'not like-for-like: 22.2% is a historical after-tax book return on capital... 5.15% is the US 10-year Treasury yield'. A chart whose own footnote says the two bars are not comparable should not be the central exhibit of the recommendation. The 5.15% is a market yield and the 22.2% is an accounting return — mixing an equity book return with a Treasury yield on the same axis is a unit mismatch dressed as a comparison.
fix: Replace the two-bar chart with a proper capital-allocation comparison: show the after-tax return on the next warehouse (or the marginal ROIC range) against the company's weighted average cost of capital, or show the after-tax yield on cash at 5.15% versus the after-tax ROIC. If neither can be sourced, demote this page to a backup and put the cash bridge on slide 2.

issue: 'the $4B program earns an EPS yield of 1.88%, below the 5.15% cash rate' compares an EPS yield (earnings/price, = 1/PE) on the $106.21 buyback price against a Treasury yield, and footnote 2 admits it is 'shown separately as an EPS yield, not a return on capital.' That is a defensible framing but the two numbers on the same page sit under a headline about 'return on capital', so a reader can conflate the 1.88% EPS yield with a capital return.
fix: Label the 1.88% explicitly on the chart/callout as 'EPS yield on the $4B buyback at $106.21' and add the reciprocal (P/E of 53.2x) so the committee sees what the buyback is actually paying for earnings.

issue: 'FY2026 capex was $6.43B' is stated in the past tense against '29 warehouses planned, 16 opened', but slide 3 says the same 16 warehouses 'opened in the first 36 weeks'. The capex figure and the warehouse count are for different periods (full fiscal 2026 capex vs. a 36-week count) and are not reconciled.
fix: Make the period explicit: 'FY2026 capex $6.43B (filed 2026-10-07); 16 of 29 planned warehouses opened through the 36-week period ended 2026-05-10 (Costco 10-Q, filed 2026-06-03).'

issue: 'About 3.6M shares at $1,106.21, 0.8% of shares outstanding' — check the unit. 3.6M shares x $1,106.21 = $3.98B, so the $1,106.21 is a per-share price, but slide 3 footnote 2 uses '$106.21' for the buyback price ('$1B retires 0.90M shares at $1,106.21'). One of the two is a typo. At $1,106.21, $1B retires 0.90M shares and $4B retires 3.6M shares (0.8% of 443.1M shares) — consistent with slide 5 but a share price 10x the $106.21 in slide 3's footnote. $1,106.21 is not a Costco share price.
fix: Reconcile the buyback price across slides 3 and 5. If the buyback price is $1,106.21, correct slide 3's footnote. If it is $106.21, correct slide 5's '$1,106.21' and the 3.6M/0.8% figures — at $106.21, $4B retires 37.7M shares or 8.5% of outstanding, not 0.8%.

issue: Footnote text is set in a size smaller than 8pt (approximately 6-7pt) and runs to four lines on slide 5. On a board book that gets printed and read in the room, footnotes that state the arithmetic basis and the special-dividend contingency ('the board has already declared the dividend') must be legible.
fix: Set footnotes at 8pt minimum and trim slide 5's footnote 1 by moving the derivation of the $13.3B/$6.9B/3.6M figures into slide 4's footnote, leaving the buyback-yield basis on slide 5.

issue: The two bars, 'Warehouse growth (after-tax return on capital, FY2026)' at 22.20% and 'Cash (US 10-year Treasury yield, 2026-11-13)' at 5.15%, are not like-for-like; footnote 1 admits this ('The two bars are not like-for-like'), which undercuts the explicit title 'Growth earns 22.2% on capital, cash earns 5.15%'.
fix: Either (a) retitle to 'Growth returned 22.2% after tax vs 5.15% on cash in FY2026, but the forward warehouse return is not disclosed' and add the words 'FY2026 actual, not forward' on the growth bar, or (b) drop the bar for cash and present the 17.1-point gap as a single figure with the 5.15% rate as a reference line. Do not leave a footnote that contradicts the title.

issue: The right column is half empty: '...but the growth plan is a plan, not a disclosed return' sits at the top, two short bullets fill the middle, and the dark callout box floats in the bottom third. The page reads as two pages stapled together.
fix: Merge the two-column split into a single left-aligned body: put the chart at the top, the two bullets and the callout directly under it, and remove the vertical rule. If the callout must stay, size the body text and chart to fill the column so no gap exceeds 40px.

issue: The footnote on the 22.2% says the underlying is 'operating income $11.698 x (1 - 24.7%) / (equity $35.808 + long-term debt $3.918)', i.e. a historical after-tax book return on capital. The title reads 'Growth earns 22.2% on capital', implying the marginal warehouse earns that. It does not; the footnote later says 'The forward return on the next warehouse is not disclosed.'
fix: Change the title to 'FY2026 after-tax return on capital was 22.2%, not the return on the next warehouse', or state the 22.2% as historical on the bar label.

issue: The 'Post-buyback (by 2030)' column shows a single 'Cash and equivalents $2.91B' row and nothing else changes: Debt, leases and interest are identical across all three columns. The table implies a 2030 cash position, but the caption and footnote 1 say 'the buyback is drawn over time to 2030, so the 2030 column is the full-draw case'. The reader will read the bottom-right cell as a forecast, not a worst case.
fix: Rename the column header to 'Post-buyback, full draw (by 2030)' and add a single line under the table: 'Full draw of the $4B authorization assumed; actual draw depends on the earnings yield test.' Alternatively show the buyback on a per-year draw schedule so the cash path is visible.

issue: The four numbered points carry no so-what beyond the title; point 4's only evidence is 'FY2026 capex was $6.43B', which is roughly the $6.5B intention, so it does not prove why capex should be held, only that it was.
fix: Replace point 4's evidence with the reason: 'Holding capex at $6.5B preserves $X of annual cash capacity after the dividend; raising it now competes with the buyback at an EPS yield of 1.88% versus 5.15% on cash.' Use only figures already in the deck.

issue: 'First tranche sized at the December review' is a sub-bullet under step 2 but there is no date for the December review in the owner/timing column, so the next step has no date.
fix: Add the review date to the owner/timing cell (e.g. 'CFO - December review, buyback tranche sized then'). The deck already references 'December review', so no new research is needed.

issue: The orange highlight bar across the 'Cash and equivalents' row is the only coloured row in the table and reads as a band rather than an emphasis on the number; the key figures ($20.21B, $6.91B, $2.91B) are the same weight as the long-term debt row.
fix: Drop the orange fill and bold the three cash figures instead; put the takeaway clause 'refills in under a year' next to the $2.91B cell rather than only in the grey box below.

issue: 'pace the $4B buyback', 'hold capex at about $6.5B' and 'the gap is 17.1 points a year' use different verbs and units for the same decision. The reader has to translate between pages.
fix: Use one phrase per decision throughout: 'approve the $13.3B special dividend', 'buy back the $4B only when the earnings yield beats 5.15%', 'hold FY2026 capex at $6.5B'. Pick these and reuse them on slides 2, 3, 4 and 5.

issue: The title block sits low with a large empty band above it and the byline rule sits close to the footer; the blue accent bar is the only element above the title.
fix: Raise the title and subtitle by roughly 40-60px to fill the upper third, and keep a consistent title baseline across slides 1-5.

issue: The central comparison is not like-for-like: slide 3 itself footnotes '22.2% is a historical after-tax book return on capital ... the forward return on the next warehouse is not disclosed' and 'The two bars are not like-for-like', yet slides 2, 3 and 5 repeat the '17.1 points' gap as the reason cash is 'surplus' and the reason to buy back shares. A hostile committee will ask why a trailing accounting ROIC is being measured against a forward 10-year Treasury.
fix: Re-label the left bar 'FY2026 historical after-tax return on invested capital, 22.2%' and the right bar 'US 10-year Treasury yield, 5.15%', and add a third bar or stated range for the forward incremental return on the next warehouse cohort with its source; if not disclosed, say so on the bar itself, not only in footnote 1. Remove 'so the company's cash is surplus' from slide 2 bullet 1.

where: slide 2 bullet 4 ('FY2026 capex was $6.43B'), slide 3 chart and callout ('about $6.5B'), slide 4 header ('the $6.5B capex intention')
issue: Capex is stated as $6.43B, $6.5B and $6.5B across three pages, with $6.43B labelled 'FY2026 capex was' and $6.5B labelled 'the company's stated intention for fiscal 2026' in footnote 2. FY2026 is not complete if the latest 10-Q is for the quarter ended 2026-05-10, so '$6.43B was' is an actual-to-date figure, not full-year capex — the two numbers are not the same measure and the cash cover denominator changes with them.
fix: Pick one basis: state 'FY2026 capex intention $6.5B (company-stated, not board-approved, footnote 2)' once on slide 2, use $6.5B as the denominator in slide 4's cover ratio, and if $6.43B is actual capex for the first three quarters of FY2026, label it '9M FY2026 capex $6.43B' and cite the 10-Q.

where: slide 4 table, row 'Cash and equivalents' and cover rows
issue: The bridge is arithmetically consistent ($20.21B - $13.38B = $6.83B, shown as $6.91B; - $4.0B = $2.83B, shown as $2.91B) but the table never shows the $13.38B and $4.0B outflow lines, so the reader cannot tie $20.21B to $6.91B to $2.91B without the footnote. The stated $6.9B and $2.9B round to 0.1, close enough to tie, but the derivation is hidden.
fix: Add two rows to the slide 4 bridge: 'Special dividend (declared) -$13.38B' and 'Share repurchase authorization -$4.00B', so the columns foot: $20.21B - $13.38B = $6.91B; $6.91B - $4.00B = $2.91B. Label the right-hand column 'Post-buyback (by 2030, full draw)' and note the draw is paced, not day one.

where: slide 4 rows 'Free cash flow (FY2026)' of $9.38B shown constant in all three columns
issue: FCF of $9.38B is held flat across the pre-payout, post-dividend and post-buyback columns and used in the callout 'the $9.38B of free cash flow refills the cash balance in under a year'. That is a strong claim resting on a single year's FCF with no source shown for the $9.38B figure, and it ignores that the buyback itself consumes cash while the dividend has already been paid.
fix: Source the $9.38B (FY2026 cash-flow statement, cite the filing) and state whether it is pre- or post-capex. Either replace the flat row with one column-per-period FCF, or delete the row and reword the callout to 'FY2026 free cash flow of $9.38B (source) would refill the post-buyback balance in under a year'.

issue: The buyback's 'EPS yield of 1.88% against 5.15% on cash' compares an accounting EPS accretion to a Treasury yield with no time value, no buyback execution price path, and no rebate for the fact that $18 of shares lifted EPS from $20.76 to $20.80 at the stated $1,106.21 price. Footnote 2 concedes it is 'not a return on capital', yet slide 3's callout uses it as the buyback-last argument without showing the alternative — retaining cash at 5.15% and reinvesting in warehouses at the (undisclosed) forward return.
fix: On slide 3, replace the single '1.88%' figure with a side-by-side of the three uses: buyback EPS yield 1.88%, cash at 5.15%, and the incremental warehouse return (with source or 'not disclosed'); footnote the assumed $1,106.21 buyback price and the 443.1M share count.

issue: The downside is asserted, not shown. Slide 4 says the buffer thins to '0.4x capex' and slide 5 says buy back shares 'only when the 1.88% earnings yield beats the 5.15% cash rate' — but the deck never shows a case where capex rises above $6.5B, FCF falls, or the buyback is suspended. The stated 'refills in under a year' claim is a single point, not a sensitivity.
fix: Add a small sensitivity to slide 4: post-buyback cash of $2.91B against capex of $6.0B / $6.5B / $7.5B and FCF of $8.0B / $9.38B / $10.5B, showing cover in years; mark the downside cells and state the trigger at which the buyback pauses.

issue: Footnote 1 on slide 3 says 'the forward return on the next warehouse is not disclosed' — that is the deck admitting the key input is missing, which belongs in the research plan, not in a footnote. Slide 4 footnote 1 says 'the 2030 column is the full-draw case', which should be in the column header or a note in the callout, not buried.
fix: Move 'forward return on the next warehouse is not disclosed' into a research request and, on slide 3, mark the warehouse bar as 'historical; forward return not disclosed' in the chart label; promote 'full-draw case' to the column header.

issue: Sources are cited (10-K, 10-Q, Yahoo Finance, coinpaper.com, market data 2026-11-13) but the closing slide 5's 3.6M shares and 0.8% of shares outstanding rely on the $1,106.21 price dated 2026-11-13, and the dividend record date is asserted on slides 2, 5 as 'set' with no source for the record date itself.
fix: Add the source and date for the record date on slides 2 and 5, and footnote the 3.6M share / 0.8% calcs on slide 5 to the same $1,106.21 price and 443.1M shares already sourced.

issue: The two bars are not like-for-like, and the footnote admits it: '22.2% is a historical after-tax book return on capital ... the forward return on the next warehouse is not disclosed.' A board member will see the 17.1-point gap as an apples-to-oranges comparison.
fix: Replace the two-bar chart with a like-for-like forward return: state the assumed incremental after-tax return on a new warehouse (or at minimum label the 22.2% as trailing, and add a third bar showing the forward warehouse return once researched). Alternatively, reframe slide 3 as 'Cash is worth returning because new warehouses earn an undisclosed but proven >5.15% after tax' and lead with the $6.5B capex evidence.

issue: The 22.2% return on capital is a claim in the title and the case for the dividend, but the underlying figures ($11.69B operating income, $35.80B capital base) appear only in a footnote. The page needs a bridge table or a two-column reconciliation showing the calculation.
fix: Add a small proof table under the bars: after-tax operating income $11.69B / capital $35.80B = 22.2%; and $1 x 5.15% = 5.15%. Show the arithmetic on the page.

issue: The page has a large dead zone below the 5.15% bar and above the right-hand text; the bars occupy the top third of the left panel and the right panel floats in space. The callout box is anchored to the bottom.
fix: Extend the bars to full width of the left panel, or reduce the chart height and move the right-hand text block to sit directly alongside the bars. Bring the 'Growth first/ Dividend second/ Buyback last' callout immediately under the bars, not at the bottom of the page.

issue: The table says debt and leases stay at $6.52B and the footnote says cover is 'divided by the $6.5B capex intention; it is not a liquidity covenant.' That is a future covenant, not a current one. More importantly, the deck never states the net debt after payout: cash $2.92B minus debt and leases $6.52B = net debt approximately $3.6B. This is the single biggest question a board will ask.
fix: Add a line to slide 4: 'Net debt after payout: cash $2.92B less debt and leases $6.52B = $3.6B net debt.' Then state whether that is acceptable against the company's stated liquidity policy or revolver availability, and cite the covenant or policy figure.

issue: The note says 'cover is divided by the $6.5B capex intention; it is not a liquidity covenant,' but the page provides no real liquidity cushion. A board must judge whether $2.92B cash against $6.52B debt and leases is acceptable.

issue: The next steps are real but the ask is not a true consensus ask: 'Ratify' the dividend (which is already declared) and 'authorize' the buyback, with first tranche 'sized at the December review.' The timing is soft and the owner for the buyback pace is the CFO, not the board.

issue: 'The declared $30 per share special dividend ... and the $4B repurchase authorization ... alongside the $6.5B fiscal 2026 capex intention' is a dense, run-on subtitle. It reads as a topic list, not an answer.
fix: Cut to two clauses: 'Return $13.3B of surplus cash via a $30/share special dividend, and pace the $4B buyback to free cash flow, while holding capex at $6.5B.'

issue: The callout 'Buyback last: the $4B program earns an EPS yield of 1.88%, below the 5.15% cash rate' uses 'earns' for a program that does not earn; it returns. Sloppy verb.

where: slide 3, Exhibit: 'Return on each $1 of capital, after tax' — bars 22.20% vs 5.15%
issue: The entire thesis is a comparison between a 22.2% after-tax return on capital and 5.15% (the 10-year Treasury). Those are not comparable hurdle rates: the correct test for retaining capital is the risk-adjusted cost of equity, not the risk-free rate. Slide 3 footnote 1 admits 'The two bars are not like-for-like', which is an admission the main exhibit is not probative. On a cost of equity of ~9-10% the 22.2% still clears, but the deck never makes that argument, so the headline '17.1-point gap' overstates the case by roughly 7 points.
fix: Replace the 5.15% cash bar with Costco's estimated cost of equity (state and source the build-up: risk-free plus beta times ERP, cite the beta source and ERP date) and re-title slide 3 to the gap versus cost of equity. Keep the Treasury yield only as a footnote reconciling the 5.15% 'earnings on cash' rate to the 10-year. Restate the 17.1-point gap as 'X points above our estimated cost of equity'.

where: slide 2, bullet 3: 'Buyback EPS yield is 1.88% against 5.15% on cash' and slide 3 callout: 'Buyback last: the $4B program earns an EPs yield of 1.88%, below the 5.15% cash rate'
issue: EPS yield is not a capital-allocation test and comparing a 1.88% EPS yield to a 5.15% interest rate is a category error: EPS yield measures earnings per dollar of price, while 5.15% is a return on cash. The deck uses this to rank buybacks last, which is the opposite of the standard Costco position and of the fact that share count is falling. It is also inconsistent with slide 5 next step 1, which tells the board to authorize the $4B on the same day.
fix: Drop the 1.88% vs 5.15% comparison. Replace the buyback ranking with a cash-flow test the board can act on: state the buyback is funded only from free cash flow, cite the $9.38B FY2026 free cash flow on slide 4 as the source, and state the maximum annual repurchase that leaves cash above a minimum operating balance. Delete 'below the 5.15% cash rate' from the slide 3 callout.

where: slide 3, left heading 'Return on each $1 of capital, after tax, % per year, FY2026 and 2026-11-13'
issue: A 22.2% return is shown as a single bar with no method, no denominator and no period reconciliation. Footnote 1 gives 11.609B x (1 - 24.7%) / equity 35.808B — the numerator is an operating income, the denominator is equity, so this is ROE, not 'return on capital'; net income is not used. Bar 1 is 'FY2026 actual' and bar 2 is a market yield on 2026-11-13 — two different periods on one axis, which violates the one-period-one-unit rule.
fix: Rebuild the exhibit on the actual FY2026 10-K: show net income, not operating income times (1 minus tax), over total invested capital, using the same FY2026 ending balance sheet for the denominator as the $20.21B cash on slide 4. Re-label 'Return on invested capital, FY2026 (per 10-K)' and state the formula and the source. Put the market rate in a dated footnote, not a co-equal bar.

where: slide 4, step 'Less buyback −4.00B', basis '3 $4B authorization through November 2030'
issue: The bridge runs the full $4B authorization against a single FY2026 closing balance even though it is drawn to November 2030, so the $2.92B 'closing' is a worst-case hypothetical, not the closing balance. The $9.38B free cash flow is then held after it, presenting the refill as one year when it is spread over four. Footnote 2 says 'held flat for illustration only'. A board member reading only the summary table would conclude the company runs at $2.9B on 2026-12-04, which is not the plan on slide 5.
fix: Split the table into two columns — 'FY2026 close, on authorization' and 'At end of fiscal 2030, buyback fully drawn' — or reduce the −$4B to the first-tranche amount that keeps the balance above the stated minimum and footnote the remaining authorization as undrawn. Move the $9.38B free cash flow above the buyback line or add an explicit 'timing' column showing years to drawdown; label the $2.92B as the fully-drawn floor.

where: slide 4, 'Closing cash and equivalents $2.92B — 0.4x the $6.5B capex intention' and the absence of any minimum-cash policy
issue: There is no stated minimum operating cash balance anywhere in the deck, yet the whole bridge is judged against one. $2.92B is 14.4% of the $20.21B opening balance and 0.4x capex, but the deck never says what level is prudent for a retailer with Costco's working-capital swings, or why 0.4x capex is acceptable. The liquidity covenant is dismissed in footnote 3 as 'not a liquidity covenant', which is not an answer.
fix: Add a stated minimum cash policy to slide 4: X billion, being at least N months of capex plus the seasonal working-capital trough (source the prior-year intra-year low cash from the 10-Qs), and show closing cash of $2.92B against it. Add the undrawn revolver amount as available liquidity so the board sees the cushion; if the revolver size is not in the material, request it.

where: slide 3 callout, 'Growth first / Dividend second / Buyback last'
issue: The deck ranks the three uses of cash without ever showing the incremental returns on the $6.5B capex and the 29 new warehouses. Slide 3 asserts 'The plan behind the 22.2% is visible, not assumed' but only counts 16 warehouses opened and 13 planned; it does not state the incremental return per new warehouse or the payback period, so the growth claim is unsupported by a number.
fix: Add to slide 3 a per-warehouse economics line: capital cost per warehouse, expected annual net income per warehouse and payback in years, sourced from the 10-K or company disclosure; if the company does not disclose it, mark it clearly as an estimate with the build-up shown. Only then rank Growth first.

issue: Every page is the base case. A $13.3B special dividend taken at FY2026 close does not convert to the downside: what happens to the $2.92B closing cash and the buyback pace if FY2027 free cash flow comes in below $9.38B, or if capex runs above $6.5B? fix: Add a downside column or a short sensitivity on slide 4: closing cash and buyback completion date if FY2027 free cash flow is 10% below plan (i.e. $8.44B) and if capex is $7.2B (10% above the intention), using the existing bridge lines. State the resulting cash balance against the minimum-cash policy.

issue: The cover carries 'Board meeting, November 2026' and 'Meshpool' with no source line, no 'Preliminary' tag and no date consistent with the body, while slides 2-5 are marked 'Preliminary' and dated 2026-11. The cover also states the dividend is 'declared' and then the body asks the board to 'authorize' it on slides 2 and 5 — the deck takes credit for the declaration without sourcing which entity declared it and when.

Reconcile the verb: if the board declared it, slides 2 and 5 should say 'ratify the declared $30 per share dividend' throughout, not 'authorize the $13.3B special dividend'; if the vote is the authorization, remove 'has already declared' from slides 2 and 5.

issue: A crypto price site is cited as a source in a Costco capital-return board book. Nothing on the page uses a crypto price, so the citation is either an error or an unexplained reference a committee member will query.

where: slide 2, footnote 2: 'The $6.5B capex figure is the company's stated intention for fiscal 2026, not a board-approved budget line in the facts'

where: Slide 4 (table_focus), title 'The $17.3B payout cuts cash to $2.9B against $6.52B of debt and leases'

where: storyline, slides 2-5: no page substantiates the growth leg of the governing thought

where: Slide 3, title 'Growth earns 22.2% on capital, cash earns 5.15% and the buyback yields 1.88%' vs slide 2, 'Ratify the $4B repurchase, no incremental buyback'

where: Slide 2 (executive_summary), 'the buyback yields 1.88%' and slide 3, '1.88% = diluted EPS $20.76 / share price $1,106.21'
issue: The 1.88% is used as an earnings yield on slide 2 but defined as diluted EPS / price on slide 3, and slide 3's own arithmetic shows the gross EPS lift is $20.80, falling to $20.64 net of the 5.15% foregone interest, below the $20.76 earned holding cash. issue: 0.5x is $2.9B / $6.43B = 0.45x, but that $2.9B is post-buyback and the 3.1x is pre-dividend; the two ratios are not on the same footing, and capex is guided to about $6.5B, not $6.43B, for FY2026.

issue: Big-number stats beside three points is right for the message, but three of the numbers shown ($30, $4B, $6.5B) appear again in slides 3, 4 and 5 with different framing. Repetition is fine if each slide advances, but here slide 4 and slide 5 restate rather than add.

issue: The cover repeats the recommendation as a title, which duplicates slide 2. A cover should set the question, not pre-empt the answer.

issue: The distribution is stated three ways that do not reconcile: Slide 1/title '$30 special dividend and $4B buyback' with no total; Slide 2 'the $13.3B special dividend and $4B buyback' and 'the $17.3B payout'; Slide 4 'The $17.3B payout cuts cash to $2.9B'. The arithmetic works ($13.3B + $4B = $17.3B; $20.21B - $17.3B = $2.91B) but the slides mix gross dividend, gross authorization and net cash outflow without a single bridge, so a director cannot tie the headline number to the balance sheet.
fix: Add one bridge line used identically on Slides 2 and 4: '$13.3B special dividend (=$30 x 443.1M) + $4B buyback authorization = $17.3B gross; $20.21B cash less $17.3B = $2.9B cash'. On Slide 2's title keep '$13.3B' and state the $17.3B gross in the first line; on Slide 4 keep '$17.3B'.

issue: 'cash cover of capex 3.1x to 0.5x' is computed on trailing capex: $2.9B / $6.43B = 0.45x, i.e. the post-payout cash balance does not cover one year of capex, and the slide's own takeaway admits the gap. fix: Re-title Slide 4 'The $17.3B payout leaves $2.9B cash; the FY2026 capex plan is serviced by $9.38B free cash flow and existing facilities' and add one line naming the committed backstop (revolver size and maturity) and the minimum operating cash the company targets; if neither is in hand, mark it '[GAP - to be confirmed from 10-K liquidity note]'.

issue: The conclusion rests on the claim 'The dividend returns cash the business does not need' but no source supports 'does not need'. $2.9B residual cash against $6.43B annual capex and ~$2.6B of lease liabilities is not obviously surplus. The F18 note itself flags that the total distribution figure is not in the source material.
fix: Replace F18 with a sourced liquidity statement: cite the FY2026 cash balance, FCF, revolver and any minimum-cash policy from the 10-K liquidity note, and state the surplus as a computed figure with its inputs named, e.g. 'surplus cash = $20.21B cash - $[x]B minimum operating cash'.

where: Slide 2 (F31) and Slide 3 (title, F32, F62, F71)
issue: The two numbers that drive the recommendation are the least sourced in the pack. '$1,106.21 per share, $490.19B market cap, 53.3x P/E' (F31) has no price date and no share count for the market cap; the P/E denominator is not shown. fix: Stamp each: 'Share price $1,106.21 at 2026-11-13 (close)'; 'Market cap $490.2B = 443.1M shares x $1,106.21'; 'P/E 53.3x = $1,106.21 / FY2026 diluted EPS $20.76'. For the cash rate, show the 2016-2026 average T-bill/yield curve or Costco's stated cost of short-term cash and label it 'opportunity cost proxy, not a Costco-specific rate'.

issue: The slide compares 22.2% return on capital, 5.15% on cash and 1.88% on a buyback as if they are the same unit, then flags the buyback as 'an EPS yield, not a return on capital'. 22.2% is a historical, book-based return (F211, equity $35.80B + long-term debt $3.91B); 1.88% is an earnings yield on market price. issue: There is no sensitivity, no downside case and no alternative. fix: Add a sensitivity block to Slide 3 or Slide 4: 'Buffer under stress' - cash after payout of $2.9B at FCF of $9.38B (FY2026), $7.0B (-25%) and $5.0B (-47%), with the capex at $6.5B held constant, showing in each case how long the balance sheet stays covered; and a one-line 'If we do not pay: $20.21B cash earns 5.15% versus 22.2% in the business'.

issue: Every liquidity figure in the deck is FY2026 historical: FCF $9.38B = $15.82B - $6.43B, cash $20.21B at 2026-08-30. issue: The cover QA flags '$6.5B not found in cited facts' in three places (F12, F39, F40, F41). The number is in F215 ('approximately $6,500', thousands, i.e. $6.5B) but the citation chain is broken, so the cover as planned carries unsourced figures.

issue: QA on Slide 2 says '156 words of body text; cut to 100' and '10 bullets; keep 6 or fewer'. Three sized lines plus one decision line plus big-number stats will not survive at that length with the 'what each option implies for cash, debt and returns' requirement added.

where: Slide 2 and slide 4, the '$6.9B cash' figure
issue: The $6.9B post-dividend cash number carries no source. $20.21B cash less the $13.3B special dividend = $6.9B is your own arithmetic on F226 and F5, but the board cannot approve a plan whose headroom figure is unstated. The $2.9B is worse: it assumes the full $4B buyback is spent, and slide 4 itself says 'the $4B authorization is drawn over time, not on day one'.
fix: Label the $6.9B on slide 2 and slide 4 as 'company calculation: $20.21B 10-K cash less $13.3B declared dividend', and change the slide 4 'post-buyback (by 2030)' column header to 'cash floor if the full $4B is drawn by 2030' so the $2.9B is a floor, not a forecast.

issue: Slide 2 calls the buyback 'drawn opportunistically' and a use of cash; slide 3 says 'A buyback at 1.88% is dilutive' and 'Buyback last'. That is a real contradiction: the deck recommends approving a $4B authorization while arguing the spend destroys value against holding cash at 5.15%.
fix: Reconcile on slide 2 in one line: 'Approve the $4B authorization as optionality, not a commitment; the board should not draw it while the cash earns 5.15% and the marginal warehouse earns 22.2%.' Carry that exact framing to slide 3's callout and slide 5 step 2.

where: Slide 4, 'committed backstop and minimum operating cash [GAP - to be confirmed from 10-K liquidity note]'
issue: You are handing the board a cash-cover table (3.1x / 1.1x / 0.4x) whose denominator, the minimum cash the business must hold, is still a gap. The 0.4x cell will be read as a red flag before anyone sees the $9.38B FCF refill line beneath it.
fix: Pull the FY2026 10-K liquidity and capital resources note for the committed revolver size, any minimum cash covenant and the operating cash floor. Until then move the cash-cover row below the FCF row and annotate the 0.4x as 'before $9.38B annual FCF'.

issue: You bridge to FY2027 'using FY2026 net income of $9.23B as the earnings base, labelled an estimate'. That is a flat-growth assumption dressed as a test, and it sits under a table of hard 10-K figures. It weakens the page.

where: Slide 3, right side, the growth leg

fix: Reframe the cover question to the live decision: 'Ratify the declared $30 special dividend, set the buyback pace, and hold capex at $6.5B for FY2026'. Keep your date line 'Board meeting, November 2026'.

issue: Both slides carry the same 'growth first' message. Slide 2's title is the recommendation; slide 3's is the rationale. That is defensible, but slide 4 restates the $17.3B and the $2.9B a third time. Three slides, one fact.
