issue: Owners are lumps ('CFO / Treasury', 'CFO / Investor relations', 'COO / CFO'). A board pack should name one accountable owner per action.
fix: Give each step one name and one date, e.g. step 1 'CFO · December 2026 board', step 3 'COO · FY2026 capital committee'. Keep the dates already on the page.

issue: The title ends in an ellipsis: 'Each $1B of buyback destroys $0.03 of value…' and the right-hand column opens with '…so pace the buyback'. An ellipsis is not a claim, and the page heading should not depend on a second column to finish the sentence.
fix: Title: 'Each $1B of buyback destroys $0.03 of value'. Drop the leading ellipsis in the right column and make its heading 'Why the deleveraging case fails' or similar standalone claim.

where: Slide 3 (waterfall_bridge), cash bridge waterfall and footnote 1
issue: The bridge does not close. Waterfall bars: +15.82 − 6.43 − 1.15 − 13.29 − 1.00 = 20.21 − 14.16 = $6.05B outflow, but the title claims $6.07B. Footnote 1 plugs the buyback at $1.08B while the waterfall bar and slide 4 both use $1.00B. The special dividend is inconsistently stated as $13.29B in the waterfall and footnote 1 versus the $13.3B headline on slides 1, 2 and 5.
fix: Recompute the bridge from a single source and make every figure tie: state the special dividend as $13.29B everywhere or round the headline to $13.29B; set the FY2027E buyback bar to the same $1.08B used in footnote 1 (or change footnote 1 to $1.00B and restate the draw) so +15.82 − 6.43 − 1.15 − 13.29 − 1.08 = $14.08B closing cash, and update the title and slide 5 footnote 1 to the recalculated draw.

where: Slide 5 (closing), Next step 2, 'What it involves' column
issue: The $4B authorisation is described as 'Retire about 3.6M shares at $1,106.21', which prices 3.6M × $1,106.21 ≈ $4.0B but contradicts slide 4's 4.0M shares at $1,106.21 for a $4B buyback. The two pages cannot both be right, and the buyback share count is the core of the EPS argument.
fix: Use one figure throughout: 4.0M shares at $1,106.21 = $4.43B is inconsistent with a $4B authorisation; at $1,106.21 a $4B buyback retires 3.62M shares, so change slide 4's 'retires 4.0M shares' to 'retires about 3.6M shares' and confirm the EPS impact is recomputed on 3.6M shares (0.81% of 443.1M, not 0.90%).

where: Slide 4 (exhibit_argument), left-hand chart and right-hand bullets
issue: The chart compares four unlike things on one '% per year' axis — return on capital ex leases (22.20%), return on capital incl leases (20.80%), the 13-week T-bill (4.12%) and the buyback earnings yield (1.88%) — and the conversion arithmetic is hard-coded: $5.15% risk-free + 5.10% ERP × 0.24 beta = 6.11% is not the standard CAPM (5.15% + 0.24 × 5.10% = 6.37%), and the ERP is admitted in footnote 3 to be an unestimated 4.0–6.0% range.
fix: Either label the y-axis 'Return on capital and cash yields, %' and footnote each bar's definition and period, or split into two charts (capital returns vs cash yields). Recompute the cost of equity from a single sourced risk-free rate (the 10-year Treasury on slide 4 is 5.10%, so 5.10% + 0.24 × 5.10% = 6.32%, not 6.11%) and state the ERP as a point estimate or show the 4.0–6.0% sensitivity explicitly rather than burying it in footnote 3.

where: Slide 2 (executive_summary), right-hand callout '$0.03' and slide 4 title
issue: The '$0.03 EPS lost per $1B of buyback' on slide 2 and 'Each $1B of buyback destroys $0.03 of value' on slide 4 are not the same measure: slide 2's 4 cents EPS vs 7 cents interest forgone is a net 3 cents EPS dilution, while slide 4's $0.03 is stated as value destruction. If the 3 cents is EPS dilution and not value, the slide 4 title overstates the case.
fix: On slide 4 retitle to 'Each $1B of buyback dilutes EPS by $0.03 against the 22.2% return on capital' and show the EPS bridge explicitly ($0.24 front-loaded vs $0.31 forgone) so the 3 cents is derived, not asserted; keep slide 2's phrasing as EPS, not value.

issue: Slide 3 footnote 1 carries two different ordinary-dividend figures — '$2.468B a year; $1.15B was paid in the nine months ... so about $1.158B of the run-rate falls in FY2027E' — while slide 2 footnote 1 uses $1.158B. The bridge uses $1.15B. Three vintages of the same number on adjacent pages.
fix: Use the same ordinary-dividend figure ($1.15B or $1.16B) in the slide 3 waterfall, slide 3 footnote 1 and slide 2 footnote 1, and delete the unused figure so the reader cannot pick the wrong one.

issue: Footnote 1 states 'Share price of $1,106.21 is the close on 2026-11-13' but slide 2 footnote 1 attributes the same date 2026-11-13 to a different citation (the 13-week T-bill), and slide 4's own second source line cites a different date (2026-11-09) for a separate set of facts. Date provenance is muddled.
fix: Give each source its own dated line in the footnote block and keep one date per figure (price 2026-11-13; T-bill 2026-11-13; special dividend/authorisation 2026-11-11), matching the model's as-of dates.

issue: Slide 2 must show 'the three options and what each implies', but no slide in the storyboard ever names the three options. The deck jumps straight to the recommendation on slide 2 without framing the choice for the board. A board briefing that argues for one path without showing the alternatives it was weighed against is an advocacy memo, not a decision document.
fix: On slide 2, add a compact three-row options table before the recommendation: (A) Keep funding growth only — implies capex stays at $6.5B planning level and no additional return; (B) Return cash via buyback only — implies every $1B retires 0.90M shares (0.20% of 443.1M) at $1,106.21, and earns 1.88% against 22.2% return on capital; (C) Declared special dividend plus $4B buyback, capex held (recommendation) — implies funding the $30 per share special dividend ($13.3B) and the $4B buyback from $20.21B cash and $9.38B free cash flow. Title the page as a claim: 'Return cash and hold capex: fund the $13.3B special dividend and $4B buyback, keep the $6.5B plan'.

issue: Slides 2 and 4 repeat the same argument — that the buyback earns 1.88% versus 22.2% return on capital. Slide 2 previews it as a supporting metric and slide 4 builds an entire page on it. The deck spends two of five pages on one point while the dividend case and the growth funded by capex get no dedicated page.
fix: Move all 1.88% vs 22.2% vs 4.12% content to slide 4 only. Strip the metric from slide 2 and replace it with the options decision (see first issue above). Then use the freed slide-2 space to state what the dividend case rests on — the $20.21B cash and $9.38B free cash flow — so slide 4 can carry the comparison on its own.

where: Slide 4 (exhibit_argument), title 'A buyback earns 1.9% against 22.2% on capital and 4.1% on cash'
issue: The 1.88% earnings yield is an EPS-over-price ratio, not the return a buyback actually earns. The deck's own F31 shows a $1B buyback at $1,106.21 lifts EPS from $20.76 to only $20.80. The 22.2% after-tax return on capital is a business-level return, not an alternative deployment the board can choose at the margin, and the 4.12% T-bill is before tax. Three numbers from three different bases sit in one bar chart and invite the reader to draw a comparison the arithmetic does not support.
fix: Either relabel the exhibit 'Buyback EPS accretion is negligible: $1B retires 0.20% of shares and lifts EPS from $20.76 to $20.80' and show the EPS bridge, or ask research to compute the after-tax cash yield forgone on the cash actually used (the $20.21B balance earning 4.12% pre-tax, net of tax) so the comparison is apples-to-apples. Do not put the 22.2% return on capital in the same bar chart as the other two without a footnote explaining it is a historical business return, not a marginal deployment option.

where: Slide 3 (waterfall_bridge), title 'Cash generation covers the $13.3B dividend and $4B buyback with $3.4B to spare'
issue: The $3.4B buffer does not appear in any fact. The waterfall in the must-show specifies opening cash $20.21B, operating cash flow $15.82B, capex $6.43B, the $13.3B special dividend and the $4B buyback. $20.21B + $15.82B − $6.43B − $13.3B − $4B = $12.3B closing cash, not $3.4B. The title's number is unsupported by the facts the slide is built on.
fix: Ask research to confirm the correct closing cash figure and the treatment of the dividend timing (is the $13.3B paid in FY2027, split across quarters, or already partly accrued?). Correct the title to the computed figure before the deck goes anywhere. If the $3.4B was meant to be a buffer above a minimum operating cash requirement, state that requirement explicitly and show it as a line in the waterfall.

issue: The deck recommends returning cash while holding the $6.5B capex plan, but no slide shows that the growth plan is worth funding. The highest-value evidence for 'keep funding capex' is that capex grew 14.2% a year over three years and revenue grew 7.8% a year over the same period, and that a buyback retires only 0.20% of shares per $1B. The reader is asked to accept the capex hold as an assumption.
fix: Add the capital-efficiency evidence to the storyline. Either fold 'capex grew 14.2% a year over three years, from $4.32B to $6.43B, while revenue grew 7.8% a year, from $242.29B to $303.15B' into slide 3 as the closing-cash context, or replace slide 4's second half with a small two-column chart showing capex growth 14.2% versus revenue growth 7.8%. This also addresses the buyback-versus-growth trade-off directly.

issue: Slide 4 carries a bar chart, the argument, and per the must-show the argument that the buyback is the weakest use of cash 'while the special dividend returns cash the balance sheet does not need.' That is two messages on one page and the page risks needing a voice-over to land. It also breaks the deck's visual variety as the only analytical page besides slide 3's waterfall.
fix: Keep slide 4 as one message: 'A $4B buyback retires 0.80% of shares and earns 1.88%; the $13.3B special dividend returns cash the balance sheet does not need.' Put the bar chart of the three returns on the left at one-third width and the EPS-accretion bridge ($20.76 to $20.80 for $1B) below it. Move the dividend-need argument to slide 3's bridge, which already shows the cash. If the page still needs two messages, split it — but then the deck is over five slides and a slide must be cut.

issue: Slides 1 and 5 carry the same title claim: 'fund the $13.3B special dividend and $4B buyback, keep the $6.5B capex plan.' The cover sets the answer up and the closing restates it, which is fine as a bookend, but the closing must not be a repeat — it must add the action, the owner and the milestone.
fix: Keep the cover title. Rewrite slide 5's title to the action: 'Fund the $13.3B dividend and $4B buyback, hold the $6.5B capex plan; report the closing cash buffer at each board meeting.' Name an owner and a date for each line in the roadmap.

issue: The must-show lists seven metrics for one page — $13.3B, $4B, $20.2B, $9.4B, 1.9%, 22.2%, 4.1% — plus three options and a recommendation. That is a dense page and the 'big numbers' format will not hold all of it without becoming a wall of figures.
fix: Cut the slide-2 metrics to the four that size the decision: $13.3B special dividend, $4B buyback, $20.21B cash, $9.38B free cash flow. Move 1.88%, 22.2% and 4.12% to slide 4 and let the options table carry the 'what each implies' text. If it still overflows, drop the return-on-capital metric from the summary entirely — it belongs on the analysis page.

issue: The slide 3 title claims cash generation covers the plan 'with $3.4B to spare,' which is the number in dispute (see prior issue), and the must-show also asks for 'a buffer' language. Two different buffer concepts on one page.
fix: Pick one. If the buffer is closing cash, title it 'Cash generation leaves $12.3B closing cash after the $13.3B dividend and $4B buyback' once research confirms the figure. If the buffer is above a stated minimum operating cash level, title it 'Cash generation covers the plan and holds the minimum operating cash buffer' and show the minimum as a line.

issue: The recommendation is stale on arrival. F40 says the $30 special dividend was 'declared' on 2026-11-11 and F41 says the $4B buyback was 'reauthorized' with an expiration of January 2030. A board briefing dated November 2026 cannot 'recommend' approving a dividend that has already been declared and a buyback that has already been reauthorized — the decision is behind us. Every action title ('Approve the $13.3B...', 'Fund the $13.3B...') is answering a question that no longer exists.
fix: Reframe the decision to what is still open as of November 2026: (a) confirm the funding plan for the already-declared $13.3B dividend, (b) set the pace of execution of the $4B reauthorized buyback given its 1.9% earnings yield, and (c) confirm the $6.5B FY2026 capex plan under the $6.43B FY2025 run-rate. Rewrite the governing thought and all five action titles to 'confirm/pace/hold' rather than 'approve/fund'. If the intent is genuinely to recommend the declaration pre-announcement, the deck must be re-dated ahead of the 2026-11-11 declaration and the source F40 restated as a proposal, not a declaration — the current date makes the current framing unrecoverable.

issue: The two load-bearing facts — the $30 special dividend ($13.3B) and the $4B buyback reauthorization — are sourced only to finance.yahoo.com ('Costco (COST) Declares $30 Special Dividend And Reauthorizes $4 Billion Buyback, 2026-11-11'). Yahoo is a secondary aggregator; for a board document the primary sources are the company's 8-K and press release, which exist if the declaration is real. Shipping a $13.3B capital action sourced to a Yahoo headline is exactly what a committee will challenge.
fix: Source F40/F41 to the Costco 8-K (item 8.01 / 2.03) and the company press release, with the accession number and filing date. If the 8-K cannot be located for 2026-11-11, the fact is not verifiable and the deck must not present it as declared.

where: F29 scaling rule, F30 earnings yield
issue: The buyback math ignores the cash cost of the buyback itself. F31 shows EPS rising to $20.80 'before lost interest on the cash', but the $4B buyback is funded by drawing down $20.21B cash yielding ~4.12% (F24) — the lost interest is ~$165M pre-tax, ~$124M after tax at 24.7%, which is ~$0.28/share. Against a buyback EPS accretion of only $0.04 (F31), the correct conclusion is that the buyback is dilutive to EPS once the cash cost is charged. The deck's central argument (buyback = weakest use of cash) is right, but the numbers shown make it look slightly accretive rather than destructive, which understates the case and will be caught.
fix: Add to slide 4 the after-interest adjusted EPS: $20.80 − $0.28 = $20.52, versus $20.76 pre-buyback, i.e. −$0.24/share. State that the $4B buyback is EPS-dilutive after funding cost and therefore should be paced, not front-loaded. Use only F13, F21, F24, F30, F31 and the 24.7% tax rate already in F32.

issue: Return on capital 22.2% is computed with equity $35.80B + long-term debt $3.91B but excludes operating lease liabilities of $2.61B (F11). With costco's lease-heavy footprint the denominator understates capital and overstates the return; including leases, capital is $42.32B and after-tax ROC falls to ~18.8%. The comparison to the 1.88% buyback yield survives either way, but the headline 22.2% is not defensible as stated.
fix: Recompute ROC both ways on slide 4: 22.2% excluding leases (as now) and 18.8% including $2.61B operating lease liabilities (F11). Label which definition is used and why. Do not silently drop leases.

issue: The bridge says 'leaves a buffer' but the storyboard never states the closing cash figure, and the takeaway '$3.4B to spare' does not reconcile: $20.21B + $15.82B − $6.43B − $13.3B − $4B = $12.30B closing cash, not a $3.4B buffer. $3.4B appears to be FCF ($9.38B, F26) less the two return actions ($17.3B) = −$7.92B, which does not equal $3.4B either. The slide title's number is wrong or orphaned.
fix: Fix the title to the actual closing cash: '$20.21B opening cash + $15.82B operating cash flow − $6.43B capex − $13.3B dividend − $4B buyback = $12.30B closing cash.' Show each bar to that arithmetic and delete the $3.4B. If a different buffer is intended (e.g. cash cover 3.1x, F27), say which metric it is and reconcile it.

issue: The must-show list names 'the three options and what each implies' but only one option (fund the dividend and buyback) is sized. There is no stated alternative (e.g. suspend the special dividend and redeploy into growth; or accelerate buyback; or hold all cash) with its own numbers, so the recommendation is asserted rather than chosen against a comparator. A board cannot ratify a decision it never saw the alternative to.
fix: Add a three-column comparison on slide 2: (A) declared plan — dividend $13.3B + buyback $4B, closing cash $12.30B, buyback EPS −$0.24 net of interest; (B) growth-first — hold dividend, redeploy $17.3B into capex/warehouses at 22.2% ROC (or 18.8% with leases); (C) hold-cash — retain $30.4B at 4.12%, EPS $20.76 + $1.05 interest. State which is recommended and the one number that decides it.

issue: The $6.5B FY2026 capex figure (F39) is 'current intention' from a document snippet with no stated source in the storyboard entry, while F37/F38 (supplychain360.io) support the rollout of ~30 net new warehouses and 33 openings in FY2027. The deck's 'hold the $6.5B capex plan' rests on a number whose provenance is not filed-source verified, and the capex plan is the single offset to the capital return — if capex is cut, the answer changes.
fix: Verify the $6.5B FY2026 capex intention against Costco's 10-K MD&A and any 8-K guidance, and cite the exact filing. Treat F37/F38 as context, not evidence, and downgrade or remove their sliding use.

issue: No page addresses risk. There is no slide or panel on (a) what happens if operating cash flow falls from $15.82B, (b) the $4B buyback pace and price risk at $1,106.21 (F21) with a 52-week range of $850.00–$1,106.21 (F22) — a 23% drawdown would make the buyback materially less dilutive and change the pacing argument, (c) the 1.15B annual dividend (F8) plus $12.9B returning in one year against $9.38B FCF, i.e. the plan consumes more than a year of FCF, (d) interest expense $145.0M (F6) and the 5.15% 10-year (F25). A committee will ask all four.

where: Slide 1 cover, slide 2 executive_summary, governing thought

where: Slide 3 waterfall_bridge, closing cash and ordinary dividend

The $2.46B is a run-rate, the $1.15B is a nine-month cash figure, and the $13.3B is a future declaration — three periods in one bar chart.
fix: Label each bar with its period: FY2026 actual ordinary dividends paid $1.15B (F8, 2026-05-10 stub) — annualized to $2.46B at $5.54 x 443.1M (F12 x F1) — versus FY2027 declared special $13.3B. Use one basis (cash paid, cash to be paid) and put the run-rate footnote below the bar, not as an in-line subtraction. If the special and the ordinary do not fall in the same 12 months, split the waterfall into FY2026A and FY2027E columns.

issue: The 22.2% return on capital is computed as 'operating income $11.69B x (1 - 24.7% effective tax rate) / (equity $35.80B + long-term debt $3.91B)' (F32). The deck then adds '18.8% including $2.61B of operating lease liabilities' (F11) as a sensitivity, but never states the resulting denominator ($42.32B) or the computation, and never reconciles the 24.7% effective tax rate to income tax expense $3.02B (F17). A committee will check that 24.7% against pretax income and find the deck has not tied it.
fix: Add a footnote cell: effective tax rate 24.7% = $3.02B (F17) / pretax income [state the pretax income line]. For the leases-included case, show the denominator explicitly: 18.8% = $11.69B x (1 - 24.7%) / ($35.80B + $3.91B + $2.61B). If pretax income is not in the fact pack, research it from the 10-K; do not leave 24.7% unsourced.

issue: No slide plans a downside or sensitivity case for what the committee will ask: what happens if FY2027 capex exceeds the $6.5B plan, or if operating cash flow compresses. The context line on slide 3 ('capex grew 14.2% a year over three years while operating cash flow grew 12.6%, so the gap is the case for pacing the buyback') is the closest thing to a risk, but it is asserted, not sized. F37 (about 30 net new warehouses annually, capex growth slowing after FY2027) and F38 (33 openings in FY2027) are in the pack and unused.
fix: Add a fourth bar or a small sensitivity table on slide 3: cash at the $1B pace if operating cash flow is flat vs FY2026, and if capex runs 10% above the $6.5B plan (that is $7.15B). Show closing cash in each case. This is the slide the board will spend the most time on.

where: Slide 4 valuation leg, "estimated cost of equity of about 5.4%"
issue: The cost of equity is called 'estimated' but no source is given for the equity risk premium. F25 (10-year Treasury 5.15%) is described as a Treasury yield index, not an ERP. The only source cited for the 5.4% is the deck's own arithmetic, which does not work (see blocking issue above).
fix: Either cite a published ERP (e.g., Damodaran, Kroll, or an internal bank figure as of November 2026) with date and source, or state the assumption explicitly as 'management estimate' and show the sensitivity of the 22.2% vs 5.4% conclusion to an ERP of 4.0-6.0%.

where: Slide 1 cover must show; slide 4 exhibit_argument
issue: The cover asks the board to decide between 'fund, pace, or hold,' but the storyboard never defines 'hold' as an actual option in the numbers — slide 2 Option C is 'defer, $0 buyback,' which is the same as 'hold' but presented as a buyback pace, not as deferring the capex plan. The $6.5B capex plan is treated as fixed throughout; if that is the case, the cover's 'hold' is misleading.
fix: On slide 1, change the third open item to 'hold the $6.5B FY2026-27 capex plan' and make clear the board is not being asked to defer capex. If deferring capex is a real option, add it as a fourth column to slide 2 with the 22.2% return on capital forgone, sourced to F32.

issue: The three options are not apples to apples. Option A spends $4B in year one; Option B spends $1B a year for four years, $4B total; Option C spends $0. But the closing-cash figures ($6.84B / $9.84B / $10.84B) are all point-in-time at the end of one year, so Option B's $9.84B is after only $1B of buyback and does not reflect the remaining $3B commitment. A board member will read $9.84B as the cash available with the buyback done, which it is not.
fix: Either show closing cash at the end of year 4 for all three options (so $4B is spent in A and B), or label each cash figure with its period: 'closing cash at end of year 1' for A and B, 'closing cash at end of year 1' for C. Add the undrawn $3B commitment as a footnote to Option B.

issue: Cover date is November 2026, which is consistent with the brief and with 'Today is 16 November 2026.' Fine, but the market data cited on slide 2 and slide 4 is as of 2026-11-13, and the $30 special dividend is dated 2026-11-11. The cover does not state an as-of date, which a board will want for market figures.
fix: Add 'Market data as of 13 November 2026' to the cover under the date.

issue: The context line 'capex grew 14.2% a year over three years while operating cash flow grew 12.6%' is sourced to F19 and F20, but the two are on different periods: capex $4.32B (year to 2023-09-03) to $6.43B (year to 2026-08-30) is three fiscal years, and operating cash flow $11.07B (2023-09-03) to $15.82B (2026-08-30) is the same three fiscal years. Consistent. Keep as is.
fix: No change.

issue: Slide 5 repeats the F40/F41/F39/F5/F26/F29/F30/F31/F24/F32/F11/F12/F22/F27 fact set without sizing any next step. 'Report the closing cash buffer at each board meeting' is a process action, not a number. Milestones have no dates.
fix: Add three dated milestones: dividend payment date [research], buyback authorization start [research], FY2026 results and capex review [date]. For each, state the number the board will measure: closing cash ($9.84B at the paced path), effective tax rate (24.7%), and return on capital (22.2%).

issue: The buyback pacing argument is made three times: slide 2 states 'net -3 cents a share', slide 3's bridge ends at 'closing cash $9.84B on the recommended paced path', and slide 4 is by your own spec 'an EPS bridge per $1B of buyback... then down to $20.73 after the $0.07 a share of after-tax interest forgone, a net -3 cents a share'. Two of these pages make the same point; the deck has no room to spare at five slides.
fix: Make slide 4 the single buyback-arithmetic page and strip every buyback-EPS calculation out of slide 3. Slide 3's title becomes the balance-sheet claim only ('Returns of $15.76B exceed $9.38B of free cash flow by $6.38B, drawing cash to $9.84B') and its body carries only the bridge, the three-year capex/OCF table and the sensitivity. Slide 4 keeps the $20.76 -> $20.80 -> $20.73 bridge, the $31.0M after-tax funding cost and the three returns on one basis. No number appears on both pages.

where: Slide 5, 'dividend payment date [GAP: payment date not in the fact pack]', 'buyback authorisation start [GAP: start date not in the fact pack]', 'FY2026 results and capex review [GAP: date not in the fact pack]'
issue: The board is being asked to confirm the funding and timing of a dividend it has already declared, and the page intended to close the meeting carries three of these placeholders including the payment date itself. A closing roadmap with three GAPs is not a closing page. The brief asked for payment timing and the material does not have it.
fix: Before this goes out, pull the declaration press release and the 8-K for the record date, payment date and the buyback authorisation effective date, and the FY2026 earnings date from the company's IR calendar. Replace all three GAPs with dated milestones carrying the number the board measures: payment date and $13.3B outflow; buyback start date and the first $1.0B tranche; four-week cadence to the audit committee against the $9.84B closing-cash path.

where: Slide 4 and slide 5, 'effective tax rate 24.7%' and 'return on capital 22.2%'
issue: Both the 24.7% rate and the 22.2% return on capital rest on the same derived number, and you have already flagged it: 'pretax income is not in the fact pack'. The whole recommendation turns on comparing a 22.2% return on capital against a 6.11% to 6.59% cost of equity. If the tax rate is wrong, the conclusion moves.
fix: Get pretax income from the FY2026 10-K income statement and recompute: 24.7% must equal $3.02B income tax expense / pretax income. If it does not tie, correct the rate, the $31.0M after-tax funding cost, the $0.07 a share and the 22.2%. Put the recomputed rate in one footnote cell on slide 4 and carry the same figure into slide 5. Delete the [GAP] flag only after the rate ties to a filed statement.

where: Slide 2, 'each $1B adds 4 cents of EPS but forgoes 7 cents of interest' and 'EPS -$0.06 a year'
issue: The 7 cents is struck off a 4.12% 13-week T-bill yield. That is the rate on cash held for weeks, not on $1B held for four years. Over a paced programme through January 2030 the relevant foregone rate is the 5.15% 10-year yield, which the deck already holds as F25 and uses nowhere in this calculation.
fix: Either pass the 4.12% explicitly as a conservatism assumption with a footnote that the alternative 5.15% 10-year yield would take the funding cost to roughly $38.7M after tax and the net to about -5 cents, or rerun the bridge at 5.15% and change the title number. Do not leave the discrepancy for the board to find in the footnote.

where: Slide 1, 'set the funding and payment timing of the declared dividend'
issue: The cover promises three things and the deck answers two. Funding and payment timing of the $13.3B dividend is named as open on page 1 and never resolved; slide 2 simply states the $13.3B as an outflow from $10.84B baseline cash, with no source named. On $10.84B of baseline cash against a $13.3B outflow the source is the whole question, and the nearest line is slide 3's footnote that ordinary dividends run at $2.46B.
fix: On slide 2, under the baseline, add the one line the board will ask for: the $13.3B is funded from cash and the FY2027 operating cash flow run-rate, leaving $9.84B at the paced path. Cite the $20.21B opening cash and the $15.82B operating cash flow already on slide 3. If the FY2027 operating cash flow is not in hand, say 'funded from the $20.21B cash balance' and put the FY2027 generation estimate in as a research request rather than a figure.

issue: The page holds a waterfall, a three-year capex/OCF table, a sensitivity table and a valuation footnote — four exhibits and two claims on one page. On a five-slide brief that is a wall. The waterfall alone is the argument.
fix: Keep the waterfall full width and the three-year table beneath it as the period-by-period support. Move the closing-cash sensitivity and the 22.4x valuation line onto slide 4 and slide 5 respectively, where both are already in play. If the sensitivity must stay, make it three cells, not a table.

where: Slide 4, 'Below it the three returns on one labelled basis: buyback earnings yield 1.88%, after-tax return on capital 22.2% excluding leases and 18.8% including $2.61B of operating lease liabilities (denominator $42.32B), 13-week T-bill 4.12% before tax'
issue: Three returns plus two lease bases plus the cost of equity leg gives five bars on five different conventions in a half-width panel next to the argument. A board member cannot read that in the room and the lease version adds a caveat, not a decision.
fix: Reduce to three bars on one basis and one line: buyback earnings yield 1.88%, return on capital 22.2%, cost of equity 6.11% to 6.59%. Move the lease-inclusive 18.8% to a footnote with the $42.32B denominator — it does not change the ranking. State the 4.12% T-bill only in the bridge above, where it is used.

where: Slide 2, 'Metrics panel limited to two numbers held constant across options: $13.3B dividend declared, $6.5B capex plan'
issue: Naming two numbers 'held constant' and then repeating them on slides 3, 4 and 5 is three restatements of what is not being decided. The panel is honest but it is also the least informative content on the page.
fix: Cut the panel to one line of footnote text under the three columns: 'Held constant across A, B and C: $13.3B dividend declared; $6.5B FY2026 capex plan.' Use the freed space for the option columns, which are the page.

where: Slide 1, 'Market data as of 13 November 2026'; slide 4, F22 '52-week closing range $850.00 to $1,106.21'
issue: The deck prices every decision off $1,106.21, the top of the 52-week range, and never says so. A board member will notice that the buyback retires 0.90M shares at the highest price of the year and will ask what it retires at a lower price. F22 is in hand and unused.
fix: Add one footnote line on slide 2 or 4: 'At the 52-week low of $850.00 the same $1B retires 1.18M shares; all figures here use the 13 November 2026 close of $1,106.21 (F21).' One line, no new research.

where: Slide 4, 'Add one row showing the $4B front-loaded program across four years, not a single year'
issue: A four-year row underneath a per-$1B bridge is a second unit on one exhibit. The reader has just been told the answer is per $1B and is now handed a $4B schedule in the same frame.
fix: Keep the bridge strictly per $1B. Put the $4B front-loaded comparison on slide 2 in the three option columns where it already lives as Option A. If you want it on slide 4, give it its own titled line beneath, not a boxed row inside the bridge exhibit.

issue: The bridge mixes a nine-month FY2026A ordinary dividend paid of $1.15B (period 2025-09-01 to 2026-05-10, F8) with a full-year FY2026A operating cash flow of $15.82B and capex of $6.43B (2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30, F7/F4), and then subtracts FY2027E items (the declared $13.3B special dividend and the $1B paced buyback). The arithmetic $20.21 + 15.82 - 6.43 - 1.15 - 13.3 - 1.0 = $14.15B, not the stated $9.84B; the gap is $4.31B and would not survive a committee reading the page. Mixing nine months of dividend with twelve months of cash flow inside one bridge means the 'closing cash' bar is unsupportable.
fix: Move to a clean cash roll-forward on one basis. EITHER (a) show FY2026A ending cash $20.21B, then a full-year ordinary dividend at the run-rate of $5.54 x 443.1M = $2.46B (state the period once: 'FY2026 declared rate annualised; FY2026A full-year dividend paid not separately disclosed'), then FY2027E special dividend $13.3B and FY2027E buyback $1.0B, closing cash $9.84B (reconciles with 20.21 + 15.82 - 6.43 - 2.46 - 13.3 - 1.0 = $12.84B only if FY2027E operating cash flow is added); OR (b) leave the bridge as pure one-year and add a clearly labelled 'FY2027E' bar row with FY2027E operating cash flow. Put the reconciliation math on the page: starting cash $20.21B, plus/minus the operating cash flow for the same period, less capex for the same period, less dividends for the same period, less special and buyback, equals $9.84B. The ordinary dividend run-rate $2.46B is currently a footnote, not an in-line subtraction, and the stated $9.84B cannot be derived from what is shown.

issue: Slide 2's deciding number applies a $1B-buyback EPS and interest calculation (4 cents / 7 cents / -3 cents) to a $4B front-load option (slide 2 option A: 'incremental buyback effect $4B, closing cash $6.84B, EPS -$0.24') as if the per-$1B economics scaled linearly, while slide 4 shows the $4B program 'across four years, not a single year'. A $4B buyback executed in four equal tranches of $1B each year at $1,106.21 share price would not have the same annual EPS impact as a front-loaded $4B in year one: shares retired in year 1 earn the full-year EPS benefit and the funding cost is on the full $4B for the full year, while tranches in years 2-4 leave cash sitting on the balance sheet in year 1. Option A's headline '-$0.24 EPS' in year 1 is $0.06 x 4, which silently assumes the shares are all retired at the start of year 1 and the cash is all spent on day one, but does not say so.
fix: On slide 2, keep the option columns on a per-year basis and state the timing explicitly: 'Option A: $4.0B retired in year 1, EPS impact in year 1 (full-year effect) -$0.24; Option B: $1.0B retired each year, EPS impact in year 1 -$0.06, $3.0B undrawn'. On slide 4, replace the four-year $4B row with a table showing each $1B tranche in its year of execution and the EPS effect only in the year it is retired, or explicitly foot the number: 'illustrative; assumes each $1B tranche retired at the start of the FY and held for the full year; actual annual EPS impact depends on execution timing and share price at purchase.' If the $0.24 in slide 2 and the '$4B across four years' row on slide 4 are intended to say different things, reconcile them on the page; if they are intended to say the same thing, one of them is wrong.

issue: The recommendation to hold the $6.5B FY2026 capex plan rests entirely on the after-tax return on capital of 22.2% (F32) clearing the cost of equity of 6.11%-6.59% (slide 4, 5.15% 10-year + 0.24 beta x 4.0-6.0% ERP). Slide 3 has a sensitivity on closing cash to a 10% capex overshoot ($7.15B) but no sensitivity on the returns side: what does ROCE look like if incremental capex earns anything less than the 22.2% historical average? A committee will ask this in the first minute and the answer is not on the page. The 22.2% is a stock, backward-looking ROCE, not the marginal return on new warehouses.
fix: Add a small grid on slide 4 (or slide 3): after-tax return on incremental capex at 3 scenarios, e.g. 22.2% (historic average, F32), 15.0%, 10.0%, and the resulting ROCE versus the 6.11%-6.59% hurdle and versus the 1.88% buyback yield. State on the slide: 'Hold-capex case fails if incremental ROCE falls below 6.59% (the top of the cost-of-equity range)'. If you cannot source an incremental return, request it (see research requests) and show the breakeven: at what incremental ROCE on the FY2027 capex does the buyback become the better use of $1B? The answer is roughly the 6.6% hurdle, but show the number.

issue: The cost of equity is built as US 10-year Treasury 5.15% (F25) + 0.24 beta (F23, two years of weekly returns to 2026-11-09) x 4.0-6.0% ERP, giving 6.11%-6.59%. A 0.24 beta on Costco is not credible and a committee will not accept it without comment: it implies Costco is roughly four times less volatile than the S&P 500, which is inconsistent with a 52-week range of $850.00 to $1,106.21 (F22, 23% drawdown) and with a 22.4x earnings multiple. A blank-cheque 4.0%-6.0% ERP range straddled around the actual number also looks like the analyst picked a range wide enough to make the conclusion robust.
fix: Source the beta from a recognised provider (Bloomberg/Barra adjusted beta) or compute it on a consistent basis (e.g. 5 years of monthly returns) and put the base case on the page. If beta stays 0.24, footnote: 'Beta measured over two years of weekly returns; a committee-grade cost of equity would use a longer window and a peer-group or bottom-up beta.' Narrow the ERP range to a stated source (e.g. Damodaran implied ERP as of the valuation date) and show one base case with a one-line sensitivity: cost of equity at beta 0.50 and beta 0.80. At beta 0.80 x 5.0% ERP the cost of equity is 9.15%, still below 22.2%, so the conclusion survives; show that it does.

issue: Slide 1 asks the board to 'confirm the already-declared $13.3B special dividend' and frames the three open items as funding and timing of a dividend that has already been declared. If the dividend is already declared (F40, 2026-11-11), the board is not choosing whether to pay it; the funding source and payment date are the decisions. That is fine, but the deck then treats the $13.3B as a fixed outflow in every option on slide 2 without showing the balance-sheet consequence if the board were to fund it from debt instead of cash, which is the one alternative the board can still choose. F6 interest expense of $145.0M and F10 long-term debt of $3.91B are in the pack and unused.
fix: Add a one-line framing on slide 1 or 2: '$13.3B funded from balance-sheet cash (current plan) vs from a $13.3B draw of short-term debt at ~4.1% costs about $0.11 a share after tax in year 1'. Use F6 ($145.0M existing interest expense) and F10 ($3.91B existing long-term debt) to show the pro forma leverage: equity $35.80B + debt $3.91B today; equity $35.80B less $13.3B dividend plus $13.3B new debt would be ~$35.80B equity, ~$17.2B debt, leverage ~0.48x. The board should see the number the funding choice produces.

issue: The $4B buyback reauthorisation (F41) is sourced only to finance.yahoo.com (a secondary aggregator) with a truncated URL. The dividend declaration (F40) and buyback authorisation are material corporate actions and the primary source is the company's 8-K and press release, both of which should be on EDGAR within four business days of 2026-11-11. The trigger date, the authorisation expiry (stated as January 2030), and the declaration and record dates for the dividend are exactly the facts slide 5 marks as [GAP].
fix: Pull the 8-K and the accompanying press release for the 2026-11-11 announcement from EDGAR and source F40 and F41 to that filing, with the EDGAR accession URL. This single research step closes all three [GAP]s on slide 5 (dividend payment date, buyback authorisation start) if the release states them.

issue: The effective tax rate is stated as 24.7% (= $3.02B / pretax income, F17/F3) but the slide itself says pretax income is not in the pack. Net income $9.23B (F3) and income tax expense $3.02B (F17) imply pretax income of $12.25B and an effective rate of 24.66%, so 24.7% is correct on a pretax-income-of-$12.25B basis, but pretax income is not the same as operating income less interest and other items and the ROCE denominator uses operating income $11.69B (F14), not pretax income. A committee will check whether 24.7% is applied consistently to the buyback interest deduction (it is: $1B x 4.12% x (1 - 24.7%) = $31.0M) and to the ROCE numerator (it is: $11.69B x (1 - 24.7%) = $8.80B).
fix: Source the pretax income line from the FY2026 10-K income statement (not the pack) and footnote: 'Effective tax rate 24.7% = income tax expense $3.02B / pretax income $12.25B (10-K FY2026 income statement); applied consistently to the buyback funding cost and to ROCE.' Add the implied pretax income $12.25B to the footnote so the reader can tie it. If the 10-K states a different pretax figure, restate the rate.

issue: Slide 2 says the metrics panel is 'limited to two numbers held constant across options: $13.3B dividend declared, $6.5B capex plan.' A board slide that holds capex constant while the question on the table is whether to fund capex at all should show at least the cash consequence of the capex choice, otherwise the panel is decoration. It also omits the market capitalisation ($490.19B, F28) and the 22.4x FY2026 EPS multiple ($1,106.21 / $20.76, F21/F13) that the reader needs to place the $13.3B return in context (the dividend is 2.7% of market cap).
fix: Expand the metrics panel to four: market capitalisation $490.19B (F28); special dividend $13.3B = 2.7% of market cap (F40 x F1 / F28); FY2026 capex plan $6.5B (F39); and 22.4x FY2026 diluted EPS (F21 / F13). Keep the two held constant and label them as such. The 2.7% of market cap is the number the board will anchor on and it is free from data already in the pack.

issue: Slide 5 promises dated milestones (dividend payment date, buyback authorisation start, FY2026 results and capex review) and then marks all three as [GAP]. A closing slide with three gaps is a working session, not a board briefing. The next steps page is the page the board keeps; it must be fully sourced.
fix: Fill the three milestones from the 8-K / press release (see research request on F40/F41) and from Costco's investor relations calendar for the FY2026 results date. If the FY2026 results date is not yet public, state the expected month ('FY2026 results expected late September 2027, per prior-year cadence: FY2025 results released 2025-09-25') and source it. Every date on the page must tie to a filing or the IR calendar.

issue: Slide 3 asks for 'one line on the minimum cash buffer the board is protecting' but the deck gives no number. The whole pacing recommendation is a cash-buffer decision dressed up as an EPS decision: Option B closing cash $9.84B vs Option A closing cash $6.84B (difference $3.0B, which is exactly the undrawn $3B the footnote mentions). If the board has not set a buffer, the analyst is setting it implicitly at somewhere between $6.84B and $9.84B, and should say so.
fix: State the buffer explicitly on slide 3: 'Recommended floor: $7.0B closing cash, equal to roughly 1.1x the $6.5B FY2026 capex plan and 0.7x the $9.38B FY2026 free cash flow.' Use F26 and F39 to support the ratio. Then the front-load case fails by a stated $0.16B and the pacing recommendation has a number behind it, not an adjective. If the buffer is genuinely a board decision, set it as the first agenda item on slide 5 with a range: '$6.0B-$8.0B, recommended $7.0B'.

issue: Cover subtitle names three open items including 'set the funding and payment timing of the declared dividend' and 'choose the $4B buyback pace', but the title says 'fund the declared $13.3B dividend, pace the $4B buyback, hold the $6.5B capex plan' as if all three were decided. The tension is fine, but the cover then does not flag that the board is confirming rather than choosing the dividend, which is the actual governance position.
fix: Amend the cover line to read: '... confirm funding and timing of the declared $13.3B special dividend, pace the $4B buyback at $1.0B a year, hold the $6.5B FY2026 capex plan.' Same length, states the action verb the board is actually being asked to take on each item.

issue: The valuation footnote is '22.4x FY2026 diluted EPS ($1,106.21 / $20.76, F21 / F13)'. 1106.21 / 20.76 = 53.29, not 22.4x. The stated multiple is wrong on its face. If 22.4x is intended, the denominator would be about $49.38, which is not in the pack. The other candidate: $1,106.21 / $20.82 (F51, multiples.vc current EPS) = 53.13x, still not 22.4x. A multiple this far off in a footnote will be caught.
fix: Correct to 53.3x = $1,106.21 / $20.76 (F21 / F13). If you want to show a 22.4x multiple, state the denominator and source it (e.g. FY2027E EPS per consensus); do not leave an unstated denominator on the page. Do not change F21 or F13.

where: slide 3, three-year capex and OCF table
issue: The slide promises a three-year table of capex and operating cash flow with FY2023 $4.32B / $11.07B and FY2026 $6.43B / $15.82B (F19/F20). Two years is not a three-year table. The pack only gives growth rates and the FY2023 and FY2026 endpoints (F19, F20), not FY2024 and FY2025 levels.
fix: Either source FY2024 and FY2025 capex and operating cash flow from the FY2026 10-K cash flow statement (the two comparative years) and produce a genuine three-year or four-year table, or relabel the exhibit 'FY2023 to FY2026: capex CAGR 14.2%, operating cash flow CAGR 12.6%' and show the two endpoints with the CAGR. Do not title it a three-year table with two years of data.

where: Slide 4, grid — 'keeps flexibility' criterion against the buyback row, and the callout '[GAP: share price and repurchase history]'
issue: The single load-bearing claim against buybacks — that a buyback commits the board to ongoing repurchases while a special dividend does not — is a judgment with no evidence. The page itself admits share price and repurchase history are missing. A board member will ask 'why does a buyback commit us to anything?' and there is no answer on the page. This is the argument the recommendation stands on, and it is currently empty.
fix: Research Costco's authorization structure and repurchase history from the 10-K and prior filings: any stated buyback authorization size, shares repurchased in fiscal 2026 and the prior two years, and average price paid. Replace the 'keeps flexibility' judgment with a fact: 'The board's existing authorization is $X and Costco repurchased $Y of stock in fiscal 2026; a special dividend carries no recurring commitment, while a buyback authorization is standing.' If the filings show Costco has a large open authorization, say so and address it head-on.

where: Slide 3 ('Earnings cover growth spending, and $20.2B of cash is still on hand') and Slide 4 ('A special dividend returns surplus cash and keeps more flexibility than buybacks')
issue: Slide 3 makes two points — earnings cover growth, and cash is on hand — and both reappear in Slide 4's side stats ($20.21B cash, $9.23B net income, $145M interest). The cash-on-hand point is the balance-sheet-room argument; the earnings-cover point is the fund-growth argument. Right now the reader gets the same two numbers three times across slides 2, 3 and 4, and no slide owns the comparison to the alternatives.
fix: Give each content slide one job. Slide 3 owns 'growth is affordable': bar chart, net income 9.23 vs capex 6.43 vs cash 20.21, takeaway 'capex is 70% of net income, cash is 3.1x capex'. Slide 4 owns 'surplus cash exists and a special dividend beats a buyback': cut the net income per share stat and the 64x interest stat from the side part (both belong on slide 3 or nowhere), keep cash per share $45.6 and add the researched buyback facts. Retitle slide 3 'Fiscal 2026 capex of $6.43B is 70% of net income; $20.2B of cash sits on top' and slide 4 'A special dividend has no recurring commitment; a buyback authorization is standing'.

where: Slide 5, closing — steps 2 and 3 ('Set a minimum cash buffer' and 'Size a special dividend from cash above the buffer')
issue: The governing thought is 'return only surplus cash, as a one-off special dividend sized after the board confirms a cash buffer' — the buffer is the hinge of the whole recommendation, and the deck never says what it should be or how to set it. The closing defers the only decision that matters to a future meeting, which is fine for a process step but leaves the board voting today on nothing they can size. Also, step 4 ('Confirm open items from the 10-K') is a research task, not a board next step; it does not belong on a roadmap.
fix: Move the open-items research off slide 5 and into this review. On slide 5, replace step 4 with a decision gate that names the two inputs the buffer depends on: 'CFO brings minimum cash buffer recommendation (floor at one quarter of capex, $1.6B, plus operating cash flow coverage) to the December meeting.' Keep step 3 as sizing only, and add the sizing formula to the step: 'Size the special dividend at cash above the buffer, per-share on 443.1M shares.'

where: Slide 2, executive summary — 'only $145M interest expense' and slide 4 — 'net income about 64x interest'
issue: Interest expense of $145M on $303.15B of revenue is presented as evidence of balance-sheet room, but the pages never show debt. $145M of interest could sit on very little debt or a great deal. The '$20.21B cash' figure is also gross — it ignores debt entirely. A board member will not accept 'room on the balance sheet' without the debt number.
fix: Research total debt and net cash from the fiscal 2026 10-K balance sheet. Restate the balance-sheet argument as net cash: 'Cash of $20.21B against total debt of $X gives net cash of $Y.' If debt is material, the $45.6 cash-per-share figure on slide 4 must become net cash per share, or the number misleads.

where: Slide 3 — 'cash covers capex three times over' and 'the earnings left after capex are about $2.8B'
issue: The $2.8B 'left after capex' is net income minus capex, which is not free cash flow and the page says so. But the deck then never gives the reader the actual cash the business generates. Without operating cash flow and the existing dividend, the board cannot judge whether $20.21B is genuinely surplus or is the normal working balance a warehouse retailer must carry. Capital allocation without cash generation is an incomplete argument.
fix: Research operating cash flow, dividends paid, and any share repurchases from the fiscal 2026 10-K cash flow statement. Add one line to slide 3: 'Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow $X, less capex $6.43B, less dividends $Y leaves $Z of free cash flow.' Replace the $2.8B approximation with that figure. Withhold the takeaway sentence on slide 3 until this is in hand — the current takeaway ('cash is 3.1x the year's capex') is true but does not prove surplus.

where: Slide 4, grid — criteria 'protects growth funding, uses surplus cash, keeps flexibility, balance sheet risk' with 'the scores are judgments, labelled as such'
issue: A 3x4 grid of judgment scores where every score is the author's opinion is a long way to say 'special dividend wins.' Boards read grids as analysis; this one is editorial. The layout also mixes a judgment grid with a side stats box, which means the reader is decoding two different things on one page.
fix: Cut the grid to three rows and two criteria that are actually evidence-backed: 'funds growth in full' and 'creates no recurring commitment,' scored Yes/No, not 1-5. Move the remaining criteria to speaker notes. Keep the side stats box with cash per share and the researched buyback facts.

where: Slide 1, cover — 'Costco capital allocation: return more cash or keep building?'
issue: The cover poses the question but the deck answers it on slide 2. A board cover that asks what the deck answers is a wasted page, and the question is already in the reader's head.
fix: Change the title to the answer: 'Keep building: fund growth in full and return surplus cash as a one-off special dividend.' Keep 'Board meeting, November 2026' as the date line. Save the question for the executive summary body if the chair wants the framing.

where: slide 2, point (1) and slide 3 bullet: "$9.23B net income against $6.43B capex" and "the earnings left after capex are about $2.8B (net income minus capex)"
issue: Net income is not the funding source. Capex is funded from operating cash flow, and cash at 2026-08-30 ($20.21B) is a point-in-time balance, not a fiscal-year flow. Comparing a balance sheet stock to a P&L flow and to a cash flow item mixes periods and bases; $9.23B less $6.43B = $2.80B is an accrual residual, not surplus cash, and the deck itself concedes 'operating cash flow is not in the facts [GAP]'. If the true OCF is, say, $11B, the surplus is nearer $4.6B, not $2.8B — the special dividend is sized off the wrong number.
fix: Rewrite the executive summary point (1) and slide 3's bullet as: 'Fiscal 2026 capex of $6.43B equals X% of operating cash flow of $Y.YYB [research]'; delete 'about 70% of earnings' and 'about $2.8B' until the operating cash flow figure is sourced from the same FY2026 10-K.

where: slide 2 notes and slide 5 step (4), all reading '[GAP]': operating cash flow, existing dividend, debt, share price, repurchase history
issue: The recommendation is 'return only surplus cash as a one-off special dividend sized after the board confirms a cash buffer' — but every input needed to size the dividend (free cash flow, minimum cash buffer, existing dividend commitment, debt maturity wall, D&A and maintenance capex within the $6.43B growth figure) is unsourced. Slide 4's 'special dividend returns surplus cash and keeps more flexibility' is asserted, not evidenced. A board cannot vote on a number the deck does not contain.
fix: Add a sourcing column to slide 5: for each of operating cash flow, dividends paid, total debt and maturities, D&A, maintenance vs growth capex, cash and equivalents plus short-term investments, name the 10-K line item and page. Do not declare a special dividend recommendation until the FY2026 statement of cash flows is in hand.

where: slide 4, options grid: 'fund growth only, ongoing buybacks, special dividend' against 'protects growth funding, uses surplus cash, keeps flexibility, balance sheet risk', 'The scores are judgments, labelled as such'
issue: Three options scored against four criteria with no quantification and no discount rate or hurdle. 'Uses surplus cash' is not a criterion — surplus is the answer, not the test. Buybacks are dismissed as committing 'to ongoing repurchases' with no buyback yield (share price [GAP]) and no cost of capital comparison; a special dividend also commits capital irreversibly once declared. The grid as drawn will not survive the first question.
fix: Replace judgment scores with drivers: for each option give (i) cash returned per share on 443.1M shares, (ii) pro forma cash balance and interest cover from $145M interest expense, (iii) impact on the $6.43B capex plan. State the share price [research] so buyback yield can be shown against the special dividend per-share amount.

where: slide 2, point (2): 'The balance sheet has room: $20.21B cash and only $145M interest expense'
issue: Interest expense of $145M is a P&L flow for FY2026; there is no gross debt, no lease liability (material for Costco), no coverage ratio and no maturity profile. '$20.21B cash' also ignores that a minimum operating cash buffer for stores and payables is precisely what the deck says must be confirmed — so the investable cash is less than $20.21B and possibly far less. 'Room' is asserted.
fix: Delete 'only $145M'; replace with 'net cash of $Z after minimum operating buffer of $B [research]' and, if material, distinguish cash and short-term investments from total debt and finance lease liabilities.

where: slide 3 bar chart: 'net income 9.23, capex 6.43, cash 20.21' on one axis
issue: Three bars of one year's flow, one year's flow and one day's stock, plotted together without footnoting the period. Capex $6.43B / revenue $303.15B = 2.12% is a valid ratio; '$20.21B cash is 3.1x the year's capex' is a stock-to-flow ratio that is arithmetically true but decision-irrelevant — three years of capex is not available for distribution while the business runs.
fix: Keep the chart but split panels: Panel A flows (revenue $303.15B, net income $9.23B, capex $6.43B, operating cash flow $Y.YYB [research]); Panel B balance sheet (cash $20.21B, short-term investments and debt [research]). Retitle slide 3 'Capex is 2.1% of revenue and N% of operating cash flow'.

where: slides 2, 3, 4, 5 — no slide addresses the growth case
issue: The governing thought is 'keep funding warehouse growth in full'. There is zero evidence in the deck on warehouse openings, the 2027 plan, returns on new warehouses, or what ends the growth phase. The board is told to approve $6.43B (or more) with no answer to 'how many warehouses and what return on capital?' That is the first question a committee asks of a capital allocation paper.
fix: Either add a growth slide (openings, capex per warehouse, ROMI or comparable-warehouse returns from the 10-K) or fold the growth case into slide 3 as a second panel; cut the judgment grid on slide 4 down to make room.

where: storyline, governing thought: 'return only surplus cash, as a one-off special dividend sized after the board confirms a cash buffer'
issue: The recommendation follows from an unsourced 'surplus'. No sensitivity on the dividend: what does per-share look like if capex overruns, if OCF falls, if the buffer is set at one, two or three months of revenue ($25B–$75B range — larger than the cash balance itself)? A committee will ask this in the first two minutes.
fix: On slide 4 or 5 add a one-row sensitivity: special dividend per share on 443.1M shares at surplus of $2B / $4B / $6B, footnoted as illustrative pending the operating cash flow and buffer figures. Label the three scenarios and the source of each input.

issue: The deck ships its own data gaps to the board. A [GAP] on a slide is a promise the analyst did not keep; on a closing roadmap it reads as 'we have not done the work'. Slide 5 can carry open items for management, but the deck itself must resolve the numbers the recommendation depends on.
fix: Move every [GAP] off slides 2, 3 and 4 into a single 'Open items for management' line on slide 5, and resolve the ownership ones (operating cash flow, share price, debt, dividends) from the 10-K before the board pack goes out.

where: slide 4 side stats: 'cash per share $45.6 (20.21B / 443.1M shares), net income per share about $20.8 (9.23B / 443.1M)'
issue: Arithmetic is right (20.21/0.4431 = 45.61; 9.23/0.4431 = 20.83). But 'cash per share' uses cash at 2026-08-30 against 443.1M shares at 2026-09-29, a one-month mismatch, minor but avoidable; and neither per-share metric is decision-relevant without the share price.
fix: Use the same as-of date for both inputs or footnote the mismatch; keep both per-share figures only if the share price [research] is shown alongside so a buyback yield can be calculated.

issue: Slide 2 says the $13.3B special dividend is 'declared and fully funded' and shows a single $13.3B box, but slide 1 says '$30 special dividend' and slide 4's right panel says '$20.21B plus free cash flow $9.38B covers capex $6.5B and ordinary dividends' — the $13.3B special dividend is not in that coverage list, and the two pages disagree on what is being funded.
fix: Pick one funding statement and use it everywhere: on slide 4, replace the right-panel bullet with 'Cash $20.21B + FCF $9.38B covers the $13.3B special dividend, $6.5B capex and ordinary dividends' — or if it does not, delete 'fully funded' on slide 2 and state the gap.

issue: The $670 floor is asserted, never derived. Slide 2 says 'Below $670 the earnings yield exceeds 3.10%' and slide 5 repeats '$670 per share' with no arithmetic on the page; the only derivation is footnote 2 in 6-point type.
fix: Put the one-line derivation on slide 2 next to the $670 box: '$670 = $20.76 EPS ÷ 3.10% after-tax cash yield'. Move it out of footnote 2.

issue: The title ends in an ellipsis and the page never resolves it — 'Capex has grown 14.2% a year against 7.8% revenue growth…' — while the right column says the plan 'holds' only 'while after-tax return on capital stays 22.2%'. That is a conditional, not an answer, and slide 3's footnote 3 admits the marginal return 'is not disclosed in the filings reviewed nor available in the sources'.
fix: Retitle to the actual claim: 'Capex grew 14.2% a year vs 7.8% revenue; the $6.5B plan holds only if return on capital stays 22.2%'. Put that conditional in a callout box so the reader cannot miss it.

where: slide 3, right column and side block
issue: 'The plan is already funded and already in the ground' is an assertion with no number behind it in the text; the supporting line ('26 net new openings expected in fiscal 2026') does not prove it. Slide 3's footnote 2 also says two buildings slipped to fiscal 2027, which contradicts 'in the ground'.
fix: Replace the bullet with the numbers that do prove it ('$20.21B cash + $9.38B FCF covers the $6.5B plan; 16 of 26 openings already signed') and move the 2027 slip to a visible risk bullet, not a footnote.

issue: The page is two half-pages joined: a three-bar chart on the left using a fraction of its area, a sparse text column on the right, and a floating dark box bottom-right that overlaps the column it belongs to. The chart has no takeaway line under it.
fix: Make the chart the full page width or drop it; add a one-line takeaway under the bars ('Capex CAGR 14.2% exceeds revenue CAGR 7.8% by 6.4 pts'); anchor the dark box to the right column edge so it stops floating.

issue: The bar chart includes 'Return on existing capital 22.20%' — a metric on a different basis and a different scale — next to 'Buyback earnings yield 1.88%'. The 22.20% bar dwarfs the comparison the title is about and invites the reader to draw the wrong conclusion. The chart also needs a legend to be read.
fix: Remove the 22.20% bar from this chart (keep it on slide 3) and show only the three comparable yields: buyback 1.88%, after-tax cash 3.10%, pre-tax cash 4.12%. Title stays; the chart then proves it.

issue: The title compares the buyback yield (1.88%) to the after-tax cash yield (3.10%), but the chart adds a 4.12% pre-tax bar and a 22.20% return-on-capital bar, so the page argues three different comparisons at once. The right panel also states a third funding claim ('cash $20.21B plus free cash flow $9.38B covers capex $6.5B and ordinary dividends').
fix: Make the page one comparison — buyback at $1,106.21 yields 1.88% vs 3.10% cash — and move the funding coverage statement to slide 2 where it belongs.

issue: Row 3 says buybacks 'earn 1.88% against 3.10% after-tax cash' at '$1,106.21' — the current price — while the decision is to set a $670 floor. The reader is never told the 65% gap between today's price and the floor, nor that the $4B authorization will therefore not be spent at today's price.
fix: Add one line under row 3: 'At $1,106.21 the buyback is 1.9% below the 3.10% cash yield; at $670 the two are equal.' That is the whole argument in one sentence.

issue: The dark callout box's left edge has a chevron/notch that sits inside the text column and does not align to any other element on the page.
fix: Remove the notch and align the box to the text column's left margin.

issue: The title breaks with a single orphan word 'floor' on line two.
fix: Shorten to 'Adopt a $670 buyback floor, hold capex at $6.5B, and confirm the dividend' or rebalance the line break.

issue: Jargon and inconsistent terminology: 'CAGR', 'after-tax cash yield', 'return on capital', 'free cash flow', 'operating cash flow' appear without a consistent definition, and slide 3 says 'operating cash flow' where slide 2 and 4 say 'free cash flow'.
fix: Use 'free cash flow' everywhere and define it once on slide 2 ('free cash flow = operating cash flow less capex') so the same number cannot be read two ways.

issue: Every owner is 'November 2026' and the timing column gives no day or dependency; row 4 says only 'First quarter after approval'. An action page without dates is a wish list.
fix: Give each row a date ('Nov 2026 board meeting', 'Q1 FY27 close') and state who signs off on the $670 floor.

where: DCF / cover model — slide 1 and slide 2
issue: The title says a $30 special dividend; the top line says $13.3B. At 443.1M shares, $30 × 443.1M = $13.293B ≈ $13.3B, so the $30 per-share and $13.3B are internally consistent — but a $30/share dividend on a ~$1,106 stock is 2.7%, which is plausible. The real discovery is that the $48.99 EPS implied by the footer of slide 2 ($20.76 / 3.10% = $669.7, rounded to $670) is far above the company's likely EPS. This doesn't tie.
fix: Recompute the implied earnings: if the $20.76 EPS is correct, then $670 ÷ $20.76 = 32.3x P/E, not the 3.10% yield. The footer must show: 'The $670 floor is the price at which the earnings yield equals the 3.10% after-tax cash alternative: $20.76 ÷ 0.0310 = $670.' If $20.76 is wrong, replace it with the correct EPS and recompute the floor. Also reconcile the $20.76 to the model: if Q3 FY2026 EPS is $20.76, the implied P/E at $1,106 is 53.3x, which is not the 1.88% yield quoted. There is a hard-coded or mis-scaled EPS plug.

issue: The 13-week T-bill yield is quoted as '4.12% pre-tax, 3.10% after tax' and the footnote says '1 – 24.7% effective tax rate'. 4.12% × (1 – 0.247) = 3.102%, which ties. But the same slide says 'The $13.3B special dividend is declared and fully funded' covered by '$20.21B cash plus $9.38B free cash flow'. $20.21B + $9.38B = $29.59B, while the uses are $13.3B dividend + $6.5B capex = $19.8B, leaving $9.79B. The slide does not show what happens to the remaining $9.79B, and the $4B buyback authorization is not deducted. The cash bridge does not balance to a source or line item.
fix: Add a cash bridge on slide 2: Sources: cash $20.21B + FCF $9.38B = $29.59B. Uses: $13.3B dividend + $6.5B capex + $4B buyback = $23.8B. Remaining: $5.79B. If the buyback is not funded in FY2026, state that explicitly: 'the $4B authorization is incremental and is not assumed in the FY2026 cash plan.' Show the arithmetic on the page or in a footnote.

issue: Slide 3 compares a 3-year capex CAGR (14.2%) to a 3-year revenue CAGR (7.8%). Slide 4 compares a buyback earnings yield (1.88%) to a 13-week T-bill (3.10%). These are different periods, units and risk. A 3-year historical CAGR is not a forward-looking return on the $6.5B. A buyback earnings yield is an earnings-capitalization measure, not a cash return. The slide calls both 'return' and puts them on the same bar chart — that is not an honest comparison.
fix: Put the comparison on one basis. Either (a) show all four metrics as realized cash-on-cash returns for the same 12-month period (FY2026E): capex return 22.2%, buyback earnings yield 1.88%, after-tax T-bill 3.10%, and pre-tax T-bill 4.12%; or (b) separate the charts with explicit labels: 'Historical CAGR, FY2023–FY2026' on slide 3 and 'Forward yield on 12-month cash flow, FY2026E' on slide 4. Do not mix realized CAGR with forward yield on the same axis without a label.

issue: The callout says 'Funded, not discretionary: cash of $20.21B plus $9.38B free cash flow covers the plan.' The 'plan' is $6.5B capex plus the $13.3B declared dividend = $19.8B. But the $4B buyback is not included. If the buyback is also to be 'covered' — and slide 5 action 3 authorizes it — the callout is wrong. If the buyback is contingent on the $670 floor, the callout should say so.
fix: Rewrite: 'Funded: cash of $20.21B plus $9.38B free cash flow covers the declared $13.3B dividend and the $6.5B capex plan ($19.8B). The $4B buyback authorization is incremental and is drawn only if the shares trade below $670.' Add the arithmetic on the page: $20.21B + $9.38B = $29.59B; uses $19.8B; surplus $9.79B.

issue: The 1.88% buyback earnings yield is computed as $20.76 EPS ÷ $1,106.21 = 1.876%. But the same page says the buyback earns 1.88% 'against 3.10% after-tax cash' — yet the $4B buyback is authorized, not executed. The 1.88% is the yield on the current price, not on the actual repurchase price. If the buyback is executed at $1,106, the yield is 1.88%. But if the floor is $670, the yield at the floor is 3.10%, which is the point. The page does not show the yield at the floor as a separate line, so the reader cannot see the trigger math.
fix: Add a column or a footnote: 'At $1,106.21: earnings yield 1.88%. At $670.00: earnings yield 3.10%.' Show the arithmetic: $20.76 ÷ $1,106.21 = 1.88%; $20.76 ÷ $670.00 = 3.10%. Then the floor is visibly the break-even price.

where: slide 4, footer note 2 and slide 2, footer note 1
issue: Slide 4 footer says '3.10% after-tax = 4.12% pre-tax 13-week T-bill × (1 – 24.7% effective tax rate)'. Slide 2 footer says the same. 4.12% × (1 – 0.247) = 3.102%. That ties. But the 24.7% effective tax rate is not shown as an input or cell reference on any page. It is a hard-coded plug in the footnote. If the effective rate changes, the 3.10% floor changes.
fix: Add the 24.7% effective tax rate as a visible input on slide 2 or slide 4, with a source line: 'Effective tax rate per Q3 FY2026 10-Q, income tax expense $3.028B ÷ pre-tax income $12.266B = 24.7%.' Then the reader can trace 4.12% × (1 – 0.247) = 3.10%.

issue: The title says 'Capex has grown 14.2% a year against 7.8% revenue growth…' and the right column says 'Capex is compounding at 14.2% a year'. But the same slide says 'Two buildings slipped to fiscal 2027' and the source line says 'the marginal after-tax return on the $6.5B plan is not disclosed in the filings reviewed nor available in the sources; the page does not claim the plan earns 22.2%.' So the page admits it cannot support the 22.2% return on the forward plan, yet the title and the callout still frame the plan as holding at 22.2%.
fix: Either (a) source the 22.2% forward return to a filing or management guidance and state the source, or (b) retitle slide 3 to 'Capex has grown 14.2% a year against 7.8% revenue growth; the forward return on the $6.5B plan is not disclosed' and add the missing return to the research request.

issue: The source line says 'Management guidance via app.ultralayer.ai'. That is not a primary source. If the 26 net new openings figure comes from a transcript or guidance, name the document and date. The same applies to the '$9.38B free cash flow' on slides 2 and 3 — if it is derived, show the derivation (operating cash flow $X minus capex $Y).
fix: Replace 'management guidance via app.ultralayer.ai' with the primary source: 'Costco Q3 FY2026 earnings call transcript, filed 2026-06-03, or Q3 FY2026 10-Q, filed 2026-06-03.' Add the FCF derivation: 'FCF = operating cash flow $X – capex $Y = $9.38B.' If the 26 openings figure is guidance, cite the call date and speaker.

issue: 'Capex grew 14.2% a year against 7.8% revenue growth; existing capital still earns 22.2% after tax.' The 22.2% is sourced to slide 4 as 'return on existing capital' — but slide 4's chart label says 'Return on existing capital' at 22.20%, and slide 2 says 'existing capital still earns 22.2% after tax'. If the 22.2% is the existing-capital return, the forward plan's 22.2% is a different number that is not disclosed. The two pages use the same 22.2% for different things.
fix: On slide 2, change to 'existing capital earns 22.2% after tax; the forward return on the $6.5B plan is not disclosed.' On slide 4, label the bar 'Return on existing capital, FY2026E' and add a footnote: 'Forward return on the $6.5B capex plan is not disclosed.'

issue: The bar chart has no zero baseline label and no y-axis. The bars are labelled 1.88%, 3.10%, 4.12% and 22.20%. The 22.20% bar is roughly 12× the 1.88% bar, which is consistent with 22.2/1.88 = 11.8. But without an axis, a reader cannot verify scale. The chart mixes a buyback earnings yield, a cash yield from a risk-free instrument, and a return on existing capital — three different things — on one axis with no unit label.
fix: Add a y-axis labelled '%' and a zero baseline. Either split into two panels (cash yields vs returns) or add a subtitle: 'All metrics are annualized yields / returns for FY2026E, after tax.' Add a footnote distinguishing buyback earnings yield from cash yield from return on capital.

issue: The right half is prose and a callout, not evidence: 'Capex is compounding at 14.2% a year' and 'The plan is funded and largely in the ground' are restated in text while the bar chart only covers the left half. The page's title claim ('holds only while return on capital stays 22.2%') is never proved with data — the 22.2% tie to capex is the whole argument and it is asserted in a bullet.
fix: Split the page: keep the three-bar CAGR chart as one exhibit, and add a second visual that plots capex CAGR against return on capital over FY23–FY26 (with a 14.2% reference line) so the reader can see the 22.2% hold. Replace the sentence bullets with that chart plus one 8-word takeaway.

issue: The top table stops about two-thirds down; the bottom third is a grey box where the left paragraph runs three lines and the right bullet 'The 24.7% effective tax rate is an input' floats alone. That is dead space and an orphan.
fix: Cut the grey box to two lines (one 10-word conclusion plus one supporting number), move the tax-rate input into the footnotes where it belongs, and add a small two-bar yield-vs-buyback chart beside the table so the 1.88% vs 3.10% gap is visible, not just tabular.

issue: Footnote 3 says 'The forward return on the $6.58 capex plan is not disclosed in the filings reviewed not available in the sources; the 22.2% is the return on the existing asset base, not a marginal return.' That admits the 22.2% does not apply to the new $6.5B — the page's core claim — and the broken grammar makes it worse.
fix: Either source a marginal return for the $6.5B plan from management guidance (see research request) and cite it, or retitle the page to what is true: 'Return on the existing asset base is 22.2%; the $6.5B plan must clear that bar,' and put the caveat in plain words as a stated assumption.

issue: Row 2 asserts 'return on capital stays 22.2%' as fact when slide 3 footnote 3 says it is the existing-base return, not the return on the new capex. The executive summary overstates its own evidence, and slide 1's '$13.3B' is not carried onto slide 2's title page and the $4B authorization appears only in row 4 and footnote 2.
fix: Rewrite row 2 to match slide 3's actual evidence and add the $4B authorization and $30 per share to row 1 so the summary carries every number a reader needs before turning the page.

issue: The right half reuses the title's phrase 'holds only while return on capital stays 22.2%' and repeats '14.2% a year' verbatim from slide 2 and slide 3's own chart label — same fact three times on one spread.
fix: State 14.2% once in the chart label and once in the title; delete it from the body bullets.

issue: Footnote typography differs page to page: slide 2 sets the notes as 1/2 in one block; slide 4 and 5 repeat the same note number for different content and slide 5's note 2 is a full sentence with an em-dash clause. Inconsistent block height pushes slide 4's grey box against the footer.
fix: Set one footnote template (same point size, same block bottom margin), number notes per page, and align the bottom of the grey box on slide 4 to that template wherever the table ends.

issue: The $670 floor is circular: 'the $670 floor is the price at which the earnings yield equals the 3.10% after-tax cash alternative', and 3.10% is itself derived as '4.12% x (1 - 24.7%)'. The 'break-even' is therefore a restatement of the T-bill after-tax yield, not evidence of value. It also ignores the fact that the $1,106.21 buyback proceeds would earn the same 3.10% if simply left in cash.
fix: Replace the 'break-even' framing with a hurdle that is independent of the T-bill: state the required spread over cash (e.g. 150-200bps) and show the implied floor price at that spread, then mark $670 as the price at a stated spread. Delete the '1.88% is below the 3.10% cash yield, so don't buy' conclusion until a spread is defined.

issue: The 22.2% 'return on existing asset base' is introduced in the title and the right-hand callout ('The plan is funded and largely in the ground / 26 new openings') but the footnote admits 'The forward return on the $6.5B capex plan is not disclosed in the filings reviewed not available in the sources; the 22.2% is the return on the existing asset base, not a marginal return.' That is an unsourced assumption doing the work of the page and it is not the metric the decision actually needs.
fix: Cut the 22.2% from the title and the callout, or replace it with the marginal return on new warehouse capex that the model actually supports. If it cannot be sourced, change the title to the one claim the data supports: 'Capex grew 14.2% a year against 7.8% revenue growth; 26 net openings are expected in FY2026.'

issue: 'return on capital stays 22.2%' and 'Capex grew 14.2% a year against 7.8% revenue growth' are used to justify holding the $6.5B plan, but the 14.2% capex CAGR and 7.8% revenue CAGR are computed on different bases — capex is 'from $4.32B (fiscal 2023) to $6.43B (fiscal 2026)' and revenue growth is nowhere broken out with the same years. The comparison is not like-for-like.
fix: Add the revenue base years to slide 3's footnote (e.g. fiscal 2023 revenue to fiscal 2026 revenue) so both CAGRs are on identical fiscal-year windows, and show the two series on the same chart with one unit per axis. Or drop the CAGR comparison and use the absolute dollar gap.

issue: 'The $13.3B special dividend is declared and fully funded' is asserted, but the funding math ('$20.21B cash plus $9.38B free cash flow') nets to $29.59B against $13.3B dividend plus $6.5B capex, leaving roughly $9.8B unaccounted for, and the $4B buyback authorization is a further claim on the same cash. No bridge from cash sources to the dividend, capex and buyback uses.
fix: Add a sources-and-uses bridge on slide 2: opening cash $20.21B + FCF $9.38B vs dividend $13.3B + capex $6.5B + buyback $4B (if drawn) = $23.8B, with the residual stated. If the dividend is declared and payable from existing cash, say so and separate it from the incremental capex and buyback.

issue: 'The $4B buyback is authorized, not executed, so 1.88% is the yield on the current price, not on the actual repurchase price.' The page then recommends buying only below $670, but no data supports whether $4B of stock is available at or below that floor, and no data supports the EPS accretion or share count effect of buying at $670 vs $1,106.21.
fix: Add a sensitivity: shares repurchased and EPS impact at $670, $850 and $1,106.21, using the $4B and $20.76 EPS already on the page. State the source for any volume/support assumption at the floor.

issue: The bar chart shows three CAGRs (14.2%, 12.6%, 7.8%) as if comparable, but capex and revenue are flow variables and operating cash flow is a different construct; the chart is honest on zero baseline, but the comparison mixes capital spending growth with cash generation and revenue growth and uses one axis without saying so.
fix: Either reframe as a single-series chart on the capex CAGR with revenue growth as a labelled reference line, or split into a two-panel exhibit (capex and revenue growth; cash flow separately). Label the axis '% per year' and the period 'fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2026' on the chart itself, not just the subtitle.

issue: 'The special dividend is declared' — 'declared' is repeated three times on one page (callout 1, callout sub-box, decision banner). Redundant and it reads like the deck is arguing with itself.
