fix: State 'declared' once, in the banner, and use the callout to give the date of declaration and the payment date.

issue: The row is labelled 'Buyback at the $1,106.21 close' with yield 1.88% = '$20.76 EPS / $1,106.21'. The $1,106.21 is sourced to 'Yahoo Finance' and dated 13 Nov 2026, which is the same day as the buyback authorization, so the price and the authorization are simultaneous and no post-authorization price is shown.
fix: Add the price range since the authorization date and the volume-weighted price if available, and label the close as 'close, 13 Nov 2026' in the row.

issue: The tax-rate derivation is internally inconsistent. Slide 2 footnote 1 defines the effective tax rate as tax expense $3.028B / net income $9.238B = 24.7%, but the Washington Post source label on slide 2 says '24.7% effective tax rate' and slide 4 shows '24.7% Effective tax rate'. A $13.3B dividend plus $6.5B capex is $19.8B against $20.21B cash plus $9.38B free cash flow of $29.59B — that part reconciles, but the 1.88% vs 3.10% gap that drives the whole recommendation rests entirely on the 24.7% rate. If that rate is wrong, the $670 floor is wrong.
fix: Check the 24.7% against the 10-K income tax note and show the calculation on the slide: state pre-tax T-bill 4.12%, tax at 24.7%, after-tax 3.10%. Add the pre-tax-to-after-tax bridge as a visible line so a reader can verify $670 = $20.76 / 3.10% without a footnote.

issue: The right third of the page is two grey boxes of text and the chart area below the bars is dead space — the bars end near the top and the x-axis sits with an empty band underneath. The chart carries the 14.2% vs 7.8% point but says nothing about the 22.2% claim in the title; the reader has to hunt for where 22.2% comes from and it only appears in footnote 3.
fix: Move the 22.2% return calculation into the right column as its own box, or add it as a labelled callout on the chart. Pull the bars down and fill the space with the FY23-FY26 capex gap ($4.32B to $6.43B, +$2.11B) annotated directly on the chart.

issue: The three big figures — 24.7%, $4B, 22.2% — sit in their own boxes with no labels linking them to the argument. 24.7% is the tax rate, $4B is the buyback authorization, 22.2% is return on existing capital. Two of these have nothing to do with the page's title about the yield gap, and the reader cannot tell why they are there.
fix: Cut the $4B and 22.2% boxes from slide 4 or move them to slide 3 where the return-on-capital point belongs. Keep only the 24.7% and label it 'Effective tax rate used in the yield calculation'. Move the cash-returned table ($1.15B, $848M, $9.38B, $20.21B) up so it fills the freed space.

issue: The bottom source and footnote apparatus is dense, runs four to five lines, and on slide 3 runs across the full width at near-illegible size. Footnotes 1 and 2 on slide 3 explain new openings and the fiscal 2027 slippage — material that belongs in the body, not the footer.
fix: Cut slide 3 footnote 2 to one line and move the new-openings point into the chart as a callout or into the right-column box. Standardise the source line to one line at 8pt on every slide.

issue: 'needs 22.2% returns' is vague about what is being returned on. Slide 4 footnote 3 calls it 'return on existing capital'. Two names for the same thing.
fix: Title slide 3 'Capex grew 14.2% a year vs revenue 7.8%; the $6.5B plan needs a 22.2% return on existing capital'. Use 'return on existing capital' on every slide.

issue: The navy decision banner repeats the page title almost word for word: title says 'Fund the declared $13.3B dividend and $6.5B capex; buy back only below $670 per share' and the banner says the same in longer form. It adds length, not information.
fix: Either cut the banner and let the title carry the decision, or rewrite the banner to state the ask and the date only: 'Board decision, November 2026: confirm the $13.3B special dividend and $6.5B capex, and adopt the $670 floor.'

issue: The cover has a large empty band between the question line and the footer. The title block sits in the upper third with nothing below to anchor the page.
fix: Raise the footer rule or add a one-line context strap under the question — e.g. 'Prepared for the November 2026 board meeting'. Do not add decoration.

where: slide 3 title, vs slide 3 footnote 3 and slide 4 callout '22.2% Return on existing capital, FY2026E'
issue: The title says the '$6.5B plan needs 22.2% returns' but footnote 3 says 'The marginal after-tax return on the $6.58 plan is not disclosed in the filings reviewed' and calls 22.2% a return 'on the existing asset base, not a marginal return.' The headline figure therefore answers a different question than the headline asks.
fix: Retitle slide 3 to what is actually measured: 'Capex compounded 14.2% a year vs 7.8% revenue; FY2026E return on existing capital 22.2%, marginal return on incremental capex not disclosed.' Put 22.2% labelled 'ROIC, FY2026E (existing capital base)' and add a standalone line stating the marginal return is not disclosed.

where: slide 4, yield table and slide 2 step 3
issue: The comparison sets a forward earnings yield (1.88%) against a Treasury yield (3.10%) and calls the difference a reason not to buy back. Equity earnings yield vs risk-free rate is not a like-for-like hurdle — no equity risk premium, no cost of equity, no WACC. The 3.10% after-tax T-bill is the floor, not the discount rate.
fix: Add a cost-of-equity or WACC line to the slide 4 table and compare the buyback yield against that, not the 3.10% T-bill. If the intended test is 'buyback yield vs cash yield on the balance sheet,' state the 3.10% after-tax cash yield on cash explicitly and label it as the alternative use of the $4B, not the company's cost of capital.

issue: Slide 2 step 3 says 'A buyback at $1,106.21 yields 1.88%, below the cash yield'; slide 4 table says earnings yield 1.88% and after-tax cash yield 3.10%, difference -1.22 pts. Slides 4 shows the $670 row with both 3.10% and difference 0.00 — internally consistent, but the $1,106.21 row's 'Difference' cell is computed against the after-tax cash yield, not the cash yield of the $4B authorization, and the two are described inconsistently across pages.
fix: Use one phrase everywhere: 'after-tax cash yield, 3.10%.' Replace 'cash yield' in slide 2 step 3 with 'after-tax cash yield (3.10%)' so slides 2 and 4 tie word for word.

where: slide 2 body step 1 and slide 3 chart
issue: Slide 2 says '$20.21B plus free cash flow $9.38B covers the dividend, $6.5B capex and ordinary dividends'; slide 3 chart shows FY2026 revenue of $303.15B against capex of $6.43B. The $20.21B cash is dated FY2026; free cash flow of $9.38B is labelled 'FY2026' in slide 4. Confirm the $9.38B is free cash flow after the $6.5B capex or before — as written, funding the dividend with FCF and also funding capex with the same $9.38B double counts.
fix: On slide 2 step 1, state 'Free cash flow after capex, $9.38B' and label the $20.21B as of FY2026 year-end. If $9.38B is before capex, show the arithmetic: $20.21B + $9.38B - $6.5B capex - ordinary dividends = dividend coverage.

issue: Both footnotes compute the effective tax rate as 24.7% from 'income tax expense $3.02B / (net income $9.23B + income tax expense $3.02B).' That is $3.02B / $12.25B = 24.65%, rounded to 24.7%, which ties. But slide 4 also shows '24.7% Effective tax rate' as a standalone blue box — the same number is derived twice with different framings; confirm it is FY2026 and sourced to the same 10-K both times.
fix: State the tax rate once, in one footnote, with the source (Costco 10-K FY2026, income statement). Remove the duplicate derivation on slide 4 footnote 1.

issue: The only stated risk is 'timing risk' (two buildings moved to fiscal 2027). The $6.43B FY2026 capex implies a return of 22.2% on existing capital; the deck never shows what happens if the marginal return on the new $6.5B is, say, 10% or 5%. No sensitivity on the capex decision.
fix: Add a small sensitivity to slide 3: rows for marginal after-tax return on incremental capex of 5% / 10% / 22.2%, columns for NOPAT added, and show the implied effect on ROIC and on the decision. If the marginal number is genuinely not available, present the break-even marginal return required to keep ROIC flat at 22.2%.

where: slide 3 bar chart, 'Capex and revenue, fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2026'
issue: Capex ($4.32B, $6.43B) and revenue ($242.29B, $303.15B) are plotted on the same chart with one implied axis; capex is a rounding error on the revenue scale, so the visual understates the 14.2% capex CAGR that the page is built on. The legend lists both series but no axis is labelled.
fix: Split into two panels or use an indexed chart (FY2023 = 100) with both series and index values labeled. If keeping one chart, add the y-axis label ('$B') and say in the chart title that capex is plotted on a secondary scale.

where: slide 1 cover vs slide 2 executive summary
issue: Slide 1 says 'Fund the declared $30 per share special dividend'; slide 2 says 'Fund the declared $13.3B dividend.' Two units ($/share vs $B) for the same item and the reader has to do the math (443.1M x $30 = $13.29B).
fix: On slide 1 write '$30 per share ($13.3B) special dividend' so both pages carry both units.

issue: '$670 = EPS $20.76 / 3.10% after-tax cash yield' is stated as arithmetic, but the text of slide 4 and slide 2 call it a discipline threshold. Footnote 2 clarifies, but the formula in footnote 1 reads as an equation, not a policy rule.
fix: In slide 4 footnote 1, change to: '$670 is the price at which the earnings yield ($20.76 / $670 = 3.10%) equals the 3.10% after-tax cash yield; it is a discipline threshold, not a forecast.' (mirrors slide 5 footnote 1).

issue: Slide 3 shows revenue FY2023 $242.29B and FY2026 $303.15B — those are two endpoints; the '7.8% a year' is a CAGR over three years, not a year-over-year rate. The page also says operating cash flow 'grew 12.6% a year,' same endpoint issue.
fix: Add '(3-yr CAGR)' after both 14.2%, 7.8% and 12.6% on slides 2 and 3. Better: add the FY2024 and FY2025 bars so the reader sees the path, not just endpoints.

issue: 'the company draws the $4B authorization only below that price' is attributed to Costco 'declares $30 special dividend and reauthorizes $4B buyback, 2026-11-11' but the release likely does not state that the company only buys below $670 — that is management's stated intention if at all. Verify the exact source of this representation.
fix: Confirm the 2026-11-11 Costco release actually states the below-$670 condition; if it does not, change to 'the company has stated the buyback is discretionary at the current price' and cite the call or release verbatim.

issue: Both slides carry the same message about the return comparison: slide 3 is titled "Free cash flow of $9.4B covers the $13.3B dividend and the $6.5B capex plan" but its right argument already includes "22.2% after-tax return on capital versus 1.88% earnings yield on a buyback and 4.12% on Treasury bills"; slide 4 then repeats the comparison in a full table. The two claims are not MECE.
fix: Split the assignment cleanly. Make slide 3 strictly the funding and cover page — waterfall $15.82B opex cash flow less $6.43B capex to $9.38B FCF, $13.3B special dividend funded from $20.21B cash, 3.1x cover — and delete the return comparison from slide 3 entirely. Leave the 22.2% vs 1.88% vs 4.12% vs 5.15% ranking to slide 4. Keep the warehouse counts (16 opened, 13 planned) on slide 4, where the capex argument belongs.

issue: The title "Growth capital earns 22.2% after tax, so capex should stay ahead of buybacks" is the weakest of the five because it only covers two of the four rows in the table. The table also ranks cash at 4.12% and debt repayment at 5.15%. The title does not claim what the page proves.
fix: Retitle slide 4 as a ranking claim covering the set: "Warehouse growth earns 22.2% after tax, ahead of debt repayment at 5.15%, cash at 4.12% and a buyback at 1.88%". The roadmap step on slide 5 can then refer back to this ranking rather than restating the capex conclusion.

issue: The buyback price trigger moves between the two pages. Slide 2 says "buybacks only below the current price"; slide 5 says the authorization should be exercised "below $1,000 per share, where the earnings yield exceeds 2.1%". A board cannot approve a policy that changes between the recommendation and the resolution.
fix: Pick one discipline and use it on both slides. The stronger version is the $1,000 test, since it is a stated threshold rather than a moving reference: "buybacks only below $1,000 per share, where the earnings yield exceeds 2.1%". Put that exact phrase on slide 2 and repeat it in slide 5 step 3.

issue: The cover carries three decisions in its title — dividend, capex and buyback — plus F35 and F21 as backup facts. A cover does not need a capex guidance line from the 10-K; that evidence belongs on slide 3 or 4.
fix: Trim the cover to title, the decision subtitle from the brief, the November 2026 date and the navy theme, and keep at most one figure for context — the $30 special dividend (F37) — as the visual anchor. Move F35 and F21 to slides 3 and 4 where they are actually used in the argument.

issue: Answer title style is inconsistent: slides 1, 3 and 4 are action titles with numbers, while slides 2 and 5 are directional claims without a sized number in the title even though both pages are full of sized amounts.
fix: Put a number in the title of every slide that has one. Slide 2 becomes "Approve the $13.3B special dividend and $6.5B capex, and cap buybacks at $4B"; slide 5 becomes "Approve the $13.3B dividend, hold capex at $6.5B, and buy back only below $1,000". Slides 3 and 4 already follow the rule.

where: Slide 1 (cover) F37/F38; Slide 2 F37/F38; carried through Slides 3-5
issue: The $30 special dividend and the $4B buyback authorization — the two facts the entire recommendation rests on — are sourced only to 'finance.yahoo.com, Costco (COST) Declares $30 Special Dividend And Reauthorizes $4 Billion Buyback, 2026-11-11.' A board cannot approve a $13.3B payment on a secondary aggregator headline; we need the company's own 8-K/press release with declaration date, record date, payment date, and the buyback authorization terms.
fix: Replace the Yahoo source on F37/F38 with the primary filing: Costco's 8-K (Item 8.01/2.03) or the company press release announcing the special dividend and repurchase authorization. Cite accession number and URL. State the declaration, record, and payment dates and the exact authorization amount and expiry in the slide footnote.

where: Slide 2 metric '$9.4B free cash flow'; Slide 3 'Free cash flow of $9.4B'; F35/F4 basis
issue: The funding math mixes periods. F26/F4/F7 are fiscal 2026 (2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30): OCF $15.82B, capex $6.43B, FCF $9.38B. But F35 says FY2026 *intention* of '$6,500' (i.e., $6.5B) of which only $4,228M spent in the first 36 weeks — so the 'keep the $6.5B capex plan' and the '$9.4B FCF' are on different capex bases ($6.43B actual vs $6.5B plan). Combined with a $13.3B dividend against $20.21B cash, the deck must show the pro-forma cash bridge, not just assert coverage.
fix: Add a one-line funding bridge on Slide 2 or 3: cash $20.21B + FCF $9.38B − special dividend $13.3B = ~$16.3B pro-forma cash (before buybacks and ordinary dividends). Label every figure with its period; footnote the $6.5B as the FY2027/next-year capex intention distinct from the FY2026 $6.43B actual, and show both.

where: Whole deck — no risk/sensitivity slide; storyline
issue: There is no sensitivity, no downside scenario, and no answer to the obvious challenge: if COST's earnings yield is 1.88% and warehouse ROIC is 22.2%, why does a buyback exist at all, and what happens if the stock falls to the 52-week low $850 (F22) or the $4B is fully deployed? The 'cap buybacks at $4B' recommendation is asserted, not shown to be the constrained-optimal use.
fix: Rework Slide 4 from a static ranked table into 'Use of $1B of capital' with a sensitivity band: warehouse ROIC 22.2% (F32) vs buyback earnings yield 1.88% (F30) vs T-bill 4.12% (F24) vs 10-year 5.15% (F25), and add a break-even line: at what buyback price does EPS accretion exceed the 4.12% cash return? Use F29/F31 ($1B retires 0.90M shares; +$0.04 EPS). Show the pro-forma cash and leverage after the $13.3B dividend and at full $4B buyback.

where: Slide 2, metric '$4B buyback authorization'; Slide 5 step (3) 'below $1,000 per share'
issue: The $1,000 buyback trigger in Slide 5 is a hard-coded number with no derivation. It implies an earnings yield of 20.76/1000 = 2.08%, stated as '2.1%', but nothing on the page shows why 2.1% is the hurdle versus the 4.12% T-bill (F24) the same slide uses as the cash alternative. As written, the buyback destroys value versus holding cash at every price above roughly $504 (20.76/4.12%).
fix: Either (a) derive $1,000 explicitly as the price at which buyback earnings yield exceeds a stated hurdle (e.g., after-tax cost of capital or a premium to the 4.12% cash yield) and show the arithmetic, or (b) drop the $1,000 trigger and state the rule as 'buy back only when the earnings yield exceeds the risk-free alternative, i.e., below $X', computed live from F24 and F13.

where: Slide 4 title 'Growth capital earns 22.2% after tax, so capex should stay ahead of buybacks'; F32 basis
issue: F32 computes a company-wide after-tax ROIC (operating income $11.69B x (1−24.7%) / (equity $35.80B + long-term debt $3.91B)) and labels it the return on warehouse growth capital. That is an average return on the existing asset base, not the marginal return on the next 13 warehouses. Using a blended historical ROIC to rank the *next* $6.5B of capex is the kind of circularity a hostile committee will catch.
fix: Rename the row to 'Company after-tax return on capital (average, existing base)' and either (a) add the marginal math — new warehouse capex per unit vs expected unit economics/EBIT — or (b) if no marginal data exists, add a research request (see below) and state the ROIC as a proxy with its limitation footnoted.

where: Slide 3, right argument '16 warehouses opened and 13 planned'; Slide 4 takeaway
issue: The warehouse-opening counts (F36) and the capex guidance (F35) come from a truncated quote of the 10-Q text ('remode...'). The exact source, period (first 36 weeks of FY2026 vs full-year guidance), and the $4,228/$6,500 units (millions) are not confirmed on the slide. This is load-bearing for 'do not cut capex to fund buybacks.'
fix: Verify F35/F36 against the 10-Q cost-20260510.htm (or the FY2026 10-K) and quote the exact sentence with filing, period, and units labeled ($4,228M spent / ~$6,500M intended, first 36 weeks). If the numbers differ, restate.

issue: No treatment of the $1.15B ordinary dividends paid (F8) or the $848M of repurchases already done in FY2026 (F9), and no pro-forma share count after a $4B buyback. The recommendation 'cap buybacks at $4B' cannot be assessed without showing the post-dividend, post-buyback cash, debt, and share count.
fix: Add to Slide 2 or 5 a small pro-forma panel: cash after $13.3B special dividend; ordinary dividend run-rate (F8/F12, $5.54/share declared); shares retired/remaining if $4B is used at $1,106.21 (use F29/F31 scaling); and net debt change (long-term debt $3.91B, F10).

issue: The cover tilts the answer into the title ('buy back only at the right price') before the evidence, and the subtitle is described but the on-slide date and navy theme are the only required elements; fine, but for a board the cover title should state the decision, not pre-empt the debate.
fix: Retitle the cover to the decision: 'Should Costco return more cash — a $13.3B special dividend and $4B buyback — or keep the $6.5B warehouse capex plan?' Keep the recommendation for Slide 2.

where: Slide 5, step (4) 'report progress ... against cash cover of capex and return on capital'
issue: Owners are unspecified for all four steps despite the brief requiring 'owners and timing.' A roadmap with no owner is not a roadmap.
fix: Assign an owner role to each step (e.g., CFO/tax for the dividend, COO/real estate for capex, Treasurer for the buyback rule, CFO for quarterly reporting) and a date consistent with the November 2026 board meeting and January 2030 authorization expiry (F38).

issue: The waterfall 'operating cash flow $15.82B less capex $6.43B to free cash flow $9.38B, then the $13.3B special dividend funded from $20.21B cash' is drawn as a flow but the $13.3B comes from the balance sheet, not the $9.38B. A reader will read it as FCF funding the dividend.
fix: Split the exhibit into two bars: (1) FCF bridge OCF $15.82B → capex $6.43B → FCF $9.38B; (2) cash sources for the dividend: cash $20.21B + FCF $9.38B = ~$29.6B available vs $13.3B dividend. Label each bar with its source.

issue: The two content slides do not build: slide 3 shows capital intensity and slide 4 shows the after-tax return by use of capital. They're different arguments (capital intensity vs. funding) but they get to the same recommendation. Slide 4 does not need to re-derive that $6.5B capex is the highest-return use, since slide 3's cash bridge already establishes the plan is funded and the argument is already made. The two content slides should be: (a) capital intensity is structural, and (b) funding the return is the answer. The pacing is odd: the question is asked on the cover and answered on slide 2, then the deck asks whether capex can be maintained, then returns to the original question on slide 4. The logic finishes where it should have started.
fix: Restructure the two content slides to be in service of the recommendation: slide 3 should establish the capital intensity constraint (capex growing 14.2% a year vs. revenue 7.8%, net PP&E $35.63B, capex guided to $6.5B) and conclude that the plan is already sized to the returns; slide 4 should be the funding argument (cash $20.21B + FCF $9.38B + buyback authorization $4B vs. the $13.3B dividend, with the buyback price discipline at $1,000/share where the earnings yield exceeds 2.1%). If you keep the capital intensity comparison on slide 4, it must be the buyback-versus-capex question on the same page — not a re-derivation of the recommendation.

issue: The board question is 'should Costco return more cash or keep funding warehouse growth?' The storyboard never actually says what 'more cash' would mean, because the $30 dividend is already declared. The decision as framed (approve the dividend vs. fund capex) is a false choice — the dividend is declared and the cash is already there. If the board question is 'should we return more cash', the deck must state the marginal alternatives: what else could be done with the $4B buyback authorization? And what would 'more cash' actually be, beyond the declared dividend? The deck answers a question the board already answered.
fix: Reframe slide 2's decision line and slide 1's subtitle to the actual open question: 'the dividend is declared; the remaining choice is how to deploy the $4B buyback authorization and what to do with any additional cash.' Slide 2 title should become, e.g., 'Approve the declared $13.3B dividend and the $6.5B capex; use the $4B buyback only below $1,000 per share.'

issue: Slide 2's title says 'Approve the $13.3B special dividend and $6.5B capex, and cap buybacks at $4B' — but 'cap buybacks at $4B' is what the buyback authorization already is. It's not a recommendation, it's a restatement of a fact. The title should claim something the board can decide.
fix: Change slide 2's title to the actual recommendation, e.g., 'Fund the declared $13.3B dividend and $6.5B capex; buy back only below $1,000 per share, where the earnings yield exceeds 2.1%' — that's a decision, not a fact.

issue: The title 'The existing asset base earns 22.2% after tax, ahead of debt repayment at 5.15%, cash at 4.12% and a buyback at 1.88%' carries four numbers and is the longest title in the deck. It's the right structure (ranked comparison) but it's doing the job of the page rather than answering it. Also, the detailed sensitivity band (break-even at $504 vs. $403, 52-week low $850, earnings yield 2.44%) is a lot of reasoning to ask a board to follow — the sensitivity band should be a chart, not a paragraph of four rates.
fix: Shorten the title to the claim: 'Growth capital is the highest-return use; buybacks earn 1.88% against cash at 4.12% and the existing base at 22.2%'. Move the sensitivity band to an annotation on the chart, not the prose. The 52-week low ($850) and break-even ($504) belong on the chart axis, not in the title.

issue: The cover title is a question, which is fine for a board briefing, but the subtitle says 'the choice (return cash vs fund warehouse growth)'. That's not the choice. The dividend is declared. The actual choice is: 'approve the declared dividend and fund the capex plan, with buybacks only below $1,000 per share'. Also, the cover shows one figure for context — the $30 special dividend (~$13.3B) — but the $13.3B is derived from 443.1M shares and is not in the facts as a stated figure. The cover must not show a number whose derivation isn't on the page, or it must state the derivation in small type.
fix: Keep the question title. Change the subtitle to name the real choice: 'Approve the declared $30 special dividend (~$13.3B) and the $6.5B capex plan, with buybacks only below $1,000 per share'. Put the derivation '443.1M shares x $30' as a footnote on the cover.

issue: The closing is a four-step roadmap, which is right, but step 1 says 'approve the $30 special dividend', which is already declared — it doesn't need board approval; it needs to be funded and communicated. Step 3 says 'set the $4B buyback authorization with a price discipline', but the authorization is already in place (reauthorized November 2026, expiring January 2030). The board's decision is the price discipline, not the authorization. The closing is giving the board homework they've already done.
fix: Rewrite the four steps as: (1) confirm funding for the declared $13.3B dividend from $20.21B cash and $9.38B fiscal 2026 free cash flow — CFO, November 2026; (2) confirm the $6.5B full-year capex plan and the 26 net new openings — COO, November 2026; (3) adopt a buyback price discipline: repurchase only below $1,000 per share, where the earnings yield exceeds 2.1% — Treasurer, authorization runs to January 2030; (4) report progress against cash cover of capex and after-tax return on capital — CFO, first quarter after approval.

issue: The buyback return calculation is an earnings yield (EPS / price), not a true capital-allocation comparison. A buyback at $1,106.21 returns 1.88% only if you ignore (a) the lost interest on the cash spent and (b) the fact that share count reduction is permanent while the cash spend is not. The 22.2% ROC is a return on the existing asset base, which is a different denominator (equity + debt, not the marginal dollar). Comparing 22.2% ROC to 1.88% earnings yield is apples-to-oranges: the company's growth capex earns 22.2% on the marginal dollar; a buyback earns 1.88% on the marginal dollar before lost cash income. The deck needs the same marginal-dollar comparison on both sides.
fix: Add a research request to compute the marginal after-tax return on incremental warehouse capex (using the 26 net new openings and warehouse-level economics) and the marginal after-tax return on a buyback after lost cash income. If the marginal returns are not available, state on the page that the 22.2% ROC is a return on the existing asset base and flag the marginal comparison as an assumption in the appendix.

issue: The 1.88% earnings yield and 22.2% ROC are both in the deck, but the deck doesn't note that the 22.2% ROC is a historical/current return on the asset base, not a forward return on the $6.5B capex plan. The board will ask: what return does the $6.5B earn? The deck assumes it earns 22.2%, but the facts do not state a forward return on the capex plan. The 22.2% is calculated from operating income $11.69B, equity $35.80B, and long-term debt $3.91B — it's a company-wide return, not a project return.
fix: Add a research request: what is the expected return on the $6.5B fiscal 2026 capex plan and the 26 net new openings? If not available, restate the 22.2% as 'current after-tax return on the existing asset base' and add an explicit assumption on the page.

issue: The cash cover of capex is 3.1x = $20.21B / $6.43B, using fiscal 2026 actual capex. But the capex plan is $6.5B, so the cover is 3.1x on actual capex and 3.1x on the plan (20.21 / 6.5 = 3.1). That's fine, but the slide should use the $6.5B plan consistently, not the $6.43B actual, when it discusses the capex plan. Mixing actual and plan in the same exhibit is a detail the board will notice.
fix: Use $6.5B capex plan consistently on slide 3 and slide 5. If you show the $6.43B actual, label it clearly as 'actual fiscal 2026' and show the $6.5B as 'plan'.

issue: The sensitivity band says 'at the 52-week low of $850 the earnings yield is 2.44%, still below cash' — but the 52-week range in the facts is $850.00 to $1,106.21, and the $1,106.21 is the current price (to 2026-11-13). The 52-week low is $850, and the earnings yield at $850 is 1.88% * (1106.21/850) = 2.44%. That's correct math, but the 52-week range is being used as if it were a buyback price assumption. It's a market observation, not a valuation input. A board will ask: why would we buy back at $850 if the stock is at $1,106? The answer is: you wouldn't, unless the stock falls. The sensitivity band should be framed as 'if the price falls to X, the earnings yield rises to Y', not as a statement about the 52-week range.
fix: Reframe the sensitivity band: 'The buyback earns 1.88% at today's $1,106.21; it exceeds cash (4.12%) only below $504 per share and exceeds the 22.2% ROC only below $93 per share.' Drop the 52-week low reference unless you're using it as a scenario, and if you do, label it as 'if the stock falls to its 52-week low of $850, the earnings yield rises to 2.44%, still below cash'.

issue: The table ranks 'the existing asset base earns 22.2% after tax' against 'debt repayment at 5.15%' and 'cash at 4.12%' and 'a buyback at 1.88%'. But these are not the same kind of return. 22.2% ROC is a return on the existing asset base; 5.15% is the 10-year Treasury yield (a cost of debt / opportunity cost, not a return on capital); 4.12% is the 13-week T-bill yield (a cash return); 1.88% is the earnings yield on a buyback. Ranking them in one table implies they're directly comparable. They're not: the 22.2% is a marginal return on growth capital, the 1.88% is a marginal return on buyback capital, and 4.12% is the return on holding cash. The 5.15% is a financing cost, not a use of capital.
fix: Separate the table into two blocks: (a) marginal return on the next dollar of capital — growth capex 22.2% (with the marginal caveat), buyback 1.88%, cash 4.12%; and (b) cost of debt 5.15% as a footnote, not a ranked row. Or reframe the table as 'return on the next $1B of capital' with three rows (growth capex, buyback, cash) and the 5.15% debt cost as a reference line.

issue: The executive summary is a big-numbers panel with nine metrics. That's too many for a board executive summary. A board wants: the recommendation, the size, the funding, the return comparison, and the open decision. The panel has: $13.3B dividend, $9.4B FCF, 22.2% ROC, 1.88% buyback yield, 4.12% T-bill, $4B buyback authorization, pro-forma cash $16.3B, decision line. That's eight items, plus the buyback price discipline. It's a density problem: the page is doing the work of two pages.
fix: Cut the panel to five: (1) $13.3B special dividend (443.1M x $30), (2) $6.5B capex plan, (3) $20.21B cash + $9.38B FCF = $29.6B available, (4) 22.2% return on the existing asset base vs. 1.88% buyback yield and 4.12% cash, (5) buyback only below $1,000 per share (earnings yield > 2.1%). Move the pro-forma cash line ($16.3B) and the $4B authorization to slide 3 or 4.

issue: The cover says 'One figure for context only: the $30 special dividend (~$13.3B)'. But the $13.3B is not a stated fact; it's derived from 443.1M shares x $30. The cover must not show a derived number without the derivation, or it must state the derivation.
fix: Add a footnote on the cover: '$13.3B = 443.1M shares x $30 special dividend'. Or show only the $30 per share on the cover and put the $13.3B in the executive summary with the derivation.

issue: Slide 3's exhibit is a two-bar free cash flow bridge (operating cash flow $15.82B less capex $6.43B to FCF $9.38B) and a cash sources bar (cash $20.21B + FCF $9.38B = $29.6B). Two labelled bars is fine, but the page has a right-side argument with four bullets (cash cover 3.1x, capex $6.5B plan, 26 net new openings, pro-forma cash $16.3B). That's a lot of prose for a page whose job is to show the funding. The pro-forma cash line ($16.3B) is the same calculation as the executive summary. It's duplicated.
fix: Cut the pro-forma cash line from slide 3; it belongs on slide 2 or on slide 4. Keep slide 3 to: the cash bridge, the $29.6B available, and the capex plan ($6.5B). Add the 26 net new openings as a single annotation under the capex bar, not a bullet.

issue: The title says 'ahead of debt repayment at 5.15%' — but debt repayment at 5.15% is not a use of capital the board is considering. The 10-year Treasury is a market rate, not Costco's cost of debt. Costco's interest expense is $145.0M on $3.91B long-term debt, which is ~3.7% — not 5.15%. The 5.15% is the 10-year Treasury yield, which is a proxy, not Costco's actual cost of debt.
fix: Either use Costco's actual cost of debt (interest expense $145.0M / long-term debt $3.91B = 3.7%) or relabel the 5.15% as '10-year Treasury, a proxy for the opportunity cost of debt repayment'. Don't call it 'debt repayment at 5.15%' as if it's Costco's cost.

issue: The table includes 'debt repayment 5.15% (10-year Treasury)' as a ranked row. This is the weakest row in the table: it's not a use of capital the board is considering, and 5.15% is not Costco's cost of debt. It dilutes the argument.
fix: Remove 'debt repayment' as a ranked row. If you want to show the cost of debt, put it as a footnote: 'Costco's long-term debt is $3.91B at an implied ~3.7% interest rate (interest expense $145.0M); debt repayment is not a capital-allocation priority at this level.'

issue: The sensitivity band includes 'against the 5.15% debt alternative $403' — but if the debt cost is a proxy and not a real alternative, the $403 break-even is a weak number. The $504 break-even against cash (4.12%) is the one that matters.
fix: Drop the $403 break-even. Keep the $504 break-even against cash (4.12%) and add the break-even against the 22.2% ROC if you want a second number — but be clear that the 22.2% is the existing asset base, not a marginal return.

issue: The slide says 'at the 52-week low of $850 the earnings yield is 2.44%, still below cash' — but the fact F22 says the 52-week range is $850.00 to $1,106.21 to 2026-11-13. The 2.44% is computed, not stated in the facts. That's fine, but the deck should show the math: $20.76 / $850 = 2.44%.
fix: Add the math to the annotation: 'at $850 (52-week low), earnings yield = $20.76 / $850 = 2.44%, still below cash at 4.12%'.

issue: The slide says 'a buyback earns 1.88%' but the fact F30 says 'earnings yield 1.88% = diluted EPS $20.76 / share price $1,106.21 (the return a buyback earns on each dollar, before lost interest on the cash)'. The parenthetical is important: the 1.88% is before lost interest on the cash. The deck should state this caveat on the page, not just in the fact.
fix: Add to the buyback row: 'earnings yield 1.88% (before lost interest on cash; after lost cash income at 4.12%, the net return is negative)'.

issue: The slide says 'growth capital is the highest-return use, so the $6.5B capex plan and the 26 net new openings should not be cut to fund buybacks'. This is a strong claim, but the evidence is the 22.2% ROC, which is a return on the existing asset base, not on the $6.5B capex plan. The claim 'growth capital is the highest-return use' is not supported by the facts as stated.
fix: Either add research on the marginal return on the $6.5B capex plan (see research request) or rephrase the takeaway to: 'the existing asset base earns 22.2% after tax, well above the 1.88% earnings yield on a buyback; the $6.5B capex plan should not be cut unless the marginal return on that plan is shown to be below the buyback yield'.

issue: The decision line says 'approve the $13.3B special dividend and the $6.5B capex plan at the November 2026 board meeting, with buybacks only below $1,000 per share, where the earnings yield exceeds 2.1%'. The phrase 'approve the $13.3B special dividend' is wrong — the dividend is declared, not pending approval. The board approves the funding, not the declaration.
fix: Change to: 'confirm funding for the declared $13.3B special dividend and the $6.5B capex plan at the November 2026 board meeting, with buybacks only below $1,000 per share, where the earnings yield exceeds 2.1%'.

issue: The measure of success says 'after-tax return on capital stays above 20% and cash cover of capex stays above 1.0x'. These are reasonable, but they're not tied to the decision. The decision is about the buyback price discipline; the success measure should include the buyback: 'average buyback price below $1,000 per share' or 'no buybacks above $1,000 per share'.
fix: Add a third measure: 'buybacks executed only below $1,000 per share; average buyback price below $1,000'.

issue: The slide title says 'ahead of debt repayment at 5.15%' but the table row for debt repayment is the weakest part of the argument. The title is carrying a row that should be cut. Titles should carry the strongest claims, not the weakest.
fix: Shorten the title to: 'The existing asset base earns 22.2% after tax, ahead of cash at 4.12% and a buyback at 1.88%'. Drop the debt repayment from the title and the table.

where: slide 4, table title: 'The existing asset base earns 22.2% after tax, ahead of debt repayment at 5.15%, cash at 4.12% and a buyback at 1.88%'; F32: 'operating income $11.69B x (1 - 24.7% effective tax rate) / (equity $35.80B + long-term debt $3.91B)'
issue: The comparison is not like-for-like and is weighted heavily in favour of the recommendation. 22.2% is a trailing after-tax return on operating income over a book capital denominator of equity $35.80B plus long-term debt $3.91B; $35.63B of that denominator is net PP&E at historical cost (F16) and excludes operating lease liabilities of $2.61B (F11). The other three rows are current market returns on cash. A board member will say the 22.2% includes returns on warehouses bought decades ago, the marginal new warehouse does not earn 22.2%, and the correct comparison is the return on new capex versus the 1.88% buyback. Nothing in the storyboard answers that.
fix: Retitle slide 4 to state the method honestly: 'Existing base earns 22.2% after tax on book capital; new capex is underwritten against a buyback at 1.88%'. Add the forward test to the slide: the $6.5B fiscal 2026 capex plan implies roughly $1.65B of incremental operating income at the existing 25.4% after-tax margin ($6.5B x 25.4%, from F32), which is the number that has to clear the 1.88% buyback hurdle — and flag it as the open item to be underwritten by the finance team. If it cannot be evidenced, do not make the recommendation rest on it.

where: slide 4, sensitivity band: 'buyback break-even price against the 4.12% cash alternative is $504 per share (EPS $20.76 / 4.12%), against the 5.15% debt alternative $403'; and slides 2 and 4: 'buybacks only below $1,000 per share, where the earnings yield exceeds 2.1%'
issue: Two problems. First, the break-even prices ignore tax on the foregone interest: the after-tax cash alternative is 4.12% x (1 - 24.7%) = 3.10%, so the break-even is roughly $670, not $504, and the delivered number overstates the case by about 25%. Second, the $1,000 threshold has no derivation anywhere — $20.76 / $1,000 = 2.08%, so the 2.1% in the decision line is wrong, and no argument is given for why the hurdle is 2.1% rather than the 3.10% after-tax cash yield. As written the recommendation asserts a number the model does not produce.
fix: Restate the sensitivity on an after-tax basis: buyback break-even against the after-tax 13-week T-bill yield is EPS $20.76 / 3.10% = about $670 per share, against the after-tax 10-year yield $20.76 / 3.88% = about $535. Then anchor the threshold: either set the buyback price discipline at the 3.10% after-tax cash alternative, EPS $20.76 / 3.10% = $670 per share, or state plainly that the board is accepting a lower return than cash to retire stock at $1,000 and say why. Fix the arithmetic in the decision line — at $1,000 the earnings yield is 2.08%, not 2.1%.

where: slide 4, takeaway: 'growth capital is the highest-return use, so the $6.5B capex plan and the 26 net new openings should not be cut to fund buybacks'
issue: The conclusion is asserted from the accounting return on the existing base, not from the return on the $6.5B marginal spend, and the slide does not test the counterfactual a committee will raise: what is lost if capex is trimmed to, say, $5.0B and the $1.5B difference is returned? F19 shows capex compounding at 14.2% a year against revenue growth of 7.8% a year (F18) — that gap is the obvious challenge to the capex plan and no slide addresses it.
fix: Add one row or one callout on slide 4 that frames the trade: '$1.5B of capex deferred equals roughly $0.38B of foregone operating income at the 25.4% after-tax margin, versus $1.5B of buyback at 1.88% equals roughly $0.03B of EPS accretion' — using only F32's margin and F30's yield — and state the assumption that new warehouses earn at the existing rate. Label it an assumption to be confirmed.

where: slide 2, metrics panel: '$13.3B special dividend (443.1M shares x $30)' and pro-forma line: 'cash $20.21B + FCF $9.38B - $13.3B dividend = ~$16.3B'
issue: The pro-forma mixes a stock (cash at 2026-08-30, F5) with a flow (fiscal 2026 free cash flow, F26) and then subtracts the dividend, so no date ties: the $16.3B is neither the 30 August 2026 cash balance nor a forward figure. It also ignores the ordinary dividend already being paid — $5.54 declared per share in fiscal 2026 (F12), roughly $2.46B on 443.1M shares, plus $848.0M of repurchases (F9). Carrying the dividend at an annualised $5.88 per share (F45) for FY2027 is about $2.61B, so the pro-forma should be about $13.7B, not $16.3B, and that excludes any FY2027 buyback.
fix: Re-label the pro-forma as of 30 August 2026 and show the bridge: cash $20.21B + FY2026 free cash flow $9.38B - $13.3B special dividend - $2.46B ordinary dividends (443.1M x $5.54, F12) = about $13.8B. If the intent is a forward FY2027 figure, date it and use the annualised $5.88 per share (F45): about $13.7B, and state that no buyback is assumed at the current price.

where: slide 2 and slide 4: '22.2% after-tax return on capital' resting on F32; slide 4 sensitivity: 'at the 52-week low of $850 the earnings yield is 2.44%'
issue: The 22.2% uses an effective tax rate of 24.7% that is not stated as a fact anywhere in the material — F17 gives income tax expense of $3.02B but no pre-tax income and no rate. A committee will ask for the derivation. The 2.44% at the $850 52-week low (F22) is internally consistent ($20.76 / $850), but the slide gives the low without saying it is the low of the 52 weeks to 2026-11-13, and the $850 is a closing low, not an intraday low.
fix: Add the tax derivation to slide 4's source line: effective rate 24.7% = $3.02B / pre-tax income around $12.2B (F17 and F14), and confirm it against the 10-K tax footnote. Label the $850 as the 52-week closing low to 2026-11-13 (F22).

where: storyline: no slide on what happens if the decision is wrong; slides 2 and 5 give only the measure of success: 'after-tax return on capital stays above 20% and cash cover of capex stays above 1.0x'
issue: There is no downside case and no proposed amount for the buyback. The governing thought says 'use the $4B buyback authorization only below $1,000 per share' but no slide asks whether $4B is the right size or what $4B at $1,106.21 buys: F29 gives 0.90M shares per $1B, so $4B retires about 3.6M shares, 0.81% of 443.1M, and the FY2026 $848.0M of repurchases (F9) was done well below that. The committee will ask what is left if the $13.3B is paid and sales slow, and the material has no answer.
fix: Replace one of the two content slides with a risk-and-downside page titled 'If comparable sales slow and capex overruns, the $13.3B dividend still leaves about $13.8B of cash and the buyback is the flexible leg'. Show: (a) the $4B authorization retired only below $1,000 — $4B / $1,000 = 4.0M shares, 0.90% of 443.1M; (b) the cash minimum after the dividend, using the reworked pro-forma from slide 2; (c) the trigger that suspends buybacks — cash cover of capex below 1.0x or after-tax return on capital below 20%.

where: slide 3, F36 and F47: 'every $1B paid as a speci...' is truncated; the slide also sits on a call-based capex guide
issue: The $6.5B capex figure is a management intention from the 36-week update and the full-year call — F35 and F46 — not a reported actual, while the $6.43B in the FCF bridge (F26) is the fiscal 2026 actual. The page uses both and does not distinguish them. The $9.38B free cash flow that the whole argument rests on will fall if the full-year $6.5B is spent rather than the $6.43B actual.
fix: On slide 3, label the $6.43B as fiscal 2026 actual and the $6.5B as management's full-year intention (F35, F46), and show the pro-forma free cash flow if $6.5B is spent: $15.82B - $6.5B = $9.32B against the $9.38B headline. State that the $0.07B difference does not change the cover conclusion.

where: Slide 3, title 'Capex is compounding at 14.2% a year against 7.8% revenue growth, so the $6.5B plan is already sized to the returns'
issue: The title asserts 'sized to the returns' but no ROI or new-warehouse return figure appears on the slide or in the evidence list. A board member will ask 'which returns?' and the page has no number. The gap between 14.2% and 7.8% is stated as benign without being resolved.
fix: Retitle to the claim the data supports: 'Capex has grown 14.2% a year against 7.8% revenue growth; the $6.5B plan holds while returns on capital stay at 22.2%'. Or keep the title and add the new-warehouse return figure from the 10-K/earnings call as evidence. Do not claim 'sized to the returns' without the number.

where: Slide 4, right argument: 'the $4B authorization retires about 4.0M shares below $1,000, 0.90% of 443.1M'
issue: The arithmetic is wrong. $4B / $1,000 = 4.0M shares, but 4.0M / 443.1M = 0.90% only if you use the $1B scaling rule (0.90M shares per $1B at $1,106.21). At $1,000 the retirement is 0.90% only coincidentally; at $1,106.21 the correct figure is ~3.6M shares, ~0.81%. Mixing two prices in one sentence will get caught in diligence.
fix: Pick one price. State: 'the $4B authorization retires about 3.6M shares at today's $1,106.21, 0.81% of 443.1M; at $1,000 it retires 4.0M shares.' Cite F29's scaling rule (0.90M shares per $1B) consistently.

where: Slide 4 title and slide 2, decision line
issue: The $670 buyback floor is derived from the 3.10% after-tax cash yield, but the 3.10% is never shown as a derivation on any slide. F24 gives the 4.12% pre-tax 13-week T-bill yield; the 3.10% after-tax figure appears only in the governing thought and slide 4's callout. A board member will ask where 3.10% comes from.
fix: Add the derivation to slide 4's exhibit footnote: '3.10% after-tax = 4.12% pre-tax x (1 - 24.7% effective tax rate)'. One line, one source (F24, F17).

where: Slide 4, funding bridge: 'cash $20.21B plus fiscal 2026 free cash flow $9.38B less the $13.3B special dividend less $2.46B ordinary dividends leaves about $13.8B'
issue: The $13.8B residual is then unused on the slide. It implies the board has $13.8B of discretionary cash after the dividend and capex, but the slide never says what that cash funds or why it is not being returned. The logic gap invites the question 'why hold $13.8B?'
fix: Either state what the $13.8B covers (working capital, debt maturity, the $4B authorization with headroom) or retitle slide 4 to the buyback floor decision only and move the bridge to a backup. Do not leave a large residual unexplained.

issue: The subtitle names the $13.3B and $6.5B figures but not the $670 floor, while the cover title says 'Should Costco return more cash, or keep funding warehouse growth?' — the question and the subtitle answer do not line up. The subtitle answers a question the cover does not ask.
fix: Align the cover title to the real decision: 'Funding the declared $30 special dividend and the $6.5B capex plan, with buybacks only below $670 per share'. Keep the board question as a subtitle. No answer on the cover is fine; a mismatched question is not.

issue: 'after-tax return on capital stays above 20%' and 'cash cover of capex stays above 1.0x' are new thresholds introduced only on the closing slide. They are not tied to the 22.2% and 3.1x shown earlier, so they read as arbitrary.
fix: Anchor them: 'after-tax ROC stays above 20% (currently 22.2%, F32)' and 'cash cover of capex above 1.0x (currently 3.1x, F27)'. Same slide, one clause each.

issue: The 26 net new openings figure (F47) is stated as fact but F36 gives 16 opened plus 13 planned = 29, and F47 says 26 net, down two from prior call. The two sources disagree in the slide's own evidence list and the slide does not reconcile them.
fix: Use F47 as the board number: '26 net new openings, down 2 from the prior call, with 2 buildings slipped to fiscal 2027'. Footnote the reconciliation to F36 (16 opened + 13 planned, less relocations/slips).

where: Slide 2, metric (4): '22.2% after-tax return on the existing asset base against a 1.88% buyback earnings yield and 4.12% cash'
issue: Three different bases compared in one clause: return on capital, earnings yield, and cash yield. The board will not know whether 22.2% is the hurdle the buyback must clear or the return on capex.
fix: Split into two lines: 'Existing asset base earns 22.2% after tax (F32); the $6.5B capex plan is the marginal call.' Then: 'A buyback at today's $1,106.21 earns 1.88% against 3.10% after-tax cash (F30, F24).'

issue: The 3.10% after-tax cash yield is the single load-bearing number for the entire recommendation — it sets the $670 floor — and it appears with no derivation. Fact F24 gives the 4.12% pre-tax 13-week T-bill yield; Fact F32 uses a 24.7% effective tax rate; but nothing in the material states '3.10% = 4.12% x (1 - 24.7%)'. As drafted, 3.10% is a hard-coded plug and the board will ask for it before they ask anything else.
fix: On Slide 4, replace the callout with: 'Set the buyback floor at $670 per share, where the earnings yield equals the 3.10% after-tax cash alternative (3.10% = 4.12% US 13-week T-bill, F24, x (1 - 24.7% effective tax rate, F32)).' Add the arithmetic as a footnote to the exhibit. If a different tax rate is intended for the cash alternative, source it and restate.

where: Slide 1 cover subtitle and Slide 2 metric (1)
issue: The deck treats the $30 special dividend as declared and the board's decision as one of funding ('Confirm funding for the declared $30 special dividend (~$13.3B)'), while the brief asks whether Costco should 'return more cash to shareholders (buybacks or a special dividend) or keep funding warehouse growth'. The C-suite brief governs over the brief.md question, but the storyboard does not reconcile the two: a board member reading the cover against the question will ask whether the dividend is a done deal or still open.
fix: On Slide 1, add one line under the subtitle: 'The $30 per share special dividend was declared on 11 November 2026 (F37); this briefing addresses funding, the capex plan, and the $4B buyback authorization, not whether to declare.' issue: The slide says 'the $4B authorization retires about 4.0M shares below $1,000, 0.90% of 443.1M' and separately that '$4B at today's $1,106.21 earns 1.88% before lost interest'. fix: Rewrite: '$4B at the 13 November 2026 close of $1,106.21 (F21) retires 3.62M shares (0.82% of 443.1M), using the scaling rule of 0.90M shares per $1B at $1,106.21 (F29); at the $670 floor, the same $4B retires 5.97M shares (1.35%).' Cut the $1,000 reference entirely.

where: Slide 3 right argument, '26 net new openings expected in fiscal 2026'

issue: The deck compares the 22.2% after-tax return on capital (F32) against the 1.88% buyback earnings yield (F30) and the 4.12% cash yield (F24) as if they were commensurable. They are not: 22.2% is a return on the existing equity plus long-term debt base ($35.80B + $3.91B); 1.88% is an earnings yield on incremental buyback dollars; 4.12% is a pre-tax money-market yield. Presenting them on one line invites a committee member to say the comparison is apples-to-oranges.

State the decision rule in one sentence: incremental buyback dollars must clear the 3.10% after-tax cash alternative; at $670 they do.

issue: '$29.6B available, $20.21B cash plus $9.38B fiscal 2026 free cash flow' double-counts: the $9.38B FCF is operating cash flow less capex; adding it to the $20.21B cash balance and presenting $29.6B as 'available' ignores the $6.5B forward capex plan the board is being asked to confirm. fix: On Slide 2, restate metric (3) as 'Sources: $20.21B cash at 30 Aug 2026 (F5) plus $9.38B fiscal 2026 free cash flow (F26) = $29.6B before the $6.5B fiscal 2026 capex plan and $2.46B ordinary dividends; net $20.6B after capex and ordinary dividends, before the $13.3B special dividend and $4B buyback.' where: Slide 4 exhibit, buyback earnings yield line vs share price

where: Slide 2 metric (4) and Slide 5 measures of success

where: Slide 2 metric (5), Slide 4 callout, Slide 5 step (3)
issue: The $670 floor is stated three times with three slightly different phrasings: 'where the earnings yield clears the 3.10% after-tax cash yield', 'where the earnings yield equals the 3.10% after-tax cash alternative', and 'where the earnings yield clears the 3.10% after-tax cash yield'. issue: The cover footnote derives only '$13.3B = 443.1M shares x $30 special dividend'. issue: The claimed capex CAGR of 14.2% from $4.32B (FY2023) to $6.43B (FY2026) is 14.2% only if compounded over three years. $4.32B x (1.142)^3 = $6.43B, so the arithmetic works. Revenue 7.8% from $242.29B to $303.15B: $242.29B x (1.078)^3 = $303.22B, close but not exact; $303.15B / $242.29B = 1.2512, third root = 1.0776, so 7.8% is right. Operating cash flow 12.6% from $11.07B to $15.82B: $11.07B x (1.126)^3 = $15.81B, right. The rates tie, but the slide does not state they are three-year CAGRs.
fix: On Slide 3, label the exhibit 'Three-year CAGR, fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2026' and footnote each rate to its endpoints (F19 capex, F18 revenue, F20 operating cash flow). A committee member should not have to infer the compounding period.

issue: The $670 floor is 39.4% below the 13 November 2026 close of $1,106.21 (F21) and 21.2% below the 52-week low of $850.00 (F22). issue: Cites 'after-tax return on capital stays above 20%', 'cash cover of capex stays above 1.0x', and 'buybacks executed only below $670'. fix: Restate: 'After-tax return on capital at or above 20% (22.2% at 30 Aug 2026, F32); cash cover of capex at or above 2.5x (3.1x at 30 Aug 2026, F27) after the special dividend; buybacks executed only below $670 with average price below $670.' 2.5x is a floor the board can defend; 1.0x is not.

where: Slide 5, step 1 vs Slide 2, sources line
issue: Slide 5 says 'confirm funding for the declared $13.3B special dividend from $20.21B cash and $9.38B fiscal 2026 free cash flow, net of the $6.5B fiscal 2026 capex plan and $2.46B ordinary dividends'. Slide 2 already builds $20.6B net cash before the special dividend. fix: On Slide 5 step 1, rewrite to the same arithmetic used on Slide 2: '$20.21B cash at 30 Aug 2026 + $15.82B operating cash flow - $6.43B capex - $1.15B ordinary dividends paid to date - $13.3B special dividend = $4.15B ending cash before any buyback', and add one clause: 'the $13.3B is funded from cash and in-year cash flow; the $4B buyback authorization is not drawn unless the price condition is met'. Do not describe the dividend as funded "net of" the $6.5B capex plan on one slide and "plus" it on another.

where: Slide 5, step 3 against Slide 2, metric (3) and Slide 4, right argument
issue: Slide 5 step 3 says 'adopt a buyback price discipline, repurchase only below $670 per share'. At $1,106.21 the earnings yield is 1.88% (Slide 2 metric 3 and Slide 4, right argument). The deck is therefore asking the board to approve a $4B authorization it does not intend to use — that is the honest read, but the closing page presents it as an action item alongside two genuine funding decisions. issue: Slide 3 title claims 'the $6.5B plan holds while returns on capital stay at 22.2%'. The 22.2% is computed on the existing asset base (operating income $11.69B x (1 - 24.7%) / (equity $35.80B + long-term debt $3.91B)). It is a fiscal 2026 actual, not a forward return on the $6.5B of new capex. The slide then notes net new openings were revised to 26 from 28, with two buildings moved to fiscal 2027. The title asserts a forward return the evidence does not support.
fix: Change Slide 3's title to a claim the facts support: 'Capex is growing 14.2% a year against 7.8% revenue growth; the $6.5B plan holds but openings slipped to 26 from 28'. In the right argument, label the 22.2% as 'after-tax return on capital, fiscal 2026 actual, existing asset base' and add one line: 'the return the incremental $6.5B must clear is the 22.2% existing-asset return and the 3.10% after-tax cash alternative; the plan is confirmed on the basis that it clears the cash alternative, not that it repeats 22.2%'.

where: Slide 3 versus Slide 2 metric (3) and Slide 4 right argument

On Slide 2 metric (3), keep the funding arithmetic on the actual $6.43B: '$20.21B cash + $15.82B operating cash flow - $6.43B capex - $1.15B ordinary dividends paid to date = $28.45B before the $13.3B special dividend'. where: Slide 4 vs Slide 5, measure 'cash cover of capex at or above 2.5x (3.1x at 30 Aug 2026)'

Add a second, post-dividend measure that is actually achievable: '$4.15B ending cash after the special dividend = 0.65x fiscal 2026 capex; monitor against the $9.38B fiscal 2026 free cash flow as the rebuild source'. where: Slide 2, F30 ('earnings yield 1.88% = diluted EPS $20.76 / share price $1,106.21') and Slide 4, F13 ('diluted EPS $20.76 ... for the period 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30')

where: Slide 3, exhibit ('capex growing 14.2% a year from $4.32B to $6.43B, revenue 7.8% a year from $242.29B to $303.15B, operating cash flow 12.6% a year from $11.07B to $15.82B')

where: Slide 2, five metrics and Slide 5, measures of success
issue: Dilution is not mentioned once. A $30 special dividend on 443.1M shares is $13.3B of cash leaving a company with $20.21B of cash and $3.91B of long-term debt (F10). The board will ask whether the special dividend increases leverage or reduces the equity base, and the deck has no answer.

where: Slide 2, '(4) three separate figures with their bases' and Slide 4, left exhibit ('the 22.2% return on the existing asset base')
