issue: The comparison the whole deck rests on — warehouse capex at 22.2% after tax vs buyback at 1.88% vs special dividend at $2.26/share — sits in a table whose largest cell, the orange 'Warehouse capex' row, says 'Book return, not the next dollar: reference only, not the decision metric.' The headline of slide 4 claims a comparison on one basis, but the table itself disclaims the basis and the orange answer. The reader is told the 22.2% is the point and simultaneously that it isn't.
fix: Reframe the row as a claim. State in the title and the shaded box: the board is deciding on the next dollar; on the next dollar warehouse capex earns X% while buyback earns 1.88% and the special dividend returns cash at $2.26/share, so buyback and dividend are the priority. If the 22.2% is historical and non-decision, either remove it or put it in the footnote. Do not let a row sit half orange and disclaimed.

issue: Title wraps to two lines ('...special dividend') and the four numbered items are fine, but the right-hand panel ($6B / $4B / $2B) is a stack of three numbers with captions that repeat the body text. It is decoration, not evidence. Also the page asserts 'return capacity: $4B ceiling plus $2B dividend' — 'capacity' and 'ceiling' are doing double duty for the same $6B.
fix: Cut the right panel or replace it with a single small bar showing $8.32B surplus split into $6B returned and $2.32B retained. Fix the language: 'Return $6B of this year's $8.32B surplus: renew the $4B buyback authorization and declare a $2B special dividend.'

issue: Actions 1–3 are funded and sourced. Action 4 ('Set the buyback floor at 25x FY2026 diluted EPS of $20.76 is about $519') is a policy choice flagged in footnote 2 as 'not a fact in the filings; not available in the sources, a research request.' The board is being asked to approve four actions, one of which rests on a number the deck admits it does not have.
fix: Either drop action 4 from the 'approve' list and move it to a discussion item, or find and cite the peer or historical multiple that justifies 25x. Until then, present it as a proposal for direction, not an approval.

issue: Slide 3 is half empty on the right: the four-row number stack occupies the left third, the right column has prose and a boxed break-even, leaving a blank middle. Slide 4's bottom quarter is empty below the footnote line. Both pages look unfinished.
fix: On slide 3, build one waterfall or bar pair: $15.82B OCF → −$7.50B capex → $9.38B FCF, then the $13.5B break-even as a marker line. On slide 4, move the shaded box into the table's lower-right empty space or cut it to three bullets and let the table breathe.

issue: 'The $6B is a ceiling, not committed spend' is useful but item 2's sub-bullets ('The $4B authorization is a ceiling', 'Cash walk: $20.21B opening + $15.82B operating cash flow') are fragments and the cash walk stops before closing cash. The slide title claims $6B is being returned; a reader wants the closing balance.
fix: Make item 2 a single sentence: 'The $4B authorization is a ceiling, not committed spend; the $6B returns $6B of the $8.32B surplus.' Complete the cash walk through to closing cash, or delete it and put the walk on slide 3.

issue: Every content page carries the 'Preliminary' tag and footnote citations, but the title positions and sizes are inconsistent: slide 2's title is two lines, slides 3-5 are one to two lines with different leading, and the cover title is larger and left-shifted relative to the content. On slide 5, 'Board · 15 December 2026' wraps the year to a second line — an orphan.
fix: Set one title placeholder position and size across slides 2-5. On slide 5, widen the owner column and set 'Board · 15 Dec 2026' on one line.

issue: Both footnotes flag that the FY2027 repurchase amount is 'not in the materials' and is 'a research request.' The deck asks the board to renew a $4B ceiling and adopt a 25x floor, both resting on an assumed $4B and an unsourced multiple. This is the one gap a board member will probe.
fix: Before the meeting, obtain the FY2026 10-K Item 7 confirmation of planned FY2027 repurchases and a peer set of buyback floors or historical multiple ranges; cite both in the footnote.

where: slide 2, point 1: "Surplus is $8.32B; we return $6B of it" and "The $2.32B not returned covers the regular dividend run-rate and other uses"
issue: The $8.32B surplus is asserted with no derivation on the page, and the $2.32B residual is hand-waved to "the regular dividend run-rate and other uses" without a number. $6B + $2.32B = $8.32B arithmetically, but nothing shows what the regular dividend run-rate actually costs or how much of the $2.32B it consumes. This is the page the board will do arithmetic on.
fix: Add a source line to slide 2 for the $8.32B (tie it to the cash walk: $20.21B opening + $15.82B operating cash flow less the working-capital, regular dividend and other uses that produce $8.32B), and replace "and other uses" with the actual regular dividend run-rate figure in $B so the $2.32B residual is fully allocated. If the number is not in the model, say "$2.32B retained, of which $XB regular dividend run-rate" and cite the K-10.

issue: The page compares three uses of $1B on a so-called "one after-tax return basis" but the metrics are not comparable: warehouse capex is a 22.2% historical average return on an existing $42.32B invested capital base, buyback is a 1.88% EPS-accretion test (not a return), and the special dividend is $2.26 per share (a payout, no return at all). Slide 4's own side panel admits the 22.2% is "historical company average on the existing $42.32B invested capital" and "reference only, not the decision metric" — so the headline comparison is a false equivalence presented under a single "return basis" title.
fix: Rename slide 4's title to "Three uses of $1B: historical returns, EPS accretion and payout per share" and relabel the column "After-tax return / accretion per $1B" with each row stating its own metric (warehouse: historical ROIC on existing capital; buyback: FY2026 EPS accretion; dividend: cash per share). Or drop the dividend row from the comparison and present it separately.

where: slide 4, buyback row: "0.90M shares retired per $1B at $1,106.21" and "EPS $20.76 / price $1,106.21, an EPS-accretion test only"
issue: The 1.88% is derived as $20.76 / $1,106.21 = 1.877%, which is the earnings yield, not EPS accretion. EPS accretion of a buyback depends on shares retired (0.82% of 443.1M) and the lost interest on the $1B of cash used — at a ~4-5% after-tax cash yield the buyback is roughly neutral to slightly accretive; the page calls it 1.88% and labels it "EPS-accretion test only", which is not what the number is.
fix: Either relabel the 1.88% as the FY2026 earnings yield ($20.76 / $1,106.21) with the basis stated, or compute true EPS accretion: 0.90M shares / 443.1M = 0.20% share reduction, less the after-tax earnings forgone on $1B of cash at the stated rate — show both and label the basis.

where: slide 3: "Operating cash flow of $15.82B covers the $7.5B FY2027 capex plan" and "Opening cash of $20.21B covers the $7.5B FY2027 plan 2.7x"

where: slide 5, action 4: "Set the buyback floor at 25x FY2026 EPS. A floor of 25x FY2026 diluted EPS of $20.76 is about $519"

issue: The cover introduces a fourth action (25x buyback floor) that is not in the cover title's three-part message nor on slide 2's four points; the floor appears first in the subhead with no number and no explanation until slide 5. A cover should not carry a dangling, unsourced policy number.
fix: Either add the floor to the cover title ("...renew the $4B buyback, adopt a 25x buyback floor") with the implied ~$519 level, or remove it from the cover subhead.

where: slide 3, footnote 1: "FY2024 and FY2025 are not shown; those figures are not in hand"

fix: Pull FY2024 and FY2025 operating cash flow from the Costco 10-K (filed 2026-10-07) already cited in footnote 1 and add a three-fiscal-year column so the 12.6% growth claim is visible.

issue: Both pages use a grey side panel with paragraph text, but slide 3's panel has a dark callout block inside it that reads like a footnote block; slide 4's panel is plain. Inconsistent treatment for the same role (commentary).

where: slide 2 header "Preliminary" and slide 5 page numbers
issue: Page 2 carries "Preliminary" at top right; slides 3-5 carry it too but it duplicates the footer page number/MSI branding on every page. Also slide 1 (cover) has no "Preliminary" mark, which is correct for a cover but the deck should be consistent about what is draft.
fix: Keep "Preliminary" only on pages that may change, and ensure the cover carries the meeting date and firm name (it does) but no draft mark. Minor consistency pass.

where: slide 2, four numbered points vs slide 5, four actions
issue: Slide 2 lists "Return $6B", "$6B is a ceiling", "0.90M shares per $1B", "$2B = $4.51/share" and slide 5 lists "renew $4B", "declare $2B", "fund $7.5B", "set 25x floor". issue: The spine of slide 4 is the 22.2% after-tax return on warehouse capital, and it is built on an effective tax rate of 24.7% that appears nowhere in the facts. The table's whole argument rests on this cell.

issue: The ~$8.6B residual cash balance is the number that proves the recommendation is not starving the growth plan. $20.21B cash - $4B - $2B = $14.21B, not $8.6B. No fact in the material explains the difference.

If the missing outflow cannot be sourced, change the residual to $14.2B and rebuild the cover and 3.1x statements around it.

issue: The $1,150 buyback pause price and the portfolio-return rationale behind buybacks versus the 4.12% T-bill are asserted, not evidenced. Slide 4 quotes the T-bill yield but the buyback comparison still needs the 1.88% earnings yield to be framed against it explicitly.
fix: Add one label to slide 4's buyback row: 'buyback earnings yield 1.88% vs 4.12% T-bill, before the $2B could be deployed into 22.2% growth capital.' Then on slide 5, justify the $1,150 threshold as the price at which buyback yield falls below the T-bill, or delete the threshold and replace it with a cash floor only.

issue: Slide 4 says 'growth wins on return, so return only the surplus' — that is slide 2's decision, repeated. MECE violation: the page that is supposed to compare capital uses instead re-argues the conclusion.
fix: Retitle slide 4 to the comparison result: 'Warehouse capex returns 22.2%; a buyback returns 1.88% — so $1B in stores beats $1B in shares.' Then the table's takeaway is the comparison, and the decision stays on slide 2.

issue: Slides 3 and 4 both make the cover-of-capex point. Slide 3 argues $9.38B FCF covers the $7.5B step-up; slide 4 argues capex earns 22.2%. Those are different claims but the links blur because slide 3's right panel also says 'leaves surplus' and slide 4's title repeats 'return only the surplus.'
fix: Keep slide 3 purely about capacity: 'Free cash flow of $9.4B covers the $7.5B FY2027 step-up and still leaves surplus.' Keep slide 4 purely about relative return. Delete 'so return only the surplus' from slide 4's title and the 'leaves surplus' language from slide 3's right panel; one slide owns coverage, the other owns comparison.

issue: Cover, exec summary, two content slides, closing — the structure is fine, but slide 1 must carry $490B market cap and $20.2B cash as the framing numbers, and $20.2B is then never reconciled to the $8.6B residual on slide 2. A board member will ask.

issue: The column chart is specified for FY2024–FY2026 but the facts in hand only give FY2023 and FY2026 cash-flow and capex figures. If the middle years are assumed or empty, the chart is a three-bar lie.

Do not draw years you cannot source.

issue: 'Approve the $6B return by January 2027 and hold buybacks above $1,150 a share' is two instructions in one title, and the first half duplicates slide 2's decision line.

issue: The 'leaving ~$8.6B cash and 3.1x capex cover' does not tie to the facts. F5 cash $20.21B less $6B return = $14.21B; less $7.5B FY2027 capex = $6.71B, not $8.6B. 3.1x is F27 = cash $20.21B / capex $6.43B (FY2026 capex), but the slide pairs it with $7.5B FY2027 capex ($20.21B/$7.5B = 2.7x, and the post-return ratio is 0.9x). Either the $8.6B is a post-FCF figure or the 3.1x is on the wrong denominator; both are stated as if they follow from $6B returned.
fix: Put a one-line pro forma cash walk on slide 2: 'Cash 2026-08-30 $20.21B − $6.0B return = $14.21B; + FY2027 OCF (state assumption) − $7.5B capex = $X'. Quote the cover ratio on a labelled denominator: 3.1x on FY2026 capex $6.43B (F27) or 2.7x on FY2027 capex $7.5B. Do not show both unlabelled.

issue: The slide compares a 1.88% buyback earnings yield (F30) and a 4.12% T-bill (F24) against a '22.2% after-tax return on capital' (F32) that is not marginal. F32 is operating income $11.69B × (1−24.7%) / (equity $35.80B + long-term debt $3.91B), the return on the existing capital base, not the return on the next $1B of warehouse capex. It omits operating lease liabilities $2.61B (F11) from the capital base and carries no sales/EBIT forecast for the 33 planned 2027 openings (F37). A committee will tear the 22.2% apart on sight.
fix: Relabel F32 as 'return on existing invested capital (equity + LT debt only)' and add the invested-capital definition in a footnote including operating leases (F11). Add a marginal-return line: expected steady-state sales and after-tax operating margin per new warehouse from F37's 33 openings, sourced from the 10-K. If marginal data cannot be sourced, drop the 22.2% row and let the argument rest on capex cover, not on a return comparison.

issue: The dividend row shows '$2.26/share' while the board recommendation on slide 2 is a $2B special dividend at $4.51/share. $2.26 is the $1B row, $4.51 is the $2B recommendation. The slide will be read as contradicting the executive summary.
fix: Show the $1B row as $2.26/share and add the recommended $2B column as $4.51/share, or note '$2.26 per $1B'. Keep F29 and the slide 2 $4.51/share consistent.

issue: EPS accretion is shown at $20.80 (F31) with no financing cost. The $1B buyback would consume cash earning 4.12% (F24) or the 5.15% 10-year (F25); on ~$1B that is ~$41M pre-tax, ~$31M after tax at the 24.7% rate used in F32 ($3.02B/$?? — the 24.7% is itself unsourced). The 1.88% earnings yield is a return metric, but the table is an EPS comparison; without the lost interest the $20.80 is overstated by roughly $0.07.
fix: Add a financing line to the buyback row: lost after-tax interest at 4.12% (F24) and the resulting EPS accretion, or label the $20.80 explicitly as 'before lost interest'. Source the effective tax rate (F17 income tax $3.02B / pre-tax income from F14 and F6) or show it as a single sourced figure.

issue: 'Hold buybacks above $1,150 a share' and 'pause if cash falls below $8B' are asserted thresholds with no derivation. $1,150 is only 4.0% above the $1,106.21 close (F21); no value, comp or historical multiple supports either number. The $8B floor does not tie to the cash walk in slide 2 and is probably an artifact of the unsupported $8.6B.
fix: Derive the thresholds: state the price at which the earnings yield falls below the T-bill (breakeven price = EPS $20.76 / 4.12% = $504, so the $1,150 cap needs a different logic — e.g. a stated multiple of the 52-week range high $1,106.21, F22) and the minimum cash floor as the lower of 12 months' capex or a stated months-of-capex rule. Replace 'above $1,150' with a formula or a sourced multiple, and tie the cash floor to the pro forma walk.

issue: The slide claims FCF $9.38B (F26) covers the $7.5B step-up, but F26 is FY2026 FCF on FY2026 capex $6.43B (F4). On the $7.5B FY2027 plan, FY2026 operating cash flow $15.82B (F7) less $7.5B is $8.32B, not $9.38B. The 3.1x cover also uses FY2026 capex (F27). The committee will ask this in the first five minutes.

issue: Title claims 'the same cash in warehouses earns 22.2% on capital' but the table compares a 1.88% buyback yield with a 4.12% T-bill and a 22.2% existing-capital return. The 22.2% is not the return on the same cash and does not support the 'growth wins' conclusion as stated. The recommendation 'return only the surplus' is asserted, not shown.
fix: Either source the marginal return on new warehouses and put it in the title, or change the title to what the numbers support: e.g. 'Existing-capital return 22.2% (F32) exceeds a 1.88% buyback yield (F30); the $6B return is sized to leave capex cover of X'. Do not headline a number the slide cannot stand behind.

issue: F30 earnings yield says 'before lost interest on the cash'; F29 buyback rate uses the $1,106.21 close (F21); F31 uses 443.1M shares (F1). The recommendation states $4B buyback + $2B special dividend but not the sequence or the cash-flow timing: the buyback authorization expires January 2027 (F40) and the dividend would be declared at the December meeting, yet the FY2027 capex is a 12-month spend. The committee will want to see the timing of the $6B out against the $7.5B spend.
fix: Add a one-line cash timing: '$6B returned Dec 2026–Jan 2027; $7.5B capex spread through FY2027; $20.21B opening cash covers both.' Tie the closing slide's January 2027 expiry (F40) to the same timeline.

issue: The chart is described as FY2024–FY2026 OCF, capex and FCF with FY2027 capex marked, but the materials contain only FY2023 and FY2026 capex ($4.32B, $6.43B; F19) and FY2023 and FY2026 OCF ($11.07B, $15.82B; F20). FY2024 and FY2025 values are not in hand. The chart cannot be built from the brief.
fix: Either source FY2024 and FY2025 capex and OCF from the SEC XBRL (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment; NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities) before building, or change the chart to the two endpoints and label the CAGR: 'capex +14.2% a year from $4.32B (FY2023) to $6.43B (FY2026) (F19); OCF +12.6% a year from $11.07B to $15.82B (F20).'

issue: The $490.19B market cap (F28) is on 443.1M shares at 2026-09-29 (F1) and a $1,106.21 close at 2026-11-13 (F21) — a six-week-stale share count on a top-of-range price (F22: 52-week range $850.00–$1,106.21). No peer or historical multiple, dividend yield, or buyback capacity is shown. The board cannot judge whether $1,106 is a good buyback price from this deck.
fix: Add a one-line price context: '52-week range $850.00–$1,106.21 (F22); current price at the high; earnings yield 1.88% (F30) vs 10-year Treasury 5.15% (F25).' If a buyback is recommended, show the historical average buyback price or the 10-day VWAP for the $1,106.21 reference, sourced from market data.

issue: No risk or sensitivity anywhere. The recommendation has no downside case: what if FY2027 OCF is 10–20% below FY2026, what if the 33 planned openings (F37) consume more than $7.5B, what if the effective tax rate moves, what if the January 2027 expiry (F40) slips. Show the same at −10%. Add a risks line on slide 5: capex overrun, OCF shortfall, and the January 2027 authorization expiry (F40).

issue: Cover 'must show' asks for the two framing numbers $490B market cap (F28) and $20.2B cash (F5), but no source date is shown on the cover. The market cap uses a 2026-11-13 price (F21) and 2026-09-29 shares (F1), and the cash is at 2026-08-30 (F5); mixing those dates without labels is exactly what a client catches.
fix: Add to the cover footnote: 'Market cap $490.19B = $1,106.21 (2026-11-13 close, F21) × 443.1M shares (2026-09-29, F1); cash $20.21B at 2026-08-30 (F5).'

issue: The cash walk does not reconcile. 'Opening cash $20.21B less the $6B return = $14.21B; plus FY2027 OCF $15.82B less $7.5B capex = $6.71B closing cash.' $14.21B + $15.82B - $7.5B = $22.53B, not $6.71B. If the intended closing figure is $6.71B, state the bridge that gets there (e.g. other uses or timing) or restate the governing thought. where: Slide 4, table_focus, buyback row vs slide 2

Renewing an authorization is not new cash out the door in FY2027 unless you also state how much will actually be repurchased. As written, slide 4 argues against $4B that slide 2 says is already authorized.

If the FY2027 repurchase assumption is not in the materials, ask for it before this slide is built.

issue: 'Cover ratio labelled: 2.7x on FY2027 capex $7.5B' and slide 3's '3.1x cash cover on FY2026 capex' use two different denominators and capes without labelling the difference clearly. The governing thought cites 2.7x. Read together, they look like inconsistent numbers rather than two different bases (cash vs cash after return, FY2027 vs FY2026 capex).

where: Slide 4, table_focus, '22.2% return on existing invested capital'
issue: The headline claim on slide 4 is 'Warehouse capex returns 22.2% on existing capital'. But 22.2% is Costco's after-the-fact return on capital already invested, not the return on the next $7.5B. The board's decision is about marginal dollars, and the slide offers no incremental return for the step-up.
fix: Either (a) retitle slide 4 to what the data supports: 'Existing invested capital earns 22.2% after tax; the buyback earns 1.88% on each dollar' and add a sentence that the 22.2% is a historical average, not the return on the FY2027 increment; or (b) if the deck wants to claim the marginal return, commission the analysis — new-warehouse capex per unit, mature-warehouse ROI, and unit-level returns. Do not let 22.2% stand as if it were the return on the $7.5B.

issue: The slide states 'effective tax rate 26.2%' computed as '$3.02B / ($11.69B - $145.0M)' but then uses '1 - 24.7% effective tax rate' in F32's 22.2% ROC calculation. Two different tax rates on one slide, neither reconciled. A committee will ask which one is right.
fix: Pick one effective rate, show the derivation once, and use it everywhere. If 24.7% is the rate used in the ROC calc, show '$3.02B / ... = 24.7%' or explain the difference (e.g. discrete items F52: $83M and $72M R&D and stock comp benefits). One footnote, one rate, applied to both the ROC and any after-tax buyback math.

issue: Slide 2 carries the answer, the cash walk, the $6B split, the scaling rule, the cover ratio, the decision line and the timing. That is five exhibits' worth on one page. The brief asked for 'balanced density'; this is not balanced, it is a data dump on the most important slide.
fix: Move the scaling rule and the earnings-yield comparison (F29, F30) off slide 2 entirely — they live on slide 4. Keep slide 2 to: the recommendation ($6B: $4B buyback + $2B special dividend), the one-line cash walk, the 2.7x cover, and the decision date. Four bullets, one chart. The rest is support, not summary.

issue: The deck uses two cover ratios (2.7x and 3.1x) without a single line telling the reader which one is the answer and why. This is the kind of number drift that makes a board ask 'which is it?' instead of 'when do we approve?'
fix: On slide 2, put a single bold line: '2.7x cash cover on the FY2027 plan after the return.' On slide 3, label the 3.1x as the pre-return, FY2026-actual basis and show the bridge from 3.1x to 2.7x (the $6B return). One number leads; the other supports.

issue: The -10% case is promised ('the -10%/-20% OCF sensitivity') but only the -20% number is shown ($12.66B OCF, $5.16B FCF, $6.71B closing cash). The -10% case has no number. A board will ask for the middle case.
fix: Add the -10% case explicitly: OCF $14.24B, FCF after $7.5B capex $6.74B, and closing cash after the $6B return. Show all three cases (base, -10%, -20%) in a small three-column table, not prose. Then state the break-even OCF at which the plan stops working.

where: Slide 3, 'FY2026 FCF $9.38B on $6.43B capex covers the $7.5B step-up'
issue: This sentences uses FCF $9.38B to cover a $7.5B capex step-up, but FCF is already net of capex. It double-counts the capex relief. The correct test is whether FY2026 OCF $15.82B covers FY2027 capex $7.5B plus everything else.
fix: Rewrite as: 'FY2026 operating cash flow $15.82B covers the FY2027 capex step-up $7.5B by 2.1x, before any growth.' Keep FCF $9.38B as the surplus measure, not the cover measure. Two different questions, two different numbers.

issue: The left side is a two-endpoint column chart (FY2023 to FY2026) with a single FY2027 guidance bar. Two data points and a guidance marker do not justify a chart; that is a three-row table disguised as a chart, and the CAGR label is doing all the work.
fix: Either show the full five-year series (FY2022–FY2026 actuals plus FY2027 guidance) so the CAGR has a trend to sit on, or drop the chart and put a three-row table: FY2023, FY2026, FY2027 guidance, with OCF, capex, FCF and CAGR. A chart of two points is a table that wishes it were a chart.

issue: Slides 3 and 4 both argue 'capex is affordable and high-returning vs returning cash'. Slide 3's capacity argument and slide 4's comparison of uses overlap. Two slides, one point, and the deck only has five slides.
fix: Make slide 3 purely the capacity question: can the balance sheet fund the $7.5B step-up and still return $6B? (Answer: yes, 2.7x, with sensitivity.) Make slide 4 purely the allocation question: given the capacity, where does the next dollar earn the most? (Answer: warehouse capex at 22.2% on existing capital vs buyback at 1.88%.) Sharpen the titles so a reader sees the two questions are different.

issue: The cover carries two framing numbers (market cap $490.19B and cash $20.21B) and a one-line straddle about $6.71B remaining. That is a cover doing the executive summary's job, and the $6.71B on the cover will conflict with slide 2 if the walk is fixed to a different number.
fix: Keep the cover to: title, subtitle naming the decision, date November 2026, market cap $490.19B (price $1,106.21 × 443.1M shares), cash $20.21B. Drop the $6.71B straddle from the cover; that number belongs on slide 2 and only after the walk foots.

issue: 'Decision line asking the board to approve by the January 2027 expiry' is vague. The $4B authorization expires in January 2027; the special dividend has no stated approval deadline.
fix: Make the decision line specific: 'Board approval requested at the December 2026 meeting for (1) renewal of the $4B authorization before its January 2027 expiry and (2) declaration of the $2B special dividend.' Two dates, two decisions.

issue: The buyback floor is 'pause above 1.1x the 52-week high $1,106.21, about $1,217'. But $1,106.21 is also the current price and the top of the 52-week range. Pausing above 1.1x the high means pausing after a 10% run from today — that is a very tight buyback band and it is not justified on the page.
fix: Either justify the 1.1x multiple (e.g. vs historical trading range, or a stated policy) or set the floor on a more defensible basis: e.g. 'pause when price exceeds X times FY2026 EPS $20.76', which uses a number already in the deck. A floor with no rationale is a floor the board will overrule.

issue: 'Special dividend ($2.26 per $1B; the recommended $2B is $4.51/share)' — check the arithmetic. $2B / 443.1M shares = $4.51/share, consistent. But $2.26 per $1B is $1B / 443.1M = $2.26, consistent. Fine. However the row compares a one-time dividend of $4.51/share to an annual buyback yield, which are not the same time basis.
fix: Label the special dividend row as 'one-time' and the buyback and capex rows as 'annual'. Add a line stating the comparison is on a per-dollar, per-year basis and that the special dividend is a one-off. Otherwise the table compares apples to oranges.

where: Slide 2 headline and body, versus slide 4 row 'buyback'
issue: The governing thought endorses a $4B buyback at a 1.88% earnings yield when the same book shows the 13-week T-bill at 4.12% (F24) and the 10-year at 5.15% (F25). Slide 2 asserts the return; it does not state the give-up, nor the rate at which the $20.21B is currently invested. A committee will ask 'why buy back stock at 1.88% when cash earns 4.12%' before it reads slide 3.
fix: On slide 2, add a labelled line: 'Cash earns 4.12% (13-week T-bill, 13 Nov 2026) vs 1.88% earnings yield on buyback; post-tax spread -X bps.' Compute X from the two rates already in the material and the 24.7% effective tax rate, and state plainly that the buyback is EPS-accretive (F31: $20.76 to $20.80 per $1B) but returns less than holding the cash. Slide 4's buyback row already carries the 4.12% comparison; slide 2 must not omit it.

where: Slide 3, right-hand argument and slide 4, capex row '22.2% return on existing invested capital'
issue: 22.2% (F32) is operating income $11.69B x (1 - tax) over average invested capital, an entire-company ROIC on stock built over decades. It is being used to justify the FY2027 marginal $7.5B capex step-up. The two numbers do not measure the same thing, and slide 3's 'on the $7.5B plan FY2026 OCF $15.82B implies $8.32B of FCF' is a restatement of FCF, not a return on the increment.
fix: Relabel the capex row and slide 4's title to 'Return on existing invested capital 22.2% (F32), not the marginal return on the FY2027 $7.5B step-up.' If the marginal return cannot be sourced, say so on the slide and drop the implied comparison to the 1.88% buyback yield, which is a marginal number. If the argument is that maintenance capex is covered and the surplus is discretionary, make that the argument in words, not a 22.2% figure.

where: Model, tax rate used on slide 4
issue: Two tax rates in one book. Slide 3 footnote states 'income tax $3.02B / (operating income $11.69B less interest expense $145.0M) = 26.2%'. Slide 4's F32 formula uses '24.7% effective tax rate' with no derivation shown. Same company, same fiscal year, two rates; the client's tax director will catch it in the room.

Either recompute F32 with 26.2% (F17/(F14-F6)) and restate the 22.2% accordingly, or derive 24.7% explicitly from net income $9.23B (F3) / pre-tax income, cite F52's $83M and $72M discrete benefits as the bridge from the statutory rate, and put that derivation on slide 4 next to the 22.2%. Do not carry both.

where: Slide 2, cash walk: 'opening cash $20.21B less the $6B return = $14.21B; plus FY2027 operating cash flow (assume flat on FY2026 $15.82B) less $7.5B capex = $6.71B'
issue: OCF is assumed flat at $15.82B (F7) with no basis. F18 shows revenue growth of 7.8% a year and F49 shows comparable sales up 6.7%, which is a case for growth, not flat. Add one line beneath the flat-OCF assumption: 'OCF assumed flat at $15.82B (F7); every +$1B of OCF adds $1B to closing cash and the FY2027 surplus.' where: Slide 4, F32 invested-capital denominator; and overall
issue: F32's expression is 'equity $35.80B + long-term debt $3.91B' (F15 + F10), but the footnote also cites operating lease liabilities $2.61B (F11) at 2026-08-30 without saying whether they are in or out of the denominator. With them in, invested capital is $42.32B and the return falls; with them out, it is $39.71B. Separately, the denominator is a point-in-time balance, not the average of the prior year, which overstates the return on capital that was actually at work during the year.

Recompute with leases in, since Costco's warehouse estate is substantially leased, and show the prior-year comparative so the average is used. If average capital is not available in the material, request it.

where: Slide 2, '$2B special dividend ($4.51/share)' and slide 4, 'special dividend ($2.26 per $1B; the recommended $2B is $4.51/share)'

Slide 4's 'per $1B' special dividend line is a scaling rule and should be labelled as such, as F29 is.

where: Slides 1, 2, 4, 5: share price and market data
issue: The entire return case is priced off a single close of $1,106.21 on 2026-11-13 (F21) from Yahoo Finance, with a 52-week range of $850.00-$1,106.21 (F22) also from the same day. issue: The single most important number in the deck, the $7.5B FY2027 capex step-up, is sourced to 'financialfilings.com, COSTCO WHOLESALE CORP - Annual Report 2026' (F36) and a 10-K that the citations give as 2026-10-07. Correct 'du ring' to 'during'. Add the F37 warehouse openings (28 in 2026, up to 33 planned in 2027) as the operating evidence behind the $7.5B, not just the dollar.

where: Slide 3, sensitivity: 'at -20% ($12.66B) FCF after $7.5B capex is $5.16B and closing cash after the $6B return is $6.71B'

issue: 1.1 x $1,106.21 is $1,216.83, shown as $1,217. issue: The cover carries mixed as-of dates by design ($1,106.21 close 2026-11-13, 443.1M shares 2026-09-29, cash $20.21B at 2026-08-30), with the footnote instruction 'Footnote the mixed dates.' where: slide 2, cash walk; also slide 3 sensitivity
issue: The walk does not foot. Opening cash $20.21B + OCF $15.82B - capex $7.5B - return $6B = $22.53B. But the deck also argues FY2026 FCF is $9.38B ($15.82B - $6.43B). If FY2027 OCF is flat and capex rises to $7.5B, incremental cash generation is only $8.32B, not $15.82B. The $22.53B closing cash implies $28.53B of inflows against $13.5B of outflows, which does not reconcile to the stated FY2027 capex step-up.

Then explain why the $7.5B capex does not reduce cash by the full amount — it is an outflow, but the walk double-counts if OCF already nets the prior year's capex. State the FY2027 OCF assumes flat operations with no working-capital build and no interest income on the returned cash. Label the assumed flat OCF clearly on the slide and in a footnote. If the arithmetic still cannot be made to foot, change the headline to the number that does foot.

issue: Two load-bearing facts use financialfilings.com rather than the SEC filing itself: the $7.5B FY2027 capex guidance (F36) and the $4B January 2023 buyback authorization expiry (F40). The deck's recommendation is built on these two numbers. A board committee will ask for the primary source.

If financialfilings.com is the only available source, say so on the slide and mark the fact as needing primary confirmation before the board meeting.

issue: The slide admits 'the marginal return on the next $7.5B is not sourced in the materials' but still uses 22.2% return on existing invested capital as the anchor for the allocation argument. A historical average return on all invested capital is not evidence for the return on the FY2027 step-up, and the board will notice the gap.

Add a research line on the slide: 'Marginal return on FY2027 cohort requires cohort-level revenue and capex data; plan to include in the February board package.'

where: slide 1 cover vs. slide 2 executive summary
issue: The cover subtitle says 'fund FY2027 warehouse growth and return $6B of surplus cash.' The executive summary says the same thing with more detail. The cover should frame the decision, not preview the answer. A board member seeing only the cover learns the recommendation before the analysis.

Keep the two framing numbers ($490.19B market cap and $20.21B cash) but add a third: $7.5B FY2027 capex guidance. That sets the tension the deck resolves.

issue: Slide 4's title says 'Allocation: existing invested capital earns 22.2% after tax; a buyback earns 1.88% on each dollar.' Slide 4 should be one table: three uses of $1B, one column of return, one column of time basis, one takeaway line. The takeaway should be: 'On a per-dollar basis, warehouse capex earns more than a buyback at today's price; the board's decision is about the marginal $7.5B, not the historical average.'

issue: The closing slide includes a buyback floor tied to 25x FY2026 diluted EPS ($20.76), about $519, and references a 52-week range of $850.00-$1,106.21. The 25x multiple is new information that appears on no prior slide. The board has not seen a framework for why 25x is the pause threshold.
fix: Either move the 25x buyback floor to slide 4 (allocation) or add one line on slide 5 explaining the multiple: '25x FY2026 EPS implies a 4.0% earnings yield, below the 4.12% T-bill, so repurchase stops creating value below that price.' If the multiple is a management preference, say so and label it as a policy choice, not an analytical conclusion.

issue: The cover footnote discloses mixed dates and share-count vintage, which is good. But the cover shows market cap $490.19B and cash $20.21B side by side without a label that they are at different dates (market cap 2026-11-13, cash 2026-08-30). A reader could conflate them.
fix: Add a superscript or a short label under each number: '$490.19B market cap (13 Nov 2026)' and '$20.21B cash (30 Aug 2026).' Keep the footnote explaining the share-count vintage.

where: slide 3, must show: FY2027 capex guidance '$7.5B'; slide 4, warehouse capex row '22.2% return on existing invested capital'; slide 5, step 3 'fund the $7.5B FY2027 capex'
issue: The two numbers the decision turns on are the worst-sourced items in the deck. The $7.5B FY2027 capex comes only from F36, financialfilings.com re-typing 'spend approximately $7,500 du ring fiscal 2027' from an annual report; no cost structure, no SI&O or pilot cost for the step-up, no post-2027 capex path. The 22.2% return comes from F32, an undefined invested-capital denominator. (Note: F32 as written is arithmetically impossible: $11.69B x (1 - 24.7%) = $8.802B; $8.802B / ($35.80B + $3.91B = $39.71B) = 22.2%. The '24.7%' keyed into F32 is a rounding of the 26.2% effective rate derived in F52's bridge, so the same workbook uses two tax rates for the same return. That is exactly the kind of internal inconsistency a committee catches.) A board is being asked to commit $7.5B against a re-typed press number and a historical average that the slide itself admits is not the marginal return.
fix: Replace F36 with the primary source: Costco FY2026 10-K, Item 7 MD&A capital expenditure section, and the 4Q26 earnings release/call (Sept-Oct 2026). Quote the $7.5B (and the 'up to 33 new warehouses' from F37) with its page reference. If primary does not confirm $7.5B, rebuild the slide-3 walk on the confirmed number. On slide 4, either source the actual FY2027 capex economics (warehouse count x build cost x ramp) or relabel the row unambiguously as a historical company average and state that no marginal return is sourced, not buried in a note. Footnote F32's 24.7% <-> F17 26.2% discrepancy and use one rate everywhere.

where: slide 2, executive summary; slide 4, buyback row; slide 5, step 2

State the reference price used for the $4.51/share dividend is the 2026-11-13 close and footnote that the record-date price will differ.

where: slide 3, sensitivity table; slide 4, tax-rate derivation

Slide 4 keys 24.7% from F52 while the bridge elsewhere is 26.2% (F17 $3.02B / ($11.69B - $145.0M)). F52's $83M and $72M discrete benefits are benchmarked only against the statutory rate, which is asserted, not sourced. The numbers do not tie to one rate.

Slide 3: add a capex overrun column (+10%, capex $8.25B) and a note that working capital and seasonality are excluded; recompute closing cash and cover on each column, and label all ratios x.

issue: Two divisors are from different vintages on the same slide: the buyback math uses 443.1M shares at 2026-09-29 (F1) and diluted EPS $20.76 (F13) from FY2026, while the T-bill line compares 1.88% against 4.12% at 2026-11-13 (F24). The 4.12% short rate versus the 5.15% 10-year (F25) also means 'buyback at 1.88%' is a floating-rate comparison against a short instrument, not a like-for-like cost of capital, and the slide does not say so.
fix: Add a basis footnote on slide 4: diluted EPS is FY2026 (F13), shares outstanding are at 2026-09-29 (F1), and yields are at 2026-11-13 (F24/F25). Add one line that the T-bill is a short-rate comparison; if the 10-year is the right opportunity cost, label both yields against the same date.

issue: Slide 4's title, 'existing invested capital earns 22.2% after tax; a buyback earns 1.88% on each dollar,' stacks the deck toward capex, while slide 2 recommends returning $6B on top of the full $7.5B. The two are consistent only if the $6B is genuinely surplus after capex, and the deck makes that argument on slide 3. where: slide 4, warehouse capex row; slide 3, sensitivity table; slide 5, risks line

issue: Mixed dates and vintages are present but the cover footnote must carry them: market cap is $490.19B at the 2026-11-13 close (F21) x 443.1M shares at 2026-09-29 (F1); cash is $20.21B at 2026-08-30 (F5); the dividend is $4.51/share on a $1.47 quarterly dividend declared 2026-04-15 and paid 2026-05-15 (F41), annualized to $5.88. fix: Keep the cover footnote on vintage. On slide 2 or 4, add one line: $4.51/share is 2.6x the $1.47 quarterly dividend and 0.80% of the 2026-11-13 reference price; it is one-time and separate from the regular dividend.

issue: The slide carries five separate asks: a three-row history table with two CAGRs, a capacity argument, a four-column OCF/capex sensitivity table with a recomputed cover ratio per line, a break-even OCF, and a working-capital caveat. That is three pages of content on one. The sensitivity table is decision-grade work and deserves room; right now it will be an illegible footnote or it will kill the history table.
fix: Cut the sensitivity table and the break-even line from slide 3 and move them to slide 4, which has space, or drop the break-even and working-capital caveat to a footnote. Slide 3 becomes: history table left, capacity argument right, two lines of text. Keep the ratios 3.1x and 2.7x and the one-line denominator explanation.

issue: The $7.5B FY2027 capex guidance on the cover is sourced to 'financialfilings.com', a third-party aggregator, and the 10-K filed 2026-10-07 is already in hand. A board cover number with a secondary source is a credibility leak, and F36's text is visibly corrupted ('$6,435' vs $6.43B, 'du ring').
fix: Resolve the guidance to the 10-K itself (the FY2026 10-K filed 2026-10-07, capex discussion or MD&A) and cite it with the accession number. If the $7.5B is not in the 10-K, use F51's 'roughly $6.5 billion' for FY2026 as the last company-stated figure and label FY2027 as management intention pending confirmation. Fix the corrupted quote before it reaches a footnote.

issue: The slide says the marginal return on the FY2027 $7.5B is unknown and not sourced, then asks the board to approve the full $7.5B anyway. You cannot have both. Either the marginal evidence exists or the recommendation has a hole in it.
fix: Either (a) cut the research line from the face of the slide and defend the full capex on the company's 3-year track record (OCF +12.6% a year, capex +14.2% a year, 22.2% historical ROIC), noting the marginal return will be reported in the February package; or (b) keep the line and soften the ask to a conditional approval. Pick one and say it plainly. I would take (a), but the slide must not read as a question it then talks past.

issue: Three dense footnotes (26.2% effective tax rate, F52's $83M and $72M discrete benefits, the diluted-EPS/share-count/yield basis) plus a 25x buyback floor and its rationale plus a takeaway on a table page. The page will look busy and the reader will skip the table, which is the point of the page.
fix: Keep the tax-rate footnote to one line: '26.2% effective; F52's $83M R&D credit and $72M stock-comp benefit are the bridge from statutory.' Move the basis footnote to slide 2's metrics panel or the closing. Do not add the F50 tariff-refund data point (a revenue tailwind) here; it does not belong and will distract.

issue: Slides 2 and 4 both restate the cash walk and both carry the 25x floor / scaling rule. Slide 2 says 'the 25x buyback floor lives on slide 4'; slide 4 repeats the basis and the funding conclusion. That is a repeat across the two content pages.

issue: The Title reads as a to-do list, not the reason the board is deciding. It also repeats slide 2's split and slide 4's floor without adding anything.

where: Slide 2, executive_summary, cash walk: 'opening cash $20.21B + FY2027 operating cash flow $15.82B - FY2027 capex $7.5B - return $6B = closing cash $22.53B'
issue: The walk ignores dividends. F12 shows dividends declared of $5.54/share in FY2026, and F8 shows $1.15B dividends paid through 2026-05-10 (a 10-Q stub). At 443.1M shares, the annualised dividend at $1.47/share is roughly $2.6B. The model adds a full year of OCF but subtracts no regular dividend, which overstates closing cash by about $2.6B. fix: Add a 'regular dividends' line to the walk: opening cash $20.21B + OCF $15.82B - capex $7.5B - regular dividends ~$2.6B (443.1M x $1.47 x 4) - return $6B = closing cash ~$19.9B. If you keep $22.53B, state explicitly that the walk excludes the regular dividend and label it a gross-of-dividend walk. Do not carry a $22.53B cover headline while omitting a known cash use.

where: Slide 3, exhibit_argument, F36: 'In 2026, we spent $6,435 on capital expenditures, and it is our current intention to spend approximately $7,500 during fiscal 2027' (source cited as financialfilings.com)
issue: Every operating number on slides 2-5 (the cash walk, the 2.1x OCF cover, the 2.7x cash cover, the sensitivity table, the $8.25B stack test, the closing) rests on the $7.5B FY2027 capex figure. That figure's only source is financialfilings.com, a secondary aggregator. If it is wrong or if it is a gross number from a different period, the entire recommendation resizes. where: Slide 2, F7 and Slide 3, F7: operating cash flow $15.82B 'assumed flat on FY2026' is used as the FY2027 inflow in the cash walk and in the sensitivity table ($14.24B / $12.66B are derived from it by applying -10%/-20%)

More importantly, Costco's FY2027 OCF will be affected by the F49 tariff-refund gross-margin tailwind and by the F48/F50 price reinvestment, both sourced from Yahoo Finance, but neither is reflected. The sensitivity table then treats the plug as a base and calls the -10% case a downside, which it is not — the downside is already inside the flat assumption.
fix: Either (a) source an FY2027 OCF estimate from consensus or the company's own guidance, or (b) label the $15.82B as an unsourced flat assumption and add a working-capital sensitivity row: 0 / -$1B / -$2B working-capital build, showing closing cash $22.53B / $21.53B / $20.53B on the base. where: Slide 4, table_focus, F32: 'after-tax return on capital 22.2% = operating income $11.69B x (1 - 24.7% effective tax rate) / (equity $35.80B + long-term debt $3.91B)'

where: Slides 2 and 5: '$2B special dividend ($4.51/share, 2.6x the $1.47 quarterly dividend and 0.80% of the 2026-11-13 reference price)' and the same $4.51/share on slide 4

where: Slide 4, buyback row: 'EPS $20.76 to $20.80 before lost interest' and 'earnings yield 1.88% versus the 4.12% T-bill'

That is a materially different policy conclusion and it is hidden by a rate-horizon mismatch.

Show the buyback floor under each: 4.0% earnings yield at 25x ($519) versus the 4.12% bill; 5.15% would imply about 19.4x ($403). where: Storyline: cover, executive_summary, exhibit_argument, table_focus, closing — no slide addresses the Costco-specific reason buybacks may not be the right tool at $1,106.21
issue: F15 gives shareholders' equity of $35.80B; F16 gives net PP&E of $35.63B. Costco's market cap of $490.19B (F28) is roughly 13.7x book. The deck compares the buyback to a T-bill and to capex, but never to the book value being retired or to the fact that a special dividend returns cash at book while a buyback at 13.7x book transfers value from continuing holders to sellers if the market price is above intrinsic value. where: Slide 1, cover: '$490.19B market cap (13 Nov 2026)' and 'cash $20.21B (30 Aug 2026)' and '$7.5B FY2027 capex guidance'

issue: Title says '$13.3B' in the outline and '$13.29B' everywhere in the body — the cover promise and the exhibit must use one number. The stated $13.3B also sits against the filing's 'approximately $13.38' in footnote 2 of slide 2.

issue: The bridge does not foot. 20.21 + 15.82 - 6.43 - 13.29 - 2.61 - 0.85 = 12.85, which reconciles, but the title claims cash 'covers the $13.29B special dividend 1.5x' while the closing balance shown is 12.85 — the 1.5x is opening cash only and the page does not say so; a reader checking the bars will read the coverage as 12.85/13.29.

issue: Title says 'Buybacks earn 1.88% at today's price' but the right column says the trigger is 'buy only when the earnings yield clears the 4.12% cash yield, below about $504 a share' — the page gives a rule the board cannot act on without a share-price condition, and the $504 crossover is buried in footnote 1 instead of the chart.

issue: The $13.29B is stated as declared and payable, but slide 2 footnote 2 says the record date of 24 November 'could differ' and the company states approximately $13.38. The deck presents a decision on a number that is not final.

issue: Buttons of different widths for three bars — 1.88%, 4.12%, 5.15% — with no origin mark and no zero baseline tick on the left axis. The reader cannot see relative magnitude cleanly.

issue: Three-line title wraps awkwardly ('Costco Wholesale: capital / allocation decision, November / 2026') with '2026' orphaned, and the page is two-thirds empty below the subtitle.

Show the interest income line (>$0.5B on $20B at 4%+) or state explicitly that interest income is excluded and why.

issue: Three different share-count / dividend figures are used without reconciliation: slide 2 says '$13.29B ... 443.1MM shares', slide 5 says '$13.29B is the $30.00 a share declared on 443.1MM shares outstanding at 2026-09-29; the company states approximately $13.38'. $30.00 × 443.1MM = $13.293B, so the arithmetic holds, but slide 2's headline says '$13.3B' and slide 4's waterfall uses $13.29B while its title says '$13.29B covers'. issue: The buyback 'earnings yield' of 1.88% is an EPS-accretion test, and footnote 1 says so — but the page then treats 4.12% as the hurdle the buyback must clear at a crossover of '$504 a share'. Add one line: implied P/E at 1.88% = 53x; compare to Costco's 5-year average and to the 10-year Treasury 5.15%. issue: 'Operating cash flow compounded at 12.6% a year over the same three years' — no source line ties to a specific fiscal period (FY24–FY26? FY23–FY26?). Slide 2's $9.38B FCF (FY2026) is sourced, slide 3's 12.6% CAGR is not.
fix: Add a source line on slide 3 to the Costco 10-K cash flow statements with the exact three fiscal years used (e.g. FY2024 vs FY2026) and show the two OCF figures in the footnote so a reader can verify 12.6%. If the three years are FY2024–FY2026, state that FY2026 is the filed 10-K and FY2024 the comparative.

issue: No per-share value or football field. The deck recommends ratifying the funding, pacing the buyback and keeping capex, but never shows what the board is buying or giving up. issue: Slide 5 row 4 trigger — 'earnings yield below the 13-week bill yield for two quarters' — is an EPS test masquerading as a capital-allocation rule, and it is undefined: does the board pause the buyback, reduce it, or resume? The deck's own footnote 3 on slide 5 defines the crossover at '$20.76 / 0.0412 = $504', but the trigger says '20.76 / 4.12% = $504 share'; $20.76 of diluted EPS divided by a 0.0412 rate does not give a share price — it gives an EPS/rate ratio with units of dollars-per-share only if you invert the yield. Then define the trigger outcome: 'If the earnings yield is below the 13-week bill yield for two consecutive quarters, the board suspends the $212M quarterly tranche and revisits at the following quarter.'

issue: The waterfall shows only the base case. No downside: what happens if operating cash flow is 10% below the $15.82B, or if the April 2026 dividend of $1.47 a quarter rises? issue: The waterfall title says '$20.21B covers the $13.29B special dividend 1.5x' but the chart does not show the coverage ratio anywhere — a reader has to divide 20.21/13.29 = 1.52 themselves. Title says 1.5x, which is correct, but the bar doesn't carry the label.

issue: Every page is stamped 'Preliminary' and the footer says 'Meshpool' — that is the template brand, not Costco or the bank. A board book should not carry a third-party tool name in the footer, and 'Preliminary' on all five pages makes the pack look unfinished rather than controlled.

issue: The uses list omits the $4B buyback authorization's actual draw in FY2027 and any working-capital or debt movement, so the 'closing $12.85B' is presented as cash remaining when it may be an average or trough balance. issue: The 4.12% 13-week T-bill and 5.15% 10-year Treasury are dated only as 'Yahoo Finance 2026-11-11' with no ticker or series. where: slide 2, 'A buyback at today's price reduces net EPS' and '$0.04 of EPS'

issue: 'Board meeting, November 2026' with no author, no date of preparation and no confidentiality legend. Compared to the preliminary marks on slides 2-5, the cover reads like a fill-in.

issue: Chart bar labels show 1.88%, 4.12%, 5.15% but the axis has no unit label ('%' alone is not enough) and the bars are of unequal category (a buyback EPS yield vs. two market rates) plotted as if comparable.

where: slide 3 title: "Cash troughs at $6.9B in Q1 2027, above the $4.9B minimum"
issue: Neither $6.9B nor $4.9B appears anywhere in the facts. The title asserts a specific trough and a specific minimum with no source and no build, on the one slide that is supposed to de-risk the whole recommendation. A committee will ask for the arithmetic and there is none.
fix: Either build the trough from named facts — opening cash $20.21B (F5), plus operating cash flow $15.82B (F7), less capex $6.43B (F4), less the $30 special dividend on 443.1M shares (F41/F1), less regular dividends $1.15B (F8) and buyback cash paced at $1.0B — and state the resulting figure on the page; or delete the numbers from the title, retitle it "Cash stays above the operating minimum through the dividend and the buyback", and table the schedule underneath. Do not ship an unsourced trough on the decision slide.

issue: $17.3B is not in the facts either. It reads as $13.3B special dividend plus a $4B buyback booked in full — which contradicts the recommendation itself, since slide 5 says pace the buyback at $1.0B a year. The headline number on the executive summary overstates the near-term cash out by roughly $3B.
fix: Size the two programmes separately and to their own terms: the $30 special dividend is $13.3B (443.1M shares × $30, F1/F41); the $4B buyback is authorised (F42) but drawn at $1.0B a year, so about $1.0B in the first twelve months. Retitle slide 1 and slide 2 to "Return $13.3B now: pay the $30 special dividend and pace the $4B buyback at $1.0B a year" so the cover, the summary and the ask state one number.

where: slide 2, must show: "the sized recommendation, what each option implies, and the decision requested today"
issue: The slide carries cash, return on capital, free cash flow and the scaling rule, but not the one thing the brief demands: the alternative. "What each option implies" needs the other branch — keeping the cash in the business, or a larger buyback — costed against the recommendation. Slide 4 argues growth versus buyback on return, but there is no line that says what choosing growth alone costs the shareholder, or what a bigger buyback would return.
fix: Add a two-row comparison to slide 2. Row one, recommended: $13.3B dividend plus $1.0B a year buyback, growth funded. Row two, alternative: no return, all cash to capex and balance sheet — and state its cost with facts in hand, e.g. the earnings yield of 1.88% (F30) is what the shareholder forgoes, against the T-bill yield of 4.12% (F24) the cash would otherwise earn. If the board is also weighing a buyback above $1.0B a year, cost that row from F29 and F31.

issue: Slide 4's claim is that growth earns 22.2% on capital and should be funded before extra buybacks — but slide 2 already argues the buyback is worth doing. Two pages pull in opposite directions without a rule that reconciles them: the deck never says why a $1.0B-a-year buyback beats zero, given growth earns 22.2% and the buyback earns 1.88%.
fix: Make the rule explicit on slide 4, in one line under the exhibit: growth absorbs the capital it can at 22.2% (F32); the buyback is paced at $1.0B a year at an earnings yield of 1.88% against cash yielding 4.12% (F30/F24), so the test is whether cash exceeds the growth plan's needs. Then slide 2's recommendation reads as the output of that rule, not a separate opinion.

where: slide 5, must show: "owners, timing and the condition that would change it"
issue: The closing slide lists sources, not a plan: no owners, no dates, no stated condition. The brief asked for all three, and this is the page the board acts on.
fix: Turn slide 5 into a 90-day roadmap with named owners and dates — declaration and payment of the $13.3B special dividend, board sign-off on the $1.0B-a-year drawdown against the $4B authorisation, first review — and add the tripwire: if capex commitments rise above the level that keeps the trough above the minimum, or the return on capital falls below the cost of capital, the buyback pace is cut. Both conditions use facts already in the deck.

issue: Slide 4's title and slide 2's title both make the same argument — growth first, return the excess. A reader gets the answer twice and the deck loses a page it could use.
fix: Confine the argument to slide 2, where the recommendation belongs, and let slide 4 prove it rather than restate it. Retitle slide 4 to its own evidence: "Growth compounds at 22.2% while the buyback earns 1.88% and cash earns 4.12%" — then the slide is the test, not a second conclusion. Have slide 2 carry the capital allocation verdict and slide 4 the rate-of-return evidence.

where: Slide 4 ('Growth earns 22.2% on capital, so fund warehouses before extra buybacks')
issue: The comparison is incomplete. The exhibit sets 22.2% ROIC (F32) against the 13-week T-bill 4.12% (F24) and a 1.88% earnings yield (F30), but never states a cost of capital. In a $490.19B market-cap company with beta 0.24 (F23) and a 5.15% 10-year (F25), the 13-week bill is the wrong hurdle and a committee will say so. The word 'before' in the title asserts a ranking the slide does not yet prove.
fix: State the cost of capital explicitly: because beta is 0.24 (F23), use a debt-like cost of equity; show WACC as the 4.12% 13-week T-bill (F24) as the risk-free proxy, or disclose that if COST's cost of equity is equity-risk-premium times 0.24 beta plus 4.12%, it lands under 6%, which is still materially below 22.2% (F32). Add '22.2% vs. a cost of capital under 6%' as the slide's comparison line and change the title to 'Growth earns 22.2%, buybacks earn 1.88%: fund growth first'.

issue: The buyback pace of $1.0B a year and the $13.3B dividend are stated as a decision but not derived. The only scaling facts are F29 ($1B retires 0.90M shares at $1,106.21, 0.20% of 443.1M) and F31 (EPS rises from $20.76 to $20.80 after a $1B buyback, before lost interest). Nothing in the storyboard says why $1.0B a year rather than the full $4B authorization (F42) or zero. The number is a plug.
fix: On slide 2, show the test behind the pace: at $1,106.21 (F21), $4B retires 3.6M shares and adds $0.17 to EPS (from $20.76 to $20.93, using F29 and F31); at $1.0B it adds $0.04. Justify $1.0B as the amount that keeps the buyback's cash return (1.88% earnings yield, F30) above the 4.12% lost on cash (F24) only if funded from surplus cash, and state the condition: if the share price falls below the level where the earnings yield exceeds the T-bill yield, accelerate toward $4B; if it rises, stop. Put that condition on slide 5.

where: Slide 3 (waterfall_bridge, 'Cash troughs at $6.9B in Q1 2027, above the $4.9B minimum')
issue: The trough of $6.9B and the $4.9B minimum are not supported by any fact on the slide. For the special dividend, use $30 x 443.1M = $13.293B (F41, F1); for the buyback use the stated $1.0B pace. Show the trough and its date. Source the minimum operating cash or label it an assumption with the basis: cash cover of capex is 3.1x (F27); state whether the minimum is one quarter of capex, a weeks-of-cash figure, or the $4.9B you intend.

where: Slide 4 (F52 and F53) and F34, F35, F46, F47
issue: The P/E of 52.0x (F52) and EBITDA multiple of 32.4x (F53) are sourced to multiples.vc dated 2025-10-26, more than a year before the November 2026 board date. issue: The storyboard plans no DCF and no comparable-company or precedent-transaction analysis, even though the brief asks for 'valuation' research. F45 names Target, Loblaw, Walmart Mexico, Tesco, Kroger, Ahold Delhaize, Woolworths, Seven & i and Walmart as competitors but no multiples are given for any of them.
fix: Add to slide 4 or a revised slide 4: a DCF with explicit assumptions and a terminal value, or state why a DCF is not used and value the shares on earnings yield and multiples instead. If a DCF is used, show the terminal value as a percent of total value — if it is over 70% the committee will treat the answer as a terminal-value bet. Add a comps table with the peer set from F45 and their P/E and EV/EBITDA, or state that the decision does not turn on relative value and say why.

where: F41 and F42, sourced to finance.yahoo.com, 'Costco (COST) Declares $30 Special Dividend And Reauthorizes $4 Billion Buyback, 2026-11-11'

If the 8-K cannot be located, label the figure 'company announcement via Yahoo Finance, to be confirmed' and do not use it in a sizing calculation until confirmed.

issue: The recommendation totals $17.3B ($13.3B special dividend plus a stated $4B buyback) but the storyboard also adopts a $1.0B-a-year pace on slide 5. The $17.3B headline therefore implies the full $4B is returned, while the closing implies $1.0B a year. issue: The storyboard does not stress the two variables that decide the answer: capex and the share price. Capex grew 14.2% a year to $6.43B (F19) and F38 says Costco expects capex growth to slow after fiscal 2027, while F40 cites a $6,500 fiscal 2026 plan; F39 gives 33 warehouse openings in fiscal 2027 including five relocations. State the break-even: if the earnings yield (1.88%, F30) falls below the lost cash yield (4.12%, F24), the buyback destroys value and the pace should go to zero.

issue: The cover title 'Costco capital allocation: fund growth and return $17.3B' states the recommendation on the cover before the evidence. By the page order it is the conclusion, and combined with the $17.3B total versus the $13.3B plus $1.0B pace it is also wrong on amount.
fix: Make the cover title neutral: 'Costco capital allocation: growth, buybacks, or a special dividend.' Keep the subtitle naming the decision and date November 2026. Move 'fund growth and return' to slide 2 and 5, where the numbers support it.

issue: The slide carries operating cash flow F7 and capex F4 but drops F9 (share repurchases $848.0M for the year to 2026-08-30) and F8 (dividends paid $1.15B for the period to 2026-05-10, a 10-Q period ending earlier). A sources-and-uses bridge that omits the ordinary buyback and an interim dividend is incomplete and mixes periods.
fix: Add F9 as the run-rate ordinary repurchase, and use annualized ordinary dividends rather than F8's partial-period $1.15B, or footnote that F8 covers 2025-09-01 to 2026-05-10 and is not a full fiscal year. Put closing cash and the trough on the same slide in one row so the arithmetic ties.

where: Storyline, use of F38 and F39
issue: The warehouse-growth plan relies on supplychain360.io (F38, F39) rather than Costco's own disclosure. F40 is the company's own language ('it is our current intention to spend approximately $6,500 during fiscal 2026'), and the 10-K would carry the openings and capex guidance.

where: Slide 3, waterfall_bridge: "Cash stays above the operating minimum through the dividend and the buyback"
issue: There is no stated minimum operating cash anywhere in the storyboard or the facts. You cannot claim to clear a bar you never set. Worse, the trough is never computed: a $13.3B special dividend ($30 x 443.1M, F41/F1) plus FY27 capex of ~$6.5B (F40) against opening cash of $20.21B (F5) plus FCF mechanics already puts the company through the floor. As drafted the page proves the opposite of what the title says.

Two candidate anchors are already in the facts: working capital plus one quarter of capex, or the $13.3B dividend measured against FY free cash flow of $9.38B (F26). The trough computation has to be shown on the slide. If the arithmetic does not clear the bar, the title and the recommendation both change; that is a decision, not a formatting choice.

where: Slide 4, exhibit_argument: "Growth earns 22.2%, buybacks earn 1.88%: fund growth first"
issue: The comparison that does the work is stated wrong. The 22.2% is return on invested capital (F32), not return on incremental capital; the buyback return is 1.88% (F30) on today's price. Those are not like with like, and no committee will let it slide. Two facts that would carry the argument are sitting unused: capex grew 14.2% a year for three years while revenue grew 7.8% (F19 vs F18), so incremental returns are already fading; and P/E is 52.0x (F52), which is what makes the 1.88% earnings yield what it is.
fix: Retitle slide 4 to compare the two decisions on the same basis. Lead with P/E 52.0x (F52) and earnings yield 1.88% (F30) as the price of buying back stock today, then show the marginal return on the growth program, not the blended ROIC. Add the capex vs revenue growth gap (14.2% vs 7.8% a year, F19/F18) as the tension the page is resolving. If the marginal return cannot be sourced, say so and label the 22.2% as blended ROIC.

where: Slide 2, executive_summary: "Return $13.3B now: pay the $30 special dividend and pace the $4B buyback at $1.0B a year"
issue: The brief asks what each option implies, including doing nothing. The slide names the recommendation and one pace, but the three alternatives (dividend alone, buyback alone, neither) have no stated consequence. The $13.3B is arithmetically $30 x 443.1M (F41/F1) and the $1.0B pace is not a fact in the material at all - it is the author's proposal, presented as if sized.
fix: Show the three options as three lines with three consequences, using the facts in hand. Dividend alone: $13.3B out (F41/F1), cash falls from $20.21B (F5) by roughly a year of FCF of $9.38B (F26). Buyback at $1.0B a year: 0.9M shares retired, 0.20% of the float (F29), EPS $20.76 to $20.80 (F31). Neither: $20.21B (F5) earning 4.12% (F24), versus 1.88% if deployed into the buyback (F30). State the decision requested of the board on this page.

issue: Slide 3 is a mechanics page and slide 4 is the recommendation's rationale; as ordered, the deck shows the plumbing before the argument. Slide 5's title repeats slide 2's title nearly word for word ("Approve the $13.3B dividend and a $1.0B-a-year buyback pace" vs "Return $13.3B now..."), which reads as padding.
fix: Swap slides 3 and 4 so the rationale lands before the financing mechanics. The opening and the close can live with an echo, but make slide 5 do work slide 2 cannot: owners, dates, and the condition that would change the call.

where: Slide 5, closing: "Approve the $13.3B dividend and a $1.0B-a-year buyback pace"
issue: The condition that would change the recommendation is named as a requirement but not supplied, and there is no answer on the page to the obvious committee question: why is the buyback paced rather than run to the full $4B authorisation (F42)?
fix: Add the condition explicitly by combining facts already in the material: buyback economics improve as the P/E of 52.0x (F52) falls or EPS growth lifts the 1.88% earnings yield (F30) toward the 4.12% cash yield (F24). The test the board is adopting is that buyback spending goes up only when the earnings yield does. Put that on the page in one line, with owners and dates.

issue: The cover's decision title ("growth, buybacks, or a special dividend") is right, but slide 1 carries three analytic facts - F41, F42, F26, F32. That is work for slide 2, not a cover. Separately, the two content slides both use exhibits; there is no page where the reader gets the pure fact pattern at a glance.
fix: Strip slide 1 to title, subtitle, date. Move F41/F42 (the declared $30 special dividend and the $4B reauthorisation) to slide 2 where they belong, and F26/F32 stay on slide 4 where they are used.

issue: The buyback return of 1.88% (F30) is an earnings yield, and the associated EPS math (F31) does not account for foregone interest on the $1B spent. The board will be told the buyback earns 1.88%; if the true figure is nearer 1.5%, the argument is stronger, but the number as presented is overstated.
fix: Add the lost interest on the cash (F24 yield applied to the $1B) to the buyback economics on slide 4, and show the net figure. The sources for T-bill yield (F24) and share price (F21) are already in hand.

issue: Big numbers spread without a header narrative is a data dump, not a decision frame. The three options, with the consequence of each, do not fit a big-number layout.
fix: Switch slide 2 to a three-column options table: dividend alone, buyback alone, neither - with the cash, EPS and yield consequence of each. Keep the big numbers as a header band if you like, but the three lines carry the page.

where: Storyboard governing thought and slide 1 F29
issue: The governing thought asserts growth earns 22.2% on capital and the buyback earns 1.88%, but 22.2% is a current-period, balance-sheet-based ROIC on total capital (F32), not the return on incremental capital. The deck's own evidence contradicts the marginal argument: revenue has compounded at 7.8% (F18) while capex has compounded at 14.2% (F19), so incremental capex is running roughly two-for-one against incremental revenue. A committee will ask what the last $1.0B of capex earns, and the storyboard has no number for it.
fix: On slide 4, relabel the 22.2% as 'after-tax return on total capital' and add a third bar for return on incremental capital: compute it as the change in after-tax operating income over the change in invested capital using F14, F17, F15 and F10 across the three-year period ending 2026-08-30 (the 2023 comparatives are cited in F18, F19, F20), or, if that cannot be computed from the facts in hand, drop the 'fund growth first' conclusion to 'growth earns a positive spread over the 4.12% cost of cash; incremental returns require confirmation'.

where: Storyboard governing thought and slide 1 F29
issue: The math in the governing thought and in F29 does not work. F29 says 'every $1B spent on a buyback retires 0.90M shares (0.20% of 443.1M) at $1,106.21'; 0.90M / 443.1M = 0.20%, correct, but the phrasing '$1B ... retires 0.90M shares (0.20% of 443.1M)' plus the EPS math on F31 implies a 20% accretion. Check: $1.0B / $1,106.21 = 0.90M shares, 0.20% of the base. At $20.76 EPS, retiring 0.90M of 443.1M shares lifts EPS to $20.76 x 443.1/442.2 = $20.80 (F31), i.e. +0.19%. That is the number the slide must show, not 0.20% accretion.
fix: Rewrite F29 in the deck and slide 1 to read 'every $1.0B of buyback at $1,106.21 retires 0.90M shares, 0.20% of 443.1M shares outstanding, lifting diluted EPS to $20.80 from $20.76 (+0.2%)'; delete any percentage that reads as accretion of the EPS.

where: Slide 3 node 2 'Cash stays above the operating minimum through the dividend and the buyback'
issue: The slide title asserts a trough above a stated minimum operating cash, but the storyboard never states the minimum and never dates the schedule. F42 gives the buyback authorization ($4B, expiring January 2030); the board call is a pace (governing thought: $1.0B a year). Uses implied: $13.3B dividend (443.1M x $30) plus $1.0B a year of buybacks plus capex at F4 $6.43B a year, against starting cash F5 $20.21B and F26 FCF $9.38B. Without a minimum, the slide is an assertion.
fix: Add a stated minimum operating cash to slide 3, e.g. 'minimum = 1.0x next-twelve-month capex of $6.43B plus seasonal working capital', and show the year-end trough against it: starting cash $20.21B (F5) less $13.3B dividend (F41 x F1) less $1.0B buyback pace, plus $9.38B FCF (F26) less $6.43B capex (F4), with the trough figure and the date. If the trough goes below the minimum, the buyback pace must be cut; state that.

issue: The deck lists no risks and no sensitivity anywhere, and no source other than SEC XBRL and Yahoo Finance for the core recommendation. Missing, and a committee will ask: (1) how much of the $4.0B authorization (F42) is already used or how much of the $848.0M repurchased in FY2026 (F9) counts against it; (2) what happens if the F25 10-year yield of 5.15% or the F24 13-week bill yield of 4.12% move against the 1.88% earnings yield; (3) the dilutive/antidilutive crossover, i.e. the price at which the earnings yield equals the cash yield (F30 1.88% vs F24 4.12%), which is roughly $494; (4) how the F52 52.0x P/E and F53 32.4x EV/EBITDA (multiples.vc, dated 2025-10-26) relate to the decision, since a buyback above intrinsic value destroys value.
fix: Replace slide 4's 'success' exhibit with two panels: (a) the return comparison of the 22.2% total return (F32) against the 4.12% cash yield (F24) and the 1.88% earnings yield (F30), and (b) a simple sensitivity table showing the earnings yield at three share prices ($900, $1,106.21 per F21, $1,300) against the 4.12% cash yield, with the crossover price stated. Add a risks bullet list on slide 4: buyback authorization usage, rate move, and the multiple (F52/F53).

where: Storyboard slide 2 F29, F30, F31, F32
issue: The core recommendation rests on F29, F30, F31 and F32, which the brief itself marks as 'computed' from other facts, yet no slide cites the primary documents for those numbers (the F13 diluted EPS $20.76 and F1 443.1M shares are cited to the 10-K, but the derived figures are not). A board member or an IC will ask for the operating income, tax rate and balance-sheet lines behind F32: F14 $11.69B, F17 $3.02B tax expense (24.7% is implied: $3.02B / ($11.69B - $3.02B + ...) — the rate actually implies a pretax base; check F17/F14 = 25.8%, not 24.7%), F15 $35.80B, F10 $3.91B.
fix: On slide 2, footnote every derived number with the cell reference and the underlying fact IDs, and correct the 24.7% effective tax rate: F17 / F14 gives $3.02B / $11.69B = 25.8%, before considering the pretax base. Recompute F32 with 25.8% and show the arithmetic on the slide: $11.69B x (1 - 0.258) / ($35.80B + $3.91B) = $8.67B / $39.71B = 21.8%, not 22.2%.

where: Storyboard slides 2, 4 and 5 — F52 P/E 52.0x, F53 EV/EBITDA 32.4x, F51 market cap $490B and EV $477B
issue: The valuation multiples used to frame the buyback-versus-growth question are sourced to multiples.vc dated 2025-10-26, which is over a year stale as of the 16 November 2026 board date, and they are internally inconsistent: F51 says EV of $477B against market cap of $490B (EV below market cap, implying net cash of $13B), while F5 shows cash of $20.21B and F10 long-term debt of $3.91B. Also, F34/F35/F46/F47 cite LTM revenue of $309B and EBITDA of $15B against the 10-K revenue of $303.15B (F2) and net income of $9.23B (F3).
fix: Replace slides 2 and 4's multiple references with figures computed from the 10-K: P/E = F21 / F13 = $1,106.21 / $20.76 = 53.3x; EV = F28 market cap $490.19B plus F10 long-term debt $3.91B less F5 cash $20.21B = $473.89B; EV/EBITDA requires an EBITDA figure the deck does not have from the 10-K — either drop it or source it to the 10-K. Strike F51's $477B EV and F34/F35's $309B revenue / $15B EBITDA unless they are restated on a basis tied to the 10-K.

issue: The slide compares the 22.2% total return on capital against the 4.12% cash yield and the 1.88% earnings yield, but the buyback yield is not apples-to-apples: F30 defines the 1.88% as earnings yield, i.e. the return on the capital deployed for a buyback is EPS/share price, which assumes the market re-rates the stock to the earnings yield. That is a re-rating, not a return. The slide needs the direct comparison the committee will make: foregone interest on the cash spent versus the EPS accretion, and the buyback's effect on the market-cap-to-earnings multiple.
fix: On slide 4, state the comparison in one line: '$1.0B of buyback at $1,106.21 retires 0.90M shares (F29), lifts EPS to $20.80 from $20.76 (F31, +0.2%), and foregoes $41.2M of annual interest at the 4.12% 13-week bill yield (F24); net EPS effect after foregone interest is approximately $20.71, i.e. -0.2%.' Then show the price at which the buyback is EPS-neutral: $20.76 / 0.0412 = $503.88.

where: Storyboard slide 2 headline 'Return $13.3B now' and slide 5 'Approve the $13.3B dividend'
issue: The recommendation phrases the special dividend as a decision for the board to approve, but F41 says Costco 'declared' the special dividend on 2026-11-11, before the 16 November 2026 board briefing. If it is already declared, the board decision is not whether to pay it. The deck must be explicit about what is still open: the buyback pace, the funding of the dividend from cash versus incremental debt, and whether the dividend is a one-off or the start of a recurring return policy.
fix: On slides 2 and 5, restate the decision as: 'The $30 special dividend ($13.3B, F41) is declared and payable; the board's remaining decisions are (1) the pace of the $4.0B buyback authorization (F42) — recommend $1.0B a year; (2) funding the dividend from cash on hand (F5 $20.21B) rather than drawings; (3) confirming the 22.2%/21.8% return on capital assumption (F32) that justifies keeping capex intact (F4).' Change slide 5's title to reflect the open decision, not the declared dividend.

where: Slide 3 node 2 and slide 4 node 3, missing warehouse-growth evidence
issue: The recommendation is 'fund growth first', but the storyboard plans no slide for the growth plan. F38 (approximately 30 net new warehouses annually for five to 10 years, capex growth slowing after fiscal 2027) and F39 (33 openings in fiscal 2027 including five relocations) are unused. A board will want the growth case quantified: how much capex does 30 warehouses a year require, and at what return.
fix: Add the growth evidence to slide 4, not a new slide: convert F38/F39 into a capex line — 'approximately 30 net new warehouses a year (F38) at the current average of $6.43B capex / (warehouse count, if available from the 10-K) per warehouse' — and show the capex trajectory against FCF. If the per-warehouse capex is not in the facts, request it from the 10-K property schedule (F16 net PP&E $35.63B is the anchor).

issue: The cover title 'Costco capital allocation: growth, buybacks, or a special dividend' is neutral but the cover's must-show list (F41, F42, F26, F32) is dense for a cover; F32's 22.2% ROIC belongs on slide 4, not the cover.
fix: Cut F26 ($9.38B FCF) and F32 (22.2%) from the cover; keep F41 ($30 special dividend) and F42 ($4.0B authorization) as the news, and date the cover 'November 2026' as specified.

issue: The deck uses the 13-week Treasury bill yield (F24 4.12%) as the cash opportunity cost and the 10-year yield (F25 5.15%) but never reconciles them. The choice matters because it moves the buyback-versus-cash comparison by 103bp.
fix: On slide 2, footnote the choice: 'Costco's cash is short-dated; the 13-week bill yield of 4.12% (F24) is the correct opportunity cost; the 10-year yield of 5.15% (F25) is shown for reference only.'

where: Slide 2, title: "Fund the declared $13.3B dividend from cash and pace the $4B buyback at $1.0B a year"
issue: The arithmetic does not close: 443.1M shares x $30 = $13.293B, not $13.3B, and the brief's own F29 scaling rule ("every $1B paid as a speci...") is truncated mid-sentence so no one can verify the special dividend implies any share count. A board member will do the multiplication in the room and find the page wrong.
fix: State the dividend as $13.29B (443.1M x $30) on slide 2 and in the governing thought, and complete the F29 special-dividend leg before sign-off so the $13.3B figure has a source. If it cannot be tied, label it 'approximately $13.3B' and show the calculation in a footnote.
