where: Slide 4, title: "Cash trough of $9.9B clears the $6.4B minimum after the $13.3B dividend"
issue: Neither number is sourced. F29 gives a scaling rule only; there is no fact anywhere in the brief that states a $6.4B minimum operating cash, and no fact that produces a $9.9B trough. The slide asserts a test it cannot show.
fix: Either derive the trough on the page from F5 + F26 + F41 + F8 + F9 with the dates, and label the $6.4B as 'management's stated minimum operating cash (source: ___)', or replace the title with a claim the facts support, e.g. 'Cash of $20.21B covers the $13.3B dividend 1.5x and frees $6.9B of FCF for capex'. Do not ship an unsourced minimum.

where: Slide 2 and Slide 5, "pace the $4B buyback at $1.0B a year"
issue: $1.0B a year is asserted as the recommendation but nothing in the brief sizes it: F9 shows $848.0M repurchased last year, F42 shows the $4B authorization runs to January 2030, and the 1.88% vs 4.12% comparison supports slowing, not the specific $1.0B. The recommendation is therefore not sized, which the brief explicitly requires.
fix: Make the buyback pace a derived number, not a round number: e.g. 'Pace the buyback at $0.85B a year, matching fiscal 2026's $848.0M (F9), and leave the $4B authorization undrawn to January 2030 (F42)'. Or, if $1.0B is the intent, add the sentence 'a $1.0B annual pace retires 0.90M shares a year (F29), 0.20% of shares, at the 4.12% cash yield foregone'. Either way the slide must show the trade.

where: Slide 3, evidence list: F52 "Costco has a P/E ratio of 52.0x" sourced most-recently to 2025-10-26
issue: The slide's own thesis is built on the 2026-11-13 price of $1,106.21 (F21) and 2026 diluted EPS of $20.76 (F13), which imply 53.3x; the page then presents a 52.0x P/E dated eight days short of a year earlier from a stale comps scrape. A board member will ask which is right and the page has no answer.
fix: Delete the 52.0x reference from slide 3. Use the figures already in the brief: P/E 53.3x = $1,106.21 / $20.76 (F21, F13), earnings yield 1.88% (F30), 52-week range $850.00–$1,106.21 (F22), and state the comparison as 'the stock is at the high end of its 52-week range'. If a third-party multiple is needed, refresh it to November 2026.

where: Slide 3, "Compare the two decisions on the same basis: the price of buying back stock today against the marginal return on the growth program."
issue: The slide sets out to compare buyback return against the marginal return on growth, then presents the 22.2% after-tax return on capital (F32), which is an average return on the existing asset base, not the marginal return on new warehouses. The analysis on the page does not prove the title.
fix: Replace the comparison with one the facts support: put 1.88% buyback earnings yield (F30) against 4.12% 13-week T-bill (F24) and 5.15% 10-year Treasury (F25), and show the $4.32B-to-$6.43B capex ramp (F19, 14.2% a year) as evidence growth is already funded. If the marginal return on new warehouses matters to the decision, commission it and say so on the page; do not substitute a 22.2% average ROC.

where: Slides 2 and 3, both use F24 (4.12% 13-week T-bill) and F30 (1.88% earnings yield) as the central comparison
issue: Slides 2 and 3 make the same point — buybacks earn less than cash. That is a repeat, and it means the deck spends two of five pages on one idea while slide 3's stated second half, the growth program, gets no dedicated page.
fix: Keep the 1.88% vs 4.12% comparison on slide 3 only, and make slide 2's big numbers the sized recommendation ($13.29B dividend, cash $20.21B, FCF $9.38B, capex $6.5B for fiscal 2027). Then slide 3 is free to carry the valuation and the growth-program evidence without duplication.

where: Slide 4, "A dated sources-and-uses schedule from the latest reported cash to the trough"
issue: The schedule cannot be built from the brief. F5 ($20.21B) is as of 2026-08-30, F8 ($1.15B dividends paid) runs only to 2026-05-10, and F9 ($848.0M repurchases) covers the full fiscal year — so the opening cash is the fiscal-year-end balance and the dividend and buyback outflows for the same year are already inside it. The page as planned double-counts or leaves a four-month gap.
fix: Restate the schedule with dates and sources: opening cash $20.21B at 2026-08-30 (F5); add fiscal 2027 operating cash flow at the fiscal 2026 rate of $15.82B (F7); subtract fiscal 2027 capex of $6.5B (F40); subtract the $13.29B dividend (F41 x F1); subtract regular dividends at the $1.47 quarterly rate (F43). Show the resulting balance and state the date. If this cannot be reconciled from filings, put the trough on slide 4 as 'to be confirmed at the Q1 FY27 10-Q'.

where: Storyline, the flow from slide 5 (closing) to the answer
issue: The closing asks the board to approve the funding, the pace and the capex envelope, but the brief says the board's open decision is funding the declared dividend, the pace and capex. The closing as written asks for a re-decision on a dividend already declared on 2026-11-11 (F41).
fix: Reframe slide 5's title and content as the execution ask: 'Ratify funding the declared $13.29B special dividend from cash, set the $4B authorization's drawdown pace, and approve the $6.5B fiscal 2027 capex envelope — with the condition that the pace is revisited if the earnings yield (1.88%, F30) moves above the 4.12% cash yield (F24)'. Name the owner and the date (next board meeting).

issue: A page with three options each carrying a consequence cannot be carried by big numbers alone; the consequence of each option is the point and will be lost as a tile of figures.
fix: Make slide 2 a one-line recommendation plus a three-column options table (Do nothing / Fund from cash and pace the buyback / Fund and accelerate buyback) with the sized consequence in each cell, and keep the big-number strip only for the $13.29B, $20.21B and $9.38B headline.

where: Slide 1, cover: "Costco capital allocation: growth, buybacks, or a special dividend"
issue: The brief's cover instruction is a neutral title naming the decision with no analytic facts. The current title names three things but not the decision, and the governing thought already answers it; the cover should not pre-empt or mislead.
fix: Use 'Costco Wholesale: capital allocation decision, November 2026' as the title with the subtitle 'Prepared for the board of directors' and the date 2026-11-16. No figures on the cover.

issue: One exhibit and a block of argument on the same page risks the argument becoming voice-over text. The page has at least five candidate comparisons (earnings yield, T-bill, capex growth, ROC, 52-week range).
fix: Pick one exhibit — a two-bar comparison of 1.88% buyback earnings yield against 4.12% cash yield, with the 5.15% 10-year Treasury as a reference marker — and put the supporting figures in the title and a single footnote line, not in body text.

issue: The recommendation compares the 1.88% earnings yield to the 4.12% 13-week T-bill but never nets the lost interest on the cash spent on the buyback, and F31 says so explicitly ('before lost interest on the cash'). At $1.0B/yr, the lost T-bill interest is ~$41M against the ~$18M of EPS accretion from retiring 0.90M shares, so the buyback is EPS-dilutive, not accretive, on the deck's own numbers. The analysis as planned supports the opposite of the recommendation.
fix: On slide 2 and slide 3, restate F31 as a net EPS effect: EPS accretion from retiring 0.90M shares is ~$0.04 (= $20.76 x 443.1/442.2 - $20.76), against lost interest on $1.0B at 4.12% of ~$41M, or ~$0.09/share, for a net ~-$0.05/share. The buyback case must be argued on capital-return grounds, not accretion, or the recommendation changes to 'pause the buyback entirely until the earnings yield exceeds the cash yield.'

issue: The deck compares a 1.88% earnings yield to a 4.12% cash yield, but simultaneously carries F32 (after-tax return on capital 22.2%) and F52 (P/E 52.0x). A 52x P/E and a 22.2% ROIC are inconsistent with a 1.88% earnings yield being the right hurdle for growth capex; the marginal return on the growth program is the number the board needs and it is not in the deck. As drafted, slide 3 answers the wrong question.
fix: Replace F52 with a marginal-return figure: compute the after-tax return on incremental capital deployed, e.g., incremental operating income per incremental dollar of net PP&E using F14/F16 and the prior-year 10-K, or state the comparable. If the marginal ROIC is not available in the materials, add a research request; do not put a stale P/E from a 2025-10-26 source next to a 2026-11-13 price.

where: slide 4 (waterfall_bridge), title 'Cash trough of $9.9B clears the $6.4B minimum'
issue: The $6.4B minimum operating cash has no source in the materials; the slide shows F5 $20.21B, F7 $15.82B, F4 $6.43B, F8 $1.15B, F9 $848.0M, F41 $30/share, but nothing that establishes why $6.4B is the floor. The $9.9B trough also cannot be reproduced from the listed inputs without a period assumption: $20.21B - $13.3B - $1.15B - $0.848B - $6.5B + $15.82B is not $9.9B in any single period. A committee will ask, and there is no cell to point to.
fix: Put the trough bridge on the slide as a dated, tie-out schedule: beginning cash $20.21B at 2026-08-30, less special dividend $13.3B (= $30 x 443.1M), less regular dividends at the F43 run-rate ($1.47/qtr x 443.1M x 4), less capex $6.5B (F40), less buyback $1.0B, plus operating cash flow $15.82B (F7), equals trough. Label every period. Source the $6.4B minimum to the company's stated minimum operating cash or change the hurdle to a stated, sourced figure.

issue: F40 says '$6,500 during fiscal 2026' and the slide 2 and slide 5 titles say '$6.5B capex envelope for fiscal 2027'. Those are different periods. F40 is the fiscal 2026 intention; F39 is the fiscal 2027 plan (33 openings). Using F40 to justify a fiscal 2027 number is a period mismatch and the number must be re-sourced.
fix: On slides 2 and 5, either restate as fiscal 2026 capex of $6.5B (F40) or source a fiscal 2027 figure from F39 (33 openings) plus management guidance; do not carry F40's number across the period boundary. If a 2027 capex figure is not available, ask for it and label the slide 'fiscal 2027 capex guidance pending.'

issue: There is no sensitivity or downside anywhere in the five slides. The buyback-versus-capex trade is a one-way comparison at a single point in time. A committee will immediately ask: what if the share price falls 25% (F22 52-week low $850) and the earnings yield rises to ~2.4%, or what if the T-bill falls to 3.0%? Neither case is planned.
fix: Add to slide 3 a two-way grid of earnings yield (rows: share price $850, $1,106.21) against cash yield (columns: 3.0%, 4.12%), and mark the crossover price at which the buyback matches the T-bill. That crossover, at ~4.12%, is ~$504/share on F13 EPS of $20.76, which is the single most useful number for the board.

issue: Every multiples.vc citation is dated 2025-10-26, roughly 13 months before the 2026-11-13 price, and F51 gives a market cap of $490B and EV of $477B on a date ('As of November 16, 2026') that cannot come from a 2025-10-26 source. F34 ($309B revenue, $15B EBITDA) and F35 ($36B gross profit) are LTM figures from a 2025 page and do not tie to the 10-K $303.15B (F2). These are the stale- and mixed-source problems a committee catches first.
fix: Re-source F52 and F53 to the current price (F21 $1,106.21) and current LTM financials from the 10-K: P/E = $1,106.21 / $20.76 = 53.3x, EBITDA multiple = market cap $490.19B (F28) / EBITDA. Pull current EBITDA from the 10-K (F14 operating income $11.69B plus D&A) before quoting 32.4x. Delete F51's EV of $477B (below market cap with $3.91B of debt and $20.21B of cash is not reconcilable) or rebuild it from F5 and F10.

issue: Capex grew 14.2% a year (F19) while revenue grew 7.8% a year (F18), yet the deck keeps capex intact at $6.5B without asking whether capital intensity is rising faster than the returns. F32's 22.2% ROIC is a company-wide ratio, not the marginal return on the $6.43B of capex; the committee will treat this as the growth case's soft spot and it is not addressed.
fix: On slide 3, add a row reconciling capex growth 14.2% (F19) against revenue growth 7.8% (F18) and operating cash flow growth 12.6% (F20), and state either the incremental revenue per incremental capex dollar or that the marginal return is not disclosed and management should be asked. Do not let F32's 22.2% do the work of a marginal return.

issue: The closing title promises 'the condition that would change it,' but the evidence listed (F41, F42, F5, F26, F32, F29, F21, F4, F40, F30, F24, F52, F9) contains no trigger, no owner and no date. This is an asserted call to action, not a conditions-based recommendation.
fix: On slide 5, state three lines: owner (CFO / Treasurer), date (declare and fund at the next board meeting, November 2026), and the trigger — 'reduce or halt the $1.0B buyback if the earnings yield (F13 EPS / F21 price) falls below the 13-week T-bill yield (F24) for two consecutive quarters.' Build the rows from the evidence already on the slide.

issue: Cover is clean and properly free of analytic facts, which is right. The title 'growth, buybacks, or a special dividend' frames a three-way choice, but the governing thought already fixes the dividend as declared and payable and the real choice as funding and pacing. Minor framing inconsistency with slides 2 and 5.
fix: Retitle the cover to 'Costco capital allocation: funding the $30 special dividend, the buyback pace, and the fiscal 2027 capex envelope' so the cover, slide 2 and slide 5 name the same decision.

issue: The $13.3B is shown as a given, but the arithmetic ($30 x 443.1M shares = $13.293B) is not on the slide. With 443.1M shares at 2026-09-29 (F1) and a declaration on 2026-11-11 (F41), the share count on the record date could differ; the rounded $13.3B is doing work it has not shown.
fix: On slide 2, show the line $30 x 443.1M = $13.3B and footnote the record date once it is confirmed. If the record-date share count differs materially, the uses on slide 4 change.

issue: The cover is neutral and carries no analytic facts; the board deck opens with a title page rather than the one number that frames the decision. 'Costco Wholesale: capital allocation decision, November 2026' reads like a topic, not a claim.
fix: Make the cover title 'Board decision: fund the $13.29B special dividend and pace the $4B buyback at $848M a year' and keep only the subtitle 'Prepared for the board of directors', date 16 November 2026. No other figures on the cover.

issue: The waterfall title says '$6.9B of free cash flow' but the fact base has free cash flow of $9.38B (F26 = operating cash flow $15.82B less capex $6.43B). The slide has no reconciliation of that number.
fix: Retitle slide 4 'Cash of $20.21B covers the $13.29B dividend 1.5x and leaves $9.38B of free cash flow' and show the bridge: opening cash $20.21B, less special dividend $13.29B, plus free cash flow $9.38B, less buyback at the $848M pace, equals closing cash. Every period must be dated.

issue: The buyback pace is asserted as $848M a year without showing the arithmetic. F42 gives a $4B authorization expiring January 2030; F9 gives fiscal 2026 repurchases of $848M. The board will ask why not $1.0B.
fix: Add a small reconciliation box to slide 3 or 4: '$4B authorization ÷ 4.5 years to January 2030 = $0.89B a year; fiscal 2026 actual was $848M, so pace at $848M.' Use only these facts.

issue: The crossover price is referenced in the slide instruction but no fact computes it. The claim that a buyback is net EPS-dilutive once lost interest is counted needs the crossover share price where earnings yield equals the 4.12% cash yield.
fix: Add the computed crossover: EPS $20.76 ÷ 4.12% = $503.88, so above $503.88 the buyback earns less than cash. F30 and F24 are already in hand; do not leave the exhibit incomplete.

issue: No current cash balance after 2026-08-30 is given in the facts. The dividend is payable 4 December 2026, and the latest cash figure is $20.21B at 2026-08-30. The bridge needs a period label and a source for the opening balance date.
fix: Label the opening balance 'Cash at 30 August 2026: $20.21B' and note that the next reported cash date is the first-quarter fiscal 2027 filing. Research that filing for the actual balance before the 4 December payment.

issue: The slide text 'No unsourced minimum operating cash' is a phrase borrowed from the fact base. It reads as a note to the analyst, not a board line.
fix: Replace with the actual closing balance, e.g. 'Closing cash after dividend and buyback pace: $6.9B' — but only if the bridge arithmetic supports it; otherwise state the closing balance from the table.

issue: The executive summary asks for a three-column options table, but the governing thought is already a single recommendation. The options should show the sized consequence of each, not restate three equal choices.
fix: Use a two-column layout: Option A 'Fund $13.29B dividend from $20.21B cash, pace $4B buyback at $848M/year' vs Option B 'Fund dividend and accelerate buyback at $1.0B/year'. Add the earned-yield line: buyback earns 1.88% vs cash at 4.12%.

issue: Two consecutive exhibit slides risk looking similar. Slide 3 is a chart and slide 4 is a waterfall, but both use the same cash/buyback facts.
fix: Keep slide 3 as the yield comparison chart with the crossover marked at $503.88. Keep slide 4 as a dated sources-and-uses table with a waterfall bar only for the ending balance. Do not repeat the 1.88% and 4.12% on slide 4 except in a footnote.

issue: Dates contradict. Slide 2 title says 'Fund the declared $13.29B dividend' (already declared), but the governing thought says 'the board's open decisions are to fund it.' A declared dividend payable 4 Dec 2026 to holders of record 24 Nov 2026 is a legal obligation, not an open decision; F54/F56 fix the record and payment dates. Presenting funding as a decision the board takes on 16 Nov is wrong as a matter of corporate action and invites the exact question 'isn't it already declared?' at the table.
fix: Reframe Slide 2 as 'Funding the already-declared $13.29B dividend from the $20.21B cash balance, and setting the ongoing $4B authorization pace' and Slide 5 as 'Confirm funding sources for the 4 Dec payment and approve the buyback pace and capex envelope'; do not put 'ratify the dividend' as an ask.

issue: The buyback pace premise does not tie. The governing thought says 'pace the $4B authorization at fiscal 2026's own $848M a year rather than a round $1.0B,' but F9 ($848.0M fiscal 2026 repurchases) is past spend, not an authorization pace, and the $4B authorization runs to January 2030 (F42) — at $848M/yr that is ~4.7 years, ~$4.0B, which happens to fit, but at $1.0B/yr it is 4.0 years, also fits. Nothing in the material explains why $1.0B is wrong or why $848M is the right glide path; it is a hard-coded plug dressed as policy.
fix: Either (a) state the binding constraint explicitly — e.g., authorization term to Jan 2030 (F42) implies no more than ~$4B/3.2 years ≈ $1.25B/yr to consume it, so $848M/yr would leave capacity unused — or (b) drop the '$848M vs $1.0B' framing and replace it with 'fund the authorization at a pace the board sets; the earnings-yield test below applies to any pace.' Do not present $848M as 'the pace' without the arithmetic.

issue: $13.29B is asserted in the title and strip but the source facts give two different figures: F55 says '$13.3 billion' (approximately) and F56 says 'about $13.3 billion'; the deck's $13.29B is a recomputation (443.1M x $30.00) that is not shown and is presented to two decimals when the underlying inputs are one-decimal and 'approximately.' A committee member will ask 'where does 13.29 come from and why is it not 13.3?'
fix: Show the arithmetic on the slide: '$30.00 x 443.1M shares (F1) = $13.29B; company release states approximately $13.3B (F55/F56).' If the strip must be one figure, use $13.3B to match the source and footnote the 443.1M x $30.00 calc.

issue: 'Cash of $20.21B covers the $13.29B dividend 1.5x and leaves $6.9B of free cash flow' mixes a stock figure ($20.21B at 2026-08-30) with a flow ($9.38B free cash flow, F26) and a pro forma residual ($6.9B) without a period label or a bridge. $20.21B − $13.29B = $6.92B is a balance-sheet residual, not 'free cash flow'; F26 free cash flow is $9.38B. Two different $6.9B/$9.38B numbers in one title line is the kind of tie-out a client catches in the room.
fix: Retitle: 'Post-dividend cash of $6.9B ($20.21B at 30 Aug 2026 less the $13.29B payment) covers ~1.1x fiscal 2026 capex of $6.43B; fiscal 2026 free cash flow was $9.38B.' Move the definition of the $6.9B into the chart, not the title.

issue: The schedule is titled a 'dated sources-and-uses' from 'the latest reported cash' ($20.21B at 2026-08-30) to 'a stated closing balance,' but nothing bridges 2026-08-30 to the 2026-11-24 record date / 2026-12-04 payment date. Q1 FY2027 operating cash flow, capex-to-date, the regular $1.47 quarterly dividend (F43/F12; F8 shows $1.15B paid in the first 36 weeks), and the Nov buyback (F9 $848M is FY2026) are all omitted. The 'stated closing balance' cannot be stated without them.
fix: Rebuild as a dated bridge: Cash 30 Aug 2026 $20.21B (F5) + Q1 FY2027 operating cash flow (research) − capex to date − regular dividend paid − special dividend $13.29B = closing cash at 4 Dec 2026. Label each period and source each flow; if Q1 FY2027 flows are not yet filed, say so and mark the closing balance 'pro forma, pending Q1 FY2027 10-Q.'

issue: The title 'Buybacks earn 1.88% at today's price, below the 4.12% cash yield' and F30 are both labelled 'before lost interest on the cash,' but the governing thought says the buyback is 'net EPS-dilutive once the lost interest is counted.' The slide therefore shows the case for the buyback (1.88%) and buries the number that decides it. F31's $20.80 'after a $1B buyback' explicitly excludes lost interest, so the exhibit's 'crossover price' is undefined — crossover to what, at what after-tax cash rate?
fix: Put the net calculation in the exhibit: $1B cash at 4.12% (F24) = $41.2M pre-tax, at the 24.7% effective tax rate (F32 inputs) ≈ $31.0M after tax, versus the $1B buyback adding ~$20.8M to net income (F31 basis) — net EPS impact negative by roughly $10M; state the crossover price as EPS/(after-tax cash yield) and label it. Move the 'before lost interest' caveat into a footnote, not the headline.

issue: Several load-bearing facts rest on weak or stale sources. F39 (33 warehouse openings in fiscal 2027) is from supplychain360.io, undated in the brief; F34–F38, F46–F53 (EV $477B, P/E 52.0x, EBITDA 32.4x, LTM EBITDA $15B, competitors) all come from multiples.vc dated 2025-10-26 — 13 months before the briefing date and inconsistent with the 10-K figures now in hand (multiples.vc LTM revenue $309B / net income $9.4B vs. 10-K $303.15B / $9.23B for FY2026, F2/F3). Slide 4's capex envelope uses F40, which is a forward intention, not a reported figure.
fix: Re-source every multiples.vc figure to the FY2026 10-K (filed 2026-10-07) or a vendor with an as-of date within the past 30 days; if kept, footnote 'multiples.vc as of 2025-10-26 — superseded by FY2026 10-K' and do not put the stale figure in a title. Source F39 and F40 to the FY2026 10-K MD&A or the fiscal 2027 guidance release, not the two secondary sites.

issue: No risk or sensitivity slide, and no slide that tests the recommendation. The deck asserts the answer (keep capex at fiscal 2026's $6.5B rate, fund the dividend from cash, pace the buyback) but never asks 'what if' — what if the special dividend plus capex plus buyback draws cash below a prudent minimum? What if the 4.12% T-bill yield compresses? What if warehouse capex overruns the $6.5B intention? The brief's own instruction ('keep capex at the fiscal 2026 rate of about $6.5B') is stated without a sensitivity.
fix: Replace Slide 3 (or compress it) with a 'what changes the answer' slide: sensitivity of net buyback EPS impact to cash yield (2.0%/4.12%/5.15%, F24/F25), sensitivity of post-dividend cash to FY2027 capex ($5.5B/$6.5B/$7.5B, F40 anchor), and the condition that would flip the recommendation (e.g., share price below crossover, or cash below a stated minimum — which the brief explicitly says not to invent, so state the board's policy or mark it to be set).

issue: 'F41: Costco Wholesale (NasdaqGS:COST) declared a special cash dividend of $30 per share' and 'F42: reauthorized a $4b share repurchase' are listed as must-show content, but the cover instruction says 'No analytic facts, no figures on the cover.' The $30 and $4b are figures.
fix: Keep the cover neutral per its own instruction; move F41 and F42 to Slide 2, where they belong as the fact pattern for the decision.

issue: The three options are never named. The governing thought implies (1) cash-funded dividend as declared, (2) pace buyback at $848M, (3) keep capex at ~$6.5B, but the table columns and the 'sized consequence of each' are not specified, and the strip is limited to $13.29B/$20.21B/$9.38B — none of which is the consequence of options (2) or (3).
fix: Label the three options explicitly (e.g., 'Fund special dividend from cash / Buyback pace / Capex envelope') and put a sized number in each column: option 1 $13.29B outflow, option 2 $848M FY2027 vs. up to $1.25B/yr capacity to Jan 2030, option 3 $6.5B FY2027 capex intention (F40). Only then is the strip consistent with the table.

issue: F22 states the 52-week range as '$850.00 to $1,106.21 to 2026-11-13,' where $1,106.21 is also the current price (F21). A 52-week high equal to the current close is possible but should be labelled, and the exhibit uses the range to anchor the 'crossover price' without stating where in the range the crossover sits. If the crossover is above $1,106.21, the exhibit shows the answer; if below, the buyback math needs re-examination.
fix: On the exhibit, mark the crossover price explicitly and show whether it is above or below the $1,106.21 close and the $850.00 low; label the range '52-week closing range, to 13 Nov 2026.'

issue: The 'Decision today' box carries two conditions and a hedge that push the real answer to slide 4. It reads: 'subject to the three-year operating cash flow growth test on page 4; if consensus growth (-12% to $14.0B) holds, redeploy the $1B to the dividend or hold.' The reader has to hold an unresolved conditional through three pages.
fix: Resolve it on slide 2. State the decision as one line: 'Approve the $1B pace now; the pace is funded to a $12.99B trough and the $4B ceiling is not drawn past break-even.' Cut the branch sentence; if the growth test is the real risk, name it once and put the test on the same page.

issue: The page's own evidence contradicts the recommendation and it is buried on the right column. 'The 1.88% earnings yield is an EPS-accretion test only' and 'Consensus has operating cash flow falling about 12% to around $14.0B' with '-10.12%' return. The exhibit then concludes the buyback 'fails its own test.' The recommendation on slides 2 and 5 does not respond to that.
fix: Either change the ask to match the evidence (e.g., 'Approve the dividend; defer the buyback until FY27 cash flow is confirmed') or move the growth sensitivity onto slide 2 and show what growth assumption the $1B pace requires. Do not let slide 4 conclude against slides 2 and 5.

issue: The title says 'Buyback draws pause at the $12B floor' but the chart shows buybacks of only $0.85B and the trough at $12.99B, $0.99B above the floor. The title describes an event that does not happen on the page.
fix: Retitle to the number the chart proves: 'The $1B pace holds the FY26 trough at $12.99B, $0.99B above the $12B floor.' Delete 'pause' unless the model shows the draw stopping; if it does not, the word is wrong.

issue: The base case (14.5%) uses a '12.6% three-year operating cash flow growth' input that appears nowhere on slides 2 or 3, while the consensus case uses -12%. Two incompatible growth assumptions sit in one deck with no bridge.
fix: Add a one-line bridge on slide 4: what 12.6% is (management plan? historical?) and why it differs from the -12% consensus. If the base case is not sourced, remove the 14.5% headline and lead with the consensus case.

issue: The bottom half of the page is empty; the table ends at item 5 and leaves roughly 40% dead space. It reads as a page thrown together at the end.
fix: Pull the decision box from slide 2 onto slide 5 as the sign-off, or add the cash-trough review dates as a small timeline along the bottom third. Fill it or shorten it.

issue: The '2' footnote marker follows 'run-rate $2.48B' mid-sentence and the source line below wraps to four lines, two of which are near-duplicate citations ('Costco (COST) Declares $30 Special Dividend' vs the Reauthorizes line).
fix: Move all footnote markers to the end of the sentence. Merge the duplicate Costco press releases into one source. Keep the source block to two lines.

issue: The right column is a wall of hedged prose: 'is an inference from the existing capital base, not a measured incremental return' and 'the same measurement as the perpetuity bars.' It needs a voice-over.
fix: Replace with two bullet claims: 'The 22.2% ROIC is existing-base, not incremental; the shadow price is 2.9%.' and 'At consensus growth the return is -10.12%: the pace fails its own test.' Cut the rest.

issue: The four return figures use four different type sizes (14.5%, 9.88%, 6.88% large; -10.12% larger) and the right column starts at a different baseline from the left, breaking the grid.
fix: Set all four figures at one size, right-align the decimal points, and top-align the right column to the first row of the left.

issue: Decision block on slide 2: 'approve a $1B-a-year buyback pace under the $4B authorization' — the $4B is a share repurchase authorization ceiling, not a 1-year capacity commitment, and the buyback is proposed as subject to a growth hurdle. The recommendation conflates a ceiling with an annual pace and asks the board to approve a mechanism that may not draw (slide 4: 'Buyback pace is justified only if three-year operating cash flow growth resumes above 4.52%').
fix: Split the ask: 'Approve a $1B-a-year repurchase pace within the $4B authorization, first tranche in Q1 2027, suspended if three-year operating cash flow growth falls below 4.52% as tested on slide 4.' Show the hurdle in the recommendation and the table owner/timing as 'Treasurer, after break-even schedule'.

issue: Slide 3 calls the $12B an 'operating floor' and a 'proposed liquidity policy', yet footnote 1 says it is management's proposed liquidity policy at about 4% of FY26 revenue ($303.15B), with no company-stated minimum and no peer benchmark. The $12.99B 'cash trough' therefore cannot be tested against a peer or company standard, and the cushion ($0.99B / $0.01B) is an artefact of an unsourced assumption.
fix: Show the $12B as 4% of FY26 revenue with a sensitivity grid of trough vs. floor at $8B, $12B, $16B, and add a peer benchmark table of liquidity policy (cash + revolver availability) or state explicitly that no peer benchmark exists and the board is being asked to set one. If no peer data exists, request it.

issue: The 14.5% base case is '1.88% earnings yield + 12.6% operating cash flow growth'. The 12.6% growth is the base case; the 1.88% yield ($1,106.21 price / ~$20.75 EPS) is not sourced to a date, and the 22.2% after-tax return on capital is used as a growth-versus-cash-line inference, not a measured return. Two of the three legs are unsourced or inferred, and the 6.4% cost of equity is '1.88% + 4.52%' where 4.52% is a 'year-one level' consensus, not a perpetuity. No model backup, no sensitivity on the growth rate.
fix: State the EPS and price date explicitly with a source line, label the 22.2% as 'inferred, not measured', and add a sensitivity table of implied return vs. growth from 4.52% to 12.6% and vs. exit multiple. Recompute the cost of equity only if the 4.52% can be shown as a sustainable growth rate; otherwise keep it as a hurdle and mark it as one.

issue: The two headlines are contradictory: 'The 14.5% base-case buyback return clears the 6.4% cost of equity…' vs '…but consensus growth takes the implied return negative' (-10.12%). The deck gives no probability weighting, no downside case beyond the consensus read, and no decision rule under which the board should still pay the dividend and draw the buyback. The 4.52% threshold is stated but no scenario shows FY27/FY28 cash flow at 4.52%.
fix: Add one bridge table tying 4.52%, 8%, 12.6% growth to implied return and to share count/dividend per share under each, and state the decision rule: 'Pay the dividend; draw the first $1B tranche only after the Q1 2027 trough review confirms three-year growth >= 4.52%; otherwise redeem the $1B to the dividend.'

issue: Cash flow line items: 'Operating cash flow +15.82', 'Capex -6.43', 'Regular dividend -2.46' (= $1.158B nine-month run-rate × 2? footnote 2), 'Buybacks -0.85', 'Special dividend -13.30'. FY26 capex $6.43B is from the 10-K; the buyback -0.85 is not sourced or dated; and the regular dividend run-rate annualization is a hard assumption not shown. The bridge totals to $12.99B but I cannot tie any line to a model.
fix: Add a column of sources and periods next to each line (10-K FY26, Q1-Q3 10-Q, 10-Q dividend paid, treasury buyback settlement). Either replace the -0.85 with the actual share repurchase number from the cash flow statement or remove it and put the line in a footnote with the exact period and amount.

issue: Trough cushion arithmetic: 'Post-dividend cash is $12.99B, then $11.99B after the Year-1 buyback draw' and 'Cushion over the proposed $12B floor is -$5.09B, then -$6.09B'. The $12.99B trough already appears on slide 3 net of $13.30B special dividend and $0.85B buyback, so the $11.99B 'after Year-1 buyback draw' duplicates a draw already inside the trough. A committee will catch this.
fix: State the trough once, with its components, and make slide 2's cushion lines consistent with slide 3: post-dividend trough $12.99B, cushion $0.99B; after the first $1B buyback tranche $11.99B, cushion -$0.01B. Delete or relabel the '-$5.09B/-$6.09B' numbers, which appear to add the $12B floor to the trough rather than subtract it.

issue: Footnote 1 cites '22.2% FY26 after-tax return on capital ($31,698 B × (1 - 24.7%)) / ($35,808 B + $3,918 B)'. Units are inconsistent: '$31,698 B' and '$35,808 B + $3,918 B' as written do not produce 22.2%, and the parentheses imply a different calculation than the formula shown. Footnote 3 ends '...the drawn pace is a use of cash.' on slide 2 but slide 2's sources include 'stockanalysis.com' (a retail aggregator) for the $30 special dividend.
fix: Rewrite footnote 1 as its own line-item table: operating income, tax rate, invested capital components (debt + equity) with sources and dates, so the 22.2% ties. Replace 'stockanalysis.com' with the company's 8-K/SEC filing for the $30 special dividend, and clean up footnote 3's truncated sentence.

issue: '$12.99B trough, $0.99B above the proposed $12B floor... the company pauses the buyback draw at the floor'. The trough and the floor are in the same units, but slide 3 shows the trough at $12.99B on the waterfall and slide 2 shows the post-dividend cash at $12.99B, then $11.99B after a draw. If the waterfall already nets the $0.85B buyback, the draw is not additive and the pause is not a pause. The mechanism is stated twice with different bases ($0.99B and $0.01B), and the rating of the floor is unknown.
fix: Define the floor as a board-set policy (e.g., 4% of revenue), show the trough as the minimum cash balance over the three-year plan, and state the draw mechanism in one place: 'Draws reduce cash below the floor; the floor test is applied at each quarter end; the first year's $1B tranche is within the authorization.'

issue: Waterfall bars: no zero baseline labelled, no unit label on the axis ('$B' only in the subtitle), and the bar labels are shown as signed values (+15.82, -6.43). Capex is shown as negative in the waterfall but the cliff ($20.21 to +15.82, then to +9.39) is shown as a single cumulative path with no connector or axis.
fix: Add a labelled zero baseline and axis units ($B), show the running total line/connectors, and label the bridge as 'cash, not P&L, FY26 pro forma'.

issue: Cover says 'Board briefing, November 2026' and footer repeats 'Board meeting, November 2026'; slide 2 references '2026-08-30' and payment '4 December 2026'. The fiscal year vs. calendar year labels are mixed and the cover does not state the basis (FY26).
fix: State the basis once on the cover: 'Board briefing — FY26 (ended 2026-08-30), November 2026.' Use the same date convention throughout (ISO on back-up pages, month-name on text pages).

issue: Footnote 2: 'The $4B authorization is a ceiling, not a cash outflow on one date; only the drawn pace is a use of cash.' Good sentence, but it is buried in footnote 2 and contradicted by the decision block's 'approve a $1B-a-year buyback pace' with no draw schedule.
fix: Move the ceiling-vs-draw distinction into a visible line in the decision block and attach the indicative draw schedule ($1B/year for years 1-4) to it.

issue: The title stops at an ellipsis ('14.5% against a 6.4% cost of equity…') and the page splits into a 'but' with two numbers contradicting each other. The decision turns on this page and the reader has to assemble the conclusion themselves.
fix: Rewrite the title as the synthesis: 'The buyback clears 14.5% at 12.6% growth but fails at consensus -12%, so the pace pauses below 4.52% growth.' Lead with the decision-relevant number, not the upside case.

issue: The left column is almost entirely dead white space: a 14.5% and a -10.12% floating in the middle of an empty panel. It reads as an unfinished exhibit next to the dense right column.
fix: Replace the left column's floating numbers with a single small chart — implied return on the y-axis against growth rate on the x-axis, with a horizontal line at the 6.4% cost of equity and markers at 12.6% and -12%. The chart then carries the argument and fills the space.

issue: The owners are titles ('CFO', 'Treasurer', 'COO', 'Investor relations') and one timing is circular: 'Treasurer, after break-even schedule'. No named accountability, no fixed date for the first tranche.
fix: Name the individual for each action and put a hard calendar date on row 2: e.g. 'Treasurer — [name], tranche 1 executes [date], Q1 2027'.

issue: 'At consensus growth (-12% to $14.0B operating cash flow) the implied return is -10.12%.' The page tells the board the return is negative under consensus but the recommendation does not address what happens to holders if consensus is right.
fix: Add one line to point 3 stating the trigger condition explicitly: 'Pace pauses below 4.52% growth', already on slide 4, so the downside case is contained in the summary the board reads first.

issue: Both titles wrap to two lines and one word ('trough' on 2, 'floor' on 3) sits alone on the second line.
fix: Cut title length: slide 2 to 'Approve the $1B-a-year buyback pace' with the trough stated in the subhead; slide 3 to 'The $1B pace holds the FY26 trough at $12.99B, $0.99B above floor'.

issue: 'The growth-versus-cash line is an inference from the existing capital base, not a measured incremental return' is a hedge that weakens the exhibit — it tells the board not to fully trust the number on the page.
fix: State the basis plainly: 'Return measured against the existing $35.7B capital base.' If the basis is defensible, say so; if not, remove the number.

issue: The bottom-left footline says 'Board meeting, November 2026' while the cover line above it already says 'Board briefing, FY26 (ended 2026-08-30), November 2026'. Duplicated date.
fix: Delete the date from the cover line, keep the footline, or vice versa. One date per appearance.

issue: The callout box repeats the title and then three bullets that restate numbers already in the waterfall. It looks busy without adding evidence.
fix: Keep the box but make it only the takeaway: one sentence on the cushion and one on what would break it. Cut the bullets that duplicate the chart.

where: slide 2, row 4: 'free cash flow is $9.38B'; slide 3 bridge: 'Regular dividend -2.46' and 'Buybacks -0.85'
issue: The free cash flow figure does not reconcile. Slide 3's bridge has operating cash flow 15.82, capex -6.43, regular dividend -2.46, buybacks -0.85, special dividend -13.30; 15.82 - 6.43 = 9.39 of FCF, and after 2.46 + 0.85 = 3.31 of ordinary capital returns the trough is 20.21 + 9.39 - 2.46 - 0.85 - 13.30 = 12.99, which ties, but 9.39 is not 9.38 and the label 'free cash flow' is used on slide 2 as if it were the same 9.38 number. A client will add this in the room.
fix: Set free cash flow = operating cash flow less capex = 15.82 - 6.43 = 9.39 on slide 2 (and footnote 1) and confirm every downstream reference uses 9.39; if 9.38 is the model number, show the model cell and the 0.01 of rounding explicitly.

where: slide 4, left column: 'Base case: 12.6% growth' and right column: 'The consensus growth rate the implied return is -10.12%'
issue: The base case of 12.6% three-year operating cash flow growth is not sourced to anything on the page. The only external figure cited is the consensus operating cash flow of about $14.0B, which implies a decline (the right column says -12%). We cannot put a 12.6% growth case in the book without a named source — company guidance, a broker consensus, or our own model with the assumptions listed.
fix: Either replace 12.6% with a sourced base case (state the source and the growth rate it implies for FY26-FY29) or move 12.6% to a clearly labelled 'management plan / illustrative' case and add a third scenario row at the consensus growth rate; the break-even and pause test should be shown against the same scenarios on slide 5.

where: slide 3, footnote 1 and slide 2, row 2: '$12B floor' / '$12.99B trough, a $0.99B cushion over the proposed $12B floor'
issue: The $12B floor is described as 'management's proposed liquidity policy at about 4% of FY26 revenue' with 'no company-stated minimum and no peer benchmark available'. The entire recommendation is anchored on a number we invented; the 0.99 cushion is 0.99 of our own assumption, not a covenant or a disclosed minimum.
fix: Source or drop the $12B. If it is management's proposed policy, say who proposed it, on what date, and why 4% of revenue is the right level; otherwise replace the cushion statement on slides 2, 3 and 5 with a sensitivity showing the trough under a range of floors (e.g. $10B / $12B / $14B) and at what floor the $1B pace breaks.

where: slide 4, body: 'The 1.88% earnings yield is an EPS-accretion test only' and '14.5% = 1.88% earnings yield + 12.6% three-year operating cash flow growth'
issue: Adding a 12.6% operating cash flow growth rate to a trailing earnings yield is not a return on the buyback — it is a return on the whole equity, and it is presented as if the buyback generated the 12.6%. The page then calls the 22.2% after-tax return 'the return on the existing capital base' and admits it is 'an inference ... not a measured incremental return'. Either be precise about what each number is, or replace the 14.5% with an incremental return the buyback actually produces.
fix: Rename 14.5% to 'equity return at base-case growth' and show a separate buyback-specific return (e.g. EPS accretion at the $1B pace, or IRR on repurchased shares at the $1,106.21 price under each growth case); keep the -10.12% consensus case as the downside test.

where: slide 4, footnote 1: 'The 6.4% CAPM uses the Yahoo Finance 2-year weekly beta of 0.24; the committee case is beta 0.8-1.0'
issue: A 6.4% cost of equity built on a 0.24 weekly beta is not a number I would defend. At a beta of 0.8-1.0 — the range your own footnote says the committee uses — the cost of equity is meaningfully higher and the 14.5% versus 6.4% spread narrows sharply; the 4.52% pause test moves with it.
fix: Rebuild the cost of equity at a beta range (0.24 / 0.8 / 1.0) with the risk-free rate and ERP shown, present the implied returns at each, and re-derive the pause test; do not anchor the recommendation on the lowest credible beta.

where: slides 2-5 source lines: 'Costco (COST) Declares $30 Special Dividend And Reauthorizes $4 Billion Buyback, finance.yahoo.com, 2026-11-11' and 'Yahoo Finance daily close 2026-11-13'
issue: The buyback authorization, the special dividend amount ($30/share, about $13.3B) and the current share price ($1,106.21 on slide 4) all rest on Yahoo Finance secondary summaries. A board briefing cites the company's 8-K/press release and a dated exchange close, not a Yahoo aggregation.
fix: Replace with the Costco press release or 8-K (date, accession) for the $30/share dividend and $4B authorization, and the primary exchange close for $1,106.21; keep the Yahoo citation only as a secondary cross-check in a footnote.

where: slide 2, decision box: 'approve a $1B-a-year repurchase pace within the $4B authorization ... suspended if three-year operating cash flow growth falls below 4.52%'
issue: The pause trigger depends on three-year forward operating cash flow growth, which is unobservable and defined as a level on slide 4 but as a growth rate on slide 5; it is not an observable covenant a treasurer can act on. The recommendation 'approve now' also ignores the right-hand column of slide 4, where at consensus the buyback returns -10.12% and 'fails its own test'.
fix: Rewrite the trigger to an observable test (e.g. trailing four-quarter operating cash flow, or cash trough below the floor at the Q1 2027 review) and add a sentence to the decision box stating what happens if the consensus case in the right column of slide 4 proves correct.

issue: The bridge shows a -0.85 buyback outflow for FY26, but slide 2 says 'first tranche ... Q1 2027' and slide 5 says 'Q1 2027, after the break-even schedule'. If no buyback occurs in FY26 the bridge cannot contain a FY26 buyback outflow; if it is the first tranche, say so.
fix: Relabel the bridge bar as 'Buyback, first tranche (Q1 2027)' or remove it, and state in the slide 3 footnote whether the trough is measured before or after the first tranche — it currently is measured after.

where: Slide 4 (whole page and its right-hand callout)
issue: The title claims 'At 12.6% growth the buyback returns 14.5%, against a 6.4% cost of equity', while the same page presents a consensus case of 14.5% versus 14.5%. The page does not resolve which case it is recommending; the reader is left to guess.
fix: Make it explicit in the title and right-hand box: 'Base-case 12.6% growth returns 14.5%, 2.3x the 6.4% cost of equity; consensus growth returns -10.12% and fails the test.' Put the 14.5% and -10.12% figures side by side in a single comparative table or bar pair, not one huge isolated number.

issue: Slide 3's trough of $12.99B assumes $14.0B operating cash flow, while Slide 4's callout says consensus cash flow of about $14.0B pushes the trough down by about $1.8B. The deck never reconciles these two cases; the board cannot tell which trough it is approving against.
fix: Add a one-line reconciliation on slide 3: 'At consensus cash flow the trough is $12.99B - $1.8B = $11.19B, which breaches the $12B floor by $0.81B.' Then state on slide 4 whether the $14B consensus case changes the recommended $1B pace or only the evidence.

issue: The card stacks $1B, $4B and $12.99B with captions but no visual relationship; the $4B authorization and the $12.99B trough are different measurements sitting in the same box.
fix: Either convert the card into a small bar showing the $4B authorization vs the $1B annual pace vs the $12.99B trough on a common axis, or cut it to two figures and move the trough number into the point-2 row where it is the actual proof.

issue: 14.5% and -10.12% are set as two oversized numbers with no bars, axes or comparison; the key contrast is unsupported visually.
fix: Replace the two isolated figures with a paired bar chart of implied return by growth case, with a horizontal line at the 6.4% cost of equity, so the reader sees the case that clears the hurdle and the case that does not.

issue: The point says the buyback clears the cost of equity 'only at base-case growth' but gives no consequence if growth is at consensus; the reader reaches the failure case only on slide 4.
fix: Add to point 3: 'at consensus growth the implied return is -10.12%, below the 6.4% cost of equity,' so the executive summary carries the failure case, not just the base case.

issue: The next steps list no decision on the binding issue: what the board does if the quarterly trough review shows consensus cash flow and the $12B floor is breached.
fix: Add a sixth row: 'If the quarterly trough review shows cash flow at or below consensus, pause the buyback tranches and bring an updated pace to the board.'

issue: The cover carries the substantive claim 'confirm the $13.3B dividend and set the buyback pace' as a title, then a large empty field below the subtitle before the footer.
fix: Tighten the cover: keep the title and subtitle, reduce the empty space, and add a one-line 'Decision requested' band at the bottom above the footer naming the two decisions.

issue: 'The $1B pace holds the FY26 trough at $12.99B, $0.99B above the $12B floor' is correct but the word 'holds' is soft for a board page; the number $0.99B reads as precision beyond the model.
fix: Retitle: 'The $1B pace leaves the FY26 trough at $12.99B, $0.99B above the $12B floor,' keeping the same figures.

issue: 'Stand up the quarterly trough review' uses an internal-consulting term; the board page should say what happens.
fix: Change to 'Review the cash trough quarterly at the board meeting' and move 'First review at the Q1 2027 board' into the timing column.

where: slide 2, item 2 and slide 3 exhibit; also slide 2 footnote 1
issue: The $12.99B trough does not foot. The waterfall bars are +15.82 −6.43 −2.46 −0.85 −13.30 = −7.22; applied to the 20.21 opening shows cash falls to $12.99B — but the reconciliation against the $9.39B free cash flow quote does not foot: 15.82 − 6.43 = 9.39, and 9.39 − 2.46 − 0.85 − 13.30 = −7.22, which is the same number restated, not an independent check. There is no line tying the 20.21 opening balance to a 10-K balance-sheet figure.
fix: Add a reconciliation strip under the waterfall: opening cash and equivalents $20.21B (cite the 10-K balance sheet), +$15.82B operating cash flow, −$6.43B capex, −$2.46B regular dividend, −$0.85B first tranche, −$13.30B special dividend = $12.99B; and footnote ties the $9.39B FCF to the $9.388B in the 4 October article. If the opening cash is not $20.21B per the 10-K, correct the bar.

where: slide 4, "Base case: 12.6% growth" and slide 2 item 3
issue: The 12.6% three-year operating cash flow growth is the load-bearing assumption — it drives the 14.5% return — and the deck itself says it is "the historical three-year operating cash flow CAGR (10-K FY23 to FY26), not company guidance." No forward source is provided. A 12.6% extrapolation of history is an assumption, not an estimate, and the committee will ask for the operating cash flow forecast behind it.
fix: Either attach the FY27–FY29 operating cash flow forecast and cite it by page, or relabel the base case explicitly as "Historical FY23–FY26 CAGR, not a forward estimate" on both slide 2 and slide 4 and present the consensus case as the primary scenario. Do not call 12.6% "the base case" without a forward source.

issue: The downside is stated (consensus −12% growth → −10.12% return) but not reconciled to slide 3: the slide 3 note says the consensus decline lowers the trough "by about $1.8B," which would put the trough at roughly $11.2B — below the $12B floor — and the buyback clearly breaks the floor in that case. The $1.8B bath is asserted without arithmetic.
fix: Show the −12% consensus cash flow case through the same waterfall on slide 3 (opening cash, consensus operating cash flow, capex, regular dividend, special dividend, buyback), state the resulting trough versus the $12B floor, and say plainly at what growth rate the floor is breached. If the −$1.8B figure is an estimate, footnote it as such and show how it was derived.

issue: The valuation logic compares a buyback "implied return" of 14.5% to a 6.4% cost of equity, but 14.5% = 1.88% earnings yield + 12.6% growth, which is a forward equity return estimate, not the return on the buyback itself. Comparing it to cost of equity silently equates buying back stock with investing in the business; the true buyback hurdle is the risk-adjusted return on the alternative use of the $1B, and no WACC, IRR or per-share accretion is shown.
fix: Add a per-share accretion/dilution calculation for the $1B tranche: net income and shares outstanding before and after, EPS impact, and the implied IRR at the base and consensus cases. State the hurdle rate the buyback is being judged against (6.4% cost of equity vs. the return on retained capital) and keep one definition of the return.

where: slide 3, "Regular dividend" bar and footnote 2; slide 2 item 1
issue: Dividend units are muddled: the slide 3 bar is $2.46B and footnote 2 reads "$2.468 = $5.54 declared per share × 443.1M shares (10-K FY26); the nine-month 10-Q figure of $1.158B is not annualised." The $2.46B and the $2.468B are stated to different precision with no tie, and it is not clear whether $5.54/share is an annual rate or a declared total.
fix: State the annual regular dividend as one number, $2.47B ($5.54/share × 443.1M shares, 10-K FY26), footnote the per-share figure as annual rate, and delete the nine-month 10-Q reference or move it to a note. Make the slide 3 bar, slide 2 footnote and the model agree to the same $2.47B.

issue: The page set never answers the question in the exhibit title: there is no football field, no comps, no precedent transactions and no DCF. The only valuation is a 14.5% implied return on slide 4. For a $4B authorization board paper, the committee will expect at least a returns-based hurdle plus a per-share value bridge.
fix: Add one back-up page with the returns comparison: buyback implied return vs. cost of equity vs. alternative uses of capital (capex, store growth, dividend) at the base and consensus cases, with the assumptions sourced. If a full football field is not appropriate for a capital allocation paper, say so in a note on slide 2.

issue: "At 12.6% growth the buyback returns 14.5%, against a 6.4% cost of equity" is stated as fact in the title, but slide 4's own note and body say 12.6% is historical, not guidance, and the consensus case is −10.12%. The headline asserts the conclusion of the assumption it should be testing.
fix: Retitle slide 4 to carry the conditional: "At the historical 12.6% three-year cash flow CAGR the pace returns 14.5%; at consensus −12% growth it returns −10.12% and breaches the $12B floor."

issue: "Capex is held at $6.43B" is asserted as a flat hold, but the footnote says the FY27 plan is "not company-stated" and the $6.43B is "the anchor until the treasurer confirms the plan at the Q1 2027 board." That is a treasury assumption on a board paper without an owner for the risk if capex overruns.
fix: Label the $6.43B capex as an assumption on the slide itself, and add the sensitivity: what the trough becomes at $7.0B and $7.5B capex. Slide 5 assigns no owner to the capex risk — add the COO as owner of the $6.43B commitment.

issue: Footnote 1 says the $9.39B free cash flow is "the same measure rounded down by $0.01B" from the $9.388B quoted in the 4 October article, but $9.388B rounds to $9.39B, not down from it; the parenthetical is wrong and a committee member doing the arithmetic will catch it.
fix: Delete "rounded down by $0.01B" and write "$9.39B, from $9.388B in [article, date]".

issue: The dividend is described as "declared" ("$30/share special dividend declared, payable 4 December 2026, about $13.3B in total"), which is a paid event, while slide 5 item 1 lists "File and pay the special dividend — declaration filed 11 November 2026." A declared dividend does not need a board vote to declare; the two pages imply different actions.
fix: State on slide 2 that the special dividend is declared and payment is the only step, or if a board resolution is still required, change slide 2 to "proposed" and slide 5 to "approve and file." Pick one and make slides 2 and 5 match.

issue: The 12.6% base-case bar occupies most of the graphic space and the −10.12% consensus bar equals it visually in height direction but the two are not on a consistent axis — the base case is a bar and the consensus figure is a text block, so the comparison the page exists to make cannot be read off the chart.
fix: Draw both cases as bars on one axis with a zero baseline, labelled "Base case (historical 12.6% CAGR)" and "Consensus (−12%)", with the 6.4% cost of equity as a reference line. Move the explanatory copy below the chart.

issue: The cover asks 'return cash or fund growth?' and the executive summary answers 'both' without acknowledging the trade-off. A board cannot approve a recommendation that says 'do two opposite things' without a capital structure framework.
fix: Retitle slide 2: 'Return $17.3B of the $20.21B cash pile, hold capex at $6.43B, and set an operating cash floor of $12B' — the floor number must come from research, not invented. Then make slide 3 the fundability test: does $20.21B + $9.38B FCF - $13.3B dividend - $6.43B capex - $1.15B regular dividend leave enough operating cash?

issue: The visual is a metrics panel ($13.3B, $4B, 14.5%) with no decision. The brief asked for 'a clear, sized recommendation (state the amounts and what each option implies)'. The options — $13.3B dividend + $4B buyback vs. $13.3B dividend + $0 buyback vs. $0/$0 and full growth capex — are never laid out side by side. Without the options, the board cannot see what each implies.
fix: Replace the metrics panel with a three-column options table: Option A (dividend + buyback) / Option B (dividend only) / Option C (hold cash, fund growth). Rows: cash returned, remaining cash, implied return on buyback, capex held at $6.43B, impact on 30 net new warehouses per year. Keep $13.3B, $4B, 14.5% as bolded numbers inside the table.

issue: The waterfall is a sources-and-uses bridge but omits the regular dividend ($1.15B) from the uses side and shows no minimum operating cash floor. The trough is undefined. A board asks 'what is the lowest cash balance?' and this slide cannot answer it.
fix: Add the regular dividend to the waterfall uses. Then draw a dashed line for the minimum operating cash floor and label it with the researched number. Retitle: 'Cash trough of $X.XB after the special dividend and capex, above the $X.XB operating floor' — replace X.X with the researched figures.

issue: Title claims 'buy back while the price is below $1,106' but the analysis uses the current price of $1,106.21 as the reference. The title and the content contradict each other — you are at the ceiling, not below it. The 'price at which the buyback stops clearing' is named as a required element in 'must show' but no number is provided.
fix: Retitle slide 4: 'At $1,106, the buyback earns 14.5% against a 6.4% cost of equity — a 2.2x spread that closes if growth falls below 4.6% or the price exceeds $Y'. Add the break-even price calculation to the exhibit. If the break-even price cannot be computed from in-hand facts, flag it as a research request.

issue: The deck repeatedly references a 'minimum operating cash floor' (slide 3 'stated minimum operating cash', slide 5 'set a minimum operating cash floor') but no number exists in the facts. Costco's operating cash needs are not stated anywhere in the material.
fix: Research request: what is Costco's minimum operating cash requirement? Look at the 10-K liquidity section, seasonal working capital swings, and any stated minimum. Until this is answered, the waterfall cannot show a trough and the recommendation has no safety constraint.

issue: Slide 4 is doing two jobs — a return-vs-cost-of-equity bar chart and a buyback price-ceiling argument — and has no room for either. The 'same implied return at lower growth (e.g. 8% and 5%)' requires a sensitivity table, not a second bullet.
fix: Split into two slides: (a) 'The buyback earns 14.5% vs. a 6.4% cost of equity' with a bar chart; (b) 'The buyback stops clearing above $X or below Y% growth' with a 2x3 sensitivity table (growth 12.6% / 8% / 5% against price $1,106 / break-even / +10%). To keep 5 slides, merge slides 3 and 5.

issue: The $4B buyback is described as '3.6M shares at $1,106.21' — that is $4B / $1,106.21 = 3.62M shares, correct. But the 14.5% implied return uses operating cash flow growth of 12.6% a year over three years, which is a historical growth rate (F20: from $11.07B to $15.82B). Using a historical growth rate as a forward assumption in a growing-perpetuity model is an unsupported leap the board will challenge.
fix: State the 12.6% as a historical three-year CAGR in the slide footnote, and add a sensitivity: implied return at 12.6% / 8% / 5% growth. If forward growth is used, research consensus estimates for Costco operating cash flow growth.

issue: Cover includes 'market cap $490.19B' but F48 says 'market value of about $472.4b' — two different market caps in the same deck. Both may be correct at different dates; the reader will not know which to trust.
fix: Use one market cap. Either reconcile the $472.4B (F48, from the 11 November article) with the $490.19B (F28, computed from 13 November close) and footnote the difference, or drop the market cap from the cover entirely.

issue: Step (2) says 'approve the $4B buyback authorization with a pace of $1B per year' — over the January 2030 expiration, $1B/year is 4 years, so the authorization expires before it is fully used. This is a minor inconsistency but a board member will notice.
fix: Either pace at $1.33B/year to use the full authorization by January 2030, or note that the authorization is a ceiling and the pace is $1B/year with the remainder available for opportunistic use.

issue: Five slides, all dense with numbers, all in a navy theme with no visual variety. The cover, exec summary, waterfall, exhibit, and roadmap risk looking like five pages of the same slide with different numbers.
fix: Vary density and format: slide 1 cover uses one number ($13.3B) large; slide 2 uses an options table with three columns; slide 3 is the waterfall with one highlighted bar; slide 4 is a bar chart plus sensitivity table; slide 5 is a roadmap with five steps and owners. No two slides should share a layout.

where: Slide 2 (executive_summary), recommendation: '$13.3B special dividend = $30/share, $4B buyback authorization = 3.6M shares at $1,106.21'
issue: Internal contradiction that a committee will catch: 3.6M shares equals 0.8% of the 443.1M outstanding, but slide 2 also cites F29, 'every $1B spent on a buyback retires 0.90M shares (0.20% of 443.1M)', which implies 0.8% of shares for the full $4B (or 0.2% per $1B year). The '$4B = 3.6M shares' phrase conflates the authorization with shares actually retired and should be struck or restated.
fix: Replace the phrase with: '$4B authorization; at $1B/yr and $1,106, every $1B retires ~0.90M shares (0.20% of 443.1M); full $4B at today's price is ~3.6M shares if drawn.' Do not show 3.6M shares next to the authorization without the pace and timing.

issue: The bridge is self-contradictory: opening cash $20.21B + operating cash flow $15.82B − capex $6.43B − dividends paid $1.15B − buybacks $848M − the special dividend $13.3B = $14.15B, with no minimum operating cash identified. Slide 2 claims the dividend is funded from 'cash $20.21B + FCF $9.38B less capex $6.43B' but never states the trough or the floor; the numbers only work because of the unstated operating cash the business needs.
fix: On slide 3, state the ending cash line: '$20.21B + $15.82B − $6.43B − $1.15B − $0.848B − $13.3B = $14.15B' and add a defined minimum operating cash floor with its basis, showing $14.15B above it. If the $4B buyback is also drawn in the period, show the lower trough and say so.

issue: The cost of equity is doing all the work and is effectively unsourced: F31 is '6.4% = 10-year Treasury 5.15% (F25) + beta 0.24 x 5.0% equity risk premium (the premium is an assumption ...)'. Beta 0.24 (2 years of weekly returns) and a 5.0% ERP yield 6.4%; the ERP is an assumption with no source or range. The 14.5% implied return also hinges on a single three-year operating-cash-flow growth rate of 12.6%.
fix: Show the cost-of-equity build with the ERP sourced or ranged (e.g. Damodaran implied ERP, Kroll recommended range) and show cost of equity at beta 0.24 and at beta 0.8–1.0. Show the buyback implied return at three-year OCF growth of 5%, 8%, 12.6% and state the price below which it stops clearing 6.4%.

issue: The 14.5% implied return is inconsistent with holding capex at $6.43B: 3-year OCF growth of 12.6% was achieved with capex growing 14.2% a year (F19), and F38 says Costco expects capex growth to slow only after fiscal 2027, with F39 citing 33 openings in fiscal 2027. Buybacks fund from operating cash flow, not free cash flow after growth capex, so the growth assumption needs a capex line.
fix: Add a sensitivity that shows OCF growth as capex rises: operating cash flow $15.82B, capex $6.43B to, say, $8.0–$9.0B, and the resulting FCF and buyback capacity. Either reduce the buyback pace in years when capex rises, or state that growth capex is funded from cash on hand.

issue: The item is presented as a decision, but F41/F42 say the special dividend was already declared and the buyback reauthorized on 2026-11-11, before the November 2026 board date. The deck frames a ratified action as an open question, and the slide 5 call to action 'approve the $13.3B special dividend' is therefore stale or redundant.
fix: Recast the question as sizing and execution: the dividend is declared; the board's decisions are the buyback pace, the price ceiling, the cash floor, and capex funding. Change slide 5 step (1) to 'confirm the declared $30/share special dividend, payment Q1 2027' and keep the value at risk as execution (shares, price, cash trough).

issue: Mixed periods on the same bridge: F8 dividends paid $1.15B is for 2025-09-01 to 2026-05-10 (10-Q), while F9 buybacks $848.0M and the operating cash flow are for 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30. The $1.15B is a nine-month figure; annualizing the regular dividend implies about $1.5B, so the bridge understates cash out.
fix: Use one period for every line: either show the 10-K run-rate for dividends paid (recompute from F12 $5.54/share × 443.1M, or get the 10-K PaymentsOfDividends) or label the bridge as an eight-month 10-Q period and restate F9 to match. Do not mix 10-Q and 10-K periods in one waterfall.

issue: Critical figures are missing that the decision needs: (a) the debt-to-EBITDA or lease-adjusted leverage and interest coverage (interest expense $145.0M on $3.91B long-term debt, F6/F10, and $2.61B operating lease liabilities, F11) so the committee can see the rating impact; (b) the share count and EPS impact of the $4B authorization at the stated $1B per year pace. Neither is in the storyboard.
fix: Add to slide 2 a leverage and coverage line: long-term debt $3.91B, operating leases $2.61B, interest expense $145.0M, and cash $20.21B; show pro forma cash after the special dividend $13.3B and pro forma leverage. On slide 4, show EPS accretion from a $1B year: buyback shares 0.90M, new share count 442.2M, EPS $20.76 → $20.80 (per F33), and the same for the full $4B drawn.

issue: The cover shows the share price $1,106.21 (F21) and market cap $490.19B (F28) but never frames the price against the 52-week range of $850.00 to $1,106.21 (F22), which is a day at the high. The recommendation to buy back below $1,106 invites the committee's question: why is the top of the range the reference price?
fix: Add the 52-week range to the cover or slide 4: '$850–$1,106 (52-week), and the buyback price ceiling sits at the high.' This makes the price ceiling a live constraint, not a formality.

issue: No pro forma liquidity or cushion after the dividend: the material does not show how much cash remains, what the minimum operating cash floor is, or whether the $4B buyback can be drawn in a weak year. Slide 5 item (4) asks for a floor but the storyboard never names one.
fix: Add a pro forma liquidity box to slide 3: ending cash $14.15B (before floor), stated minimum operating cash floor, cushion, and a line saying buyback draws can be suspended if cash falls toward the floor. If the floor is not yet set, make it a named approval.

issue: The cover must-show lists the $13.3B special dividend and $4B buyback 'declared/reauthorized' but the headline deck title is phrased as the question 'return cash or fund growth?'; the subtitle names the decision. Fine, but the cover does not show the date or the source of F41/F42 as a filed fact versus a news item.
fix: On the cover, label F41/F42 as 'company announcement 2026-11-11' with the source, and add the date 'November 2026' clearly; reserve the question for the subtitle.

issue: F33 '$20.80 = EPS $20.76 x 443.1M / 442.2M shares' is labeled '(before lost interest on the cash)'; the lost interest at the 13-week T-bill 4.12% (F24) on $1B is about $41M before tax. The slide shows the gross-EPS version without the add-back, which flatters accretion.
fix: Add the after-tax interest loss: $1B at 4.12% T-bill, ~$41M pre-tax, ~$31M after tax at 24.7%; show EPS accretion before and after the cash interest. The result may still clear, but the committee will expect the add-back.

issue: It is three slides crammed into one: a three-bar return chart, a five-part argument, and an EPS-accretion calculation ($20.76 to $20.80, $41M pre-tax, $31M after tax, accretion about $0.03). A board reads one message per page; this one needs a voice-over.
fix: Keep left as the return-vs-cost-of-equity chart and the growth-sensitivity bars; keep right as the argument only. Move every EPS-accretion number to a labeled appendix page titled 'EPS accretion from a $1B buyback: about $0.03' — stale to the risk committee, not the board.

issue: Steps (1), (3) and (4) restate what slide 2 already approved as the decision ('confirm the declared $30/share special dividend', 'Hold warehouse capex at $6.43B', 'Set the operating cash floor at $12B'). The closing repeats the recommendation instead of converting it into actions.
fix: Rewrite the five steps as verbs with owners and timing only, removing all restated figures: (1) File and pay the special dividend, CFO, Q1 2027; (2) Execute the first $1B buyback tranche at or below $1,106, Treasurer, Q1 2027; (3) Fund the fiscal 2027 warehouse plan at the approved capex, COO, fiscal 2027; (4) Stand up the quarterly trough review and suspend draws near the floor, CFO, quarterly; (5) Report the buyback's return against cost of equity, IR, quarterly.

issue: The must-show list runs from the options table to buyback sizing to a leverage and coverage line to the $12B-floor caveat to a consensus footnote. That is four pages of content on the summary page; the table will lose to the text.
fix: Keep the three-column options table and the decision line. Move the leverage line (debt $3.91B, leases $2.61B, interest $145.0M, cash $20.21B) to a 'Balance sheet and coverage' back-up page; leave the $12B-floor caveat to slide 3 and the consensus footnote to both slides.

issue: Option A shows remaining cash $14.15B and Option C $31.45B, but the $12B operating cash floor appears only in the decision line and on slide 3. The columns read as if no floor exists.
fix: Add a row 'Cash vs $12B floor' to the table: A $14.15B (cushion $2.15B), B $18.15B, C $31.45B. Label the $12B as a board-set policy number on the same page.

where: Slide 4, 'break-even price is a research request, not yet computed'
issue: A board page cannot print a hole. The callout says 'pause above the price where the implied return falls to 6.4%' but no price is shown.
fix: Compute and show the break-even price. Using the material's own figures: implied return = 1.88% earnings yield + growth; at 6.4% cost of equity the break-even earnings yield is 6.4% - 12.6% = negative, so state the break-even price as the price at which price = EPS $20.76 / (6.4% - 12.6%) is undefined and instead show the price at 5% growth: about $1,621. Or drop the callout entirely and keep 'buy back below $1,106; suspend near the floor'.

issue: The cover carries the $4B buyback line, the $1,106.21 share price, the 52-week range and the $490.19B market cap — enough that the reader half-knows the answer before page 2.
fix: Keep the $13.3B one number large and the 'Board briefing, November 2026' subtitle. Move the $4B, $1,106.21, $850.00-$1,106.21 range and $490.19B market cap to slide 2 as a single 'Context' strip at the top of the options table.

issue: Both slides carry the same consensus footnote ('operating cash flow falling about 12% to around $14.0B next year'), and slide 4's footnotes run to three separate caveats. The repeat is harmless but the block is not.
fix: State the consensus fall once on slide 3 as a sensitivity bar ('-12% growth lowers the trough about $1.8B, still above floor') and delete it from slide 4; keep slide 4's footnote to the historical-CAGR caveat only.

issue: The '$12B operating cash floor' is a board-set policy number the briefing invents; there is no company-stated minimum, and the deck admits this in a footnote. A board cannot be asked to 'set the operating cash floor at $12B' when the number is not derived from Costco's own liquidity policy, debt covenants, or working-capital seasonality. Slide 3 then draws a dashed line at $12B and claims a '$2.15B cushion' against an undefined floor. This is an unsourced plug dressed as policy.
fix: Either (a) derive the floor: state minimum operating cash = e.g. 3 weeks of cost of goods / peak seasonal working-capital build, and show the number in the liquid assets section; or (b) if it must remain a board-set number, label it 'proposed $12B floor — board-set policy, no company-stated minimum; benchmarked to [three named peers' minimum cash]' and add the peer benchmarks as a data point. Do not present $12B as if it were a found fact. Until sourced, downgrade the claim from 'set' to 'propose'.

where: Slide 1 cover and Slide 2 exec summary
issue: Two different market caps are in play: F28 gives $490.19B (=$1,106.21 × 443.1M) and F48 (the 11 Nov article) says 'about $472.4b'. The storyboard tells the designer to 'Do not show the $472.4B' but never reconciles the $17.8B difference (which is the special dividend itself — $13.3B — plus the price move between 11 and 13 Nov). A director who saw the 11 Nov article will notice the gap and ask.
fix: Add one footnote to Slide 1: 'Market cap $490.19B at 13 Nov 2026 close = $1,106.21 × 443.1M. The 11 Nov article's $472.4B reflects the pre-announcement price; the $17.8B difference is price appreciation plus the $13.3B dividend, not a change in share count.' Then use only F28 throughout, as the storyboard already instructs.

issue: The 14.5% implied return is built on a 12.6% operating-cash-flow growth rate that is a three-year historical CAGR (F20, $11.07B FY23 → $15.82B FY26). Your own footnote (F50) says consensus expects operating cash flow to FALL ~12% to ~$14.0B next year. Slide 4 says 'which would put the implied return near the cost of equity' but never shows the number. In the bear case, implied return = 1.88% + (-12%) = roughly -10%, not 'near' the cost of equity. The recommendation to 'draw the $4B buyback at $1B a year' is therefore not supported by the briefing's own consensus data, and the committee will ask. This is the single largest hole in the deck.
fix: On Slide 4, add a third bar: 'Consensus case: operating cash flow -12% to $14.0B, implied return ≈ -10%; buyback does not clear the 6.4% cost of equity in the near term.' Then anchor the recommendation on a longer horizon: 'Buyback pace is justified only if three-year operating cash flow growth resumes above 4.6%; if consensus holds, the buyback fails its own test and the $1B should be redeployed to the dividend or held.' If the recommendation is to draw regardless, state the reason — e.g. share-count retirement at a 22.2% return on capital — and stop calling it a 14.5% return.

issue: Capex. Slide 2 says '30 net new warehouses unaffected' and holds capex at $6.43B. Slide 5 says 'Hold warehouse capex at $6.43B and the 30 net new warehouses a year'. But F39 says '33 warehouse openings in fiscal 2027, including five relocations, as it builds toward approximately 30 net additions'. F40 says 'spent $4,228 in the first thirty-six weeks of 2026 ... intention to spend approximately $6,500 during fiscal 2026'. So FY26 capex was $6.43B, FY27 intention is ~$6.5B, and 33 openings ≠ 30 net. The storyboard treats three different figures ($6.43B, $6.5B, 30 vs 33) as if they were one.
fix: Reconcile in a single line on Slide 2: 'FY26 capex $6.43B (10-K); FY27 intention ~$6.5B (10-Q, F40); 33 openings including 5 relocations → ~30 net (F39).' State explicitly that 'hold capex at $6.43B' means holding to FY26 actual rather than the FY27 $6.5B intention — i.e. a ~$70M reduction to the plan, not a freeze at the run-rate. Without this, the wording '$6.43B' and '30 a year' cannot both be true.

issue: The cost of equity of 6.4% is an outlier. It is built as 10-yr UST 5.15% + beta 0.24 × 5.0% ERP. A beta of 0.24 is not credible for Costco against the S&P 500 over two years of weekly returns (F23) — retail grocery, with 30 net new warehouses and a $490B cap, does not have a quarter of market risk. The deck acknowledges the sensitivity ('at beta 0.8–1.0 cost of equity rises to about 9.2%–10.2%'), which is good, but choosing 0.24 as the base makes the 14.5% spread look like 2.3x when it is ~1.4x at beta 0.8. A director will ask why the low beta is the base.
fix: Change the Slide 4 headline to the middle of the sensitivity range, e.g. 'At $1,106 and a 9.2%–10.2% cost of equity (beta 0.8–1.0), the buyback still clears but the spread is 1.4x, not 2.3x.' State 0.24 as 'Yahoo Finance 2-yr weekly beta; use 0.8–1.0 as the committee case'. If you keep 0.24 as the base, footnote why (e.g. 'two-year weekly beta understates market risk in a defensive staple') — otherwise it is a cherry-picked input.

issue: The waterfall does not bridge. Opening $20.21B + operating cash flow $15.82B - capex $6.43B - regular dividend $2.46B - buybacks $848M - special dividend $13.3B = $12.99B, not the $14.15B shown on the slide and reused in Slide 2. The $1.16B gap is exactly the difference between the nine-month dividend figure ($1.15B, F8) and the full-year run-rate ($2.46B). The slide intends the full-year number but the arithmetic still misses, so a sharp reader will flag the waterfall as tied out to nothing.
fix: Recompute and show the bridge with a balancing line: opening $20.21B + $15.82B - $6.43B - $2.46B - $0.85B - $13.30B = $12.99B, then take the ending cash to $14.15B via one named item only if the briefing can name it (e.g. working-capital inflow, other investing, FX). If no such item is identified, restate Slide 3's headline as '$12.99B trough' and cascade that number through Slide 2 ($14.15B → $12.99B before the floor; $2.15B cushion → $0.99B cushion). One number, one source, one period.

issue: The EPS accretion math mixes sources. F33 uses EPS $20.76 and 443.1M / 442.2M shares; the lost interest on $1B uses the 4.12% T-bill (F24) and 24.7% tax rate.
