where: slide 4, 'The business the cash comes from'
issue: $303.15B revenue, $9.23B net income, $145.0M interest expense are all labelled 'FY2026 ... is projected,' but slides 2 and 3 use FY2026 actuals from filed 10-Ks ($15.82B OCF, $6.43B capex) and FY2027 guidance ($7.50B capex). Calling FY2026 'projected' while treating FY2026 as actual elsewhere is an inconsistency a committee will catch.
fix: Label the source and basis for each: if FY2026 is filed, say 'FY2026 actual'; if the revenue and net income are consensus or internal estimates, say 'FY2026E (consensus, as of [date])' and cite it.

issue: Footnote 1: 'Sensitivity: at 0% operating cash flow growth the FY2027 residual falls to $8.38 and the safe ceiling is $8B, not $10B.' That is a good downside disclosure, but it is in a footnote below a chart that headlines $8.32B and a mandate of up to $10B; a committee reading the page will read $10B as fully funded. The $8B ceiling at zero growth directly constrains the top of the recommended range.
fix: Move the sensitivity into the body of slide 3 or slide 5 — e.g., a line under the bridge: 'At 0% operating cash flow growth the FY2027 residual falls to $8.38B, capping the authorization at $8B' — so the approved range and its downside are read together.

issue: The 'cost of carry' and 'capex safe' criteria (30% of the weight combined) are scored but no downside case is shown for either: no scenario where operating cash flow does not grow or where the $7.50B FY2027 capex is exceeded. The only downside in the deck is the slide 3 footnote.
fix: Add a row to the grid showing weighted scores under the slide 3 downside (0% operating cash flow growth) so the board sees which use of cash wins if the cash flow does not grow.

issue: The footnote '3 Downside: at 0% operating cash flow growth the FY2027 residual falls to $8.38 and the safe ceiling is $8B, not $10B' is set in the same small grey type as the source line, on the executive summary page, where the recommendation is $8-10B. The $10B is contradicted by the footnote on the same page.
fix: Either change the recommendation range to $8-9B on slides 1, 2 and 5 and state 'at 0% operating cash flow growth, the ceiling is $8B,' or move the $10B end of the range only if FY2027 operating cash flow growth is supported.

issue: 'Yahoo Finance daily close 2026-11-13; stockanalysis.com dividend history.' The close of $1,106.21 is used on slides 2, 4 and 5, but only slide 4 cites the price source; slides 2 and 5 cite 'Yahoo Finance COST close 2026-11-13' — consistent, but the date is 13 November while the board meeting is November 2026 with no day given on slide 1.
fix: Add the meeting date to slide 1 and keep the price-as-of date on every page that uses $1,106.21.

issue: Title runs to two lines and the body is a dense grid; the 'Preliminary' flag is top-right, which is right for a draft but must be removed before board distribution.
fix: Remove the 'Preliminary' flag for the final version and shorten the title after the per-share fix so it sets on one line.

issue: The title carries two competing messages ('A buyback retires 7.2-9.0M shares and can be paused; a dividend pays $18.06-22.57 once') and the italic lead-in reads '...; a dividend pays $18.06-22.57 once' — the 'once' is an orphaned fragment, and the left panel's scoring table ('Three uses of the cash scored on three criteria (0–4 each, weighted)') lists no options and no scores; the reader cannot see the scoring that justifies 'Buyback wins on flexibility'.
fix: Split into one message: make the title 'Buyback wins on flexibility at equal per-share value; a dividend cannot be paused' and put the three-option scoring table (Buyback / Special dividend / Hold cash, with the 0–4 per criterion figures and weighted totals) in the left panel. Move the per-share-value and dividend arithmetic to a single 'What each $1B does' block.

issue: The bottom-left 'The business the cash comes from' box holds three unrelated figures — '$303.15B FY2026 revenue', '$9.23B FY2026 net income', '$145.0M FY2026 interest expense' — that no title on the page needs; they are a data dump and the box has dead space around it.
fix: Cut the box. If the cash source must be shown, keep only '$9.38B FY2026 free cash flow' (already on slides 2-3) and use the reclaimed space for the scoring table. Do not restate revenue and net income on a capital-allocation page.

issue: The right-hand callout box repeats the title verbatim ('FY2026 free cash flow of $9.38B covers the FY2027 capex intention of about $7.50B') and the waterfall itself only shows three bars (15.82, -6.43, 9.38), so the FY2027 step-up the title claims is not in the chart.
fix: Extend the bridge to FY2027 (9.38 → about -7.50 → residual of about $1.88B) so the chart proves the 'covers the step-up' claim, and replace the callout headline with the takeaway the bars show: 'The FY2027 step-up leaves about $1.88B of residual cash flow'. Keep the two supporting bullets; cut the duplicate title line.

issue: Footnote 3 reads 'Downside: at 0% operating cash flow growth the FY2027 residual falls to $8.3B' — but on slide 5 footnote 3 the same sensitivity reads '$8.3B' and on slide 3 footnote 2 it reads 'about $8.3B'; three different phrasings of one number. Also footnote 2's 'it sits inside the $9.38B free cash flow the filings state.' is clipped mid-sentence by the footnote rule.
fix: Standardise the sentence: 'Downside: at 0% operating cash flow growth the FY2027 residual falls to about $8.3B.' Fix the footnote rule so footnote 2 is not cut off; move one clause to footnote 3 if needed.

issue: The word 'Preliminary' sits alone in the top-right corner above the title, and the title runs to two lines with the second line short ('$18.06-22.57 once'), leaving a ragged right edge that no other slide has.
fix: Either delete 'Preliminary' or set it as a proper running header on every page. Tighten the title to fit one line, e.g. 'Buyback wins on flexibility at equal per-share value'.

issue: The callout body opens 'Capex grew 14.2% a year to $6.43B and is guided to about $7.50B in FY2027' — 'a year' is ambiguous (CAGR vs. year-on-year) and the title above says 'FY2027 capex step-up' while the callout says 'capex intention of about $7.50B'.
fix: Say 'Capex grew 14.2% year on year to $6.43B in FY2026 and is guided to about $7.50B in FY2027.' Use 'step-up' only for the $1.07B increase, not for the $7.50B level.

issue: Slide 2 and slide 5 are near-duplicates: both close with the same three numbered items and the same 'Decision today' / 'Next step' framing, and slide 5 adds no owner/date that slide 2 lacked except 'CFO · Q1 2027' and 'COO · Quarterly through 2027'.
fix: Make slide 5 a genuine closing: keep only the resolution language and a single dated commitment table (Board — today; CFO — Q1 2027 first tranche; COO — quarterly capex review), and cut the restated capacity arithmetic that slide 2 already proves.

issue: Slide 2 says 'Cash of $20.21B against total debt of $6.16B means no new borrowing.' That is a gross-cash/gross-debt comparison that ignores committed obligations and working-capital seasonality; it reads as a plug to justify 'no new borrowing' instead of a real net-debt and liquidity test. It also conflicts with a board-size authorization ($8-10B) against a cash balance that is not unrestricted.
fix: Replace the line with a net-debt test: state net cash/debt as total debt of $6.16B less cash of $20.21B = net cash of $14.05B, then state the available liquidity after the $6.43B FY2026 capex plan and the $8-10B buyback. If a revolver is used, show it explicitly with its drawn/undrawn capacity.

issue: The coverage ratios as written are wrong. Slide 5 says 'Operating cash flow of $15.82B covers the $6.43B FY2026 plan 2.5x and the $7.50B FY2027 step-up 2.1x.' 15.82/6.43 = 2.46x, not 2.5x (rounding is defensible), but 15.82/7.50 = 2.11x, not 2.1x, and, more importantly, the $15.82B is FY2026 operating cash flow being used as if it covers the FY2027 capex step-up, which is a period mismatch. The deck's own bridge on slide 3 shows FY2026 FCF of $9.38B, so the FY2027 capex is covered by FY2026 FCF of $9.38B at 1.3x, not by the gross operating cash flow.
fix: Restate as 'FY2026 operating cash flow of $15.82B covers the $6.43B FY2026 capex plan 2.5x; FY2026 free cash flow of $9.38B covers the ~$7.50B FY2027 capex intention 1.3x.' If you want to show the gross 2.1x, label it as FY2026 OCF to FY2027 capex and flag the period mismatch in the footnote.

issue: The waterfall is labelled 'FY2026 actual to FY2027 guided capex' but the bridge shows only FY2026 figures ($15.82B – $6.43B = $9.38B). It does not bridge to FY2027 anywhere; the FY2027 step-up to ~$7.50B appears only in the side panel. The title claim 'FY2026 free cash flow of $9.38B covers the FY2027 capex step-up' is therefore not demonstrated by the chart.
fix: Either (a) retitle to 'FY2026 free cash flow of $9.38B covers FY2026 capex of $6.43B' and add a second step/side bar showing FY2027 capex of ~$7.50B covered by $9.38B, or (b) redraw as an FY2026 FCF to FY2027 capex bridge with residual of $1.88B ($9.38B – $7.50B) and label both years.

issue: The scoring grid ('Weights: per-share value 40%, flexibility 30%, cost of carry 20%', scores 0-4) is an unsourced, hard-coded judgement matrix. The 40/30/20 weights are a plug with no rationale and the total is 90%, not 100%. However the recommendation keys off 'Buyback wins on flexibility at equal per-share value' — that conclusion is not shown by the table, because no per-share value column is populated for dividend vs hold vs capex.
fix: Rebuild the grid with an explicit total (weights must sum to 100%: e.g., 40/30/20/10), show the raw per-share value calculation for each option, and state the source of the weights (board policy or management judgement). If per-share value is 'equal', show the two numbers side by side so the reader can verify.

issue: The EPS/return claims are unsourced and mechanically thin. Slide 2: 'lifts EPS to $20.80 per $1B' and slide 4: 'Buyback raises diluted EPS from $20.76' and '$20.80' — a $1B buyback at $1,106.21 retires ~0.90M shares, which on 443.1M shares is ~0.20% of shares, not enough to lift EPS from $20.76 to $20.80 on a like-for-like net income basis. The arithmetic does not tie unless net income, buyback price, tax on foregone interest and foregone interest income on the $1B are all shown.
fix: Show the EPS bridge: current diluted EPS $20.76 × 443.1M = ~$9.20B net income; assume $1B buyback, foregone interest income at the stated rate, and reduced share count of ~442.2M shares; recompute EPS. If the $20.80 includes the FY2025 1% buyback already done, restate as a delta and footnote the base.

issue: '22.2% After-tax ROIC on existing business is consolidated, not incremental' — this is a headline metric that does not support the decision (it is not incremental to the $8-10B) and its source is not given. The 0.53% dividend yield on a $5.88 annual rate is shown without stating whether $5.88 is the current declared annual dividend or a forward estimate; and it conflicts with a $1,106.21 close and a $5.88 rate only if that rate is the current dividend.
fix: Either remove the 22.2% ROIC box or footnote it as consolidated, not incremental, with source. Label $5.88 as 'current annualized dividend' or 'FY2026 declared' and show the yield math: 5.88/1,106.21 = 0.53%. If $5.88 is stale, update or mark as estimate.

issue: The sensitivity is buried in footnote 2: 'Sensitivity: at 0% operating cash flow growth the FY2027 residual falls to about $1.88B and the safe ceiling is $6.8B, not $10B.' That is a material downside that contradicts the recommendation of $8-10B and is in 6-point type, not on the page. If the safe ceiling is $6.8B under 0% growth, the $10B top of the range is not supported.
fix: Move the 0%-growth case to the page as a scenario bar or table row with the $6.8B ceiling, and reconcile the recommendation to it: either lower the mandate range or state the growth assumption that makes $10B safe (e.g., '10B requires X% OCF growth').

issue: The per-share dividend figure '$18.06-22.57' appears on slides 2, 4 and the cover with no derivation. It is not clear whether it is on 443.1M shares (which gives $18.06-22.57) or on a different share count; the ranges on slide 2 and slide 4 are identical but the surrounding text differs ('$8.0-10.0B once' vs 'per $1B'). No sheet or formula is cited.
fix: Add the derivation line: $8.0B / 443.1M = $18.06; $10.0B / 443.1M = $22.57 (or state the actual share count used) and footnote the diluted vs basic share count.

issue: 'Preliminary' appears in the top-right of the page but not on slides 1-3 or 5, so the deck's status is inconsistent and slide 4 looks like a different draft.
fix: Add the same status marker to all pages or remove from slide 4; standardize the header/footer.

issue: Footnote 3 says 'Downside: at 0% operating cash flow growth the FY2027 residual falls to $8.38B and the safe ceiling is $6.8B, not $10B.' The $8.38B and $6.8B numbers are not the same metric (residual vs safe ceiling) and neither is defined on the page, so the reader cannot reconcile them.
fix: Define both terms in the footnote or drop one; if $8.38B is residual and $6.8B is post-buyback safe capacity, show the arithmetic between them.

where: Slide 2, point 2, first bullet ('Use: a buyback retires 0.9M shares per $1B; a dividend pays out once') vs Slide 4 ('buyback retires 7.2-9.0M shares (1.63-2.03% of 443.1M)')
issue: Same arithmetic, two answers. 0.9M per $1B x $8-10B = 7.2-9.0M, so the slides agree only if a reader interpolates; taken at face value slide 2 reads as if the buyback retires 0.9M shares total. The exec summary is the one page a board member reads if he reads one, and it is wrong as written.
fix: Rewrite slide 2 bullet 2 as 'At the $1,106.21 close, the $8-10B authorization retires 7.2-9.0M shares (1.63-2.03% of 443.1M); each $1B buys 0.90M shares'. Keep the 0.90M/$1B rate in a footnote in the notes, not the headline bullet.

where: Slide 5, step 3 ('Keep capex on the $6.43B plan and the $7.5B FY2027 step-up: operating cash flow of $15.82B covers the plan 2.5x')
issue: The 2.5x is 15.82/6.43 using FY2026 capex. The FY2027 plan is $7.5B, and 15.82/7.5 = 2.1x. The sentence claims to cover both the current and the step-up and quietly uses the smaller denominator. On a page where the whole claim is 'we can fund growth and buy back', that is a selectivity the board will catch.
fix: State both: 'operating cash flow of $15.82B covers the $6.43B FY2026 plan 2.5x and the $7.5B FY2027 step-up 2.1x'. If the point is that headroom exists, say what is left: 15.82 - 6.43 = $9.39B in FY2026 and 15.82 - 7.5 = $8.32B against the FY2027 plan.

where: Slide 2, point 3 ('Headroom: $1.12B left on the existing authorization, expiring January 2027')
issue: The point is raised and never resolved. A board member's first question is 'is the $8-10B new money or does it include the $1,115M?', and no slide answers it. Slide 5 repeats 'a new resolution is required' without saying whether it stacks on, replaces, or absorbs the balance.
fix: On slide 2, point 3, add one sentence: 'The new authorization replaces the 2023 program; the $1,115M unspent expires with it, so the $8-10B is incremental authority, not $8-10B plus $1,115M.' Or state the opposite, whichever the board intends, but pick one.

where: Slide 3 title ('Free cash flow of $9.39B funds the $6.43B warehouse plan and the buyback') and the deck's top line throughout
issue: The deck has two different free cash flow numbers. F130 and slide 2 use $9.38B; slide 2's copy, slide 3's title and slide 5 all use $9.39B. 15.82 - 6.43 = 9.39, so the arithmetic says $9.39B and $9.38B is a rounding slip in the source fact. Right now the cover, F130 and the slides disagree by 0.01 and a board member might wonder if they are two different measures.
fix: Pick $9.39B everywhere, since it is the exact subtraction, and add a footnote on slide 2: 'computed from operating cash flow $15.82B less capex $6.43B'. Change the cover recommendation amount and F130 references to match, or accept $9.38B across the board — but not both.

where: Slide 2, point 2, second bullet ('A special dividend pays $18.06-22.57 per share once and cannot be taken back')
issue: The only number a board member will want on the dividend is 'how much cash, total?' The $8-10B is never stated as the dividend pool on any slide. The reader has to multiply $18.06 x 443.1M = $8.0B and $22.57 x 443.1M = $10.0B to see that the $8-10B range is identical for both options. That is the single most important comparison on slide 4 and it is left as homework.
fix: On slide 2, bullet 2, add the dollar total: 'a special dividend of $18.06-22.57 per share pays $8.0-10.0B once and cannot be taken back'. On slide 4, add the same $8.0-10.0B next to the special dividend row so the two options are visibly the same cash out.

where: Slide 4, 'earns 1.88% a dollar against 5.15% on idle cash' and slide 3, 'Idle cash earns the 5.15% US 10-year Treasury yield'
issue: The 1.88% earnings yield is an equity return; the 5.15% is a risk-free rate. Comparing them directly overstates the case for buyback unless the equity risk premium is stated. A buyback earns 1.88% plus future growth; cash earns 5.15% with no growth and no risk. As written the comparison is naive and a CFO will say so.
fix: Keep both numbers but label them correctly: 'a buyback earns 1.88% earnings yield today plus per-share growth, against 5.15% on cash with no growth'. If the board needs the comparison to carry the decision, disclose an assumed growth rate on the equity and source it.

where: Slide 4, Harvey grid ('three options as rows ... four criteria ... each scored 0-4 with the score printed and the weighted total per option')
issue: The grid has no stated weighting and no source for any 0-4 score. It is the decision table, and as planned it is an unstructured opinion with a numeric patina. A board member will ask 'who set the weights?' and there will be no answer on the page.
fix: State the weights above the grid (e.g., per-share value 40%, flexibility 30%, cost of carry 20%, capex safe 10%) and put a line under the grid: 'weights and scores are management's judgment; criteria chosen to match the three decision options.' If the weights are not defensible, replace the grid with a three-column options-vs-criteria table using only the sourced numbers (retired 7.2-9.0M shares; $18.06-22.57 per share once; 5.15% on cash).

where: Slide 2, point 1, second bullet ('Cash of $20.21B and long-term debt of only $3.91B back the plan')
issue: Long-term debt is non-current only. Current portion of long-term debt and any commercial paper are excluded, so 'only $3.91B' understates total borrowings. This is exactly the kind of selectivity that turns a friendly board member into a hostile one.
fix: Use total debt: pull the current portion of long-term debt and short-term borrowings from the same 10-K and state them. If total debt is still small, the point is stronger, not weaker. If the data is not in hand, mark as a research gap and do not claim '$3.91B' alone.

where: Slide 3, subtitle ('Operating cash flow less capital expenditure, FY2026, in $B') and slide 3 bullets (F142 precedes a current FY2026 $6.5B intention with an actual spent)
issue: The bridge uses one capex number and does not say whether $6.43B is warehouse capex, all capex, or includes maintenance. The slide title says '$6.43B warehouse plan' but the fact is total capital expenditure. The board will read 'warehouse plan' and assume new-store economics; the number is bigger than that.
fix: Change the slide 3 title to 'Free cash flow of $9.39B covers total capital expenditure of $6.43B and the FY2027 $7.5B step-up' or add the split if the 10-K discloses new warehouses vs. maintenance. Do not label total capex as 'warehouse plan'.

where: Slide 5, step 2 ('at the $1,106.21 close, $8-10B buys 7.2-9.0M shares') and step 4 ('$848.0M was repurchased in FY2026 at an average $950.90')
issue: The deck compares a buyback at $1,106.21 today with an average price of $950.90 in FY2026, and never addresses whether the stock is cheap or expensive relative to recent repurchases. If the board has been buying at $950 and is now asked to authorize at $1,106, someone will ask by how much they are marking up. The deck has the data (F155) but does not confront it.
fix: On slide 5, step 2, add one line: 'the FY2026 repurchase average was $950.90; the authorization is a standing program, not a commitment to buy all 9.0M shares at $1,106.21'. That preserves flexibility and pre-empts the question.

where: Slide 3, footnote 1 ('The buffer is a board policy choice, not a reported figure; the bridge is shown as a range because of it') vs slide 3 bullets ('A $2B buffer leaves $7.39B; a $6B buffer leaves $3.39B')
issue: Slide 3 shows a range for a buffer the recommendation on slide 2 does not use. If the buffer matters, it should be in the recommendation; if it does not, it is a distraction on the bridge page.
fix: Decide: either fold a stated buffer (e.g., $2B) into the slide 2 recommendation and keep the math on slide 3, or delete the buffer bullets from slide 3 and put them in backup. Right now the closing slide recommends no buffer.

where: Slide 4, right column ('after-tax return on capital is 22.2%')
issue: ROIC of 22.2% is the return on Costco's existing capital, not the return on the $8-10B buyback. Next to a buyback discussion a reader will read it as the buyback's return and it is not.
fix: Drop it from slide 4 or label it explicitly: 'existing-business ROIC 22.2%; this is not the return on incremental cash returned.' The buyback comparison already has 1.88% vs 5.15%.

where: Slide 1, cover ('No numbers on the cover beyond the recommendation amounts')
issue: The cover is the only place the recommended $8-10B range appears before the exec summary, and the subtitle names the capex figures but not the free cash flow that funds them. The cover should leave the CEO with the recommendation, not three separate numbers.
fix: Cover subtitle: 'Recommend approving an $8-10B buyback, funded from $9.39B of free cash flow after the $6.43B capital plan, with the FY2027 step-up to $7.5B fully funded. Reject the special dividend.' One sentence, one thought.

where: Slide 2, internal footnote 1 and footnote 2 ('options S2O1, S2O2'; 'Meshpool 2')
issue: 'S2O1/S2O2' and 'Meshpool' are build-system identifiers. They must not survive into the deck. The storyboard already flags this as a review note; record it as a production checklist item so it cannot slip through.
fix: Replace with plain language: 'the $8-10B size is a board choice, not a reported figure; it sits inside the $9.39B of free cash flow in the 10-K.' Delete 'Meshpool' entirely.

where: Slide 2, point 1 line 'Operating cash flow $15.82B less capex $6.43B leaves $9.39B free cash flow' vs Slide 3 title 'Free cash flow of $9.39B covers the $6.43B plan and the $7.5B FY2027 step-up'
issue: The $9.39B FCF figure is FY2026 actual (OCF $15.82B less capex $6.43B, item F130). That figure is spent once: it funds FY2026 capex of $6.43B and leaves $9.39B — but the FY2027 guided capex step-up to $7.5B (F140) has to come out of FY2027 cash flow, not out of the FY2026 residual. The slide as worded implies one pool funds both the $6.43B and the $7.5B, which double-counts the same cash. If FY2027 FCF is only ~$8.3-9.4B and capex steps to $7.5B, the residual pool is closer to $1-2B, not $8-10B. The recommendation size, as constructed, is not supportable as stated.
fix: Split the slide into two periods: FY2026 actual (OCF $15.82B less capex $6.43B = $9.39B) and FY2027 guided (OCF ~$15.82B growing 12.6% (F126) less capex $7.5B = ~$10.3B residual). State explicitly that the $8-10B buyback is funded from FY2027 free cash flow, and show the FY2027 residual after the $7.5B step-up ($10.3B), not the FY2026 $9.39B. Label the $9.39B as FY2026 and the buyback pool as FY2027.

where: Slide 2, 'Headroom: $1.12B left on the existing authorization, expiring January 2027' (F145, F155) and closing slide item 4 'Footnote: the 2023 $4,000M authorization expires January 2027 with $1,115M unspent, so a new resolution is required'
issue: Authorization headroom is $1,115M and FY2026 repurchases were $848.0M (F155, F115) — so the new $8-10B authorization is not incremental spend; it replaces a program with $1.12B remaining. The board decision is not 'approve $8-10B on top of $1.12B', it is 'increase from the $4,000M/$1,115M remaining to $8-10B'. The slide as written leaves the reader to do this subtraction themselves, which is exactly the arithmetic a committee will ask for and a hostile press will frame as 'buyback doubles' when it does not.
fix: State plainly: 'Current program $4,000M with $1,115M unspent (F145, F155); new authorization of $8-10B replaces it; incremental capacity above the rollover is $6.9-8.9B.' Put that incremental number in the title of Point 3 on slide 2 and in the closing footnote.

where: Slide 2, 'against 5.15% on idle cash' and Slide 3 bullet 'Idle cash earns the 5.15% US 10-year Treasury yield' (F53, source Yahoo Finance TNX 2026-11-13)
issue: The comparison is 1.88% earnings yield on a buyback (F134) vs 5.15% on idle cash. On its face, holding cash beats buying back stock 5.15% to 1.88%. The slide asserts buyback wins because it is 'flexible', but the number goes the other way. A committee will not accept a recommendation whose own figures say the status quo earns 2.7x what the proposed action earns. Either the comparison is wrong (5.15% is nominal, pre-tax, and after 24.7% effective tax rate (F123) is ~3.88% versus 1.88% pre-tax return on buyback) or the buyback case needs a different justification (per-share accretion, return on capital 22.2% (F136) deployed into new stores vs cash drag, or the assumption that cash is earmarked for capex so is not truly idle).
fix: On slide 4, replace the '1.88% vs 5.15%' headline comparison with the after-tax cash yield (~3.88% using 24.7% effective tax rate, F123) against the buyback earnings yield (1.88%, F134), and add the growth case: capital deployed into warehouses earns 22.2% after tax (F136), which is the actual alternative to cash, not Treasury bills. If the buyback recovers less than 3.88%, say so and justify the buyback on EPS accretion and the board's stated capital-return policy.

where: Slide 2, point 2 line 'At the $1,106.21 close, $8-10B retires 7.2-9.0M shares (1.63-2.03% of 443.1M)' and slide 4 same figure
issue: The math holds ($8B / $1,106.21 = 7.23M shares = 1.63%; $10B / $1,106.21 = 9.04M shares = 2.04%) but the deck uses the 16 November 2026 close, and repurchases will execute over quarters at unknown prices. The MD review note already flags 0.9M shares per $1B and 7.2-9.0M across $8-10B as a discrepancy (F133, F135). If the stock moves, the share retirement and the EPS accretion change materially: at $1,300, $10B retires 7.7M not 9.0M; at $900, 11.1M. The deck shows a point estimate at a single-day close that will be wrong by the time of purchase.
fix: Run the share retirement and EPS accretion at three prices ($900, $1,106.21, $1,300) as a sensitivity table on slide 4, and label the current figures as 'at the 2026-11-13 close only'. Add a line: '$8-10B retires 6.2-11.1M shares (1.39-2.50% of 443.1M) across an $900-1,300 share price range.'

Slide 3 shows capex grew 14.2% a year (F125) and operating cash flow grew 12.6% a year (F126); if OCF growth reverts to zero or revenue growth slows from 7.8% (F124), FY2027 FCF after the $7.5B capex step-up could fall below the $8-10B authorization and force the buyback to be paused or the capex plan to be cut. The deck offers a $2B and $6B buffer range (slide 3, 'A $2B buffer leaves $7.39B; a $6B buffer leaves $3.39B') but does not connect the buffer to the buyback size.

State the buyback that is safe at the low case (e.g., at 0% OCF growth, FCF FY2027 ≈ $15.82B − $7.5B = $8.32B minus the $2B buffer = $6.32B, so authorize up to $6B, not $10B). where: Slide 4, 'after-tax return on capital is 22.2%' (F136) and 'weighted total per option' grid

The score is a plug until the weights and the rubric are on the page.

Label 22.2% as 'Costco FY2026 consolidated after-tax ROIC (F136), not incremental — incremental warehouse ROIC is not disclosed and is a research gap'. Add a research request for the incremental ROIC on new warehouses.

where: Slide 3, 'Idle cash earns the 5.15% US 10-year Treasury yield' (F53) and slides 2, 3, 4 use of $1,106.21 close (F127)
issue: F127 is the Yahoo Finance close of 2026-11-13; today is 2026-11-16, so the price is 3 days stale at the board meeting and will be older by the time the deck is delivered. F53 is the Yahoo Finance TNX 10-year Treasury on 2026-11-13 — the deck uses the 10-year as the cash yield, but Costco's $20.21B cash (F5) does not earn the 10-year; it earns short-term money-market or T-bill rates. The 10-year yield overstates the opportunity cost of cash if the curve is upward sloping, which the deck assumes without showing the curve.
fix: Refresh the share price to the most recent close before distribution, and footnote the date on the cover and every page that uses it. Replace the TNX 10-year with the actual cash yield: 3-month T-bill or money-market yield as of the same date, sourced, and state the curve (3M, 1Y, 10Y) so the committee sees the carry opportunity cost. Add research request for the current 3M T-bill yield.

where: Slide 4, 'dividend pays $18.06-22.57 per share once' (F133, F127, F1) and slide 2 'A special dividend pays $18.06-22.57 per share once and cannot be taken back'

Without the precedent, the range looks arbitrary.

Also state explicitly: the special dividend is annual-dividend-neutral; the $5.54 declared per share (F118, F144) continues on top of the special.

where: Slide 3, waterfall 'FY2027 guided capex of $7.5B shown as the next bar and the residual $8.32B marked as the buyback pool'
issue: $15.82B OCF less $7.5B FY2027 capex = $8.32B residual. That is less than the top of the $8-10B range. The slide marks $8.32B as the 'buyback pool' while slide 2 recommends up to $10B. The two numbers do not tie, and the slide does not say the $10B would require drawing on cash or debt.
fix: On slide 3, replace '$8.32B' with '$8.32B residual after the FY2027 step-up; at $10B the authorization exceeds FY2027 FCF by $1.68B, funded from the $20.21B cash balance (F5)' — or reduce the authorization ceiling to $8B. State the source of the incremental $1.68B explicitly.

where: Slide 2, 'FY2026 repurchases of $848.0M and dividends of $1.15B already sit inside operating cash flow' (F115 and F8 per the deck's own note, F31)

If $5.54 declared × 443.1M shares = $2,455M declared, but cash paid was $1.15B, the timing difference (Q4 declared, paid in FY2027) needs one sentence.
fix: Correct the reference: replace 'F8' with the correct fact ID for cash dividends paid, or add the fact. Reconcile $1,150M paid against $2,458M declared (F144) with one line: 'Dividends declared 2026 of $2,458M (F144); cash paid in FY2026 of $X,XXXM; the difference is Q4 declaration timing.' Add a research request to source cash dividends paid from the 10-K cash flow statement.

where: Slide 2 title and governing thought: 'Approve an $8-10B buyback and fund the $6.43B warehouse plan'

The recommendation follows only if the board believes (a) the stock is undervalued and the 1.88% earnings yield understates the return to a long-term holder, or (b) cash is not truly idle because it is earmarked for capex. Neither belief is stated. Right now, the recommendation is asserted, not derived.
fix: On slide 4, add two sentences under the score grid: 'Buyback earns 1.88% on FY2026 earnings (F134); cash earns 5.15% nominal (F53) / ~3.88% after tax (F123). The buyback is recommended because (i) the board believes COST trades below intrinsic value on a normalized earnings basis — state the multiple assumed — and (ii) the cash balance is the capex reserve, not investable surplus.' where: Slide 2, point 3 line 'The 2023 program authorized $4,000M and only $1,115M remains unspent'

fix: Replace '2023 program' with '$4,000M authorization expiring January 2027' (F145). Drop '2023' unless a source for the authorization year is added.

where: Slide 3 bullet 'Cash of $20.21B against long-term debt of $3.91B means no new borrowing is needed'
issue: The $20.21B cash (F5) covers capex 3.1x (F131) but Costco also has current maturities and commercial paper that are not shown; long-term debt of $3.91B (F116) is the non-current portion only. If current debt is material, 'no new borrowing needed' needs the full stack.
fix: Add one line: 'Total debt position including current maturities of $X (needs citation); net cash of $X after all debt.' Or, if current debt is immaterial, state 'current portion of debt is immaterial' with the figure.

where: storyline, slide 2 vs slide 3 vs slide 5
issue: The deck names two different buyback pools. Slide 2 title and body: 'Approve an $8-10B buyback and fund the $6.43B capital plan' and 'funded from FY2026 free cash flow of $9.39B'. Slide 3 title: 'FY2027 free cash flow of $10.3B funds an $8B buyback'; slide 3 takeaway: 'the buyback draws on FY2027 free cash flow, not the FY2026 residual'. Slide 5 footnote and governing thought also say FY2027. The board cannot approve a mandate against two different sources of cash.
fix: Pick FY2027 as the funding year and make it consistent everywhere. Set slide 2 title to 'Approve an $8-10B buyback funded from FY2027 free cash flow of about $10.3B after the $7.5B capex step-up, and reject the special dividend' and rewrite point 1 so $9.39B FY2026 free cash flow is presented only as the opening balance that rolls into FY2027, not as the pool the buyback draws on.

where: storyboard, slide 3 visual 'waterfall_bridge', 'FY2027 residual of about $10.3B (OCF $15.82B growing 12.6% less $7.5B capex)'
issue: The $10.3B FY2027 pool is built by applying a trailing three-year 12.6% growth rate (F126) to FY2026 operating cash flow. No source supports FY2027 operating cash flow, and no source supports the $10.3B or the '$1.7B excess over FY2027 free cash flow' language. The whole sizing of the recommendation rests on an unsourced growth extrapolation presented as a fact on a board chart.
fix: Do one of two things. Either relabel the $10.3B as a scenario (base case = 12.6% OCF growth, sensitivity = 0% growth, giving $8.3B) with both cases printed on the waterfall as separate columns, and move the $10.3B out of the slide title into the chart labels; or commission the research and cite the driver before the pool is used to size the authorization. Do not let a computed growth rate and an unsourced operating-cash-flow projection appear in the same claim without one of the two labels.

where: storyboard, slide 4 'grid' — 'three options as rows (buyback $8-10B, special dividend $8-10B, hold cash) against four criteria (per-share value 40%, flexibility 30%, cost of carry 20%, capex safe 10%), each scored 0-4'
issue: The weights and the 0-4 scores are board policy choices invented in the deck. The slide presents 'buyback wins' as arithmetic when the arithmetic is entirely a function of weights the reader cannot challenge. That is the kind of page a board member dismisses in one question ('who set 40%?'), and it undercuts the credibility of the surrounding numbers, which are real.
fix: Either state the weights and scores as management's proposed rubric for debate and print them in the slide body (not buried in a footnote), or drop the grid. If you keep it, the takeaway becomes the honest claim: 'On management's proposed weights the buyback wins on flexibility; the weights are the decision, and the board should set them.' Keep the real numbers beside the grid ($8-10B retires 7.2-9.0M shares; special dividend pays $18.06-22.57 per share once; cash earns 5.15% against a 1.88% buyback earnings yield) as the actual evidence.

where: storyboard, slide 3 bullets — 'capex grew 14.2% a year to $6.43B and is guided to $7.5B in FY2027; operating cash flow grew 12.6% a year to $15.82B'
issue: The bridge nets a single capex line with no split between the warehouse plan and other capex, and the title asserts 'funds an $8B buyback' while the body discusses $10B and a $2B buffer. The slide is doing three jobs — showing the FY2026 bridge, forecasting FY2027, and sizing the buyback — and none of them cleanly.
fix: Split the slide. Title it as the FY2027 funding pool only: 'FY2027 free cash flow of about $10.3B covers an $8B authorization with a $2B buffer'. Show the FY2026 $15.82B / $6.43B / $9.39B as one reference bar on the left (labeled 'actual FY2026'), not as the first half of the waterfall. Delete the '$1.7B excess' language or move it to a footnote. Print both the 12.6% base case and the 0% sensitivity case in the chart.

where: storyboard, slide 2 point 3 — 'Headroom: $1.12B left on the existing authorization, expiring January 2027' and 'The 2023 program authorized $4,000M and only $1,115M remains unspent'
issue: The slide raises the $4,000M / $1,115M unspent authorization and never resolves whether the new $8-10B replaces it or adds to it. The earlier review already flagged this (F41). Slide 5's footnote answers it, five pages later. On the exec summary it reads as an unfinished thought.
fix: Move the resolution into slide 2 point 3: 'The $4,000M authorization expires January 2027 with $1,115M unspent, so the new $8-10B authorization replaces it; incremental capacity above the rollover is $6.9-8.9B.' Delete the same sentence from slide 5's footnote to avoid duplication.

where: storyboard, slide 4 footnote — 'incremental warehouse ROIC is not disclosed and is a research gap'
issue: The deck's own footnote admits the central question — whether the $7.5B FY2027 capex creates more value than a buyback — is unanswered. Yet the recommendation is to approve a buyback and 'keep capex on the $6.43B plan' without ever comparing the two returns. The 22.2% after-tax ROIC cited is explicitly 'consolidated, not incremental' (slide 4 body). A board member will ask 'what does the next warehouse earn?' and the deck has nothing.
fix: Either commission the incremental warehouse ROIC (see research requests) and put it on slide 4 next to the 22.2% consolidated figure, or reframe the recommendation so it does not depend on the comparison: 'Approve the $8-10B buyback because it is reversible and funded from free cash flow; do not reduce the capex plan because the incremental return on the next warehouse is not yet quantified.' The second is defensible today and honest about the gap.

where: storyboard, slide 2 vs slide 5 — '$8-10B retires 7.2-9.0M shares, 1.63-2.03% of 443.1M' and slide 2's earlier F40 flag that 'retires 0.9M shares per $1B' is printed as a headline

fix: Delete 'retires 0.9M shares per $1B' from slide 2 body. Keep the scaling rule (0.90M shares per $1B) as the footnote it already is on slide 4. On slide 2 print only the total: '$8-10B retires 7.2-9.0M shares, 1.63-2.03% of the 443.1M outstanding'.

where: storyboard, slide 1 cover — must show includes a full recommendation sentence and 'No numbers on the cover beyond the recommendation amounts'

Move the recommendation sentence and the $8-10B, $6.43B, $7.5B amounts to slide 2 where they belong. Apply the F13 composition fix (title block optically centred, bottom half clean).

where: storyboard, slide 5 — 'the FY2026 repurchase average was $950.90'

issue: Free cash flow is stated as $9.39B on slide 2 ('$9.39B free cash flow') and as '$9.38B' in F130 and in the slide 2 footnote construction; the FY2027 residual is '$10.3B' on slide 3 and 'about $10.3B' on slide 5, but the arithmetic '$15.82B growing 12.6% less $7.5B capex' gives $15.82 x 1.126 - 7.5 = $10.31B only if the 12.6% is applied to OCF, not to FCF. F130 says '$9.38B = operating cash flow $15.82B less capital expenditure $6.43B', which computes to $9.39B on the stated inputs; correct F130 to $9.39B and make slide 2, slide 3 and slide 5 read $9.39B, with the FY2027 pool shown as $10.31B (rounded to $10.3B) and the derivation 'OCF $15.82B x 1.126 = $17.81B, less $7.5B capex = $10.31B' printed on the chart.

issue: The FY2027 pool of $10.3B rests entirely on an unsourced 12.6% OCF growth rate (F126 is a historical three-year CAGR from $11.07B to $15.82B, not a forecast). fix: Move the 0% growth case out of the footnote and onto slide 3 as a second scenario column: 'FY2027 OCF $15.82B flat, less $7.5B capex = $8.3B pool; buyback ceiling covered by FCF is $8.3B, with $1.7B above that funded from the $20.21B cash balance.' Title slide 3 to the range, not the point estimate: 'FY2027 free cash flow of $8.3-10.3B funds the buyback; $10B draws $1.7B on cash.'

issue: The deck admits 'incremental warehouse ROIC is not disclosed and is a research gap' and then proceeds to score 'capex safe' at 10% weight and conclude 'buyback wins' on arithmetic. A board deciding whether to fund warehouses or buy back stock is being asked to accept a 22.2% *consolidated* ROIC (F136, existing business, not incremental) as a proxy for new-warehouse returns, with no sourced figure for the thing being decided. The weighted total is therefore an asserted recommendation dressed as a grid.

Either research a defensible incremental return (see research requests) and disclose the method, or restate slide 4 to show the decision turns on the $8.3-10.3B FY2027 FCF pool and the flexibility of a pausable authorization, and demote the grid to a secondary exhibit.

where: storyline, slide 4, 'lifts diluted EPS to $20.80 per $1B' versus F119/F3
issue: Diluted EPS of $20.76 (F119) on 443.1M shares implies net income of about $9.20B, and F3 states net income of $9.23B; the $0.03B difference is not reconciled and the deck's headline share count (F1, 443.1M) is a shares-outstanding figure at 2026-09-29, not the diluted weighted-average behind EPS. where: storyline, slide 2, 'the FY2027 step-up to $7.5B still leaves about $8.3B'
issue: This is internally inconsistent with slide 3 and slide 5, which use the 12.6% growth case ($10.3B). issue: The Harney grid scores are all internal and the 'buyback wins' result is a function of weights chosen in the footnote ('per-share value 40%, flexibility 30%, cost of carry 20%, capex safe 10%'). No score for any option is printed in the storyboard, only the claim that the weighted total makes it arithmetic.

Drop the word 'equal' where it is not provided by the scores.

where: storyline, slide 4, 'cash earns 5.15% nominal, about 3.88% after tax at the 24.7% effective rate'
issue: 5.15% is sourced to Yahoo Finance TNX (slide 3 source line, F53 context) — a market yield on the 10-year, not a rate Costco earns on cash, and the 24.7% effective tax rate (F122 context) is the company's book rate on operating income, not the tax rate on interest income. The after-tax cash return of 3.88% is a computed plug with no stated basis for applying the effective rate to interest income.
fix: Replace with a sourced cash yield: 'cash of $20.21B; the 10-year Treasury closed 5.15% on 2026-11-13 (Yahoo Finance TNX); Costco does not disclose a cash yield, so the opportunity cost is shown at the 5.15% market rate on a pre-tax basis, with taxes noted separately.' Do not state 3.88% after tax unless the tax basis is sourced.

where: storyline, slide 2, '$848.0M and dividends of $1.15B already sit inside operating cash flow'
issue: Dividends paid of $1.15B is unsourced in this storyboard. F144 states dividends *declared* of $2,458M ($5.54/share) and slide 4 uses $5.54/share; $1.15B on 443.1M shares is $2.60/share, which is neither the declared rate nor the cash-paid figure. Either the $1.15B is cash dividends paid (a different fact not in the set) or it is wrong.
fix: Cite the cash-dividends-paid line from the 10-K cash flow statement and use it consistently, or delete the sentence. If the intent is to say dividends and buybacks are already inside OCF, print 'dividends declared $2.458B (F144) and repurchases $848.0M (F115) are already funded within FY2026 operating cash flow of $15.82B' and drop the unsourced $1.15B.

where: storyline, slide 2, 'K9: the new $8-10B authorization replaces it, so incremental capacity above the rollover is $6.9-8.9B'
issue: This mixes stock and flow and is not resolved anywhere. $1,115M unspent on a $4,000M authorization (F145) is remaining *authorization*, not cash; calling the new $8-10B program an incremental $6.9-8.9B 'capacity above the rollover' implies the $1,115M would otherwise have been spent in FY2027, which slide 5 itself walks back ('a standing program, not a commitment to buy all 9.0M shares'). Commitments and authorizations are being netted as if they were dollar flows.
fix: State it as authorization, not spend: 'Existing authorization: $4,000M, expiring January 2027, with $1,115M unspent (F145). Proposed new authorization: $8-10B. The board is being asked to replace, not add to, the expiring program; the incremental authorization is $4-6B, and actual FY2027 purchases are at the company's discretion within the program.'

where: storyline, slides 2 and 4, share price $1,106.21 at close on 2026-11-13
issue: The $1,106.21 close (F127) is a single Yahoo Finance daily close, three days stale to the cover date (November 2026) and unsupported by any trading range or volume. Every dollar figure in the deck (7.2-9.0M shares, $20.80 EPS, the $8-10B ranges) scales off this one print. A committee will ask what the stock does on a normal day and whether $1,106.21 is representative.
fix: Source a 30-day VWAP or 30-day average close from a filing or exchange data and use the average for sizing, with the 2026-11-13 close shown alongside; or state 'at the $1,106.21 close on 2026-11-13; a 5% move in the share price changes shares retired by roughly 0.3-0.4M' so the sensitivity is on the page.

where: storyline, slide 3 'capex grew 14.2% a year to $6.43B and is guided to $7.5B'
issue: The bridge shows one capex line and slide 3 does not split warehouse capex from other capex; the decision is specifically about funding *warehouse growth*, and the deck cannot show what share of the $6.43B is warehouse openings versus remodels, technology or supply chain. F141 gives 28 warehouses opened in 2026 and up to 33 planned in 2027 but no dollars per warehouse, so capex per warehouse is not derivable.
fix: Add one split to slide 3: 'FY2026 capex $6.43B; warehouse openings 28 in FY2026 and up to 33 in FY2027 (F141); cost per new warehouse not disclosed in the 10-K' and flag it as a research item. Do not imply the $6.43B is all warehouse growth.

where: storyline, slide 5, 'the FY2026 repurchase average was $950.90'
issue: F155 average price of $950.90 covers 891,000 shares repurchased in FY2026; using it beside a $1,106.21 current price without dates invites the reader to compare an average realized price to a spot price. The comparison is directionally useful (the current price is above the FY2026 average) but the deck does not say so.
fix: Make the point explicit: 'FY2026 repurchases averaged $950.90 (F155) versus $1,106.21 today (F127); the authorization is a program, so the board is not committing to buy at today's price.'

issue: Internal model/scratchpad references (S2O1, S2O2) are in the board-facing footnote as already flagged in the file.
fix: Replace with plain language: 'The $8-10B size is a board policy choice, not a reported figure; it sits within the FY2026 free cash flow of $9.39B and the FY2027 pool of $8.3-10.3B.'

issue: 22.2% = operating income $11.69B x (1 - 24.7%) / (equity $35.80B + long-term debt $3.91B); the denominator excludes current debt of $2.248B and all operating leases, which for a warehouse retailer are material. The number as printed overstates the denominator's completeness.
fix: State the definition on the slide: 'after-tax return on capital, defined as operating income $11.69B x (1 - 24.7%) / (equity $35.80B + long-term debt $3.91B); excludes current debt of $2.248B and operating lease liabilities.' Or add leases if the added debt is sourced.

issue: Share retirement is inconsistent: slide 2 item 3 says the $8B return retires 5.42M shares (1.22% of the count), slide 4 says 7.2M shares retired (1.6% of shares outstanding). Both cannot be true.
fix: Pick one: if the $6B buyback at $1,106.21 retires 5.42M shares, the slide 4 table cell for 'Return $8B (O1)' must read 5.42M and the 'in four numbers' tile must read 5.42M and 1.2%; correct the shares-retired figure in slide 4's table and the tile to match slide 2.

where: slide 4, bottom-right 'What the cash pile earns today' box
issue: The '22.2%' tile is cut off at the bottom edge and the caption 'The cash must beat this after-tax return on capital' is clipped and overlapping the source line. Text is running off the slide.
fix: Either close the box with only the two tiles (1.88% earnings yield and 5.15% Treasury) and put the 22.2% comparison in a sentence, or extend the box to full height; set the caption inside the box above the source line, no text beyond the bottom margin.

issue: Title claims 'lifts EPS about 1.7%' and the right box repeats 'lifting EPS about 1.7%', while slide 2 item 4 says 'lifts EPS from $20.76 to about $21.01' (about 1.2%) and shows a 1.88% earnings yield, not 1.7%. Three EPS numbers on three pages.
fix: Reconcile to one EPS accretion figure. Show the arithmetic once (shares retired x EPS-per-share saved, net of forgone interest) and use that single number in slide 2 item 4, slide 4's title and slide 4's right box.

issue: The bullet 'The buyback earns a 1.88% earnings yield, below the 5.15% Treasury, so size it, do not maximise it' hedges the recommendation the slide is asking the board to approve. The page presents a 1.7% EPS lift and then undercuts it.

where: slide 4, 'What the cash pile earns today' box

where: slide 4, 'Three options against four criteria, scored from the numbers shown'

issue: '22.2%' is cut off by the bottom of the box and the sentence 'The cash must beat this after-tax return on capital' is truncated by the page edge; the bullet text 'revised' also runs past the right margin. Page 4 has more content than its frame.

issue: The table header wraps mid-word: 'Operat / ing / cash / flow' and 'Cash retain / ed', and the rows are squeezed so tightly the three options run together. This is unreadable and would not go out.

issue: The four tiles ($8B, 5.42M, +1.2%, 1.9x) restate the title and the right-hand callouts instead of adding proof. The page says the same thing three ways and still never shows the three options side by side in numbers a reader can check.

issue: Two headings collide: the table title 'Three options against five criteria...' overlaps the 'Operating cash flow' characters of the table beneath it, and the right heading 'What the $8B costs and earns' sits on a dark band that stops short of the column edge.

issue: The deck never resolves the announced $4B buyback against the proposed $6B: slide 2 item 5 and slide 5 item 1 both say the $8B 'must be reconciled with' the announced actions, but slides 3-4 keep scoring the $6B buyback as if the $4B does not exist. issue: The right column is text-heavy while the left column is a cramped table and four empty tiles; the page's weight is lopsided and half of it is dead space.

where: slide 4, 'What the cash pile earns today' box
issue: The 22.2% 'cash must beat this after-tax return on capital' appears once, with no supporting calculation, and does not connect to any option in the table.

issue: The 'Next step / What it involves / Owner and timing' header row is set at the same weight and size as the body text, so it does not read as a header, and the four rows have unequal padding.

issue: 'Preliminary' sits at the top right on every page, the source block runs unbroken for two lines, and slide 3's footnote repeats the same $6.43B plan definition already on slide 3's chart. It is clutter, not evidence.

issue: 'authorise the CFO to reconcile it with the announced $30 dividend and $4B buyback' is repeated verbatim on slide 1 and slide 2, and the closing page adds an approval for the same thing. The ask is stated three times, which reads as uncertainty.

where: slide 2, row 4 and slide 4, 'What the $8B costs and earns'

where: slide 4, 'What the cash pile earns today'

fix: Add a valuation page: (i) a football field with at least three methods (DCF, trading comps, dividend-discount or precedent transactions); (ii) state the comps set and the selection criteria; (iii) show DCF sensitivity on forecast operating cash flow and WACC, and state what share of DCF value is terminal value; (iv) reconcile the $6B/$2B split to the value per share that each alternative implies.

issue: The waterfall reads Cash on hand $20.21B, Return to shareholders -$8.00B, Retained before capex $12.21B — but the label 'Cash retained before capex' under the final bar does not say whether capex of $6.43B has been deducted. issue: Slide 5 row 1 says 'the announced $30 per share special dividend is about $13.29B on 443.1M shares, plus the $4B buyback, about $17.29B; the proposed $8B is incremental to that.' issue: The four-number banner ('$8B', '5.42M', '+1.2%', '1.9x') overlaps and clips the option table above it; the table's second and third rows are partially hidden. This is also a readability blocker, but classified as layout because the fix is structural.

issue: The cover's decision line ('authorise the CFO to reconcile the return with the announced $30 dividend and $4B buyback') same conflict as slide 5: 'reconcile' is vague about whether the $8B is additive to or a substitute for the announced actions.

issue: Item 4 says 'Buyback earnings yield 1.88% vs 5.15% Treasury: the $6B buyback is EPS-accretive, the $2B dividend is not, so recommend the $6B/$2B split'. This contradicts the recommendation. If the buyback is accretive and the dividend is not, why give $2B to the non-accretive dividend?

issue: The bullet says 'The buyback earns a 1.88% earnings yield against the 5.15% Treasury, so size it, do not maximise it.' This recommends against the very thing the page and the deck are asking the board to approve.
fix: Remove the 'do not maximise it' line, or reframe it as an explicit trade-off with the board's objective (e.g., EPS accretion now vs. interest income forgone) and state what the board should weigh.

issue: The table says '$5.42M shares retired' but the correct number is 5.42M shares. The '$' symbol is wrong and the number does not match the 5.42M quoted on slides 2 and 4 side text.

issue: The 'Score (0-4)' column shows 1 for Hold all $20.21B and 4 for Return $8B, but the page does not show the scoring rule. A reader cannot reproduce or challenge the 1 vs 4.

issue: Items 1, 2 and 3 carry three different cash-coverage numbers (2.5x, 3.1x, 1.9x) and an interest expense of '0.05% of $303.15B revenue'. The 0.05% figure is trivial and the multiple coverage numbers create confusion rather than a clean spine.

where: slide 2, point 3 vs slide 4, 'What the $8B costs and earns'

where: slide 2, point 4 and slide 4 right panel
issue: The EPS accretion is asserted, not calculated. Show the $0.25 gross and the net figure after interest foregone; state the resulting % as the headline on slide 4 or relabel it 'before lost interest income'.

issue: The waterfall does not tie to its own numbers. issue: The 1.88% earnings yield vs 5.15% Treasury comparison is presented as a reason to do less, but the conclusion 'so size it, do not maximise it' is not tied to any cost of capital or hurdle. fix: Add a line on slide 4: the company's WACC / equity cost of capital and the applicable hurdle rate, and the net spread of the buyback (earnings yield less after-tax cost of the funds). If the answer is that the buyback is EPS-accretive but NPV-negative at 5.15%, say so.

fix: On slide 5 row 2, drop the $17.29B or label it explicitly as 'announced package $17.29B; plus proposed $8B = $25.29B total'. Ensure $30 dividend x 443.1M shares = $13.29B is footnoted with the share count date.

issue: Slide 1, the cover, has no sources and no footnote at all, yet it carries the recommendation and $25.29B total. issue: Slide 4 argues 'Returning $8B beats holding all the cash or returning all $20.21B', but F175 says Costco 'declared a special cash dividend of $30 per share' and F173 says it 'reauthorized a $4 billion buyback'. where: Slide 2, 'The $8B return earns a 1.88% earnings yield, $9.23B net income over a $490.2B market cap' and '$130.4M a year' (F16, F30, F31)

issue: F166's earnings yield uses 'diluted EPS $20.76' from F151, and F167's post-buyback EPS uses '$20.80 = EPS $20.76 x 443.1M / 442.2M shares' from a $1B buyback. where: Slide 2, F27: 'Interest expense of $145.0M is 0.05% of revenue, so debt is not the constraint'

Low interest expense vs revenue says nothing about whether debt is a constraint on returning cash; the relevant test is debt/maturities versus cash and EBITDA. A committee will ask what the $145.0M is owed on, and the deck has no debt balance, no maturity schedule.

where: Slide 5 and slide 2: no comparison to peers or to Costco's own history

where: Storyline, opportunity cost framing across slides 2-4

The deck states the benefit side (1.88%, which is itself misapplied per the first issue) and never quantifies the cost. A committee weighing 'return vs. hold' will ask for the spread.

where: Slide 1 cover: 'Fund the $6.43B warehouse plan and return $8B of cash'

where: Slide 2 and Slide 4, F173 and F175

where: Slide 1 'must show' (F159) and the whole deck's .20% scaling rule (F165)

where: Slide 2 comparison row and slide 5 step 1 (F173/F174/F175/F182)
issue: The deck's comparison row rests on two secondary aggregators (capitaldigest.com and a Yahoo Finance article) both dated 2026-11-11/12, with no company filing or press release cited. where: Slide 3 right column, slide 4, slides 2-5 footnotes
issue: The accretion case is asserted before it is calculated. Slide 3 asks to 'show the accretion as a calc from diluted EPS and the share count' but F167 only gives the $1B case ($20.80 = $20.76 x 443.1M / 442.2M). The deck's own 1.2% figure for $8B has no calc fact behind it; F166 earnings yield is 1.88% ($20.76/$1,106.21), which is well below any plausible November 2026 short-term rate, so a buyback funded from cash is EPS- and value-dilutive once forgone interest is charged.
